b1-nuevasrepublicas-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Uti Possidetis
b1-nuevasrepublicas-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You had a class about borders in Latin America, and Meg asks what uti possidetis was.
cues: Say what each country kept
Say what historians say about the disputes
b1-nuevasrepublicas-02.target: Según este principio, cada país conservaba los límites coloniales. Según los historiadores, hubo muchas disputas.
b1-nuevasrepublicas-02.english: According to this principle, each country kept the colonial limits. According to historians, there were many disputes.
b1-nuevasrepublicas-02.canDo: I can explain the principle of uti possidetis.

b1-nuevasrepublicas-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Liberals and Conservatives
b1-nuevasrepublicas-03.scenario: You are Meg. You watched a documentary about the 19th century, and Carlos asks what liberals and conservatives disagreed about.
b1-nuevasrepublicas-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what they disagreed about.
cues: Say what the two groups had in common
Say what they disagreed about, with a connector
b1-nuevasrepublicas-03.target: Los liberales y los conservadores eran de la élite; sin embargo, tenían ideas diferentes sobre la Iglesia.
b1-nuevasrepublicas-03.english: Liberals and conservatives were from the elite; however, they had different ideas about the Church.
b1-nuevasrepublicas-03.canDo: I can say what liberals and conservatives disagreed about, starting with the Church.

b1-nuevasrepublicas-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Pronunciamientos
b1-nuevasrepublicas-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You read a book about Mexico, and Meg asks why governments changed so often.
b1-nuevasrepublicas-04.prompt: Tell Meg what used to happen in Mexico.
cues: Say how long presidents used to govern
Say what an officer used to do
b1-nuevasrepublicas-04.target: Los presidentes solían gobernar poco tiempo. Un oficial solía escribir un plan y pedir apoyo a otros soldados.
b1-nuevasrepublicas-04.english: Presidents used to govern for a short time. An officer used to write a plan and ask other soldiers for support.
b1-nuevasrepublicas-04.canDo: I can say what presidents and officers used to do in Mexico after independence.

b1-nuevasrepublicas-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Balance of 1850
b1-nuevasrepublicas-05.scenario: You are Meg. You had a class about the first decades of independence, and Carlos asks for a summary.
cues: Open with a summary marker
Say what Mexico lost in 1846 to 1848
b1-nuevasrepublicas-05.target: En resumen, los nuevos países tenían tres grandes desafíos. México perdió cerca de la mitad de su territorio en la guerra con los Estados Unidos.
b1-nuevasrepublicas-05.english: In summary, the new countries had three big challenges. Mexico lost about half its territory in the war with the United States.
b1-nuevasrepublicas-05.canDo: I can summarise the main challenges of the new republics around 1850.

b1-nuevasrepublicas-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: New Republics Review
b1-nuevasrepublicas-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You visited a museum about the new republics with a friend, and Meg asks what you learned.
b1-nuevasrepublicas-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg one thing about unions and one about politics.
cues: Say what happened to the Gran Colombia
Say what presidents used to do
b1-nuevasrepublicas-consolidation.target: La Gran Colombia fue disuelta en 1830. Los presidentes de México solían gobernar poco tiempo.
b1-nuevasrepublicas-consolidation.english: The Gran Colombia was dissolved in 1830. Presidents of Mexico used to govern for a short time.
b1-nuevasrepublicas-consolidation.canDo: I can say what happened to some early unions and why politics was unstable.

b1-caudillismo-01.title: Communicative Challenge: What Was a Caudillo?
b1-caudillismo-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos watched a documentary about the 19th century, and he asks what a caudillo was.
b1-caudillismo-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what a caudillo was.
cues: Say that a caudillo was a chief
Say what he had, with a relative clause
b1-caudillismo-01.target: Un caudillo era un jefe que tenía su propio ejército.
b1-caudillismo-01.english: A caudillo was a chief who had his own army.
b1-caudillismo-01.canDo: I can use relative clauses with *que* and *quien* to say who a caudillo was and who followed him.

b1-caudillismo-02.title: Communicative Challenge: How Páez Held Power
b1-caudillismo-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg is reading a book about Páez and asks how he kept his power.
b1-caudillismo-02.prompt: Tell Meg what Páez counted on.
cues: Say what Páez counted on
Say who depended on him
b1-caudillismo-02.target: Páez contaba con la lealtad de los llaneros, y los jefes locales dependían de él.
b1-caudillismo-02.english: Páez counted on the loyalty of the llaneros, and the local chiefs depended on him.
b1-caudillismo-02.canDo: I can use verbs with a fixed preposition (*contar con*, *depender de*, *confiar en*) to describe a caudillo's network.

b1-caudillismo-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Montoneras
b1-caudillismo-03.scenario: You are Meg. You are preparing a class about the montoneras, and Carlos asks what happened when a war ended.
b1-caudillismo-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what the men did when the war ended.
cues: Say when it happened
Say what the men did
b1-caudillismo-03.target: Cuando terminaba la guerra, los hombres volvían a su trabajo.
b1-caudillismo-03.english: When the war ended, the men went back to their work.
b1-caudillismo-03.canDo: I can use *cuando* and *mientras* to say what happened and what was going on at the same time.

b1-caudillismo-04.title: Communicative Challenge: What Sarmiento Wrote
b1-caudillismo-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg visited a museum, and she asks what Sarmiento wrote about the countryside.
cues: Say that he wrote it
Say what the countryside represented
b1-caudillismo-04.target: Sarmiento escribió que el campo representaba la barbarie.
b1-caudillismo-04.english: Sarmiento wrote that the countryside represented barbarism.
b1-caudillismo-04.canDo: I can use reported speech (*dijo que*, *escribió que*) to say what people said and wrote about the caudillos.

b1-caudillismo-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Legacy of the Caudillos
b1-caudillismo-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks you what many historians think about the caudillos after reading your class notes.
b1-caudillismo-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what turned out to be difficult.
cues: Say what many historians think
Say what turned out to be difficult
b1-caudillismo-05.target: Según muchos historiadores, resultó difícil crear instituciones fuertes.
b1-caudillismo-05.english: According to many historians, it turned out to be difficult to create strong institutions.
b1-caudillismo-05.canDo: I can use *resultar* + adjective to say what turned out to be difficult, useful or dangerous.

b1-caudillismo-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Summing Up the Caudillos
b1-caudillismo-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing for a class, and she asks you about Rosas.
cues: Say that he was a landowner, with a relative clause
Say what he governed and until when
b1-caudillismo-consolidation.target: Rosas, que era hacendado, gobernó Buenos Aires hasta 1852.
b1-caudillismo-consolidation.english: Rosas, who was a landowner, governed Buenos Aires until 1852.
b1-caudillismo-consolidation.canDo: I can talk about the caudillos with relative clauses, verbs with a fixed preposition, *cuando* and *mientras*, reported speech and *resultar* + adjective.

b1-nacionnacionalismo-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Country They Belonged To
b1-nacionnacionalismo-01.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg visited a museum about the new republics, and she asks what country people felt part of after independence.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-01.prompt: Tell Meg about the country people belonged to.
cues: Say that the country was new
Use a relative clause with a preposition
b1-nacionnacionalismo-01.target: El país al que pertenecían era nuevo.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-01.english: The country they belonged to was new.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-01.canDo: I can use *el que*, *la que*, *los que* and *las que* after a preposition to describe the country or community people belonged to.

b1-nacionnacionalismo-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Mexican Anthem
b1-nacionnacionalismo-02.scenario: You are Meg. You are preparing a class about national symbols, and Carlos asks about the Mexican anthem.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-02.prompt: Tell Carlos when the Mexican anthem was first sung.
cues: Say what was sung
Say the year
b1-nacionnacionalismo-02.target: El himno mexicano se cantó por primera vez en 1854.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-02.english: The Mexican anthem was sung for the first time in 1854.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-02.canDo: I can use the passive with *se* (*se crearon himnos*) to say what was created and when.

b1-nacionnacionalismo-03.title: Communicative Challenge: What Historians Say Is Important
b1-nacionnacionalismo-03.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg watched a documentary about Mexico's symbols, and she asks what historians say today.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-03.prompt: Tell Meg what is important, according to historians.
cues: Say that it is important
Say what should be studied
b1-nacionnacionalismo-03.target: Es importante que se estudie la vida real de las comunidades.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-03.english: It is important that the real life of the communities is studied.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-03.canDo: I can use the subjunctive after value judgments (*es importante que*, *es necesario que*) to say what historians think matters.

b1-nacionnacionalismo-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Borders and Families
b1-nacionnacionalismo-04.scenario: You are Meg. You read a book about the borders of the Andes, and Carlos asks what happened to families.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-04.prompt: Tell Carlos what families did although there was a border.
cues: Say that there was a border
Say what many families did all the same
b1-nacionnacionalismo-04.target: Aunque había una frontera, muchas familias mantuvieron sus contactos.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-04.english: Although there was a border, many families kept their contacts.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-04.canDo: I can use *aunque* to contrast what a border said with what people did.

b1-nacionnacionalismo-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Heroes in the History Books
b1-nacionnacionalismo-05.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks you how the history books of the 19th century presented the heroes of independence.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-05.prompt: Tell Meg how the heroes were presented.
cues: Say how they were presented, with ser and a participle
Say that they were fathers of the nation
b1-nacionnacionalismo-05.target: Los héroes fueron presentados como padres de la patria.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-05.english: The heroes were presented as fathers of the nation.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-05.canDo: I can use the passive with *ser* (*fueron presentados como padres de la patria*) to say how heroes and books were presented.

b1-nacionnacionalismo-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Summing Up the Nation
b1-nacionnacionalismo-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are preparing for a class, and he asks what the new republics created after independence.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos what was created after independence.
cues: Say what was created
Name two kinds of symbols
b1-nacionnacionalismo-consolidation.target: Después de la independencia se crearon banderas y himnos.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-consolidation.english: After independence flags and anthems were created.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-consolidation.canDo: I can talk about the nation with relative clauses with a preposition, the passive with *se*, the subjunctive after value judgments, *aunque* and the passive with *ser*.

b1-liberalismomodernizacion-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Trade and Ports
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos watched a documentary about the 19th century, and he asks how trade changed the cities.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what happened as trade grew.
cues: Say that trade grew
Say what grew with it
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-01.target: A medida que crecía el comercio, crecían los puertos y las ciudades.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-01.english: As trade grew, the ports and the cities grew.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-01.canDo: I can use *a medida que* and *cuanto más… más* to say how one change grew with another.

b1-liberalismomodernizacion-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Lerdo Law
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg is reading about the Reforma in Mexico and asks what the Lerdo Law required.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-02.prompt: Tell Meg what had to be sold.
cues: Say what had to be sold
Use the passive with ser
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-02.target: Las tierras de la Iglesia y de las comunidades tenían que ser vendidas.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-02.english: The lands of the Church and of the communities had to be sold.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-02.canDo: I can use the passive with *ser* (*fue aprobada*, *fueron vendidas*) to say what the liberal reforms did.

b1-liberalismomodernizacion-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Church and State in Ecuador
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-03.scenario: You are Meg. You are preparing a class about the Church, and Carlos asks about Ecuador in 1869.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what was necessary to be a citizen.
cues: Say what was necessary
Say the country
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-03.target: En Ecuador se necesitaba ser católico para ser ciudadano.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-03.english: In Ecuador it was necessary to be Catholic to be a citizen.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-03.canDo: I can use impersonal *se* (*se decidió*, *se necesitaba*, *se podía*) to say what was decided and what was possible.

b1-liberalismomodernizacion-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Immigrants at the Ports
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg visited a museum about immigration, and she asks how the immigrants arrived.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-04.prompt: Tell Meg how the immigrants arrived.
cues: Say that they arrived at the ports
Say what they were looking for, with a gerund
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-04.target: Los inmigrantes llegaban a los puertos buscando trabajo.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-04.english: The immigrants arrived at the ports looking for work.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-04.canDo: I can use the gerund to say what two actions were happening at the same time.

b1-liberalismomodernizacion-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Sides of Modernization
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks you to sum up the liberal period for a class.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-05.prompt: Tell Carlos the two sides of the period.
cues: Say one gain
Say one limit
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-05.target: Por un lado, crecieron las ciudades; por otro lado, muchas personas quedaron sin tierra.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-05.english: On the one hand, the cities grew; on the other hand, many people were left without land.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-05.canDo: I can use ordering markers (*primero*, *además*, *por un lado… por otro lado*, *por último*) to organise an explanation of the liberal period.

b1-liberalismomodernizacion-consolidatio.title: Communicative Challenge: Summing Up the Liberals
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-consolidatio.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing for a class, and she asks what the liberals wanted.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-consolidatio.prompt: Tell Meg what the liberals wanted.
cues: Say what they wanted for the citizens
Mention the law
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-consolidatio.target: Los liberales querían leyes iguales para todos los ciudadanos.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-consolidatio.english: The liberals wanted equal laws for all citizens.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-consolidatio.canDo: I can talk about liberalism with *a medida que* and *cuanto más… más*, the passive with *ser*, impersonal *se*, the gerund and ordering markers.

b1-economiasexportacion-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Export Model
b1-economiasexportacion-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about Latin America between 1870 and 1914. Carlos asks what the countries sold to Europe.
b1-economiasexportacion-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what Brazil and Colombia exported.
cues: Say what Brazil and Colombia exported
Use a relative clause about the products
b1-economiasexportacion-01.target: El producto que exportaban Brasil y Colombia era el café.
b1-economiasexportacion-01.english: The product that Brazil and Colombia exported was coffee.
b1-economiasexportacion-01.canDo: I can say what the export model was and when it grew.

b1-economiasexportacion-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Coffee and Its Price
b1-economiasexportacion-02.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are at a museum with a map of export products. Carlos asks what you learned about coffee.
b1-economiasexportacion-02.prompt: Tell Carlos what the museum said about coffee.
cues: Say that Brazil was the biggest coffee producer
Say that the price of coffee went up and down
b1-economiasexportacion-02.target: Brasil era el mayor productor de café del mundo. El café, cuyo precio subía y bajaba, era un riesgo.
b1-economiasexportacion-02.english: Brazil was the biggest coffee producer in the world. Coffee, whose price went up and down, was a risk.
b1-economiasexportacion-02.canDo: I can say what Argentina, Brazil, Chile and Central America exported.

b1-economiasexportacion-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Railways and Ports
b1-economiasexportacion-03.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg watched a documentary about railways in Latin America in the 1800s, and Meg asks what you noticed.
b1-economiasexportacion-03.prompt: Tell Meg what the documentary said about the railways.
cues: Say that the railways joined the ports with the interior
Say that many lines did not join the regions
b1-economiasexportacion-03.target: Aunque los ferrocarriles unían los puertos con el interior, muchas líneas no unían unas regiones con otras.
b1-economiasexportacion-03.english: Although the railways joined the ports with the interior, many lines did not join one region with another.
b1-economiasexportacion-03.canDo: I can say who built and paid for the railways.

b1-economiasexportacion-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Immigrants in Argentina
b1-economiasexportacion-04.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading a book about Argentina in 1914. Carlos asks what the census showed.
b1-economiasexportacion-04.prompt: Tell Carlos what the 1914 census showed.
cues: Say what share of the population was born abroad
Use the pluperfect
b1-economiasexportacion-04.target: Según el censo de 1914, alrededor del treinta por ciento de la población había nacido en el extranjero.
b1-economiasexportacion-04.english: According to the 1914 census, about thirty per cent of the population had been born abroad.
b1-economiasexportacion-04.canDo: I can explain how debt kept labourers on the hacienda.

b1-economiasexportacion-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The End of Guano
b1-economiasexportacion-05.scenario: You are Carlos. You are telling Meg about a class on Peru in the 1800s.
b1-economiasexportacion-05.prompt: Tell Meg what happened to Peru's guano business in the 1870s.
cues: Say that guano stopped being the big business
Say that the state stopped paying its debt in 1876
b1-economiasexportacion-05.target: El guano dejó de ser el gran negocio del Perú. En 1876 el Estado dejó de pagar la deuda.
b1-economiasexportacion-05.english: Guano stopped being Peru's big business. In 1876 the state stopped paying its debt.
b1-economiasexportacion-05.canDo: I can say when Peru's guano boom happened and how it ended.

b1-economiasexportacion-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: What I Learned About Export Economies
b1-economiasexportacion-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are talking about a class on export economies. Carlos asks what the main problem of the model was.
b1-economiasexportacion-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos what the main problem of the model was.
cues: Say that the countries depended on few products
Say what happened when prices fell
b1-economiasexportacion-consolidation.target: Los países que dependían de pocos productos perdían ingresos cuando el precio bajaba.
b1-economiasexportacion-consolidation.english: Countries that depended on few products lost income when the price fell.
b1-economiasexportacion-consolidation.canDo: I can say what the export model was and what Latin American countries sold abroad.

b1-cambiosocial-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Cities Around 1900
b1-cambiosocial-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are at a museum exhibition about Buenos Aires around 1900, and Carlos asks what the city was like.
b1-cambiosocial-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what Buenos Aires was like.
cues: Say that the city grew every year
Say that the cities had trams
b1-cambiosocial-01.target: Buenos Aires crecía todos los años. Las ciudades tenían tranvías.
b1-cambiosocial-01.english: Buenos Aires grew every year. The cities had trams.
b1-cambiosocial-01.canDo: I can say how Buenos Aires and other cities grew.

b1-cambiosocial-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The New Middle Class
b1-cambiosocial-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading a book about the new social classes, and Meg asks what the middle class wanted.
b1-cambiosocial-02.prompt: Tell Meg what historians say about the middle class.
cues: Name the source of the information
Say what the middle class asked for
b1-cambiosocial-02.target: Según los historiadores, la clase media pedía más participación política.
b1-cambiosocial-02.english: According to historians, the middle class was asking for more political participation.
b1-cambiosocial-02.canDo: I can say who belonged to the new middle class.

b1-cambiosocial-03.title: Communicative Challenge: How They Found Work
b1-cambiosocial-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are talking about a class on immigration, and Carlos asks how immigrants found out about work.
b1-cambiosocial-03.prompt: Tell Carlos how many immigrants got information about work.
cues: Say how they got the information
Mention who wrote to them
b1-cambiosocial-03.target: Muchos conseguían información sobre el trabajo a través de cartas de familiares y amigos.
b1-cambiosocial-03.english: Many got information about work through letters from relatives and friends.
b1-cambiosocial-03.canDo: I can say where most immigrants came from and where they went.

b1-cambiosocial-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Strike in Mexico
b1-cambiosocial-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg watched a documentary about strikes in Mexico, and Meg asks what happened in Río Blanco.
b1-cambiosocial-04.prompt: Tell Meg what happened to the strike of 1907.
cues: Say what happened to the strike
Say who did it
b1-cambiosocial-04.target: La huelga de 1907 fue reprimida por el ejército.
b1-cambiosocial-04.english: The strike of 1907 was put down by the army.
b1-cambiosocial-04.canDo: I can say what workers asked for and who led the unions.

b1-cambiosocial-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Women and the Vote
b1-cambiosocial-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are talking about a book on women in Latin America, and Carlos asks what women could do around 1900.
b1-cambiosocial-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what women could and could not do.
cues: Say that women could not vote
Say that many worked as teachers
b1-cambiosocial-05.target: Aunque las mujeres no podían votar, muchas trabajaban como maestras.
b1-cambiosocial-05.english: Although women could not vote, many worked as teachers.
b1-cambiosocial-05.canDo: I can say what the university reform of Córdoba asked for.

b1-cambiosocial-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: What I Learned About Social Change
b1-cambiosocial-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are talking about a class on social change, and Carlos asks what the workers wanted.
b1-cambiosocial-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos what the workers asked for.
cues: Say what they asked for
Say what they did when the boss did not accept
b1-cambiosocial-consolidation.target: Los obreros pedían salarios más altos y hacían huelga.
b1-cambiosocial-consolidation.english: The workers asked for higher wages and went on strike.
b1-cambiosocial-consolidation.canDo: I can describe how the cities of Latin America changed around 1900.

b1-revolucion-01.title: Communicative Challenge: What Is a Revolution?
b1-revolucion-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are talking about a class on revolutions. Carlos asks what a coup is.
b1-revolucion-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what happens in a coup.
cues: Say who takes power in a coup
Say what usually does not change
b1-revolucion-01.target: En un golpe, los militares que toman el poder cambian al gobernante, pero la sociedad muchas veces sigue igual.
b1-revolucion-01.english: In a coup, the military who take power change the ruler, but society often stays the same.
b1-revolucion-01.canDo: I can say what a revolution is for historians.

b1-revolucion-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Land in Bolivia
b1-revolucion-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading about Bolivia in 1952, and Meg asks what happened with the land.
b1-revolucion-02.prompt: Tell Meg what Bolivia did after the revolution of 1952.
cues: Say that Bolivia made a land reform
Use a phrase for the cause
b1-revolucion-02.target: A raíz de la revolución de 1952, Bolivia hizo una reforma agraria.
b1-revolucion-02.english: As a result of the revolution of 1952, Bolivia carried out a land reform.
b1-revolucion-02.canDo: I can say why many peasants had no land.

b1-revolucion-03.title: Communicative Challenge: How the Students Protested
b1-revolucion-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are at a museum with a section on social movements, and Carlos asks what the students did.
b1-revolucion-03.prompt: Tell Carlos how the students protested.
cues: Say that the students protested
Say how they did it
b1-revolucion-03.target: Los estudiantes protestaban escribiendo periódicos y haciendo reuniones.
b1-revolucion-03.english: The students protested by writing newspapers and holding meetings.
b1-revolucion-03.canDo: I can name the groups that formed social movements.

b1-revolucion-04.title: Communicative Challenge: After the Revolution
b1-revolucion-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are talking about a documentary on new governments, and Meg asks what they had to do.
b1-revolucion-04.prompt: Tell Meg what the new governments had to do.
cues: Say what they had to organise
Say that they had to find money
b1-revolucion-04.target: Los nuevos gobiernos tuvieron que organizar el Estado y buscar dinero.
b1-revolucion-04.english: The new governments had to organise the state and find money.
b1-revolucion-04.canDo: I can say what the new governments had to do after a revolution.

b1-revolucion-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Why Do Revolutions Happen?
b1-revolucion-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are talking about a book on revolutions, and Carlos asks what historians think.
b1-revolucion-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what some historians believe.
cues: Say what some historians believe
Say what others do not believe
b1-revolucion-05.target: Algunos historiadores creen que la desigualdad es la causa principal, pero otros no creen que sea suficiente.
b1-revolucion-05.english: Some historians believe that inequality is the main cause, but others do not believe that it is enough.
b1-revolucion-05.canDo: I can say what some historians believe about the causes of revolutions.

b1-revolucion-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: What I Learned About Revolutions
b1-revolucion-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are talking about a class on revolutions, and Carlos asks which countries had one in the twentieth century.
b1-revolucion-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos which countries had a revolution and when.
cues: Name the countries
Give the years
b1-revolucion-consolidation.target: Hubo revoluciones en México en 1910, en Bolivia en 1952, en Cuba en 1959 y en Nicaragua en 1979.
b1-revolucion-consolidation.english: There were revolutions in Mexico in 1910, in Bolivia in 1952, in Cuba in 1959 and in Nicaragua in 1979.
b1-revolucion-consolidation.canDo: I can say what a revolution is and name the revolutions of the twentieth century.

b1-revolucionmexicana-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Mexico before 1910
b1-revolucionmexicana-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos have just watched a documentary about Mexico under Porfirio Díaz, and Carlos asks what you remember about 1910.
b1-revolucionmexicana-01.prompt: Tell Carlos how long Díaz had been governing and what Mexico had been receiving.
cues: Say that in 1910 Díaz had been governing for more than thirty years
Say that Mexico had been receiving foreign investment for decades
b1-revolucionmexicana-01.target: En 1910 Díaz llevaba más de treinta años gobernando. México llevaba décadas recibiendo inversión extranjera.
b1-revolucionmexicana-01.english: In 1910 Díaz had been governing for more than thirty years. Mexico had been receiving foreign investment for decades.
b1-revolucionmexicana-01.canDo: I can say how long something had been going on, with *llevar* + gerund.

b1-revolucionmexicana-02.title: Communicative Challenge: What Díaz Said in 1908
b1-revolucionmexicana-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are in a museum looking at an exhibition about Madero, and Meg asks what Díaz said to the American journalist in 1908.
b1-revolucionmexicana-02.prompt: Tell Meg what Díaz said to the journalist.
cues: Say that Díaz told a journalist that Mexico was ready for democracy
Say that he said he would accept an opposition party
b1-revolucionmexicana-02.target: En 1908 Díaz le dijo a un periodista que México estaba preparado para la democracia. También dijo que aceptaría un partido de oposición.
b1-revolucionmexicana-02.english: In 1908 Díaz told a journalist that Mexico was ready for democracy. He also said he would accept an opposition party.
b1-revolucionmexicana-02.canDo: I can report what someone said, with *dijo que* and the verb shifted back.

b1-revolucionmexicana-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Zapata and the Plan of Ayala
b1-revolucionmexicana-03.scenario: You are Meg. You are reading a book about the Mexican Revolution, and Carlos asks you who Zapata was.
b1-revolucionmexicana-03.prompt: Tell Carlos who Zapata was and what he did in 1911.
cues: Say that Zapata was a peasant from Morelos
Say that in November 1911 he proclaimed the Plan of Ayala
b1-revolucionmexicana-03.target: Zapata era un campesino de Morelos. En noviembre de 1911 proclamó el Plan de Ayala.
b1-revolucionmexicana-03.english: Zapata was a peasant from Morelos. In November 1911 he proclaimed the Plan of Ayala.
b1-revolucionmexicana-03.canDo: I can tell a story in the past, with the preterite for events and the imperfect for the background.

b1-revolucionmexicana-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Article 27
b1-revolucionmexicana-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg missed a history class about the Constitution of 1917 and asks you what Article 27 says.
b1-revolucionmexicana-04.prompt: Tell Meg what Article 27 is about.
cues: Say that Article 27 is the article in which the land is discussed
Say that the land and the subsoil belong to the nation
b1-revolucionmexicana-04.target: El artículo 27 es el artículo en el que se habla de la tierra. Dice que la tierra y el subsuelo pertenecen a la nación.
b1-revolucionmexicana-04.english: Article 27 is the article in which the land is discussed. It says that the land and the subsoil belong to the nation.
b1-revolucionmexicana-04.canDo: I can describe a thing or a person with a relative clause such as *en el que* or *para los que*.

b1-revolucionmexicana-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Cárdenas and the Oil
b1-revolucionmexicana-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos have watched a documentary about Lázaro Cárdenas, and Carlos asks what happened in 1938.
b1-revolucionmexicana-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what happened to the oil, and to the haciendas.
cues: Say that the oil was expropriated in 1938
Say that many haciendas were shared out among the peasants
b1-revolucionmexicana-05.target: El petróleo fue expropiado en 1938. Muchas haciendas fueron repartidas entre los campesinos.
b1-revolucionmexicana-05.english: The oil was expropriated in 1938. Many haciendas were shared out among the peasants.
b1-revolucionmexicana-05.canDo: I can say what was done, with *ser* + past participle.

b1-revolucionmexicana-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: How the Revolution Began
b1-revolucionmexicana-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are looking at a timeline of the Mexican Revolution in a museum, and Meg asks how it began.
b1-revolucionmexicana-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg how the revolution began.
cues: Say that Madero's plan said the elections had been a fraud
Say that Díaz resigned and went to France
b1-revolucionmexicana-consolidation.target: El plan de Madero decía que las elecciones habían sido un fraude. Después Díaz renunció y se fue a Francia.
b1-revolucionmexicana-consolidation.english: Madero's plan said that the elections had been a fraud. Then Díaz resigned and went to France.
b1-revolucionmexicana-consolidation.canDo: I can say how long something had been going on, with *llevar* + gerund, to describe the Porfiriato.

b1-nacionalismo-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The New States
b1-nacionalismo-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos have watched a documentary about Latin America in the early twentieth century, and Carlos asks what changed in the governments.
b1-nacionalismo-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what was created in those years.
cues: Say that new ministries were created
Say that central banks were created in the 1920s
b1-nacionalismo-01.target: Se crearon nuevos ministerios. En la década de 1920 se crearon bancos centrales.
b1-nacionalismo-01.english: New ministries were created. In the 1920s central banks were created.
b1-nacionalismo-01.canDo: I can say what was created or introduced, with *se* + a verb.

b1-nacionalismo-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Mexican Muralists
b1-nacionalismo-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are at a museum exhibition about Mexican murals, and Meg asks about the painters.
b1-nacionalismo-02.prompt: Tell Meg about the three painters.
cues: Say that the three painters had different styles
Say that all of them painted the history of the country
b1-nacionalismo-02.target: A pesar de que los tres pintores tenían estilos distintos, todos pintaron la historia del país.
b1-nacionalismo-02.english: Although the three painters had different styles, all of them painted the history of the country.
b1-nacionalismo-02.canDo: I can admit a contrast and go on, with *a pesar de*, *a pesar de que* or *pese a*.

b1-nacionalismo-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Schools in the Countryside
b1-nacionalismo-03.scenario: You are Meg. You are reading about the rural schools of Mexico after 1921, and Carlos asks about the teachers.
b1-nacionalismo-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what happened as rural schools opened.
cues: Say that as rural schools opened, more teachers were needed
Say that the more the school spread, the more visible the State was
b1-nacionalismo-03.target: A medida que se abrían escuelas rurales, se necesitaban más maestros. Cuanto más se extendía la escuela, más visible era el Estado.
b1-nacionalismo-03.english: As rural schools opened, more teachers were needed. The more the school spread, the more visible the State was.
b1-nacionalismo-03.canDo: I can link two changes that grow together, with *a medida que* or *cuanto más ..., más ...*.

b1-nacionalismo-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Life in Isolated Regions
b1-nacionalismo-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks you about life in the mountains before the railways, after a class on Latin American history.
b1-nacionalismo-04.prompt: Tell Meg how people lived and travelled.
cues: Say that in the mountains people lived almost without contact with the government
Say that with the railway people travelled faster
b1-nacionalismo-04.target: En las montañas se vivía casi sin contacto con el gobierno. Con el ferrocarril se viajaba más rápido.
b1-nacionalismo-04.english: In the mountains people lived almost without contact with the government. With the railway people travelled faster.
b1-nacionalismo-04.canDo: I can say what people in general did, with *se* + a singular verb.

b1-nacionalismo-05.title: Communicative Challenge: How the State Changed
b1-nacionalismo-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos have been reading about the early twentieth century, and Carlos asks how the State changed.
b1-nacionalismo-05.prompt: Tell Carlos how the State changed.
cues: Say that the State became a very important actor
Say that the bureaucracy became bigger
b1-nacionalismo-05.target: El Estado se convirtió en un actor muy importante. La burocracia se hizo más grande.
b1-nacionalismo-05.english: The State became a very important actor. The bureaucracy became bigger.
b1-nacionalismo-05.canDo: I can say how something changed, with *convertirse en*, *hacerse*, *volverse* and *quedarse*.

b1-nacionalismo-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Nationalism and the State
b1-nacionalismo-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. After a class on nationalism and the State, Meg asks you what the new states created.
b1-nacionalismo-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what changed in the states.
cues: Say that ministries and central banks were created
Say that the State became a more important actor
b1-nacionalismo-consolidation.target: Se crearon ministerios y bancos centrales. El Estado se convirtió en un actor más importante.
b1-nacionalismo-consolidation.english: Ministries and central banks were created. The State became a more important actor.
b1-nacionalismo-consolidation.canDo: I can say what the new states created, with the passive with *se*.

b1-grandepresion-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Before the Crash
b1-grandepresion-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos have watched a documentary about the crash of 1929, and Carlos asks what had happened before the crisis.
b1-grandepresion-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what had happened before the crisis.
cues: Say that many countries had already asked for large loans when the crisis came
Say that the prices of shares had risen a lot
b1-grandepresion-01.target: Cuando llegó la crisis, muchos países ya habían pedido grandes préstamos. Los precios de las acciones habían subido mucho.
b1-grandepresion-01.english: When the crisis came, many countries had already asked for large loans. The prices of shares had risen a lot.
b1-grandepresion-01.canDo: I can say what had already happened before another moment in the past, with *había* + past participle.

b1-grandepresion-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Coffee in Brazil
b1-grandepresion-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading a book about Latin America in the 1930s, and Meg asks what Brazil did about coffee.
b1-grandepresion-02.prompt: Tell Meg what Brazil did with coffee and what happened to the price.
cues: Say that the government burned part of the coffee
Say that, however, the price stayed low
b1-grandepresion-02.target: El gobierno quemó una parte del café. Sin embargo, el precio siguió bajo.
b1-grandepresion-02.english: The government burned part of the coffee. However, the price stayed low.
b1-grandepresion-02.canDo: I can show a contrast, with *sin embargo* and *no obstante*.

b1-grandepresion-03.title: Communicative Challenge: How Bad Was the Crisis?
b1-grandepresion-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos have been to a museum exhibition about the 1930s, and Carlos asks how bad the crisis was in Latin America.
b1-grandepresion-03.prompt: Tell Carlos how bad the crisis was.
cues: Say that the crisis of 1929 was the worst economic crisis Latin America had known
Say that the mining areas were among the most affected
b1-grandepresion-03.target: La crisis de 1929 fue la peor crisis económica que América Latina había conocido. Las zonas mineras fueron de las más afectadas.
b1-grandepresion-03.english: The crisis of 1929 was the worst economic crisis that Latin America had known. The mining areas were among the most affected.
b1-grandepresion-03.canDo: I can say that something is the worst, the most or the least, with a superlative.

b1-grandepresion-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Protecting Factories
b1-grandepresion-04.scenario: You are Carlos. After a class about the 1930s, Meg asks you how governments protected the factories of their countries.
b1-grandepresion-04.prompt: Tell Meg how governments protected the factories.
cues: Say that governments protected the country's factories
Say how: by means of higher tariffs
b1-grandepresion-04.target: Mediante aranceles más altos, los gobiernos protegieron las fábricas del país.
b1-grandepresion-04.english: By means of higher tariffs, governments protected the country's factories.
b1-grandepresion-04.canDo: I can say by what means something is done, with *mediante* + a noun.

b1-grandepresion-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Turning Point
b1-grandepresion-05.scenario: You are Meg. You are summing up a chapter about the crisis of 1929 for Carlos.
b1-grandepresion-05.prompt: Sum up for Carlos what the crisis changed.
cues: Say in summary that the crisis was a turning point
Give two sides: industry grew in the cities, the countryside lost importance
b1-grandepresion-05.target: En resumen, la crisis de 1929 fue un punto de cambio. Por un lado, la industria creció; por otro lado, el campo perdió importancia.
b1-grandepresion-05.english: In summary, the crisis of 1929 was a turning point. On the one hand, industry grew; on the other hand, the countryside lost importance.
b1-grandepresion-05.canDo: I can build and close an explanation, with *por un lado ... por otro lado* and *en resumen*.

b1-grandepresion-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Great Depression
b1-grandepresion-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. After a class on the Great Depression, Meg asks you what you remember about the crisis and the way governments answered it.
cues: Say that many countries had already asked for large loans when the crisis came
Say how governments protected their factories
b1-grandepresion-consolidation.target: Cuando llegó la crisis, muchos países ya habían pedido grandes préstamos. Mediante aranceles más altos, los gobiernos protegieron las fábricas.
b1-grandepresion-consolidation.english: When the crisis came, many countries had already asked for large loans. By means of higher tariffs, governments protected the factories.
b1-grandepresion-consolidation.canDo: I can tell what had already happened before the crash, using the pluperfect.

b1-populismo-01.title: Communicative Challenge: What Is Populism?
b1-populismo-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos watched a documentary about Latin American populism, and he asks how the film defined the word.
b1-populismo-01.prompt: Tell Carlos how populism is usually defined.
cues: Say that the word is usually used for certain movements
Say that their leaders spoke in the name of the people
b1-populismo-01.target: Se suele llamar populismo a los movimientos que hablaban en nombre del pueblo.
b1-populismo-01.english: The movements that spoke in the name of the people are usually called populism.
b1-populismo-01.canDo: I can say how Latin American populism is usually defined.

b1-populismo-02.title: Communicative Challenge: 17 October 1945
b1-populismo-02.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos visited a museum exhibition about Perón, and he asks what happened on 17 October 1945.
b1-populismo-02.prompt: Tell Carlos what happened that day.
cues: Say that many workers marched to the square
Say what Perón did while the crowd was waiting
b1-populismo-02.target: El 17 de octubre de 1945 muchos trabajadores marcharon a la plaza. Mientras la multitud esperaba, Perón habló desde un balcón.
b1-populismo-02.english: On 17 October 1945 many workers marched to the square. While the crowd was waiting, Perón spoke from a balcony.
b1-populismo-02.canDo: I can tell how Perón gained the support of the workers.

b1-populismo-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Presidents
b1-populismo-03.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg were in a class about Latin American history, and she asks what you remember about Lázaro Cárdenas.
b1-populismo-03.prompt: Tell Meg what kind of president Cárdenas was.
cues: Say that Cárdenas was a president
Say what his government did for the peasants
b1-populismo-03.target: Cárdenas fue un presidente cuyo gobierno repartió tierras a los campesinos.
b1-populismo-03.english: Cárdenas was a president whose government gave land to the peasants.
b1-populismo-03.canDo: I can say what Cárdenas did for the peasants and the workers.

b1-populismo-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Do Historians Agree?
b1-populismo-04.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos watched a documentary about populist leaders, and he asks what the historians in the film said about the link between a leader and the people.
b1-populismo-04.prompt: Tell Carlos what some historians believe and what others do not believe.
cues: Say what some historians believe about the direct link
Say what others do not believe about it
b1-populismo-04.target: Algunos historiadores creen que el vínculo directo dio voz al pueblo, pero otros no creen que sea bueno para la democracia.
b1-populismo-04.english: Some historians believe that the direct link gave a voice to the people, but others do not believe that it is good for democracy.
b1-populismo-04.canDo: I can describe how populist leaders spoke to the people.

b1-populismo-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Praise and Criticism
b1-populismo-05.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg have just finished a class on Latin American populism, and she asks you for a short summary of the results of these governments.
b1-populismo-05.prompt: Tell Meg one good result and one criticism.
cues: Say what the governments did for the workers
Say what the critics said, with a connector
b1-populismo-05.target: Los gobiernos ampliaron los derechos de los trabajadores. Sin embargo, concentraron mucho poder.
b1-populismo-05.english: The governments extended the rights of the workers. However, they concentrated a lot of power.
b1-populismo-05.canDo: I can say what these governments left to the workers.

b1-populismo-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Populism: A Summary
b1-populismo-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos have just finished a unit on Latin American populism, and he asks you for a short summary.
b1-populismo-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos what the word populism is used for and what historians say about it.
cues: Say how these movements are usually called
Say what some historians do not believe, with a connector
b1-populismo-consolidation.target: Se suele llamar populismo a los movimientos de Perón, Vargas y Cárdenas. Sin embargo, algunos historiadores no creen que el populismo sea una ideología.
b1-populismo-consolidation.english: These movements of Perón, Vargas and Cárdenas are usually called populism. However, some historians do not believe that populism is an ideology.
b1-populismo-consolidation.canDo: I can say how populism is usually defined and why the word is disputed.

b1-industrializacion-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Why Make Things at Home?
b1-industrializacion-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos watched a documentary about the economy of Latin America in the 1930s, and he asks why the countries began to make their own products.
b1-industrializacion-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what the crisis of 1929 did to trade.
cues: Say that the countries bought fewer foreign products
Give the cause with a formal connector
b1-industrializacion-01.target: Debido a la crisis de 1929, los países pudieron comprar menos productos del extranjero.
b1-industrializacion-01.english: Because of the crisis of 1929, the countries could buy fewer foreign products.
b1-industrializacion-01.canDo: I can explain why countries began to make things at home.

b1-industrializacion-02.title: Communicative Challenge: State Companies and Factories
b1-industrializacion-02.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos visited an exhibition about the industry of Mexico and Brazil, and he asks how the governments made imported cars more expensive.
b1-industrializacion-02.prompt: Tell Carlos how the governments did it.
cues: Say what the governments used
Say what happened to imported cars
b1-industrializacion-02.target: Mediante aranceles altos, los gobiernos hacían más caros los autos importados.
b1-industrializacion-02.english: By means of high tariffs, governments made imported cars more expensive.
b1-industrializacion-02.canDo: I can name the state companies that were created, such as Pemex and Petrobras.

b1-industrializacion-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Leaving the Countryside
b1-industrializacion-03.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg were in a class about the migration to the cities in Latin America, and she asks you what changed for the peasants.
b1-industrializacion-03.prompt: Tell Meg what millions of people stopped doing.
cues: Say that millions of people stopped living somewhere
Say where they went
b1-industrializacion-03.target: Millones de personas dejaron de vivir en el campo y se fueron a las ciudades.
b1-industrializacion-03.english: Millions of people stopped living in the countryside and went to the cities.
b1-industrializacion-03.canDo: I can explain why people left the countryside for the cities.

b1-industrializacion-04.title: Communicative Challenge: New Neighbourhoods
b1-industrializacion-04.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos watched a documentary about the favelas of Brazil, and he asks what happened to some of those neighbourhoods.
b1-industrializacion-04.prompt: Tell Carlos how some neighbourhoods changed.
cues: Say that they became part of the city
Say what happened to them with time
b1-industrializacion-04.target: Algunos barrios se hicieron más grandes y se convirtieron en una parte normal de la ciudad.
b1-industrializacion-04.english: Some neighbourhoods grew bigger and became a normal part of the city.
b1-industrializacion-04.canDo: I can describe the neighbourhoods built by their own residents: favelas, villas and barriadas.

b1-industrializacion-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Results and Limits
b1-industrializacion-05.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg have just read a chapter about the industry of Latin America, and she asks you for the balance.
b1-industrializacion-05.prompt: Tell Meg that the region had achievements but also problems.
cues: Mention the achievements
Say that the region still had problems
b1-industrializacion-05.target: A pesar de estos logros, la región tenía problemas.
b1-industrializacion-05.english: Despite these achievements, the region had problems.
b1-industrializacion-05.canDo: I can say what Latin America manufactured by the 1960s.

b1-industrializacion-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Industrialization: A Summary
b1-industrializacion-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos have just finished a unit on the industrialization of Latin America, and he asks you for a short summary.
b1-industrializacion-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos why countries made things at home and what the result was.
cues: Give the cause with a formal connector
Say that the region still had problems
b1-industrializacion-consolidation.target: Debido a la crisis de 1929, los países empezaron a fabricar en casa. A pesar de los logros, la región tenía problemas.
b1-industrializacion-consolidation.english: Because of the crisis of 1929, the countries began to make things at home. Despite the achievements, the region had problems.
b1-industrializacion-consolidation.canDo: I can sum up the causes and results of import substitution.

b1-revolucioncubana-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Cuba Before the Revolution
b1-revolucioncubana-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos watched a documentary about Cuba in the 1950s, and he asks what life was like for the sugar workers.
b1-revolucioncubana-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what the sugar workers used to do.
cues: Say what the sugar workers used to do
Say when they worked
b1-revolucioncubana-01.target: Los trabajadores del azúcar solían trabajar solo durante la zafra.
b1-revolucioncubana-01.english: The sugar workers used to work only during the harvest.
b1-revolucioncubana-01.canDo: I can say how Cuba became a republic and what influence the United States had.

b1-revolucioncubana-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Rebels
b1-revolucioncubana-02.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos watched a documentary about the Cuban revolution, and he asks what the rebels had done when Batista fled.
b1-revolucioncubana-02.prompt: Tell Carlos what the rebels had already done.
cues: Say what happened on 1 January 1959
Say what the rebels had already won
b1-revolucioncubana-02.target: Cuando Batista huyó, los rebeldes ya habían ganado importantes batallas.
b1-revolucioncubana-02.english: When Batista fled, the rebels had already won important battles.
b1-revolucioncubana-02.canDo: I can say what happened at the Moncada barracks in 1953.

b1-revolucioncubana-03.title: Communicative Challenge: A Socialist Revolution
b1-revolucioncubana-03.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg were in a class about the Cuban revolution, and she asks what happened to the relations between Cuba and the United States.
b1-revolucioncubana-03.prompt: Tell Meg how the relations changed.
cues: Say that Cuba got closer to the Soviet Union
Say how the distrust of the United States grew
b1-revolucioncubana-03.target: Cuanto más se acercaba Cuba a la Unión Soviética, más grande era la desconfianza de Estados Unidos.
b1-revolucioncubana-03.english: The closer Cuba got to the Soviet Union, the greater was the distrust of the United States.
b1-revolucioncubana-03.canDo: I can describe the agrarian reform law of 1959.

b1-revolucioncubana-04.title: Communicative Challenge: On the Edge of War
b1-revolucioncubana-04.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos watched a documentary about October 1962, and he asks what the world nearly saw.
b1-revolucioncubana-04.prompt: Tell Carlos what the world almost did in October 1962.
cues: Say that it happened in October 1962
Say what the world nearly entered
b1-revolucioncubana-04.target: En octubre de 1962 el mundo estuvo a punto de entrar en una guerra nuclear.
b1-revolucioncubana-04.english: In October 1962 the world came close to entering a nuclear war.
b1-revolucioncubana-04.canDo: I can say who landed at the Bay of Pigs and what happened.

b1-revolucioncubana-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Cuba and the OAS
b1-revolucioncubana-05.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg were in a class about the Cuban revolution, and she asks what happened to Cuba in the OAS in 1962.
b1-revolucioncubana-05.prompt: Tell Meg what was done to Cuba in 1962.
cues: Say what was done to Cuba
Say which organisation did it
b1-revolucioncubana-05.target: En 1962 Cuba fue suspendida de la OEA.
b1-revolucioncubana-05.english: In 1962 Cuba was suspended from the Organization of American States (OAS).
b1-revolucioncubana-05.canDo: I can say how young people and governments reacted to the Cuban revolution.

b1-revolucioncubana-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Cuban Revolution: A Summary
b1-revolucioncubana-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos have just finished a unit on the Cuban revolution, and he asks you for a short summary of how it began.
b1-revolucioncubana-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos how things were before the revolution and what had happened when Batista fled.
cues: Say what the sugar workers used to do
Say what the rebels had already done when Batista fled
b1-revolucioncubana-consolidation.target: Los trabajadores del azúcar solían trabajar solo durante la zafra. Cuando Batista huyó, los rebeldes ya habían ganado importantes batallas.
b1-revolucioncubana-consolidation.english: The sugar workers used to work only during the harvest. When Batista fled, the rebels had already won important battles.
b1-revolucioncubana-consolidation.canDo: I can sum up how things were in Cuba before the revolution and how it began.

b1-guerrafria-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Two Blocs
b1-guerrafria-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about the Cold War, and he asks what the two blocs were.
b1-guerrafria-01.prompt: Tell Carlos about the two superpowers and what they defended.
cues: Say which country led one bloc and what it defended
Say which country led the other bloc and what it defended
b1-guerrafria-01.target: Estados Unidos, que defendía el capitalismo, dirigía un bloque. La Unión Soviética, que defendía el comunismo, dirigía el otro.
b1-guerrafria-01.english: The United States, which defended capitalism, led one bloc. The Soviet Union, which defended communism, led the other.
b1-guerrafria-01.canDo: I can add information about the two blocs with *que* and *quien*.

b1-guerrafria-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Rio Treaty
b1-guerrafria-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg is reading about the Cold War in a book for her class and asks you about the Rio Treaty.
b1-guerrafria-02.prompt: Tell Meg when and where the Rio Treaty was signed.
cues: Say that the treaty was signed in 1947
Say where it was signed
b1-guerrafria-02.target: En 1947 se firmó en Río de Janeiro el Tratado de Río.
b1-guerrafria-02.english: In 1947 the Rio Treaty was signed in Rio de Janeiro.
b1-guerrafria-02.canDo: I can say what was signed and founded using *se*.

b1-guerrafria-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Guerrillas
b1-guerrafria-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos have just seen a museum exhibition about the 1960s, and he asks what the guerrilla fighters did.
b1-guerrafria-03.prompt: Tell Carlos how the guerrilla fighters lived in the mountains.
cues: Say that they spent months in the mountains
Say what they were doing there at the same time
b1-guerrafria-03.target: Los guerrilleros pasaban meses en las montañas, planeando ataques.
b1-guerrafria-03.english: The guerrilla fighters spent months in the mountains, planning attacks.
b1-guerrafria-03.canDo: I can say what two things a person did at the same time with the gerund.

b1-guerrafria-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Guatemala, 1954
b1-guerrafria-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks about a documentary you saw on the coup in Guatemala.
b1-guerrafria-04.prompt: Tell Meg who organised the operation in 1954, citing the source.
cues: Begin by citing the documents published later
Say who organised the operation
b1-guerrafria-04.target: Según documentos publicados después por el gobierno de Estados Unidos, la CIA organizó la operación.
b1-guerrafria-04.english: According to documents published later by the US government, the CIA organised the operation.
b1-guerrafria-04.canDo: I can report what a source says with *según* and *dijo que*.

b1-guerrafria-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Secret Documents
b1-guerrafria-05.scenario: You are Meg. You are telling Carlos what you learned in a class on the Cold War about the archives.
b1-guerrafria-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what the documents were like before and what historians have done now.
cues: Say that before, the documents were secret
Say that historians have studied them
b1-guerrafria-05.target: Antes los documentos eran secretos, pero los historiadores han podido estudiarlos.
b1-guerrafria-05.english: Before, the documents were secret, but historians have been able to study them.
b1-guerrafria-05.canDo: I can contrast how things were with what has changed, using the imperfect and the present perfect.

b1-guerrafria-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Cold War in Latin America
b1-guerrafria-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are talking after a class about the Cold War in Latin America.
b1-guerrafria-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos what happened in 1947 and 1948.
cues: Say that a treaty was signed in 1947
Say that the OAS was founded in 1948
b1-guerrafria-consolidation.target: En 1947 se firmó el Tratado de Río, y en 1948 se fundó la OEA en Bogotá.
b1-guerrafria-consolidation.english: In 1947 the Rio Treaty was signed, and in 1948 the OAS was founded in Bogotá.
b1-guerrafria-consolidation.canDo: I can say how the world split into two blocs and what containment was.

b1-eeuu-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Monroe Doctrine
b1-eeuu-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about the United States and Latin America, and he asks what Monroe declared.
b1-eeuu-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what President Monroe declared in 1823.
cues: Say who declared it and in what year
Say what the European countries should not do
b1-eeuu-01.target: En 1823 el presidente Monroe declaró que los países europeos no debían fundar nuevas colonias en América.
b1-eeuu-01.english: In 1823 President Monroe declared that the European countries should not found new colonies in America.
b1-eeuu-01.canDo: I can report what a president declared, moving the tense back.

b1-eeuu-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Panama Canal
b1-eeuu-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg is writing an essay for her class and asks you about the Panama Canal.
b1-eeuu-02.prompt: Tell Meg what happened in Panama while the canal was built.
cues: Say that many workers arrived
Say when the canal opened
b1-eeuu-02.target: Mientras se construía el canal, llegaron a Panamá muchos trabajadores. El canal se abrió en 1914.
b1-eeuu-02.english: While the canal was being built, many workers arrived in Panama. The canal opened in 1914.
b1-eeuu-02.canDo: I can link events in the past with *cuando* and *mientras*.

b1-eeuu-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Bananas and Dependence
b1-eeuu-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos have just read a book about United Fruit, and he asks why bananas mattered.
b1-eeuu-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what some small countries depended on.
cues: Say which product some economies depended on
Use a relative clause with a preposition
b1-eeuu-03.target: El banano era el producto del que dependía la economía de varios países pequeños.
b1-eeuu-03.english: Bananas were the product on which the economy of several small countries depended.
b1-eeuu-03.canDo: I can say what a country depended on using *del que* and *con los que*.

b1-eeuu-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Alliance for Progress
b1-eeuu-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks you about a museum exhibition you saw on the Alliance for Progress.
b1-eeuu-04.prompt: Tell Meg how the programme ended.
cues: Say that the programme stopped working
Say when that happened
b1-eeuu-04.target: A principios de los años setenta el programa dejó de funcionar.
b1-eeuu-04.english: In the early 1970s the programme stopped working.
b1-eeuu-04.canDo: I can say how something began, stopped or went on with verbal periphrases.

b1-eeuu-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Closing Summary
b1-eeuu-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are preparing a class presentation on the United States and Latin America.
b1-eeuu-05.prompt: Give Carlos the closing sentence of your presentation.
cues: Mark it as a summary
Say that the relationship was unequal
b1-eeuu-05.target: En resumen, la relación fue desigual, pero no fue solo de dominación.
b1-eeuu-05.english: In summary, the relationship was unequal, but it was not only one of domination.
b1-eeuu-05.canDo: I can build and close an argument with *en primer lugar*, *además* and *en resumen*.

b1-eeuu-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Short Report
b1-eeuu-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks you what you remember from the class about the United States and Latin America.
b1-eeuu-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg one thing about Monroe and one about the Panama Canal.
cues: Say what Monroe declared
Say when Panama received the canal
b1-eeuu-consolidation.target: Monroe declaró que los países europeos no debían fundar nuevas colonias. Panamá recibió el control del canal en 1999.
b1-eeuu-consolidation.english: Monroe declared that the European countries should not found new colonies. Panama received control of the canal in 1999.
b1-eeuu-consolidation.canDo: I can report what a president declared and say who said what.

b1-gobiernosmilitares-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Said and Done
b1-gobiernosmilitares-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about the military governments, and he asks what the generals promised.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what the military said and what they did.
cues: Say what the military said they wanted
Contrast it with what they did
b1-gobiernosmilitares-01.target: Los militares decían que querían defender el orden. Sin embargo, no devolvieron el poder pronto.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-01.english: The military said they wanted to defend order. However, they did not give power back soon.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-01.canDo: I can contrast what the military said with what they did using *sin embargo* and *no obstante*.

b1-gobiernosmilitares-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Brazil, 1964
b1-gobiernosmilitares-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg is reading a book about Brazil and asks what happened to President Goulart.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-02.prompt: Tell Meg who was overthrown in 1964 and what happened to the Congress in 1968.
cues: Say who was overthrown and when
Say what happened to the Congress
b1-gobiernosmilitares-02.target: El presidente Goulart fue derrocado en 1964. El Congreso fue cerrado durante varios meses.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-02.english: President Goulart was overthrown in 1964. Congress was closed for several months.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-02.canDo: I can say what was done using *ser* + past participle.

b1-gobiernosmilitares-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Chile, 1973
b1-gobiernosmilitares-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos have just visited a museum exhibition about Chile.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what had happened in Chile before the coup.
cues: Say who had won the elections of 1970
Say what the country had gone through
b1-gobiernosmilitares-03.target: Allende había ganado las elecciones de 1970, y el país ya había pasado por meses de crisis.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-03.english: Allende had won the elections of 1970, and the country had already gone through months of crisis.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-03.canDo: I can say what had already happened using *había* + participle.

b1-gobiernosmilitares-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Argentina, 1976
b1-gobiernosmilitares-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks about a documentary on Argentina that you saw.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-04.prompt: Tell Meg what was done in 1976.
cues: Say what was done with the Congress
Say what was done with the political parties
b1-gobiernosmilitares-04.target: En 1976 se cerró el Congreso y se suspendió la actividad de los partidos políticos.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-04.english: In 1976 Congress was closed and the activity of the political parties was suspended.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-04.canDo: I can say what was done using *se* without naming who did it.

b1-gobiernosmilitares-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The End of Military Rule
b1-gobiernosmilitares-05.scenario: You are Meg. You are telling Carlos what you learned in a class about the end of the military governments.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-05.prompt: Tell Carlos why the Argentine military left power.
cues: Name the cause with a formal connector
Say when they left power
b1-gobiernosmilitares-05.target: A raíz de la derrota en la guerra de las Malvinas, los militares dejaron el poder en 1983.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-05.english: As a result of the defeat in the Malvinas war, the military left power in 1983.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-05.canDo: I can explain a cause using *debido a* or *a raíz de*.

b1-gobiernosmilitares-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Military Governments Review
b1-gobiernosmilitares-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks you what you remember from the class about military governments.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg one thing about Chile and one about Argentina.
cues: Say who had won the elections of 1970 in Chile
Say who was the first president of the junta in Argentina
b1-gobiernosmilitares-consolidation.target: Allende había ganado las elecciones de 1970 en Chile. En Argentina, Videla fue el primer presidente de la junta.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-consolidation.english: Allende had won the elections of 1970 in Chile. In Argentina, Videla was the first president of the junta.
b1-gobiernosmilitares-consolidation.canDo: I can contrast what the military said with what they did.

b1-represionpolitica-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The State of Siege
b1-represionpolitica-01.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg have watched a documentary about the military governments of the 1970s, and she asks what a state of siege was.
b1-represionpolitica-01.prompt: Tell Meg what happened to citizens' guarantees under a state of siege.
cues: Say that governments declared a state of siege
Say what happened to citizens' guarantees
b1-represionpolitica-01.target: Los gobiernos declaraban el estado de sitio, y las garantías de los ciudadanos eran suspendidas.
b1-represionpolitica-01.english: Governments declared a state of siege, and citizens' guarantees were suspended.
b1-represionpolitica-01.canDo: I can say what a state of siege suspended and why governments declared it.

b1-represionpolitica-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Banned Books
b1-represionpolitica-02.scenario: You are Meg. You visited a museum exhibition about the dictatorships, and Carlos asks what you learned about censorship.
b1-represionpolitica-02.prompt: Tell Carlos what was banned and who was watched.
cues: Say that books, films and songs were banned
Say that journalists were watched
b1-represionpolitica-02.target: Se prohibían libros, películas y canciones, y se vigilaba a los periodistas.
b1-represionpolitica-02.english: Books, films and songs were banned, and journalists were watched.
b1-represionpolitica-02.canDo: I can say what was censored, banned or burned.

b1-represionpolitica-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Disappeared
b1-represionpolitica-03.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading about Argentina for a class, and she asks how many people disappeared.
b1-represionpolitica-03.prompt: Tell Meg what a disappeared person was and give the CONADEP figure.
cues: Say that the disappeared were people who were detained
Give the CONADEP figure and name the source
b1-represionpolitica-03.target: Los desaparecidos eran personas detenidas, y según la CONADEP, 8.961 personas desaparecieron en Argentina.
b1-represionpolitica-03.english: The disappeared were detained people, and according to the CONADEP, 8,961 people disappeared in Argentina.
b1-represionpolitica-03.canDo: I can explain what a forced disappearance was and give a figure with its source.

b1-represionpolitica-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo
b1-represionpolitica-04.scenario: You are Meg. You saw a documentary about the Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo, and Carlos asks when they started.
b1-represionpolitica-04.prompt: Tell Carlos when the Mothers began to march and what they wore.
cues: Say when the Mothers began to march
Say what they wore while they marched
b1-represionpolitica-04.target: Las Madres de Plaza de Mayo empezaron a marchar el 30 de abril de 1977, llevando un pañuelo blanco.
b1-represionpolitica-04.english: The Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo began to march on 30 April 1977, wearing a white headscarf.
b1-represionpolitica-04.canDo: I can say when and how the Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo began to march.

b1-represionpolitica-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Then and Now
b1-represionpolitica-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos have just read about how Argentina and Chile faced the past, and he asks what has changed.
b1-represionpolitica-05.prompt: Tell Carlos how things were before and how they have changed.
cues: Say what many victims did not do before
Say what many have done over the years
b1-represionpolitica-05.target: Antes, muchas víctimas no hablaban porque tenían miedo; con los años, muchas han dado su testimonio.
b1-represionpolitica-05.english: Before, many victims did not talk because they were afraid; over the years, many have given their testimony.
b1-represionpolitica-05.canDo: I can say how things were before and how they have changed, with the imperfect and the present perfect.

b1-represionpolitica-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Repression in Review
b1-represionpolitica-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are going over your notes for a class on the dictatorships, and she asks how repression worked.
b1-represionpolitica-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg who was watched and arrested under the dictatorships.
cues: Say that opponents were watched
Say that many people were arrested at night
b1-represionpolitica-consolidation.target: Los opositores eran vigilados, y muchas personas eran detenidas de noche.
b1-represionpolitica-consolidation.english: The opponents were watched, and many people were arrested at night.
b1-represionpolitica-consolidation.canDo: I can use the passive with ser to say who was watched, arrested or tortured.

b1-centroamerica-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Somoza Dynasty
b1-centroamerica-01.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg have watched a documentary about Nicaragua, and she asks how long the Somoza family ruled.
b1-centroamerica-01.prompt: Tell Meg how long the Somoza family had ruled when the regime fell.
cues: Say when the regime fell
Say how long the family had ruled
b1-centroamerica-01.target: Cuando cayó Somoza, la familia había gobernado más de cuarenta años.
b1-centroamerica-01.english: When Somoza fell, the family had ruled for more than forty years.
b1-centroamerica-01.canDo: I can say how long the Somoza family had ruled Nicaragua when the regime fell.

b1-centroamerica-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Archbishop Romero
b1-centroamerica-02.scenario: You are Meg. You read about El Salvador for a class, and Carlos asks what happened to Archbishop Romero.
b1-centroamerica-02.prompt: Tell Carlos when and how Romero was killed.
cues: Say on which date he was killed
Say what he was doing at that moment
b1-centroamerica-02.target: Romero fue asesinado el 24 de marzo de 1980, mientras celebraba misa.
b1-centroamerica-02.english: Romero was killed on 24 March 1980, while he was saying Mass.
b1-centroamerica-02.canDo: I can say when and how Archbishop Romero was killed, using cuando and mientras.

b1-centroamerica-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Guatemalan Commission
b1-centroamerica-03.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing a presentation on Guatemala, and she asks what the commission counted.
b1-centroamerica-03.prompt: Tell Meg what the commission counted and when it presented its report.
cues: Mention the commission and when its report came out
Say how many dead or disappeared people it counted
b1-centroamerica-03.target: La CEH, que presentó su informe en 1999, contó más de 200.000 muertos o desaparecidos.
b1-centroamerica-03.english: The CEH, which presented its report in 1999, counted more than 200,000 dead or disappeared people.
b1-centroamerica-03.canDo: I can describe the Guatemalan conflict and what the commission found, with relative clauses.

b1-centroamerica-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The United States and the Contras
b1-centroamerica-04.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos have just seen an exhibition about the Cold War, and he asks what Congress did about the Contras.
b1-centroamerica-04.prompt: Tell Carlos what the United States did for the Contras and what Congress did.
cues: Say that the United States helped the Contras
Contrast this with what Congress did
b1-centroamerica-04.target: Estados Unidos ayudó a los contras. Sin embargo, el Congreso limitó esa ayuda.
b1-centroamerica-04.english: The United States helped the Contras. However, Congress limited that aid.
b1-centroamerica-04.canDo: I can explain what the United States did in Central America and what its critics said.

b1-centroamerica-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Road to Peace
b1-centroamerica-05.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are putting together a timeline for a class, and she asks how the peace process went.
b1-centroamerica-05.prompt: Tell Meg the main steps of the peace process in order.
cues: Say what the presidents signed first
Say what happened in Nicaragua next
Say how it ended in Guatemala
b1-centroamerica-05.target: Primero, los presidentes firmaron Esquipulas II en 1987. Luego, Violeta Chamorro ganó las elecciones de Nicaragua en 1990. Al final, Guatemala firmó la paz en 1996.
b1-centroamerica-05.english: First, the presidents signed Esquipulas II in 1987. Then Violeta Chamorro won the elections in Nicaragua in 1990. In the end, Guatemala signed peace in 1996.
b1-centroamerica-05.canDo: I can put the steps of the peace process in order with primero, luego, después and al final.

b1-centroamerica-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Nicaragua in Review
b1-centroamerica-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are going over your notes on Central America for a class, and he asks what you remember about Nicaragua.
b1-centroamerica-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos what the Somoza family had done before the Sandinistas took power.
cues: Say when the Sandinistas took power
Say how long the family had already ruled
b1-centroamerica-consolidation.target: Cuando los sandinistas tomaron el poder, los Somoza ya habían gobernado más de cuarenta años.
b1-centroamerica-consolidation.english: When the Sandinistas took power, the Somozas had already ruled for more than forty years.
b1-centroamerica-consolidation.canDo: I can use the pluperfect to say what had already happened in Nicaragua before 1979.

b1-conosur-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Chile under Pinochet
b1-conosur-01.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg have watched a documentary about Chile, and she asks what happened after the coup.
b1-conosur-01.prompt: Tell Meg what was banned after the coup and what was approved in 1980.
cues: Say what was banned after the coup
Say what was approved in 1980
b1-conosur-01.target: Después del golpe se prohibieron los partidos de izquierda, y en 1980 se aprobó una nueva constitución.
b1-conosur-01.english: After the coup the parties of the left were banned, and in 1980 a new constitution was approved.
b1-conosur-01.canDo: I can say what was done in Chile under Pinochet and how the dictatorship ended, using se.

b1-conosur-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Malvinas War
b1-conosur-02.scenario: You are Meg. You read about Argentina for a class, and Carlos asks what the government did in April 1982.
b1-conosur-02.prompt: Tell Carlos what the government ordered on 2 April 1982 and what the country was going through.
cues: Say what the country was going through
Say what the government ordered and when
b1-conosur-02.target: El 2 de abril de 1982, mientras el país vivía una crisis, el gobierno ordenó la invasión de las Malvinas.
b1-conosur-02.english: On 2 April 1982, while the country was going through a crisis, the government ordered the invasion of the Malvinas.
