b1-conosur-02.canDo: I can tell what happened in Argentina in 1982 and 1983, contrasting the preterite and the imperfect.

b1-conosur-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Democracy in Uruguay
b1-conosur-03.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading about Uruguay for a class, and she asks what was special about its democracy.
b1-conosur-03.prompt: Tell Meg what many historians say about Uruguay's democracy before 1973.
cues: Name the source of the opinion
Say that its democracy was one of the most stable in the region
b1-conosur-03.target: Según muchos historiadores, Uruguay tenía una de las democracias más estables de la región.
b1-conosur-03.english: According to many historians, Uruguay had one of the most stable democracies in the region.
b1-conosur-03.canDo: I can say what made Uruguay's democracy stand out and how the dictatorship ended, using superlatives.

b1-conosur-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Operation Condor
b1-conosur-04.scenario: You are Meg. You saw an exhibition about the dictatorships, and Carlos asks what Operation Condor was.
b1-conosur-04.prompt: Tell Carlos what Operation Condor was and when it began.
cues: Say that it was a network and what its aim was
Say when and where it began
b1-conosur-04.target: En noviembre de 1975 nació en Santiago la Operación Cóndor, una red cuyo objetivo era perseguir a los opositores.
b1-conosur-04.english: In November 1975 Operation Condor began in Santiago, a network whose aim was to pursue opponents.
b1-conosur-04.canDo: I can say what Operation Condor was and when and where it began, using cuyo.

b1-conosur-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Justice in Spite of the Laws
b1-conosur-05.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are talking about Argentina after a class, and she asks what happened after the laws of 1986 and 1987.
b1-conosur-05.prompt: Tell Meg what the organisations did in spite of those laws.
cues: Say that there were laws that limited trials
Say what the organisations kept doing in spite of them
b1-conosur-05.target: A pesar de esas leyes, muchas organizaciones siguieron pidiendo justicia.
b1-conosur-05.english: In spite of those laws, many organisations kept asking for justice.
b1-conosur-05.canDo: I can say what stood in the way of justice in Argentina, Chile and Uruguay, using a pesar de.

b1-conosur-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Dictatorships in Review
b1-conosur-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are going over your notes on the Southern Cone for a class, and he asks what you remember about Chile.
b1-conosur-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos what was banned and closed in Chile after the coup.
cues: Say what was banned
Say what was closed
b1-conosur-consolidation.target: Se prohibieron los partidos de izquierda y se cerró el Congreso.
b1-conosur-consolidation.english: The parties of the left were banned and Congress was closed.
b1-conosur-consolidation.canDo: I can use se with a verb to say what was done under a dictatorship.

b1-crisisdeuda-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Oil Money and Loans
b1-crisisdeuda-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos watched a documentary about the Latin American debt crisis, and he asks how the banks had so much money to lend.
b1-crisisdeuda-01.prompt: Tell Carlos where the banks got the money and what they did with it.
cues: Say what happened to the oil price in 1973 and name the cause and result
Say where the oil-exporting countries put their money
Say what the banks did with it
b1-crisisdeuda-01.target: A raíz de la subida del petróleo, los países que exportan petróleo depositaron mucho dinero en los bancos, y los bancos otorgaron préstamos a los gobiernos.
b1-crisisdeuda-01.english: As a result of the rise in oil prices, the countries that export oil deposited a lot of money in the banks, and the banks granted loans to the governments.
b1-crisisdeuda-01.canDo: I can say how the oil money of the 1970s ended up in loans to Latin American governments.

b1-crisisdeuda-02.title: Communicative Challenge: What the United States Did in 1979
b1-crisisdeuda-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg read about the debt crisis for a class, and she asks what the United States did in October 1979 and what had already happened in Latin America.
b1-crisisdeuda-02.prompt: Tell Meg what the United States decided in October 1979 and what many countries had already done.
cues: Say what the central bank decided and why
Say what many countries had already done before 1979
b1-crisisdeuda-02.target: En octubre de 1979, el banco central de Estados Unidos decidió elevar las tasas de interés para frenar la inflación. Muchos países ya habían acumulado una deuda grande.
b1-crisisdeuda-02.english: In October 1979, the central bank of the United States decided to raise interest rates to stop inflation. Many countries had already built up a large debt.
b1-crisisdeuda-02.canDo: I can explain what the US Federal Reserve did in October 1979 and why.

b1-crisisdeuda-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The IMF and the Cuts
b1-crisisdeuda-03.scenario: You are Meg. You are telling Carlos what you learned in a history class about the years after 1982, and he asks what governments did when the banks stopped lending.
b1-crisisdeuda-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what governments did after the banks stopped lending, and what was cut.
cues: Say who many governments turned to
Say what was cut, without saying who cut it
b1-crisisdeuda-03.target: Después de 1982, muchos gobiernos recurrieron al FMI. Se recortó el gasto público.
b1-crisisdeuda-03.english: After 1982, many governments turned to the IMF. Public spending was cut.
b1-crisisdeuda-03.canDo: I can say why governments turned to the IMF after 1982.

b1-crisisdeuda-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Prices and Wages
b1-crisisdeuda-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg visited an exhibition about the 1980s in Latin America, and she asks what happened to ordinary families.
b1-crisisdeuda-04.prompt: Tell Meg what happened to wages and to work as prices went up.
cues: Say what happened to wages as prices rose
Say what kind of work grew
b1-crisisdeuda-04.target: A medida que los precios subían, los salarios compraban menos, y creció el trabajo informal.
b1-crisisdeuda-04.english: As prices rose, wages bought less, and informal work grew.
b1-crisisdeuda-04.canDo: I can explain how unemployment, informal work and falling wages affected families.

b1-crisisdeuda-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Lost Decade
b1-crisisdeuda-05.scenario: You are Meg. You read a book about the 1980s in Latin America, and Carlos asks why people call that decade lost.
b1-crisisdeuda-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what CEPAL called the 1980s and why.
cues: Name the source and what it called the 1980s
Say what happened to income per person
b1-crisisdeuda-05.target: Según la CEPAL, los años ochenta fueron una década perdida, porque en muchos países el ingreso por habitante de 1990 no era mayor que el de 1980.
b1-crisisdeuda-05.english: According to CEPAL, the 1980s were a lost decade, because in many countries income per person in 1990 was not higher than in 1980.
b1-crisisdeuda-05.canDo: I can say what CEPAL called the 1980s and why.

b1-crisisdeuda-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Debt Crisis in Order
b1-crisisdeuda-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are going over your notes on the debt crisis before a class, and she asks you to tell the main steps in order.
b1-crisisdeuda-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg the main steps of the debt crisis in order.
cues: Say what the banks did first
Say what Mexico announced in 1982
Say what plan came in 1989
b1-crisisdeuda-consolidation.target: Primero, los bancos otorgaron muchos préstamos. Después, en 1982, México anunció que no podía pagar su deuda. En 1989 llegó el Plan Brady.
b1-crisisdeuda-consolidation.english: First, the banks granted many loans. Then, in 1982, Mexico announced that it could not pay its debt. In 1989 the Brady Plan came.
b1-crisisdeuda-consolidation.canDo: I can retell the main steps of the debt crisis in order, from the loans of the 1970s to the Brady Plan.

b1-neoliberalismo-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Market Ideas
b1-neoliberalismo-01.scenario: You are Meg. You read a book about the 1990s in Latin America, and Carlos asks what neoliberal ideas are.
b1-neoliberalismo-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what these ideas are and what their defenders say.
cues: Say what kind of ideas they are, using a relative clause
Say what the defenders think about the market and the state
b1-neoliberalismo-01.target: Son ideas económicas que dan más importancia al mercado. Según sus defensores, el mercado asigna los recursos con más eficiencia que el Estado.
b1-neoliberalismo-01.english: They are economic ideas that give more importance to the market. According to their defenders, the market allocates resources more efficiently than the state.
b1-neoliberalismo-01.canDo: I can say what neoliberal ideas are and what their defenders argue.

b1-neoliberalismo-02.title: Communicative Challenge: What Was Sold
b1-neoliberalismo-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg watched a documentary about privatisation, and she asks what was sold in Argentina and Mexico.
b1-neoliberalismo-02.prompt: Tell Meg what was privatised in 1990 in Argentina and in Mexico.
cues: Say what happened to the telephone company in Argentina
Say what happened to Telmex in Mexico
b1-neoliberalismo-02.target: En 1990, la compañía telefónica de Argentina fue privatizada, y Telmex fue vendida a un grupo privado.
b1-neoliberalismo-02.english: In 1990, the telephone company of Argentina was privatised, and Telmex was sold to a private group.
b1-neoliberalismo-02.canDo: I can say which Argentine and Mexican companies were privatised in the 1990s.

b1-neoliberalismo-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The State Before and After
b1-neoliberalismo-03.scenario: You are Meg. You are telling Carlos what you learned in a class about the role of the state, and he asks how it changed.
b1-neoliberalismo-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what the state did before the reforms and what many people thought afterwards.
cues: Say how the state protected industry
Contrast it with what many people thought after the debt crisis
b1-neoliberalismo-03.target: El Estado protegía la industria nacional con aranceles altos; sin embargo, después de la crisis de la deuda, muchos consideraron agotado ese modelo.
b1-neoliberalismo-03.english: The state protected national industry with high tariffs; however, after the debt crisis, many considered that model exhausted.
b1-neoliberalismo-03.canDo: I can describe the role of the state in the earlier model.

b1-neoliberalismo-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Growth Without Equality
b1-neoliberalismo-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg visited an exhibition about the 1990s, and she asks what improved and what did not.
b1-neoliberalismo-04.prompt: Tell Meg what improved in the 1990s and what did not.
cues: Say what grew and what fell
Say what did not fall, using a concession
b1-neoliberalismo-04.target: Aunque la economía creció y la inflación bajó, la desigualdad no bajó.
b1-neoliberalismo-04.english: Although the economy grew and inflation fell, inequality did not fall.
b1-neoliberalismo-04.canDo: I can say what many countries achieved in the 1990s and what did not improve.

b1-neoliberalismo-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Opinions
b1-neoliberalismo-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are talking about a book on the neoliberal reforms, and he asks what the two sides believe.
b1-neoliberalismo-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what the defenders believe and what the critics do not believe.
cues: Say what the defenders believe about inflation
Say what the critics do not believe about the market
b1-neoliberalismo-05.target: Los defensores creen que las reformas bajaron la inflación. Los críticos no creen que el mercado pueda resolver la pobreza.
b1-neoliberalismo-05.english: The defenders believe that the reforms lowered inflation. The critics do not believe that the market can solve poverty.
b1-neoliberalismo-05.canDo: I can say what the defenders of the reforms believe.

b1-neoliberalismo-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Reforms in Short
b1-neoliberalismo-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are going over your notes before a class, and she asks you to sum up the neoliberal reforms.
b1-neoliberalismo-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg the term from 1989, what governments sold, and what people still discuss.
cues: Say who coined which term in 1989
Say what governments sold
Say what defenders and critics still discuss
b1-neoliberalismo-consolidation.target: En 1989, John Williamson acuñó el término «Consenso de Washington». Los gobiernos vendieron empresas del Estado, y los defensores y los críticos todavía discuten si las reformas fueron un éxito.
b1-neoliberalismo-consolidation.english: In 1989, John Williamson coined the term “Washington Consensus”. Governments sold state companies, and the defenders and the critics still discuss whether the reforms were a success.
b1-neoliberalismo-consolidation.canDo: I can retell the main steps of the neoliberal reforms and the debate about them.

b1-democratizacion-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Back to the Ballot Box
b1-democratizacion-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos watched a documentary about the end of the dictatorships, and he asks which countries came back to elected government first.
b1-democratizacion-01.prompt: Tell Carlos which countries returned first and which one came at the end.
cues: Say which two countries returned first and in which years
Say which country came at the end, using an ordering marker
b1-democratizacion-01.target: Primero volvieron Ecuador, en 1979, y Perú, en 1980. Finalmente, en 1990, Chile tuvo otra vez un presidente civil.
b1-democratizacion-01.english: First Ecuador returned, in 1979, and Peru, in 1980. Finally, in 1990, Chile had a civilian president again.
b1-democratizacion-01.canDo: I can list the countries that returned to elected government and the years.

b1-democratizacion-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The New Constitutions
b1-democratizacion-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg visited a museum exhibition about the 1980s, and she asks what the new constitution of Brazil did.
b1-democratizacion-02.prompt: Tell Meg what Brazil's constitution of 1988 recognised and what was created.
cues: Say when the Congress enacted the constitution and what it recognised
Say what was created, without saying who created it
b1-democratizacion-02.target: En Brasil, el Congreso promulgó una nueva constitución en 1988, y reconoció muchos derechos sociales. Se creó un servicio de salud pública para todos.
b1-democratizacion-02.english: In Brazil, the Congress enacted a new constitution in 1988, and it recognised many social rights. A public health service for everyone was created.
b1-democratizacion-02.canDo: I can say what Brazil's constitution of 1988 recognised and what it created.

b1-democratizacion-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Rights and Courts
b1-democratizacion-03.scenario: You are Meg. You are telling Carlos what you read in a book about justice in the new democracies, and he asks whether people could use their rights.
b1-democratizacion-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what the problem was and what the tutela allowed.
cues: Admit a difficulty and go on
Say what a person could ask a judge to do with the tutela
b1-democratizacion-03.target: A pesar de que la ley reconocía los derechos, mucha gente pobre no podía defenderlos. Con la tutela, una persona podía pedir a un juez la protección de un derecho.
b1-democratizacion-03.english: Although the law recognised rights, many poor people could not defend them. With the tutela, a person could ask a judge to protect a right.
b1-democratizacion-03.canDo: I can say why justice was still a problem after the dictatorships.

b1-democratizacion-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Presidents in Trouble
b1-democratizacion-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are going over a class on the 1990s, and she asks what power the military kept in Chile after the dictatorship.
b1-democratizacion-04.prompt: Tell Meg what stopped in Chile and what the military kept.
cues: Say what the military stopped doing
Say what Pinochet stayed until 1998
b1-democratizacion-04.target: Los militares dejaron de gobernar en Chile, pero Pinochet siguió como comandante en jefe del Ejército hasta 1998.
b1-democratizacion-04.english: The military stopped governing in Chile, but Pinochet remained commander in chief of the army until 1998.
b1-democratizacion-04.canDo: I can say what power the military kept in Chile after 1990.

b1-democratizacion-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Imperfect Democracies
b1-democratizacion-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are talking about a book on the new democracies, and he asks what the author concludes.
b1-democratizacion-05.prompt: Sum up what the region had and what it still needed to do.
cues: Begin with a summing-up marker and say what the region had
Say what the countries still had to do
b1-democratizacion-05.target: En resumen, la región tenía democracias, pero muchas eran imperfectas. Todavía tenían problemas: la corrupción y la desigualdad.
b1-democratizacion-05.english: In summary, the region had democracies, but many were imperfect. They still had problems: corruption and inequality.
b1-democratizacion-05.canDo: I can sum up what the new democracies had and what problems they still had.

b1-democratizacion-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The New Democracies in Order
b1-democratizacion-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are going over your notes before a class, and she asks you to tell how the countries returned to elections and what problems came after.
b1-democratizacion-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg in order how the countries returned to elections and what problems came after.
cues: Say which countries returned first
Say what the military kept in Chile
Sum up with a closing marker
b1-democratizacion-consolidation.target: Primero volvieron Ecuador y Perú. Después, los militares dejaron de gobernar, pero en Chile conservaron poder. En resumen, había democracias, pero tenían problemas.
b1-democratizacion-consolidation.english: First Ecuador and Peru returned. Then the military stopped governing, but in Chile they kept power. In summary, there were democracies, but they had problems.
b1-democratizacion-consolidation.canDo: I can retell in order how the countries of Latin America returned to elected government.

b1-37-01.title: Communicative Challenge: A Safe Arrival
b1-37-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos's sister Ana has just arrived in Budapest on the evening train, and you meet her at the station.
b1-37-01.prompt: Welcome Ana: say you hope she has had a good trip and that you are glad she has arrived.
cues: Say you hope she has had a good trip
Say you are glad she has arrived
b1-37-01.target: Espero que hayas tenido un buen viaje. Me alegro de que hayas llegado bien.
b1-37-01.english: I hope you have had a good trip. I am glad you have arrived safely.
b1-37-01.canDo: I can form the present perfect subjunctive with haya + participio.

b1-37-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Good News
b1-37-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg tells you that she has passed the last exam of the term at her university.
b1-37-02.prompt: Tell Meg how you feel: you are glad she has passed, and it is a relief.
cues: Say you are glad she has passed the exam
Say what a relief it is
b1-37-02.target: Me alegro de que hayas aprobado el examen. ¡Qué alivio que hayas terminado!
b1-37-02.english: I am glad you have passed the exam. What a relief that you have finished!
b1-37-02.canDo: I can say how I feel about something that has happened, using the present perfect subjunctive.

b1-37-03.title: Communicative Challenge: I Doubt It
b1-37-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos says that your sister Kaylee has already sent the family photos, but you have not received anything.
b1-37-03.prompt: Tell Carlos that you doubt it and that you don't think she has done it yet.
cues: Say you doubt Kaylee has sent the photos
Say you don't think she has done it yet
b1-37-03.target: Dudo que Kaylee haya mandado las fotos. No creo que lo haya hecho todavía.
b1-37-03.english: I doubt Kaylee has sent the photos. I don't think she has done it yet.
b1-37-03.canDo: I can doubt or deny that something has happened, using the present perfect subjunctive.

b1-37-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Dinner After the Report
b1-37-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks when you can go out for dinner. You still have to finish a report for your office.
b1-37-04.prompt: Tell Meg you will go out with her as soon as you have finished the report.
cues: Say you will go out for dinner
Say what you have to finish first
b1-37-04.target: Saldremos a cenar en cuanto haya terminado el informe.
b1-37-04.english: We will go out for dinner as soon as I have finished the report.
b1-37-04.canDo: I can say that an action will be finished before another one, using cuando or en cuanto + present perfect subjunctive.

b1-37-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Before the Exam
b1-37-05.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg has an exam tomorrow morning and you phone her in the evening.
b1-37-05.prompt: Tell Meg you hope she has rested today and that the exam goes well tomorrow.
cues: Say you hope she has rested today
Say you hope the exam goes well tomorrow
b1-37-05.target: Espero que hayas descansado hoy y que el examen salga bien mañana.
b1-37-05.english: I hope you have rested today and that the exam goes well tomorrow.
b1-37-05.canDo: I can choose between the present subjunctive and the present perfect subjunctive.

b1-37-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: An Evening at Home
b1-37-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos has just come home from a long day at his office in Budapest.
b1-37-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos you are glad he has come home, and that you will watch a film with him as soon as he has eaten.
cues: Say you are glad he has come home
Say what you will do when he has eaten
b1-37-consolidation.target: Me alegro de que hayas vuelto a casa. Veremos una película en cuanto hayas cenado.
b1-37-consolidation.english: I am glad you have come home. We will watch a film as soon as you have had dinner.
b1-37-consolidation.canDo: I can use the present perfect subjunctive for feelings, doubts and future completion.

b1-38-01.title: Communicative Challenge: What My Parents Wanted
b1-38-01.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks about your childhood. Your parents wanted you to study hard, and your mother asked you to help at home every day.
b1-38-01.prompt: Tell Meg what your parents wanted and what your mother asked you to do.
cues: Say what your parents wanted
Say what your mother asked you to do
b1-38-01.target: Mis padres querían que estudiara mucho y mi madre me pidió que la ayudara en casa.
b1-38-01.english: My parents wanted me to study hard and my mother asked me to help her at home.
b1-38-01.canDo: I can use the imperfect subjunctive after a past main verb, as in quería que vinieras.

b1-38-02.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Teacher Said
b1-38-02.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what your teacher at the university told you before the exam. She told you to arrive early and not to talk during the test.
b1-38-02.prompt: Tell Carlos what the teacher told you to do and not to do.
cues: Say what she told you to do
Say what she told you not to do
b1-38-02.target: La profesora me dijo que llegara pronto y que no hablara durante el examen.
b1-38-02.english: The teacher told me to arrive early and not to talk during the exam.
b1-38-02.canDo: I can report orders and requests with decir que and pedir que + imperfect subjunctive.

b1-38-03.title: Communicative Challenge: What My Boss Said
b1-38-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what your boss said on the phone this morning. He said he would arrive on Monday and that he had no time that day.
b1-38-03.prompt: Tell Meg what your boss said.
cues: Say when he said he would arrive
Say what he said about his time
b1-38-03.target: Mi jefe dijo que llegaría el lunes y que no tenía tiempo aquel día.
b1-38-03.english: My boss said he would arrive on Monday and that he had no time that day.
b1-38-03.canDo: I can report what someone said in the past, shifting the tenses and the time words.

b1-38-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Doctor's Advice
b1-38-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what the doctor said about your sore back. The doctor advised you to rest, suggested that you drink more water and warned you to be careful.
b1-38-04.prompt: Tell Carlos what the doctor advised, suggested and warned.
cues: Say what the doctor advised
Say what the doctor suggested
Say what the doctor warned
b1-38-04.target: El médico me aconsejó que descansara, me sugirió que bebiera más agua y me advirtió que tuviera cuidado.
b1-38-04.english: The doctor advised me to rest, suggested that I drink more water and warned me to be careful.
b1-38-04.canDo: I can report advice, suggestions, warnings and demands with sugerir que, advertir que and exigir que.

b1-38-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Colleague's News
b1-38-05.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks about your day. This morning at the office you met a colleague. She told you she would travel to Madrid and asked you to help her with her work.
b1-38-05.prompt: Tell Meg what happened with your colleague this morning.
cues: Say that you met your colleague
Say what she told you she would do
Say what she asked you to do
b1-38-05.target: Esta mañana me encontré con una compañera. Me contó que viajaría a Madrid y me pidió que la ayudara con el trabajo.
b1-38-05.english: This morning I met a colleague. She told me she would travel to Madrid and asked me to help her with her work.
b1-38-05.canDo: I can combine past tenses, reported statements and the imperfect subjunctive in one account.

b1-38-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Lauren Phoned
b1-38-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what your sister Lauren said when she phoned. She said she would visit you in Budapest in the summer and asked you to book a hotel.
b1-38-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos what Lauren said and what she asked you to do.
cues: Say what Lauren said she would do
Say what she asked you to do
b1-38-consolidation.target: Lauren dijo que nos visitaría en verano y me pidió que reservara un hotel.
b1-38-consolidation.english: Lauren said she would visit us in the summer and asked me to book a hotel.
b1-38-consolidation.canDo: I can report statements, orders and requests that someone made in the past.

b1-39-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Nerves at the Office
b1-39-01.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks how your meeting at the office went. You were very nervous before it, and you turned red when your boss asked a question.
b1-39-01.prompt: Tell Meg how you felt before the presentation and when your boss asked a question.
cues: Say you got nervous before the presentation
Say what happened when your boss asked a question
b1-39-01.target: Me puse muy nervioso antes de la reunión y me puse rojo cuando mi jefe hizo una pregunta.
b1-39-01.english: I got very nervous before the meeting and I turned red when my boss asked a question.
b1-39-01.canDo: I can use ponerse + adjective for sudden changes of mood, health and appearance.

b1-39-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Asleep on the Metro
b1-39-02.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks why you were late for the dinner with his friends. After your classes you fell asleep on the metro.
b1-39-02.prompt: Tell Carlos why you were late.
cues: Say you fell asleep
Say where and when it happened
b1-39-02.target: Me quedé dormida en el metro después de mis clases.
b1-39-02.english: I fell asleep on the metro after my classes.
b1-39-02.canDo: I can use quedarse for the state that results from an event.

b1-39-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Neighbour Has Changed
b1-39-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks about your neighbour in Budapest. Since last year he has become very serious, and he hardly talks to anyone.
b1-39-03.prompt: Tell Carlos how your neighbour has changed.
cues: Say how he has changed
Say what he does now
b1-39-03.target: Mi vecino se ha vuelto muy serio y casi no habla con nadie.
b1-39-03.english: My neighbour has become very serious and hardly talks to anyone.
b1-39-03.canDo: I can use volverse + adjective for deep, lasting changes in character.

b1-39-04.title: Communicative Challenge: From Student to Head of the School
b1-39-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks about a friend of a colleague who is now the head of a school. She studied for ten years, became a teacher and later became head of the school.
b1-39-04.prompt: Tell Meg how she got there.
cues: Say what she became
Say what she became later
b1-39-04.target: Estudió diez años, se hizo profesora y llegó a ser directora de la escuela.
b1-39-04.english: She studied for ten years, became a teacher and came to be head of the school.
b1-39-04.canDo: I can use hacerse and convertirse en, and say llegar a ser for the high point of a long effort.

b1-39-05.title: Communicative Challenge: How My Sister Has Changed
b1-39-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks how your sister Kaylee has changed. She was always very calm, but now she gets nervous easily, and since she lives alone she has become very tidy.
b1-39-05.prompt: Tell Carlos how Kaylee was, how she is now and how she has changed.
cues: Say how she was before
Say how she reacts now
Say how her character has changed
b1-39-05.target: Kaylee siempre fue muy tranquila, pero ahora se pone nerviosa con facilidad, y desde que vive sola se ha vuelto muy ordenada.
b1-39-05.english: Kaylee was always very calm, but now she gets nervous easily, and since she has been living alone she has become very tidy.
b1-39-05.canDo: I can choose between ponerse, quedarse, volverse, hacerse and convertirse en.

b1-39-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Day at the Office
b1-39-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what happened at the office today. Your boss got furious when he read the report and then was very surprised. Later the project turned into a success.
b1-39-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what your boss did and what the project became.
cues: Say how your boss reacted
Say what the project became
b1-39-consolidation.target: Mi jefe se puso furioso al leer el informe y luego se quedó muy sorprendido. Después el proyecto se convirtió en un éxito.
b1-39-consolidation.english: My boss got furious when he read the report and then was very surprised. Afterwards the project turned into a success.
b1-39-consolidation.canDo: I can describe how people and things change, choosing the right verb.

b1-40-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Dreams and Support
b1-40-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you dream about and who you can count on. You dream of travelling to South Africa to see your family, and you can count on your sister Lauren.
b1-40-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what you dream of and who you can count on.
cues: Say what you dream of doing
Say who you can count on
b1-40-01.target: Sueño con viajar a Sudáfrica y sé que puedo contar con mi hermana Lauren.
b1-40-01.english: I dream of travelling to South Africa and I know I can count on my sister Lauren.
b1-40-01.canDo: I can use verbs with a fixed preposition such as soñar con, pensar en, contar con and depender de.

b1-40-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Not the Party, but Home
b1-40-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks if you went to the party at your office last night. You did not go to the party: you stayed at home and studied Spanish.
b1-40-02.prompt: Tell Meg that you did not go to the party, and say what you did instead.
cues: Say you did not go to the party
Say what you did instead
b1-40-02.target: No fui a la fiesta, sino que me quedé en casa estudiando español.
b1-40-02.english: I didn't go to the party, but stayed at home studying Spanish.
b1-40-02.canDo: I can choose between pero, sino and sino que.

b1-40-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Photography Course
b1-40-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you thought of your photography course. You liked the walks around the city best, and the difficult part was getting up early.
b1-40-03.prompt: Tell Carlos the best thing and the difficult part of the course.
cues: Say the best thing about the course
Say the difficult part
b1-40-03.target: Lo mejor fueron los paseos por la ciudad y lo difícil fue levantarse temprano.
b1-40-03.english: The best thing was the walks around the city and the difficult part was getting up early.
b1-40-03.canDo: I can use lo + adjective, as in lo importante, lo bueno and lo difícil.

b1-40-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Long Meeting
b1-40-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks how the long meeting at your office went. It was very difficult and you finished very tired.
b1-40-04.prompt: Tell Meg how difficult the meeting was and how tired you were.
cues: Say how difficult the meeting was
Say how tired you were
b1-40-04.target: No sabes lo difícil que fue la reunión y lo cansado que terminé.
b1-40-04.english: You don't know how difficult the meeting was and how tired I was at the end.
b1-40-04.canDo: I can say how difficult, fast or good something is, with lo + adjective + que.

b1-40-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Quiet Weekend
b1-40-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks if you are going to the cinema on Saturday. You are not going to the cinema: you are staying at home, and you are thinking about how well you are going to rest.
b1-40-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what you are not doing, what you are doing instead and what you are thinking about.
cues: Say you are not going to the cinema
Say you are staying at home
Say what you are thinking about
b1-40-05.target: No voy al cine, sino que me quedo en casa. Pienso en lo bien que voy a descansar.
b1-40-05.english: I'm not going to the cinema; I'm staying at home. I'm thinking about how well I'm going to rest.
b1-40-05.canDo: I can combine fixed prepositions, sino (que) and lo in one text.

b1-40-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Quiet Summer
b1-40-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what you dream about for the summer. You do not dream of a long trip but of a quiet week at home. The important thing is to rest, and you count on Meg.
b1-40-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what you dream of, what is important and who you count on.
cues: Say what you dream of, and what you don't
Say what the important thing is
Say who you count on
b1-40-consolidation.target: No sueño con un viaje largo, sino con una semana tranquila en casa. Lo importante es descansar, y cuento contigo.
b1-40-consolidation.english: I don't dream of a long trip but of a quiet week at home. The important thing is to rest, and I count on you.
b1-40-consolidation.canDo: I can use verbs with fixed prepositions, sino (que) and lo + adjective.

b2-01-01.title: Communicative Challenge: What Matters Most
b2-01-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos live in Budapest, and he asks what interests you most about your course. The part that interests you most is the historical background of the crisis.
b2-01-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what interests you most about your course.
cues: Say what interests you most
Mention the historical background
b2-01-01.target: Lo que más me interesa es el trasfondo histórico de la crisis.
b2-01-01.english: What interests me most is the historical background of the crisis.
b2-01-01.canDo: I can build cleft sentences with 'lo que' and 'ser' to spotlight an idea.

b2-01-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Frankly Speaking
b2-01-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You work in an office in Budapest, and Meg asks what you think of the new timetable there. You are honest: you do not like it.
b2-01-02.prompt: Give Meg your honest opinion of the new timetable.
cues: Show that you are being frank
Say you do not like the timetable
b2-01-02.target: Francamente, no me gusta el nuevo horario de la oficina.
b2-01-02.english: Frankly, I do not like the new timetable at the office.
b2-01-02.canDo: I can use stance adverbs such as 'francamente' and 'lamentablemente' to show my attitude to a whole sentence.

b2-01-03.title: Communicative Challenge: What Was Decisive
b2-01-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos live in Budapest. You have passed your exams this year, and Carlos asks what helped you most. You think studying every day was the decisive thing.
b2-01-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what was decisive for your exams.
cues: Put the quality first
Say what you did every day
b2-01-03.canDo: I can put an adjective first and the subject after the verb to stress a quality.

b2-01-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Setting It Straight
b2-01-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You work in an office in Budapest. Meg thinks you arrived late because of the traffic, but it was not the traffic: it was the rain.
b2-01-04.prompt: Correct Meg and say what really made you late.
cues: Say what it was not
Say what it really was
b2-01-04.target: No fue el tráfico, sino la lluvia lo que me retrasó.
b2-01-04.english: It was not the traffic but the rain that made me late.
b2-01-04.canDo: I can correct an assumption with 'no ... sino' and give the right alternative.

b2-01-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Why Read Borges
b2-01-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos live in Budapest. You have read a text about a story by Borges, and Carlos asks what you like most about it: the idea of many possible futures.
b2-01-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what you like most about the story.
cues: Say what you like most
Mention the possible futures
b2-01-05.target: Lo que más me gusta es la idea de muchos futuros posibles.
b2-01-05.english: What I like most is the idea of many possible futures.
b2-01-05.canDo: I can read a short text about a writer and his best-known story and answer questions about it.

b2-01-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Not Money but Teamwork
b2-01-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You work in an office in Budapest, and Meg asks what mattered most in your last project. It was not the money but the teamwork.
b2-01-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what mattered most in your last project.
cues: Say what it was not
Say what it really was
b2-01-consolidation.target: Lo que más importó no fue el dinero, sino el trabajo en equipo.
b2-01-consolidation.english: What mattered most was not the money but the teamwork.
b2-01-consolidation.canDo: I can use cleft sentences with 'lo que' and 'fue ... quien / donde / cuando'.

b2-mexicocentro-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Sinking Valley
b2-mexicocentro-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about Mexico City in Budapest. It says the ground of the city is sinking.
b2-mexicocentro-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what worries people most today, with a cleft sentence.
cues: Say that what worries people most is one thing
Name the sinking of the ground
b2-mexicocentro-01.target: Lo que más preocupa hoy es el hundimiento del suelo.
b2-mexicocentro-01.english: What worries people most today is the sinking of the ground.
b2-mexicocentro-01.canDo: I can use a cleft sentence with lo que to put a key cause or fact about the Valley of Mexico in the spotlight.

b2-mexicocentro-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Dike of Nezahualcóyotl
b2-mexicocentro-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You are telling Meg about an article on Tenochtitlan that you read in Budapest. It praised the dike of Nezahualcóyotl.
b2-mexicocentro-02.prompt: Tell Meg that the dike was very important, with the important thing first.
cues: Start with the quality
Say what the dike did for the city
b2-mexicocentro-02.target: Muy importante fue el albarradón para proteger la ciudad.
b2-mexicocentro-02.english: The dike was very important for protecting the city.
b2-mexicocentro-02.canDo: I can put a quality or a place first, as in Importante fue ..., to stress it when I tell about Tenochtitlan.

b2-mexicocentro-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Life in the Colonial Street
b2-mexicocentro-03.scenario: You are Meg. You are preparing a talk in Budapest about colonial Mexico City, and Carlos asks about the caste system.
b2-mexicocentro-03.prompt: Tell Carlos that life in the street was more mixed than the castes, using a stance adverb.
cues: Open with an adverb that corrects an idea
Say that the street was more mixed than the castes
b2-mexicocentro-03.target: En realidad, la vida de la calle era más mezclada que las castas.
b2-mexicocentro-03.english: Actually, life in the street was more mixed than the castes.
b2-mexicocentro-03.canDo: I can use a stance adverb such as en realidad or indudablemente to show how I see a fact about the colonial city.

b2-mexicocentro-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Murals for the People
b2-mexicocentro-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You are talking to Meg in Budapest about a documentary on Mexican muralism.
b2-mexicocentro-04.prompt: Tell Meg what the murals were not and what they were.
cues: Say what the murals were not
Say what they were for
b2-mexicocentro-04.target: Los murales no eran para decorar, sino para enseñar la historia.
b2-mexicocentro-04.english: The murals were not for decoration but for teaching history.
b2-mexicocentro-04.canDo: I can correct an idea with no ... sino and no ... sino que when I talk about the murals.

b2-mexicocentro-05.title: Communicative Challenge: After the Earthquake
b2-mexicocentro-05.scenario: You are Meg. You are reading an article about the 1985 earthquake in Mexico City, and Carlos asks who organised the help.
b2-mexicocentro-05.prompt: Tell Carlos who formed the rescue teams, with a cleft sentence.
cues: Say who it was
Mention the rescue teams
b2-mexicocentro-05.target: Fueron los vecinos quienes formaron brigadas.
b2-mexicocentro-05.english: It was the neighbours who formed rescue teams.
b2-mexicocentro-05.canDo: I can tell what happened in Mexico City in 1985, using clefts, fronting and no ... sino together.

b2-mexicocentro-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Fall of Tenochtitlan
b2-mexicocentro-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You are giving a short talk in Budapest about central Mexico, and you reach the year 1521.
b2-mexicocentro-consolidation.prompt: Say when Tenochtitlan fell and what was built afterwards.
cues: Say the year with a cleft sentence
Say what was built on the remains
b2-mexicocentro-consolidation.target: Fue en 1521 cuando cayó Tenochtitlan. Sobre sus restos se construyó la ciudad colonial.
b2-mexicocentro-consolidation.english: It was in 1521 that Tenochtitlan fell. On its remains the colonial city was built.
b2-mexicocentro-consolidation.canDo: I can recall the main facts about central Mexico: the lake basin, Tenochtitlan, the colonial city, muralism and the 1985 earthquake.

b2-02-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Events and Scenery
b2-02-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks how your walk home went last night. It was dark and raining, and you lost your umbrella.
b2-02-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what the evening was like and what happened.
cues: Say what the evening was like
Say what happened to your umbrella
b2-02-01.target: Era de noche y llovía mucho cuando perdí el paraguas.
b2-02-01.english: It was night and it was raining hard when I lost my umbrella.
b2-02-01.canDo: I can use the preterite for the events of a story and the imperfect for the scene around them.

b2-02-02.title: Communicative Challenge: What Had Happened
b2-02-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks why you were so tired at the office yesterday. You had not slept well the night before.
b2-02-02.prompt: Tell Meg how you were and why.
cues: Say how you felt
Say what you had not done the night before
b2-02-02.target: Estaba muy cansado porque no había dormido bien.
b2-02-02.english: I was very tired because I had not slept well.
b2-02-02.canDo: I can use the pluperfect to say what had already happened before a moment in a story.

b2-02-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Managing and Refusing
b2-02-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks how you got home last night. You were late and ran to the stop, and you managed to catch the last bus.
b2-02-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what you did and how it ended.
cues: Say that you ran
Say that you managed to catch the last bus
b2-02-03.target: Corrí mucho y por fin pude tomar el último autobús.
b2-02-03.english: I ran a lot and finally managed to catch the last bus.
b2-02-03.canDo: I can use conocí, supe, quise and pude for meeting, finding out, trying and managing.

b2-02-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Time in a Story
b2-02-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what happened when you left the office yesterday. It started to rain the moment you went outside.
b2-02-04.prompt: Tell Meg what happened when you left.
cues: Say that you left the office
Say that the rain began at once
b2-02-04.target: Apenas salí de la oficina, empezó a llover.
b2-02-04.english: As soon as I left the office, it started to rain.
b2-02-04.canDo: I can make one event follow another at once with apenas and en cuanto.

b2-02-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Polite Question
b2-02-05.scenario: You are Meg. You are at the front desk of your university and you want to ask politely about the opening hours of the library.
b2-02-05.prompt: Greet the person and politely ask about the opening hours.
cues: Greet the person
Say politely that you came to ask about the opening hours
b2-02-05.target: Buenas tardes, venía a preguntar por el horario de la biblioteca.
b2-02-05.english: Good afternoon, I came to ask about the opening hours of the library.
b2-02-05.canDo: I can make a polite request now with quería, venía a and llamaba para.

b2-02-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Telling a Short Story
b2-02-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you read about the Mexican writer Juan Rulfo. You tell him that Rulfo wrote a famous novel and that he had published very little when he died.
b2-02-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos what you read about Rulfo.
cues: Say what Rulfo wrote
Say how much he had published when he died
b2-02-consolidation.target: Rulfo escribió una novela famosa y, cuando murió, había publicado muy poco.
b2-02-consolidation.english: Rulfo wrote a famous novel and, when he died, he had published very little.
b2-02-consolidation.canDo: I can tell a short story in the past with the events, the scene and what had happened before in the right tenses.

b2-mexiconorte-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Up into the Sierra
b2-mexiconorte-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are planning a trip to the Barrancas del Cobre and reading about the region in Budapest.
b2-mexiconorte-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what happens to the climate as you go up into the mountains.
cues: Use a connector for a gradual change
Say that the climate changes
b2-mexiconorte-01.target: Conforme se sube a la sierra, el clima cambia.
b2-mexiconorte-01.english: As you go up into the mountains, the climate changes.
b2-mexiconorte-01.canDo: I can use conforme to say that something changes little by little, as in Conforme se sube a la sierra, el clima cambia.

b2-mexiconorte-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Vaqueros' Day
b2-mexiconorte-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You are telling Meg what you read in an article about vaqueros in northern Mexico.
b2-mexiconorte-02.prompt: Tell Meg that the days of work were hard, with the quality first.
cues: Start with the quality
Say whose days of work they were
b2-mexiconorte-02.target: Duros eran los días de trabajo.
b2-mexiconorte-02.english: Hard were the days of work.
b2-mexiconorte-02.canDo: I can put a quality or a place first, as in Duros eran los días de trabajo, to stress it when I describe vaquero life.

b2-mexiconorte-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Water for Monterrey
b2-mexiconorte-03.scenario: You are Meg. You are preparing a talk in Budapest about Monterrey and its water problem, and Carlos asks what could help.
b2-mexiconorte-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what would happen if Monterrey could reuse more water.
cues: Start with a condition that is only imagined
Say that the pressure would be less
b2-mexiconorte-03.target: Si Monterrey pudiera reutilizar más agua, la presión sería menor.
b2-mexiconorte-03.english: If Monterrey could reuse more water, the pressure would be less.
b2-mexiconorte-03.canDo: I can use si + imperfect subjunctive + conditional to say what would happen if something were different in Monterrey.

b2-mexiconorte-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Corrido
b2-mexiconorte-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are watching a documentary about the Mexican border in Budapest, and a corrido is playing.
b2-mexiconorte-04.prompt: Tell Meg what a corrido is, with a relative clause.
cues: Say that it is a song
Say what is told in it
b2-mexiconorte-04.target: El corrido es una canción en la que se cuentan historias de migrantes.
b2-mexiconorte-04.english: The corrido is a song in which stories of migrants are told.
b2-mexiconorte-04.canDo: I can use a preposition + el que / la que / los que / las que to describe places, songs and people on the border.

b2-mexiconorte-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Made in the North
b2-mexiconorte-05.scenario: You are Meg. You are reading an article about the factories of northern Mexico, and Carlos asks what they make.
b2-mexiconorte-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what is made in the north.
cues: Use se and a plural verb
Name two kinds of product
b2-mexiconorte-05.target: En el norte se fabrican vehículos y aparatos electrónicos.
b2-mexiconorte-05.english: In the north vehicles and electronic devices are made.
b2-mexiconorte-05.canDo: I can use se + a third-person verb to say what is made, exported or agreed in the north, as in Se fabrican vehículos.

b2-mexiconorte-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The North and Its Water
b2-mexiconorte-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You are giving a short talk in Budapest about northern Mexico, and you reach the problem of water.
b2-mexiconorte-consolidation.prompt: Tell your listeners how the cities of the north are changing and what worries people.
cues: Use a connector for a gradual change
Mention the lack of water
b2-mexiconorte-consolidation.target: Conforme crecen las ciudades del norte, la falta de agua preocupa más.
b2-mexiconorte-consolidation.english: As the cities of the north grow, the lack of water causes more concern.
b2-mexiconorte-consolidation.canDo: I can recall the main facts about northern Mexico: the deserts and canyons, vaquero culture, Monterrey, the border and the factories.

b2-03-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Maybe She Is Late
b2-03-01.scenario: You are Carlos. You are waiting for Meg at a café. She is late and does not answer her phone, and you are not sure why.
b2-03-01.prompt: Tell the waiter two things that may have happened to Meg.
cues: Give one possible reason with a lo mejor
Give another possible reason with puede que
b2-03-01.target: A lo mejor se quedó dormida, o puede que esté en el autobús.
b2-03-01.english: Maybe she fell asleep, or she may be on the bus.
b2-03-01.canDo: I can use a lo mejor with the indicative and puede que with the subjunctive.

b2-03-02.title: Communicative Challenge: How Likely Is It?
b2-03-02.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks whether the bus will be late because of the rain. You think it is likely, but you are not sure.
b2-03-02.prompt: Tell Carlos how likely it is.
cues: Say that it is probable that the bus is late
Say that it is not certain
b2-03-02.target: Es probable que el autobús llegue tarde, pero no es seguro.
b2-03-02.english: It is probable that the bus will be late, but it is not certain.
b2-03-02.canDo: I can use es probable que and no es seguro que with the subjunctive, and es evidente que with the indicative.

b2-03-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Where Can He Be?
b2-03-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos has not answered your messages all evening. You think about what he is probably doing.
b2-03-03.prompt: Say what you think Carlos is doing.
cues: Guess what he is doing now
Guess what he has already done
b2-03-03.target: Carlos no contesta; estará trabajando o ya habrá salido de la oficina.
b2-03-03.english: Carlos is not answering; he is probably working, or he has probably left the office already.
b2-03-03.canDo: I can use the future to guess about the present, as in estará en casa.

b2-03-04.title: Communicative Challenge: What Time Was It?
b2-03-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what time it was when you got home last night. You do not remember exactly.
b2-03-04.prompt: Tell Meg what time you think it was.
cues: Say that you are not sure
Guess the time you got home
b2-03-04.target: No sé, serían las diez cuando llegué a casa.
b2-03-04.english: I don't know, it was probably about ten when I got home.
b2-03-04.canDo: I can use the conditional to guess about a moment in the past, as in serían las diez.

b2-03-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Rain or Sun?
b2-03-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what the weather will be like this weekend. You think it will rain, but the sun may come out.
b2-03-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what you think about the weekend.
cues: Say that it will most likely rain
Say that maybe the sun will come out
b2-03-05.target: Seguramente va a llover este fin de semana, pero a lo mejor sale el sol.
b2-03-05.english: It will most likely rain this weekend, but maybe the sun will come out.
b2-03-05.canDo: I can use seguramente, probablemente and sin duda to say how sure I am.

b2-03-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Why Did Nobody Act?
b2-03-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos have read a text about a novel in which a whole town knows that something terrible will happen, and nobody stops it. Carlos asks why you think nobody acted.
cues: Say what is probable
Add another possibility with quizás
b2-03-consolidation.target: Es probable que nadie lo creyera, y quizás tuvieran miedo.
b2-03-consolidation.english: It is probable that nobody believed it, and perhaps they were afraid.
b2-03-consolidation.canDo: I can say how sure I am about something in the present and in the past.

b2-mexicosur-01.title: Communicative Challenge: What Is a Cenote?
b2-mexicosur-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about the Yucatán peninsula, and he asks you what a cenote is.
b2-mexicosur-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what a cenote is.
cues: Say that a cenote is a natural well
Say that you can see the water that runs under the ground
b2-mexicosur-01.target: Un cenote es un pozo natural en el que se ve el agua que corre bajo la tierra.
b2-mexicosur-01.english: A cenote is a natural well in which you can see the water that runs under the ground.
b2-mexicosur-01.canDo: I can describe a place or a thing with a relative clause (*que*, *donde*, *en el que*).

b2-mexicosur-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Despite the School
b2-mexicosur-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You have read an article about the languages of Oaxaca and you tell Meg what it says about the 20th century.
b2-mexicosur-02.prompt: Tell Meg that families kept speaking their language even though the school taught in Spanish.
cues: Say that the school taught in Spanish
Say that many families kept speaking their language at home
b2-mexicosur-02.target: A pesar de que la escuela enseñaba en español, muchas familias siguieron hablando su lengua en casa.
b2-mexicosur-02.english: Although the school taught in Spanish, many families kept speaking their language at home.
b2-mexicosur-02.canDo: I can say that something continues in spite of a difficulty, with *a pesar de*, *a pesar de que* and *pese a*.

b2-mexicosur-03.title: Communicative Challenge: What Tequio Does
b2-mexicosur-03.scenario: You are Meg. You are preparing a short talk about community life in Oaxaca, and Carlos asks what tequio is for.
b2-mexicosur-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what is done through tequio.
cues: Say that roads are repaired
Say that schools are built
b2-mexicosur-03.target: Con el tequio se arreglan los caminos y se construyen escuelas.
b2-mexicosur-03.english: With tequio roads are repaired and schools are built.
b2-mexicosur-03.canDo: I can say what is done in a community, without saying who does it, with *se*.

b2-mexicosur-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Why the Caracoles?
b2-mexicosur-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You are reading about the Zapatistas and you explain to Meg why, according to the EZLN, the Caracoles were created.
b2-mexicosur-04.prompt: Tell Meg why the EZLN says it created the Caracoles.
cues: Say that the Caracoles were created in 2003
Say that, according to the EZLN, the communities were to decide about education and health
b2-mexicosur-04.target: Según el EZLN, crearon los Caracoles para que las comunidades decidieran cómo organizar la educación y la salud.
b2-mexicosur-04.english: According to the EZLN, they created the Caracoles so that the communities would decide how to organise education and health.
b2-mexicosur-04.canDo: I can say what someone did so that something would happen, with *para que* and the subjunctive.

b2-mexicosur-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Sides of the Train
b2-mexicosur-05.scenario: You are Meg. You are writing a short article about the Maya Train and you give both sides of the debate to Carlos.
b2-mexicosur-05.prompt: Tell Carlos that the train creates jobs but that some communities criticise it.
cues: Say that the train creates jobs
Say that some communities criticise it
b2-mexicosur-05.target: Aunque el tren crea empleos, algunas comunidades lo critican.
b2-mexicosur-05.english: Although the train creates jobs, some communities criticise it.
b2-mexicosur-05.canDo: I can concede a point and then give another with *aunque*, *sin embargo* and *no obstante*.

b2-mexicosur-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: What I Learned About the South
b2-mexicosur-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are planning a trip to southern Mexico and you tell her what you have learned about Oaxaca.
b2-mexicosur-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg two facts about Oaxaca and its communities.
cues: Say how many municipalities Oaxaca has
Say that in many of them the authorities are chosen in an assembly
b2-mexicosur-consolidation.target: Oaxaca tiene 570 municipios, y en más de cuatrocientos las autoridades se eligen en asamblea.
b2-mexicosur-consolidation.english: Oaxaca has 570 municipalities, and in more than four hundred the authorities are chosen in an assembly.
b2-mexicosur-consolidation.canDo: I can describe a cenote or a jungle with a relative clause.

b2-04-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Demanding and Forbidding
b2-04-01.scenario: You are Carlos. You work in an office in Budapest, and a colleague is making a lot of noise while you are trying to work. You tell the colleague what you demand.
b2-04-01.prompt: Tell your colleague what you demand and why.
cues: Say what you demand
Give a reason
b2-04-01.target: Exijo que bajes la música porque necesito trabajar.
b2-04-01.english: I demand that you turn the music down because I need to work.
b2-04-01.canDo: I can ask, tell or forbid others to do things with exigir que, ordenar que, prohibir que and permitir que.

b2-04-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Fair or Unfair
b2-04-02.scenario: You are Meg. You are a student in Budapest. Carlos tells you that the library will close on Saturdays, and you give him your opinion.
b2-04-02.prompt: Tell Carlos what you think of the decision and why.
cues: Say how you judge the decision
Give a reason
b2-04-02.target: Es inaceptable que cierren la biblioteca los sábados porque los estudiantes la necesitan.
b2-04-02.english: It is unacceptable that they close the library on Saturdays because the students need it.
b2-04-02.canDo: I can say what is fair, normal, reasonable or unacceptable with es injusto que, es lógico que and similar expressions.

b2-04-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Reacting to News
b2-04-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg tells you that she cannot come to dinner on Saturday, and you react to the news.
b2-04-03.prompt: Tell Meg how you feel about her news.
cues: Say you are sorry she cannot come
Say you are glad she told you
b2-04-03.target: Lamento que no puedas venir a la cena, pero me alegra que me lo digas.
b2-04-03.english: I am sorry that you cannot come to the dinner, but I am glad that you tell me.
b2-04-03.canDo: I can react to news with me alegra que, lamento que and me sorprende que.

b2-04-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Me or You?
b2-04-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you want to do on Saturday in Budapest and what you want him to do.
b2-04-04.prompt: Tell Carlos what you want to do and what you want him to do.
cues: Say what you want to do yourself
Say what you want Carlos to do
b2-04-04.target: Quiero ir al parque y quiero que vengas conmigo.
b2-04-04.english: I want to go to the park and I want you to come with me.
b2-04-04.canDo: I can choose between an infinitive and que + subjunctive by asking who does the second action.

b2-04-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Polite Notice
b2-04-05.scenario: You are Carlos. Visitors are coming to your office in Budapest tomorrow, and you write a polite notice for them.
b2-04-05.prompt: Recommend to the visitors what to do.
cues: Recommend that they arrive early
Soften a second recommendation
b2-04-05.target: Se recomienda que los visitantes lleguen temprano y sería conveniente que trajeran agua.
b2-04-05.english: Visitors are advised to arrive early, and it would be a good idea for them to bring water.
b2-04-05.canDo: I can recommend politely with se recomienda que and se sugiere que.

b2-04-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Advice About a Novel
b2-04-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. A friend in Budapest is going to read La muerte de Artemio Cruz and asks you for advice.
b2-04-consolidation.prompt: Tell your friend how to read the novel.
cues: Recommend how to read it
Say what is important
b2-04-consolidation.target: Te recomiendo que leas la novela con calma y es importante que pongas atención a las voces.
b2-04-consolidation.english: I recommend that you read the novel calmly, and it is important that you pay attention to the voices.
b2-04-consolidation.canDo: I can ask, advise or recommend that someone do something with que + subjunctive.

b2-guatemala-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Built Temple I?
b2-guatemala-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about Tikal, and he asks you what you learned about Temple I.
b2-guatemala-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what was built over the ruler's tomb.
cues: Say that a temple was built
Say that it was built over a ruler's tomb
b2-guatemala-01.target: El Templo I fue levantado sobre la tumba de un gobernante.
b2-guatemala-01.english: Temple I was built over a ruler's tomb.
b2-guatemala-01.canDo: I can say who built or did something with *ser* + participle + *por*.

b2-guatemala-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Twins of the Popol Vuh
b2-guatemala-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You have read about the Popol Vuh and you tell Meg what happened to the twins.
b2-guatemala-02.prompt: Tell Meg what the twins did after defeating the lords of Xibalbá.
cues: Say that the twins defeated the lords of Xibalbá
Say that afterwards they went up to the sky
b2-guatemala-02.target: Después de vencer a los señores de Xibalbá, los gemelos subieron al cielo.
b2-guatemala-02.english: After defeating the lords of Xibalbá, the twins went up to the sky.
b2-guatemala-02.canDo: I can say what came first and what came next with *antes de* and *después de* + infinitive.

b2-guatemala-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Thick Walls in Antigua
b2-guatemala-03.scenario: You are Meg. You are planning a trip to Antigua with Carlos and you tell him what you read about its churches.
b2-guatemala-03.prompt: Tell Carlos that the churches had thick walls but were still damaged.
cues: Say that the walls were very thick
Say that many buildings were damaged anyway
b2-guatemala-03.target: A pesar de que los muros eran muy gruesos, muchos edificios sufrieron daños.
b2-guatemala-03.english: Although the walls were very thick, many buildings suffered damage.
b2-guatemala-03.canDo: I can say that something happened in spite of a difficulty, with *a pesar de que* and *pese a*.

b2-guatemala-04.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Commission Said
b2-guatemala-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You are reading about the armed conflict in Guatemala and you tell Meg what the Commission for Historical Clarification said.
b2-guatemala-04.prompt: Tell Meg what the CEH said about the number of dead and disappeared.
cues: Say that the commission said something
Say how many people had died or disappeared, according to the CEH
b2-guatemala-04.target: La comisión dijo que unas doscientas mil personas habían muerto o desaparecido.
b2-guatemala-04.english: The commission said that about two hundred thousand people had died or disappeared.
b2-guatemala-04.canDo: I can report what someone said, with *dijo que* and the verb moved back in time.

b2-guatemala-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Serves the Cantones?
b2-guatemala-05.scenario: You are Meg. You are writing a short article about the 48 Cantones of Totonicapán and you tell Carlos what their representatives say.
b2-guatemala-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what the representatives say about their authorities and their salary.
cues: Say that you are citing the representatives
Say that the authorities serve without a salary
b2-guatemala-05.target: Según sus representantes, las autoridades de los cantones sirven sin recibir un sueldo.
b2-guatemala-05.english: According to their representatives, the authorities of the cantons serve without receiving a salary.
b2-guatemala-05.canDo: I can say who does or grows something with *ser* + participle + *por*.

b2-guatemala-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Found Tikal?
b2-guatemala-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are planning a trip to Guatemala, and she asks you how Tikal became known after the jungle covered it.
b2-guatemala-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg when and by whom Tikal was explored.
cues: Say that the city was explored
Say who explored it and when
b2-guatemala-consolidation.target: Tikal fue explorada por expediciones a mediados del siglo diecinueve.
b2-guatemala-consolidation.english: Tikal was explored by expeditions in the mid-nineteenth century.
b2-guatemala-consolidation.canDo: I can say who built or explored a monument with the passive with *ser*.

b2-05-01.title: Communicative Challenge: I Do Not Think So
b2-05-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos says that his plan for the weekend is a good idea. You do not agree, and you think it is better to wait.
b2-05-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what you think of his plan.
cues: Say that you do not think it is a good idea
Say that you think it is better to wait
b2-05-01.target: No creo que sea una buena idea; creo que es mejor esperar.
b2-05-01.english: I don't think it is a good idea; I think it is better to wait.
b2-05-01.canDo: I can use no creo que and no me parece que with the subjunctive.

b2-05-02.title: Communicative Challenge: I Doubt It
b2-05-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg says that the bus is always on time. You doubt it, but you do not doubt that it is cheap.
cues: Say that you doubt that it is always on time
Say that you do not doubt that it is cheap
b2-05-02.target: Dudo que llegue siempre a la hora, pero no dudo que es barato.
b2-05-02.english: I doubt that it is always on time, but I do not doubt that it is cheap.
b2-05-02.canDo: I can use dudo que and niego que with the subjunctive.

b2-05-03.title: Communicative Challenge: It Is Not That, It Is This
b2-05-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks why you do not want to go out tonight. You are not angry with him: you are tired.
cues: Say that you are not angry
Say that the real reason is that you are very tired
b2-05-03.target: No es que esté enojada, sino que estoy muy cansada.
b2-05-03.english: It is not that I am angry, it is that I am very tired.
b2-05-03.canDo: I can reject a reason with no es que and the subjunctive.

b2-05-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Maybe, But…
b2-05-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg says that a new schedule at your office will solve every problem. You think she may be right, but you do not think it will be that simple.
cues: Say that she may be right
Say that you do not think it is that simple
b2-05-04.target: Puede ser que tengas razón, pero no creo que sea tan simple.
b2-05-04.english: You may be right, but I do not think it is that simple.
b2-05-04.canDo: I can hedge an opinion with puede ser que and es posible que.

b2-05-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Disagreeing Politely
b2-05-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos says that you should accept a plan you are not sure about. You want to disagree politely.
cues: Say that you understand his point of view
Say that you would not call it the best option
b2-05-05.target: Entiendo tu punto de vista, pero no diría que sea la mejor opción.
b2-05-05.english: I understand your point of view, but I wouldn't say it is the best option.
b2-05-05.canDo: I can disagree politely by granting a point and then stating my doubt.

b2-05-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Reading a Book Critically
b2-05-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos have read a text about a book of essays on Mexican identity. Carlos says that the book describes all Mexicans. You do not agree.
b2-05-consolidation.prompt: Give Carlos your opinion of the book.
cues: Say that you do not think a book describes all Mexicans
Say that it is possible that it has interesting ideas
b2-05-consolidation.target: No creo que un libro describa a todos los mexicanos, pero es posible que tenga ideas interesantes.
b2-05-consolidation.english: I don't think a book describes all Mexicans, but it is possible that it has interesting ideas.
b2-05-consolidation.canDo: I can say that I do not think, doubt or deny something, with the right mood.

b2-salvadorhonduras-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Whose Stelae?
b2-salvadorhonduras-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about Copán, and he asks you what makes the city special.
b2-salvadorhonduras-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what Copán is famous for.
cues: Say that Copán is a Maya city
Say whose stelae are famous
b2-salvadorhonduras-01.target: Copán es una ciudad maya cuyas estelas son famosas.
b2-salvadorhonduras-01.english: Copán is a Maya city whose stelae are famous.
b2-salvadorhonduras-01.canDo: I can say whose monuments or coasts I am talking about, with *cuyo*, *cuya*, *cuyos* and *cuyas*.

b2-salvadorhonduras-02.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Workers Said
b2-salvadorhonduras-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading an article about northern Honduras, and she asks you about the banana strike of 1954.
b2-salvadorhonduras-02.prompt: Tell Meg what the workers said and how long the strike lasted, naming the source.
cues: Say what the workers said they wanted
Say how long the strike lasted, according to historians
b2-salvadorhonduras-02.target: Los trabajadores dijeron que querían mejores salarios. Según los historiadores, la huelga duró más de dos meses.
b2-salvadorhonduras-02.english: The workers said they wanted better wages. According to historians, the strike lasted more than two months.
b2-salvadorhonduras-02.canDo: I can report what people said, with *dijo que* and the right past tense.

b2-salvadorhonduras-03.title: Communicative Challenge: A Quiet Bishop?
b2-salvadorhonduras-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are listening to a talk about El Salvador, and he asks you about Archbishop Romero.
b2-salvadorhonduras-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what people expected of Romero and what he did.
cues: Say what many people expected
Show the contrast with what Romero did
b2-salvadorhonduras-03.target: Muchos esperaban un obispo tranquilo; sin embargo, Romero habló por las víctimas.
b2-salvadorhonduras-03.english: Many expected a quiet bishop; however, Romero spoke for the victims.
b2-salvadorhonduras-03.canDo: I can show a contrast between two facts, with *sin embargo* and *no obstante*.

b2-salvadorhonduras-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Why They Left
b2-salvadorhonduras-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading an article about migration from Honduras, and she asks you why so many people left in 1998.
b2-salvadorhonduras-04.prompt: Tell Meg why many Hondurans emigrated.
cues: Give the cause
Say what the cause destroyed
b2-salvadorhonduras-04.target: A raíz del huracán Mitch, muchas familias perdieron sus casas y sus cosechas.
b2-salvadorhonduras-04.english: As a result of Hurricane Mitch, many families lost their houses and their harvests.
b2-salvadorhonduras-04.canDo: I can give a cause with *debido a* and *a raíz de* and a noun.

b2-salvadorhonduras-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Dated Fact
b2-salvadorhonduras-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are following the news about Honduras, and he asks you about the 2025 election.
b2-salvadorhonduras-05.prompt: Tell Carlos who was declared the winner and when.
cues: Say who was declared the winner
Say the date
b2-salvadorhonduras-05.target: Nasry Asfura fue declarado ganador el 24 de diciembre de 2025.
b2-salvadorhonduras-05.english: Nasry Asfura was declared the winner on 24 December 2025.
b2-salvadorhonduras-05.canDo: I can say what was approved, declared or announced, with *ser* + past participle.

b2-salvadorhonduras-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Review: El Salvador and Honduras
b2-salvadorhonduras-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are planning a trip to Honduras, and she asks what you remember about Copán and the war in El Salvador.
b2-salvadorhonduras-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg one fact about each.
cues: Say whose stelae are famous in Copán
Say how long the war in El Salvador lasted, with a contrast
b2-salvadorhonduras-consolidation.target: Copán es una ciudad cuyas estelas son famosas. La guerra duró doce años; sin embargo, en 1992 se firmó la paz.
b2-salvadorhonduras-consolidation.english: Copán is a city whose stelae are famous. The war lasted twelve years; however, peace was signed in 1992.
b2-salvadorhonduras-consolidation.canDo: I can say whose monuments or coasts I mean, with *cuyo*.

b2-06-01.title: Communicative Challenge: What Bothers You
b2-06-01.scenario: You are Carlos. You work in an office in Budapest, and a friend asks what bothers and worries you at work.
b2-06-01.prompt: Tell your friend what bothers you and what worries you.
cues: Say what bothers you
Say what worries you
b2-06-01.target: Me molesta que haya tanto ruido y me preocupa no terminar el informe a tiempo.
b2-06-01.english: It bothers me that there is so much noise, and I am worried about not finishing the report on time.
b2-06-01.canDo: I can say what bothers, worries or delights me with me molesta que, me preocupa que and me encanta que.

b2-06-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Sorry and Afraid
b2-06-02.scenario: You are Meg, a student in Budapest. Carlos tells you that he has to work this weekend, and you answer with sympathy.
b2-06-02.prompt: Tell Carlos that you are sorry and say what you fear.
cues: Say you are sorry about his news
Say what you are afraid of
b2-06-02.target: Siento que tengas que trabajar este fin de semana y temo que estés muy cansado.
b2-06-02.english: I'm sorry that you have to work this weekend and I'm afraid that you will be very tired.
b2-06-02.canDo: I can say that I am sorry or afraid about what others do with siento que, lamento que and temo que.

b2-06-03.title: Communicative Challenge: What a Shame!
b2-06-03.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague tells you that the cinema in your neighbourhood in Budapest is going to close.
b2-06-03.prompt: React to the news with exclamations.
cues: React with an outrage exclamation
Add a short exclamation about the shame
b2-06-03.target: ¡Qué barbaridad que cierren el cine del barrio! ¡Qué pena!
b2-06-03.english: How outrageous that they are closing the neighbourhood cinema! What a shame!
b2-06-03.canDo: I can react to news with ¡Qué pena que...!, ¡Qué bien que...! and ¡Qué bueno que...!

b2-06-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Fact That
b2-06-04.scenario: You are Carlos. A friend is often late when you meet in Budapest, and you tell Meg how that affects you.
b2-06-04.prompt: Tell Meg how you feel about it, starting with the fact.
cues: Start with the fact that your friend arrives late
Say how it makes you feel
b2-06-04.target: El hecho de que mi amigo llegue tarde me molesta.
b2-06-04.english: The fact that my friend arrives late bothers me.
b2-06-04.canDo: I can start a sentence with el hecho de que + subjunctive and then comment on the fact.

b2-06-05.title: Communicative Challenge: News and Problems
b2-06-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you think about a news story on unemployment.
b2-06-05.prompt: Give the fact first and then your reaction.
cues: Say that there is a lot of unemployment
Say what worries you about it
b2-06-05.target: Hay mucho desempleo y me preocupa que no haya más ayuda para las familias.
b2-06-05.english: There is a lot of unemployment and it worries me that there is no more help for families.
b2-06-05.canDo: I can talk about news and social problems by giving the fact first and my reaction second.

b2-06-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Banned Books
b2-06-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what you think about countries that ban books.
b2-06-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what worries you and what you regret.
cues: Say what worries you
Say what you regret
b2-06-consolidation.target: Me preocupa que prohíban libros y lamento que mucha gente no pueda leerlos.
b2-06-consolidation.english: It worries me that they ban books and I regret that many people cannot read them.
b2-06-consolidation.canDo: I can say what bothers or worries me, and that I am sorry or afraid, with que + subjunctive.

b2-nicaragua-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Why an Eight?
b2-nicaragua-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are planning a trip to Nicaragua, and he asks you why the island of Ometepe looks so strange on the map.
b2-nicaragua-01.prompt: Tell Carlos why Ometepe is shaped like an eight.
cues: Say what shape the island has
Give the reason
b2-nicaragua-01.target: Ometepe tiene forma de ocho porque la forman dos volcanes.
b2-nicaragua-01.english: Ometepe is shaped like an eight because two volcanoes form it.
b2-nicaragua-01.canDo: I can give a reason with *porque* and a result with *por eso*.

b2-nicaragua-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Where Darío Died
b2-nicaragua-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are listening to a talk about Rubén Darío, and she asks you where and when he died.
b2-nicaragua-02.prompt: Tell Meg where and when Darío died, putting the place first.
cues: Start with the place
Say who died and when
b2-nicaragua-02.target: En León murió Rubén Darío, en febrero de 1916.
b2-nicaragua-02.english: In León Rubén Darío died, in February 1916.
b2-nicaragua-02.canDo: I can put an adjective, a place or a time first to stress it, as in *Decisiva fue…*.

b2-nicaragua-03.title: Communicative Challenge: What If?
b2-nicaragua-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about Sandino, and he asks you what you think about the pact of Tipitapa.
b2-nicaragua-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what would have happened if Sandino had accepted the pact.
cues: Start with the condition
Say what he would not have done
b2-nicaragua-03.target: Si Sandino hubiera aceptado el pacto, no habría luchado en las montañas.
