b2-nicaragua-03.english: If Sandino had accepted the pact, he would not have fought in the mountains.
b2-nicaragua-03.canDo: I can say what would have happened if something had been different, with *si hubiera… habría…*.

b2-nicaragua-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Painters in Spite of Everything
b2-nicaragua-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading an article about Solentiname, and she asks you why the paintings are special.
b2-nicaragua-04.prompt: Tell Meg what the peasants of Solentiname did in spite of their situation.
cues: Say what they were not
Say what they began to do
b2-nicaragua-04.target: A pesar de no tener estudios de arte, los campesinos de Solentiname empezaron a pintar.
b2-nicaragua-04.english: Although they had no art training, the peasants of Solentiname began to paint.
b2-nicaragua-04.canDo: I can say that something continued in spite of a difficulty, with *a pesar de* and *pese a*.

b2-nicaragua-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Says What
b2-nicaragua-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading the news about Nicaragua, and he asks you what is known about the 2018 protests.
b2-nicaragua-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what the UN said and what the government said, naming each source.
cues: Give the UN source and a number
Say what the government said
b2-nicaragua-05.target: Según la CIDH, murieron más de trescientas personas. El gobierno dijo que las protestas eran un intento de golpe de Estado.
b2-nicaragua-05.english: According to the IACHR, more than three hundred people died. The government said the protests were a coup attempt.
b2-nicaragua-05.canDo: I can say who said what, with *según* and *dijo que*.

b2-nicaragua-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Review: Nicaragua
b2-nicaragua-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are planning a trip to Nicaragua, and she asks what you remember about the lake and about Darío.
b2-nicaragua-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg one fact about each.
cues: Say why the lake has waves
Say where Darío died, putting the place first
b2-nicaragua-consolidation.target: El lago es muy grande; por eso a veces tiene olas. En León murió Rubén Darío.
b2-nicaragua-consolidation.english: The lake is very big; that is why it sometimes has waves. In León Rubén Darío died.
b2-nicaragua-consolidation.canDo: I can give a reason with *porque* and a result with *por eso* (review).

b2-07-01.title: Communicative Challenge: As Soon As
b2-07-01.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks when you will send her the report from your office in Budapest. You will send it right after you finish it.
b2-07-01.prompt: Tell Meg when you will send the report.
cues: Say that you will send it to her
Say that you will do it as soon as you finish it
b2-07-01.target: Te lo mando en cuanto lo termine.
b2-07-01.english: I'll send it to you as soon as I finish it.
b2-07-01.canDo: I can say what I will do as soon as something happens, using en cuanto, tan pronto como and apenas with the present subjunctive.

b2-07-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Waiting Until
b2-07-02.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are going to meet in Budapest, and he says he will be late. You tell him how long you will wait.
b2-07-02.prompt: Tell Carlos how long you will wait for him.
cues: Say that you will wait for him here
Say that you will wait until he arrives
b2-07-02.target: Te espero aquí hasta que llegues.
b2-07-02.english: I'll wait for you here until you arrive.
b2-07-02.canDo: I can say how long I will wait or when I will stop, using hasta que with the present subjunctive.

b2-07-03.title: Communicative Challenge: As Long As
b2-07-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks if she can use your bicycle. You agree, on one condition.
b2-07-03.prompt: Tell Meg she can use your bicycle, with your condition.
cues: Say that she can use your bicycle
Say that it is fine as long as she looks after it
b2-07-03.target: Puedes usar mi bicicleta mientras la cuides.
b2-07-03.english: You can use my bicycle as long as you look after it.
b2-07-03.canDo: I can use mientras with the subjunctive to say "as long as", for a duration or a condition.

b2-07-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Whenever It Rains
b2-07-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you do when it rains in Budapest. You stay at home every time it rains.
b2-07-04.prompt: Tell Carlos what you do whenever it rains.
cues: Say that it happens every time it rains
Say that you stay at home
b2-07-04.target: Siempre que llueve, me quedo en casa.
b2-07-04.english: Whenever it rains, I stay at home.
b2-07-04.canDo: I can tell siempre que "whenever" with the indicative from siempre que "provided that" with the subjunctive.

b2-07-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Before You Go
b2-07-05.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg is about to go out, and you want her to phone you first.
b2-07-05.prompt: Ask Meg to phone you before she goes out.
cues: Ask her to phone you
Say that she should do it before she leaves
b2-07-05.canDo: I can use antes de que with the subjunctive and después de que with the indicative for facts or the subjunctive for the future.

b2-07-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Working Until It Is Done
b2-07-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks how long you will keep working at the office today. You will stay until you finish the report.
b2-07-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg how long you will keep working.
cues: Say that you will keep working
Say that you will stop when you finish the report
b2-07-consolidation.target: Voy a seguir trabajando hasta que termine el informe.
b2-07-consolidation.english: I'm going to keep working until I finish the report.
b2-07-consolidation.canDo: I can talk about the future with en cuanto, tan pronto como, hasta que and mientras + the present subjunctive.

b2-costarica-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Where Turtles Lay Eggs
b2-costarica-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are planning a trip to Costa Rica, and he asks you where the green turtles lay their eggs.
b2-costarica-01.prompt: Tell Carlos where the turtles lay their eggs, putting the place in the spotlight.
cues: Start with the place
Say what the turtles do there
b2-costarica-01.target: Es en Tortuguero, en la costa del Caribe, donde desovan las tortugas verdes.
b2-costarica-01.english: It is in Tortuguero, on the Caribbean coast, that the green turtles lay their eggs.
b2-costarica-01.canDo: I can put a place, a time or an idea in the spotlight with *Fue… donde / cuando* and *Lo que… es…*.

b2-costarica-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A Country Without an Army
b2-costarica-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are watching a documentary about Costa Rica, and she asks you if the country has no security at all.
b2-costarica-02.prompt: Correct her idea and say who provides security.
cues: Reject the wrong reason
Give the true one
b2-costarica-02.target: No es que Costa Rica no tenga seguridad, sino que no tiene ejército.
b2-costarica-02.english: It isn't that Costa Rica has no security; it's that it has no army.
b2-costarica-02.canDo: I can correct a reason with *No es que… sino que…*.

b2-costarica-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Fact That
b2-costarica-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading an article about the CCSS, and he asks you what challenge the health system has.
b2-costarica-03.prompt: Comment on the fact that the population is getting older.
cues: Start with the known fact
Say what it creates
b2-costarica-03.target: El hecho de que la población envejezca crea nuevos retos para la CCSS.
b2-costarica-03.english: The fact that the population is getting older creates new challenges for the CCSS.
b2-costarica-03.canDo: I can comment on a known fact with *el hecho de que* + subjunctive.

b2-costarica-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Before the Visitors Arrive
b2-costarica-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are planning a visit to a national park, and she asks what the guides do before the groups come.
b2-costarica-04.prompt: Tell Meg what the guides do and when.
cues: Say what the guides check
Say that they do it before the visitors arrive
b2-costarica-04.target: Los guías revisan los senderos antes de que lleguen los visitantes.
b2-costarica-04.english: The guides check the trails before the visitors arrive.
b2-costarica-04.canDo: I can say what happened before or after someone else's action, with *antes de que* and *después de que*.

b2-costarica-05.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Unions Want
b2-costarica-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading a report about pineapple farms in Costa Rica, and he asks you what the unions want.
b2-costarica-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what the unions want from the companies.
cues: Say who wants something
Say what the companies should do
b2-costarica-05.target: Los sindicatos quieren que las empresas paguen el salario mínimo.
b2-costarica-05.english: The unions want the companies to pay the minimum wage.
b2-costarica-05.canDo: I can choose between an infinitive and *que* + subjunctive, depending on who does the second action.

b2-costarica-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Review: Costa Rica
b2-costarica-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are planning a trip to Costa Rica, and she asks what you remember about the country.
b2-costarica-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg one fact about nature and one about the army.
cues: Put what surprises you in the spotlight
Correct the idea that the country has no police
b2-costarica-consolidation.target: Lo que más sorprende en Costa Rica es la variedad de especies. No es que no tenga policía, sino que no tiene ejército.
b2-costarica-consolidation.english: What surprises most in Costa Rica is the variety of species. It is not that it has no police, but that it has no army.
b2-costarica-consolidation.canDo: I can put a place, a time or an idea in the spotlight with *Fue… donde* and *Lo que… es…*.

b2-08-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Even If It Rains
b2-08-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos says it may rain on Saturday in Budapest. You will go out anyway.
b2-08-01.prompt: Tell Carlos you will go out even if it rains.
cues: Say that you will go out
Say that you will go even if it rains
b2-08-01.target: Aunque llueva el sábado, voy a salir.
b2-08-01.english: Even if it rains on Saturday, I'm going to go out.
b2-08-01.canDo: I can use aunque with the indicative for a fact and with the subjunctive for a possibility or a point I grant.

b2-08-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Granting a Point
b2-08-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what you think of a proposal at your office. It is expensive, but it has advantages.
b2-08-02.prompt: Tell Meg what you think of the proposal, in a formal way.
cues: Grant that the proposal is expensive
Say that it has advantages
b2-08-02.target: Si bien la propuesta es cara, tiene muchas ventajas.
b2-08-02.english: Although the proposal is expensive, it has many advantages.
b2-08-02.canDo: I can grant a true point formally with si bien and the indicative.

b2-08-03.title: Communicative Challenge: No Matter How Much
b2-08-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos keeps asking you to change your mind about something. You will not change it.
b2-08-03.prompt: Tell Carlos that his insisting will not change your mind.
cues: Say that he can insist as much as he wants
Say that you will not change your mind
b2-08-03.target: Por más que insistas, no voy a cambiar de idea.
b2-08-03.english: However much you insist, I'm not going to change my mind.
b2-08-03.canDo: I can say that no amount of effort changes the result, using por más que and por mucho que with the subjunctive.

b2-08-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Even When It Is Difficult
b2-08-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks if you will tell your colleagues the truth about a problem. It will be difficult, but you will do it.
b2-08-04.prompt: Tell Meg that you will tell the truth, even if it is difficult.
cues: Say that you are going to tell the truth
Say that you will do it even if it is difficult
b2-08-04.target: Aun cuando sea difícil, voy a decirles la verdad.
b2-08-04.english: Even if it is difficult, I am going to tell them the truth.
b2-08-04.canDo: I can use aun cuando with the subjunctive for a possibility and with the indicative for a fact.

b2-08-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Whatever Happens
b2-08-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos is worried about a project at his office. You promise to support him.
b2-08-05.prompt: Tell Carlos that you will support him whatever happens.
cues: Say that you will support him
Say that it does not matter what happens
b2-08-05.target: Pase lo que pase, te voy a apoyar.
b2-08-05.english: Whatever happens, I'm going to support you.
b2-08-05.canDo: I can say that nothing changes my decision with formulas such as pase lo que pase and diga lo que diga.

b2-08-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Keeping Your Position
b2-08-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks if you will finish the report today. You have a lot of work, but you will finish it.
b2-08-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg that you will finish the report today in spite of the work.
cues: Say that you have a lot of work
Say that you will finish the report today anyway
b2-08-consolidation.target: Aunque tengo mucho trabajo, voy a terminar el informe hoy.
b2-08-consolidation.english: Although I have a lot of work, I'm going to finish the report today.
b2-08-consolidation.canDo: I can concede a point and keep my position with aunque, si bien, por más que and aun cuando.

b2-panama-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Jungle Without a Road
b2-panama-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about the Darién, and he asks what you learned about the Pan-American Highway.
b2-panama-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what happens to the highway in the Darién.
cues: Say that the highway runs along almost the whole continent
Say that it stops in the Darién
b2-panama-01.target: La Carretera Panamericana, que recorre casi todo el continente, se interrumpe en el Darién.
b2-panama-01.english: The Pan-American Highway, which runs along almost the whole continent, stops in the Darién.
b2-panama-01.canDo: I can describe the isthmus and the Darién with relative clauses (*que*, *quien*).

b2-panama-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Before the Canal
b2-panama-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading an article about the Panama Canal, and she asks you how ships travelled before it existed.
b2-panama-02.prompt: Tell Meg what ships had to do before the canal existed.
cues: Say what ships had to do
Say that this was before the canal existed
b2-panama-02.target: Antes de que existiera el canal, los barcos tenían que rodear América del Sur.
b2-panama-02.english: Before the canal existed, ships had to sail round South America.
b2-panama-02.canDo: I can say what happened before or after an event in the history of the canal, with *antes de que* and *después de que*.

b2-panama-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Essential but Paid Less
b2-panama-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are listening to a talk about the Afro-Antillean workers of the canal, and he asks you what struck you most.
b2-panama-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what you noticed about the workers on the silver list.
cues: Say that their work was essential
Say that they were paid less
b2-panama-03.target: Si bien su trabajo era esencial, los trabajadores de la lista de plata cobraban menos.
b2-panama-03.english: Although their work was essential, the workers on the silver list were paid less.
b2-panama-03.canDo: I can grant a point in a formal sentence with *si bien* and the indicative.

b2-panama-04.title: Communicative Challenge: What Is Sold in Colón
b2-panama-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading an article about Panama's economy, and she asks what the Colón Free Zone is for.
b2-panama-04.prompt: Tell Meg what happens to goods in the Colón Free Zone.
cues: Say that goods are sold there
Say that they are later re-exported
b2-panama-04.target: En la Zona Libre de Colón se venden mercancías que luego se reexportan a otros países.
b2-panama-04.english: In the Colón Free Zone goods are sold which are later re-exported to other countries.
b2-panama-04.canDo: I can say what is sold, used or published in Panama with the *se* passive.

b2-panama-05.title: Communicative Challenge: However Much the Sea Rises
b2-panama-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a report about Gardi Sugdub, and he asks what the scientists say about the sea.
b2-panama-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what will happen to the sea level, whatever happens to emissions.
cues: Say however much emissions fall
Say that the sea level will keep rising
b2-panama-05.target: Por más que bajen las emisiones, el nivel del mar seguirá subiendo.
b2-panama-05.english: However much emissions fall, the sea level will keep rising.
b2-panama-05.canDo: I can say that nothing changes however much something happens, with *por más que* and *por mucho que*.

b2-panama-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Panama in Review
b2-panama-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing a short talk about Panama, and you want to give her one example of what you will say about the canal.
b2-panama-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what the canal does and who has had it since 1999.
cues: Say that the canal joins two oceans
Say that it has been in Panama's hands since 1999
b2-panama-consolidation.target: El canal, que une dos océanos, está en manos de Panamá desde 1999.
b2-panama-consolidation.english: The canal, which joins two oceans, has been in Panama's hands since 1999.
b2-panama-consolidation.canDo: I can describe a place or a person with *que* and *quien*.

b2-09-01.title: Communicative Challenge: If I Could Choose
b2-09-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks where you would live if you could choose anywhere. You imagine a place near a park in Budapest.
b2-09-01.prompt: Tell Carlos where you would live if you could choose, and what you would do there.
cues: Imagine where you would live if you could choose
Say one thing you would do there
b2-09-01.target: Si pudiera elegir, viviría cerca de un parque y saldría a caminar todos los días.
b2-09-01.english: If I could choose, I would live near a park and go for a walk every day.
b2-09-01.canDo: I can use si with the imperfect subjunctive and the conditional to imagine an unlikely situation.

b2-09-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A Polite Booking
b2-09-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You are at the office and ring the front desk, because you need a meeting room for tomorrow morning.
b2-09-02.prompt: Politely ask the front desk for a meeting room for tomorrow.
cues: Say politely that you would like to book a room
Say which kind of room and for when
b2-09-02.target: Quisiera reservar una sala de reuniones para mañana por la mañana.
b2-09-02.english: I would like to book a meeting room for tomorrow morning.
b2-09-02.canDo: I can use quisiera, pudiera and debiera as softer forms of querría, podría and debería.

b2-09-03.title: Communicative Challenge: If You Would Be So Kind
b2-09-03.scenario: You are Meg. You are at a ticket office in Budapest and need the clerk to explain how to buy a ticket from the machine.
b2-09-03.prompt: Ask the clerk very politely to explain how to buy a ticket.
cues: Use a polite formula to ask for help
Say what you would be grateful for
b2-09-03.target: Si fuera tan amable de ayudarme, le agradecería que me explicara cómo comprar un boleto.
b2-09-03.english: If you would be so kind as to help me, I would be grateful if you explained how to buy a ticket.
b2-09-03.canDo: I can make a polite request with si fuera tan amable de and le agradecería que.

b2-09-04.title: Communicative Challenge: On One Condition
b2-09-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Your manager offers you a position in another office. You would accept it, but only on one condition: working from home some days.
b2-09-04.prompt: Tell your manager that you accept the position, and on what condition.
cues: Say that you accept the position
Name your condition
b2-09-04.target: Acepto el puesto a condición de que me permitan trabajar desde casa algunos días.
b2-09-04.english: I accept the position on condition that they allow me to work from home some days.
b2-09-04.canDo: I can set a condition with siempre que, con tal de que and a condición de que.

b2-09-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Unless It Rains
b2-09-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos invites you to a walk in a park in Budapest on Saturday. You want to go, but the weather could stop you.
b2-09-05.prompt: Tell Carlos that you will go on Saturday, and name the one thing that could stop you.
cues: Say that you will go on Saturday
Name the one exception
b2-09-05.target: Iré al parque el sábado a no ser que llueva mucho.
b2-09-05.english: I will go to the park on Saturday unless it rains a lot.
b2-09-05.canDo: I can name the one exception that would change the outcome with a menos que, a no ser que and salvo que.

b2-09-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Different Job, On Terms
b2-09-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks whether you would change jobs. You would, but only if the new position left you free time.
b2-09-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what you would do and on what condition.
cues: Imagine changing jobs
Name the condition for the change
b2-09-consolidation.target: Si pudiera, cambiaría de trabajo, siempre que el nuevo puesto me dejara tiempo libre.
b2-09-consolidation.english: If I could, I would change jobs, provided that the new position left me free time.
b2-09-consolidation.canDo: I can imagine an unlikely present or future situation with si and the imperfect subjunctive.

b2-guyanas-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Deported to Roatán
b2-guyanas-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about Belize, and he asks what happened to the Garifuna in 1797.
b2-guyanas-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what the British did to the Garifuna.
cues: Say who was deported
Say who deported them and where to
b2-guyanas-01.target: Los garífunas fueron deportados por los británicos a la isla de Roatán.
b2-guyanas-01.english: The Garifuna were deported by the British to the island of Roatán.
b2-guyanas-01.canDo: I can say what was done, and by whom, with *ser* + past participle and *por*.

b2-guyanas-02.title: Communicative Challenge: What Makes Tepuis Special
b2-guyanas-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading an article about the Guiana Shield, and she asks you what makes the tepuis so special.
b2-guyanas-02.prompt: Tell Meg the one thing that makes the tepuis unique.
cues: Put the spotlight on what makes them unique
Say that it is their isolation
b2-guyanas-02.target: Lo que hace únicos a los tepuyes es su aislamiento.
b2-guyanas-02.english: What makes the tepuis unique is their isolation.
b2-guyanas-02.canDo: I can put one idea in the spotlight with *lo que ... es* and *es/fue ... donde*, *quien*, *cuando*.

b2-guyanas-03.title: Communicative Challenge: According to Historians
b2-guyanas-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are listening to a talk about Suriname, and he asks how the maroon communities began.
b2-guyanas-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what historians say about enslaved Africans and the plantations.
cues: Name the source
Say that thousands of enslaved Africans escaped
b2-guyanas-03.target: Según los historiadores, miles de africanos esclavizados huyeron de las plantaciones.
b2-guyanas-03.english: According to historians, thousands of enslaved Africans escaped from the plantations.
b2-guyanas-03.canDo: I can report what a source says with *según*, *explicar que* and *informar de que*.

b2-guyanas-04.title: Communicative Challenge: If the Rockets Left from Europe
b2-guyanas-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are watching a documentary about the space centre at Kourou, and she asks why Europe launches rockets from French Guiana.
b2-guyanas-04.prompt: Tell Meg what would happen if the rockets left from Europe.
cues: Imagine the rockets leaving from Europe
Say that they would need more fuel
b2-guyanas-04.target: Si los cohetes salieran de Europa, necesitarían más combustible.
b2-guyanas-04.english: If the rockets left from Europe, they would need more fuel.
b2-guyanas-04.canDo: I can say what would happen in an imagined situation with *si* + imperfect subjunctive and the conditional.

b2-guyanas-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Even Though They Are Neighbours
b2-guyanas-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading an article about the bridge over the Takutu river, and he asks what is surprising about it.
b2-guyanas-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what was missing until 2009 between Brazil and Guyana.
cues: Say that they are neighbours
Say that there was no bridge until 2009
b2-guyanas-05.target: Aun cuando Brasil y Guyana son vecinos, hasta 2009 no hubo un puente sobre el río Takutu.
b2-guyanas-05.english: Even though Brazil and Guyana are neighbours, until 2009 there was no bridge over the Takutu river.
b2-guyanas-05.canDo: I can grant a point with *aun cuando* and the indicative for a fact, or the subjunctive for a possibility.

b2-guyanas-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Paramaribo, World Heritage
b2-guyanas-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing a short talk about Belize, Suriname and the Guianas, and you want to give her one example of what you will say about Paramaribo.
b2-guyanas-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg one fact about the centre of Paramaribo, with the passive.
cues: Say what the centre of Paramaribo was declared
Say in which year
b2-guyanas-consolidation.target: El centro de Paramaribo fue declarado Patrimonio de la Humanidad en 2002.
b2-guyanas-consolidation.english: The centre of Paramaribo was declared a World Heritage Site in 2002.
b2-guyanas-consolidation.canDo: I can say what was done, and by whom, with *ser* + past participle.

b2-10-01.title: Communicative Challenge: What Would Have Happened
b2-10-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks why you were late to meet him in Budapest. You missed the tram, and you say what would have happened if you had left earlier.
b2-10-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what would have happened if you had left earlier.
cues: Say what you would have done if you had left earlier
Say what would have happened
b2-10-01.target: Si hubiera salido más temprano, habría llegado a tiempo.
b2-10-01.english: If I had left earlier, I would have arrived on time.
b2-10-01.canDo: I can use si hubiera and habría with a past participle to say what would have happened.

b2-10-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Ways to Say It
b2-10-02.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague tells you that the time of the meeting changed, and nobody told you. You say what you would have done if you had known.
b2-10-02.prompt: Tell your colleague what you would have done if you had known.
cues: Say that you did not know
Say what you would have done, using hubiera in the result
b2-10-02.target: Si lo hubiera sabido, hubiera llegado más temprano a la reunión.
b2-10-02.english: If I had known, I would have arrived at the meeting earlier.
b2-10-02.canDo: I can use hubiera and a past participle in place of habría in the result clause of a past counterfactual.

b2-10-03.title: Communicative Challenge: I Should Have
b2-10-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks if you regret anything about a day you had in Budapest. You regret not having left earlier.
b2-10-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what you should have done and say that you regret it.
cues: Say what you should have done
Say that you regret it
b2-10-03.target: Debería haber salido más temprano y me arrepiento de no haberlo hecho.
b2-10-03.english: I should have left earlier, and I regret not having done so.
b2-10-03.canDo: I can say what I or someone else should have done with debería haber and tendría que haber.

b2-10-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Without Si
b2-10-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks if you will come to the meeting on Monday. You are not sure, because of the work you have.
b2-10-04.prompt: Tell Meg what you would do if you had time, without using si.
cues: Say what you would do
Give the condition without si, using de
b2-10-04.target: De tener tiempo, iría contigo, pero tengo mucho trabajo.
b2-10-04.english: If I had time, I would go with you, but I have a lot of work.
b2-10-04.canDo: I can say a condition without si with de and an infinitive, in the present and the past.

b2-10-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Even If
b2-10-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos missed the train in Budapest. Carlos says that you should have left earlier. You answer that it would not have mattered.
b2-10-05.prompt: Tell Carlos that even if you had left earlier, you would not have arrived in time.
cues: Say "even if" about the past
Say that you would not have arrived in time
b2-10-05.target: Aun cuando hubiéramos salido antes, no habríamos llegado a tiempo.
b2-10-05.english: Even if we had left earlier, we would not have arrived on time.
b2-10-05.canDo: I can drop si and begin a past counterfactual with hubiera and a past participle.

b2-10-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Looking Back
b2-10-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks if you would do anything differently about last week. You say what you would have done and what you regret.
b2-10-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what you would have done with more time, and what you regret.
cues: Say what you would have done with more time
Say what you regret
b2-10-consolidation.target: Si hubiera tenido más tiempo, habría ayudado más, y me arrepiento de no haberlo hecho.
b2-10-consolidation.english: If I had had more time, I would have helped more, and I regret not having done so.
b2-10-consolidation.canDo: I can say what would have happened with si hubiera and habría or hubiera and a past participle.

b2-cuba-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Unfortunately, Old Havana
b2-cuba-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about Old Havana, and he asks what you thought about the state of the buildings.
b2-cuba-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what the documentary said about the buildings, with your own reaction.
cues: Say that some buildings are in poor condition
Show that you think it is a pity
b2-cuba-01.target: Lamentablemente, algunos edificios de La Habana Vieja están en mal estado.
b2-cuba-01.english: Unfortunately, some buildings in Old Havana are in poor condition.
b2-cuba-01.canDo: I can show my attitude to a fact with stance adverbs such as *lamentablemente*, *francamente* and *en rigor*.

b2-cuba-02.title: Communicative Challenge: What Martí Wrote
b2-cuba-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading an article about José Martí, and she asks what he wanted for Cuba.
b2-cuba-02.prompt: Tell Meg what Martí wrote he wanted.
cues: Say who wrote it
Say that he wanted the independence of Cuba
b2-cuba-02.target: Martí escribió que quería la independencia de Cuba.
b2-cuba-02.english: Martí wrote that he wanted the independence of Cuba.
b2-cuba-02.canDo: I can report what someone said or wrote, shifting the tenses (*quería*, *había escrito*, *haría*).

b2-cuba-03.title: Communicative Challenge: If Necessary, They Stayed
b2-cuba-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about the literacy campaign of 1961, and he asks what the young teachers did when it got late.
b2-cuba-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what the volunteer teachers did if it was necessary.
cues: Start with a condition without si
Say that they stayed to sleep at the family's house
b2-cuba-03.target: De ser necesario, los brigadistas se quedaban a dormir en la casa de la familia.
b2-cuba-03.english: If necessary, the volunteer teachers stayed to sleep in the family's house.
b2-cuba-03.canDo: I can state a condition without *si*, with *de* + infinitive or the gerund.

b2-cuba-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Meeting a Troubadour
b2-cuba-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are listening to a talk about the Nueva Trova, and she asks whether you had heard that music before.
b2-cuba-04.prompt: Tell Meg when you first got to know the son, and what you did not know then.
cues: Say that you got to know the son
Say that you did not know where it was born
b2-cuba-04.target: Cuando conocí el son, no sabía que había nacido en el este de la isla.
b2-cuba-04.english: When I got to know the son, I did not know it had been born in the east of the island.
b2-cuba-04.canDo: I can tell the difference between *conocí* and *conocía*, *supe* and *sabía*, *quise* and *quería*, *pude* and *podía*.

b2-cuba-05.title: Communicative Challenge: However Much They Open Up
b2-cuba-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading an article about Cuba in the 1990s, and he asks what the text says about tourism.
b2-cuba-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what happened in the 1990s even though Cuba opened to tourism.
cues: Say that Cuba opened to tourism
Say that the years stayed difficult
b2-cuba-05.target: Por más que se abrió al turismo, el país siguió pasando años difíciles.
b2-cuba-05.english: However much it opened to tourism, the country went on through difficult years.
b2-cuba-05.canDo: I can say that nothing changes however much something happens, with *por más que* and *por mucho que* (Cuba).

b2-cuba-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Cuba in Review
b2-cuba-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing a short talk about Cuba, and she asks when Havana was founded.
b2-cuba-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg when Havana was founded on its present site, stating it precisely.
cues: Show that you are being exact
Say when Havana was founded on its present site
b2-cuba-consolidation.target: En rigor, La Habana se fundó en su lugar actual en 1519.
b2-cuba-consolidation.english: Strictly speaking, Havana was founded on its present site in 1519.
b2-cuba-consolidation.canDo: I can show my attitude to a fact with stance adverbs such as *lamentablemente* and *en rigor*.

b2-11-01.title: Communicative Challenge: A Different Past
b2-11-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what would be different today if you had stayed in South Africa. You say you would not be living in Budapest.
b2-11-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what would be different if you had stayed in South Africa.
cues: Say what you would have done in the past
Say what would be different now
b2-11-01.target: Si me hubiera quedado en Sudáfrica, ahora no viviría en Budapest.
b2-11-01.english: If I had stayed in South Africa, I would not be living in Budapest now.
b2-11-01.canDo: I can say how a different past would change the present with si hubiera and the simple conditional.

b2-11-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A Lasting Trait
b2-11-02.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos tells you he missed the bus again this morning. You say that he would not have missed it if he were less absent-minded.
b2-11-02.prompt: Tell Carlos that he would not have missed the bus if he were less absent-minded.
cues: Name the trait that would be different
Say what would not have happened
b2-11-02.target: Si fueras menos despistado, no habrías perdido el autobús.
b2-11-02.english: If you were less absent-minded, you would not have missed the bus.
b2-11-02.canDo: I can say how a lasting trait would have changed a past event with si + imperfect subjunctive and habría + participle.

b2-11-03.title: Communicative Challenge: On One Condition
b2-11-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks to borrow your bicycle. You agree on one condition: he must bring it back tonight.
b2-11-03.prompt: Tell Carlos that he can borrow your bicycle and on what condition.
cues: Say that you lend it to him
Name your condition
b2-11-03.target: Te presto la bicicleta siempre y cuando me la devuelvas esta noche.
b2-11-03.english: I will lend you the bicycle as long as you give it back to me tonight.
b2-11-03.canDo: I can set a strict condition with siempre y cuando and con la condición de que.

b2-11-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Except If
b2-11-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks if you will come to the cinema on Friday. You say yes, unless you have a lot of work at the office.
b2-11-04.prompt: Tell Meg that you will come on Friday and name the one exception.
cues: Say that you will come on Friday
Name the exception
b2-11-04.target: Voy al cine el viernes, excepto que tenga mucho trabajo en la oficina.
b2-11-04.english: I am going to the cinema on Friday, unless I have a lot of work at the office.
b2-11-04.canDo: I can name the one exception that would change a plan with a menos que, a no ser que, salvo que and excepto que.

b2-11-05.title: Communicative Challenge: If I Am Not Mistaken
b2-11-05.scenario: You are Carlos. At the office you want to check the time of a meeting. You think it is at ten, but you are not sure.
b2-11-05.prompt: Politely say what time you think the meeting is.
cues: Say that you may be mistaken
Say the time of the meeting
b2-11-05.target: Si no me equivoco, la reunión es a las diez.
b2-11-05.english: If I am not mistaken, the meeting is at ten.
b2-11-05.canDo: I can soften a statement or a request with si no me equivoco, si mal no recuerdo, si me permite and si no es molestia.

b2-11-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Book Written as a Diary
b2-11-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos have read a text about Benedetti's novel La tregua, which does not give its ending. Carlos asks how the novel ends. You have not read the novel itself.
b2-11-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos that you would know the ending now if you had read the novel.
cues: Say what you have not done
Say what you would know now
b2-11-consolidation.target: Si hubiera leído La tregua, ahora sabría cómo termina.
b2-11-consolidation.english: If I had read La tregua, I would know now how it ends.
b2-11-consolidation.canDo: I can say how a different past would change the present, and how a lasting trait would have changed the past.

b2-dominicana-01.title: Communicative Challenge: A Lake Below Sea Level
b2-dominicana-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about the Dominican Republic, and he asks which place surprised you most.
b2-dominicana-01.prompt: Tell Carlos about the lake that surprised you, using a relative clause.
cues: Name the lake
Say that it is a salt lake and that it is below sea level
b2-dominicana-01.target: El lago Enriquillo, que es de agua salada, está bajo el nivel del mar.
b2-dominicana-01.english: Lake Enriquillo, which is a salt lake, is below sea level.
b2-dominicana-01.canDo: I can describe a mountain, a bay or a lake with a relative clause (*que*, *quien*).

b2-dominicana-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Founded Santo Domingo
b2-dominicana-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You are planning a trip with Meg and reading about the colonial city of Santo Domingo, and she asks who founded it.
b2-dominicana-02.prompt: Tell Meg who founded Santo Domingo.
cues: Say that the city was founded
Say who founded it
b2-dominicana-02.target: Santo Domingo fue fundada por Bartolomé Colón.
b2-dominicana-02.english: Santo Domingo was founded by Bartolomé Colón.
b2-dominicana-02.canDo: I can say who founded, built or created something with *fue* / *fueron* + participle.

b2-dominicana-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Bachata Goes Round the World
b2-dominicana-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are listening to a podcast about Dominican music, and he asks what happened to bachata after 1990.
b2-dominicana-03.prompt: Tell Carlos how bachata changed after 1990.
cues: Say that bachata changed
Say that it became popular in many countries
Give the date
b2-dominicana-03.target: La bachata se volvió popular en muchos países después de 1990.
b2-dominicana-03.english: Bachata became popular in many countries after 1990.
b2-dominicana-03.canDo: I can say how something changed with *ponerse*, *volverse*, *hacerse* or *quedarse*.

b2-dominicana-04.title: Communicative Challenge: What Historians Say About 1937
b2-dominicana-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You are reading an article about the border between the Dominican Republic and Haiti, and Meg asks about the number of deaths in 1937.
b2-dominicana-04.prompt: Tell Meg what the historians say about the number of deaths in 1937.
cues: Name your source
Say that the number is still debated
b2-dominicana-04.target: Según los historiadores, la cifra de muertos de 1937 se discute todavía.
b2-dominicana-04.english: According to historians, the number of deaths in 1937 is still debated.
b2-dominicana-04.canDo: I can say who reports or judges something with *según* and *explica que*.

b2-dominicana-05.title: Communicative Challenge: If the Grandparents Had Stayed
b2-dominicana-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading about Dominican families in New York, and he asks what you think about their story.
b2-dominicana-05.prompt: Imagine how a family's life would be different if their grandparents had not emigrated.
cues: Say that the grandparents did not emigrate (as an imagined past)
Say where the family would live today
b2-dominicana-05.target: Si sus abuelos no hubieran emigrado, hoy ellos vivirían en la isla.
b2-dominicana-05.english: If their grandparents had not emigrated, they would live on the island today.
b2-dominicana-05.canDo: I can say what would be different today if a past choice had been different.

b2-dominicana-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Park to Visit
b2-dominicana-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. After the unit on the Dominican Republic, Meg asks which place you would most like to visit.
b2-dominicana-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg which park you would like to visit and what it protects.
cues: Name the park
Say what it protects
b2-dominicana-consolidation.target: Los Haitises es un parque que protege manglares y colinas de roca caliza.
b2-dominicana-consolidation.english: Los Haitises is a park that protects mangroves and limestone hills.
b2-dominicana-consolidation.canDo: I can describe a place or a thing with a relative clause (*que*, *quien*).

b2-12-01.title: Communicative Challenge: So That Everyone Knows
b2-12-01.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks why you sent an email to the whole office. You sent it so that everyone would know the new time of the meeting.
b2-12-01.prompt: Tell Meg why you sent the email.
cues: Say that you sent the email
Say what you wanted everyone to know
b2-12-01.target: Mandé el correo a fin de que todos supieran la nueva hora de la reunión.
b2-12-01.english: I sent the email so that everyone would know the new time of the meeting.
b2-12-01.canDo: I can state a purpose with a fin de que and con el objeto de que and the right subjunctive tense.

b2-12-02.title: Communicative Challenge: In Order To
b2-12-02.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks why you are going to the market. You are going to buy fruit and vegetables for dinner.
b2-12-02.prompt: Tell Carlos why you are going to the market.
cues: Say that you are going to the market
Say what you want to buy
b2-12-02.target: Voy al mercado a fin de comprar frutas y verduras para la cena.
b2-12-02.english: I am going to the market in order to buy fruit and vegetables for dinner.
b2-12-02.canDo: I can state a purpose with para, a fin de and con el objeto de + infinitive when one person acts.

b2-12-03.title: Communicative Challenge: With a View To
b2-12-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks why you are saving money. You are saving it with a view to travelling next summer.
b2-12-03.prompt: Tell Meg why you are saving money.
cues: Say that you are saving money
Say what you are planning for next summer
b2-12-03.target: Ahorro dinero con miras a viajar el próximo verano.
b2-12-03.english: I am saving money with a view to travelling next summer.
b2-12-03.canDo: I can state a plan with con miras a and con vistas a + infinitive or noun.

b2-12-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Just in Case
b2-12-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos is going out for a walk and the sky is grey. You tell him to take an umbrella in case it rains.
b2-12-04.prompt: Tell Carlos to take an umbrella and say why.
cues: Tell him to take an umbrella
Say what might happen
b2-12-04.target: Lleva un paraguas, no sea que llueva.
b2-12-04.english: Take an umbrella, in case it rains.
b2-12-04.canDo: I can say what I want to avoid with para que no, a fin de que no and para no + infinitive.

b2-12-05.title: Communicative Challenge: If I Had More Time
b2-12-05.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what you would do if you had more free time. You say that you would cook for her so that she could rest.
b2-12-05.prompt: Tell Meg what you would do with more free time and why.
cues: Say what you would do with more time
Say what you would do it for
b2-12-05.target: Si tuviera más tiempo libre, cocinaría para que tú descansaras.
b2-12-05.english: If I had more free time, I would cook so that you could rest.
b2-12-05.canDo: I can add a purpose clause to a hypothetical sentence with the imperfect subjunctive.

b2-12-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Before Opening the Book
b2-12-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks why you are reading about Ernesto Sabato. You want to know who he was before you open his novel El túnel.
b2-12-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos why you are reading about Sabato.
cues: Say that you are reading about Sabato
Say what you want to know before the novel
b2-12-consolidation.target: Leo sobre Sabato para saber quién fue antes de abrir El túnel.
b2-12-consolidation.english: I am reading about Sabato to find out who he was before I open El túnel.
b2-12-consolidation.canDo: I can state a purpose with para, a fin de, con el objeto de and con miras a, with an infinitive or que + subjunctive.

b2-puertorico-01.title: Communicative Challenge: What Surprises Visitors
b2-puertorico-01.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are watching a documentary about El Yunque in Puerto Rico, and she asks what visitors notice most.
b2-puertorico-01.prompt: Tell Meg what surprises visitors most, putting that idea in the spotlight.
cues: Say that the amount of rain is what surprises them
Stress that idea
b2-puertorico-01.target: Lo que más sorprende a los visitantes es la cantidad de lluvia.
b2-puertorico-01.english: What surprises visitors most is the amount of rain.
b2-puertorico-01.canDo: I can put one idea in the spotlight with a cleft sentence (*Lo que… es…*, *Fue… cuando…*).

b2-puertorico-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Autonomy Before the War
b2-puertorico-02.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading an article about 1898 in Puerto Rico, and he asks whether Spain had already granted autonomy.
b2-puertorico-02.prompt: Tell Carlos when Spain granted autonomy, in relation to the war.
cues: Say that Spain granted autonomy
Say that it was before the war began
b2-puertorico-02.target: España concedió la autonomía antes de que empezara la guerra con Estados Unidos.
b2-puertorico-02.english: Spain granted autonomy before the war with the United States began.
b2-puertorico-02.canDo: I can say that one event happened before or after another with *antes de que* and *después de que*.

b2-puertorico-03.title: Communicative Challenge: What Statehood Would Mean
b2-puertorico-03.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading about the options for Puerto Rico's political status, and she asks what one of them would mean.
b2-puertorico-03.prompt: Describe what one option would mean, without taking sides.
cues: Name the option
Say what would change for the citizens
b2-puertorico-03.target: Si Puerto Rico fuera un estado, sus ciudadanos elegirían senadores con voto.
b2-puertorico-03.english: If Puerto Rico were a state, its citizens would elect senators with a vote.
b2-puertorico-03.canDo: I can describe what an imagined situation would mean with *si* + imperfect subjunctive and the conditional.

b2-puertorico-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Salsa and the Island
b2-puertorico-04.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are listening to a talk about Puerto Rican music, and he asks whether salsa is from the island.
b2-puertorico-04.prompt: Tell Carlos that salsa did not begin on the island but Puerto Ricans were important in it.
cues: Grant the point that it did not begin there
Give the main idea
b2-puertorico-04.target: Si bien la salsa no nació en la isla, muchos puertorriqueños fueron figuras importantes.
b2-puertorico-04.english: Although salsa was not born on the island, many Puerto Ricans were important figures in it.
b2-puertorico-04.canDo: I can grant a true point and then give the main idea with *si bien*.

b2-puertorico-05.title: Communicative Challenge: After the Hurricane
b2-puertorico-05.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading an article about Hurricane María, and she asks what the communities did afterwards.
b2-puertorico-05.prompt: Tell Meg what many communities did and for what purpose.
cues: Say that communities organised
Say what they did it for
b2-puertorico-05.target: Muchas comunidades se organizaron con el fin de repartir agua y comida.
b2-puertorico-05.english: Many communities organised in order to hand out water and food.
b2-puertorico-05.canDo: I can say what an action is for with *con el fin de*, *con miras a* and *de modo que*.

b2-puertorico-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: When Was It Protected
b2-puertorico-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. After the unit on Puerto Rico, Carlos asks what you remember about El Yunque.
b2-puertorico-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos when El Yunque was protected, putting the date in the spotlight.
cues: Say that the Spanish crown protected the region
Stress the year
b2-puertorico-consolidation.target: Fue en 1876 cuando la corona española protegió esta región.
b2-puertorico-consolidation.english: It was in 1876 that the Spanish crown protected this region.
b2-puertorico-consolidation.canDo: I can put one idea in the spotlight with a cleft sentence (*Lo que… es…*, *Fue… cuando…*) (review).

b2-13-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Looking for a Flat
b2-13-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what kind of flat you want in Budapest. You do not have one yet; you want a spacious flat that has a lift.
b2-13-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what kind of flat you are looking for.
cues: Say you are looking for a flat
Say what it should be like
b2-13-01.target: Busco un apartamento que sea amplio y que tenga ascensor.
b2-13-01.english: I'm looking for a flat that is spacious and has a lift.
b2-13-01.canDo: I can describe something I am looking for but have not found, using que + subjunctive.

b2-13-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Is There a Plumber?
b2-13-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks if you know a plumber for a leak. You do not know anyone who can come today.
b2-13-02.prompt: Tell Meg that you do not know any plumber who can come today.
cues: Say you do not know anyone
Say what that person should be able to do
b2-13-02.target: No conozco a ningún plomero que pueda venir hoy.
b2-13-02.english: I don't know any plumber who can come today.
b2-13-02.canDo: I can say that nobody or nothing fits a description, using nadie, nada or ningún + que + subjunctive.

b2-13-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Right Charger
b2-13-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks about your phone charger. You needed one that fitted your phone, and you have found one that works.
b2-13-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what you needed and that you found it.
cues: Say what kind of charger you needed
Say that you found one that works
b2-13-03.target: Necesitaba un cargador que sirviera para mi celular y encontré uno que servía.
b2-13-03.english: I needed a charger that would work for my phone and I found one that worked.
b2-13-03.canDo: I can choose between indicative and subjunctive after que by asking whether the thing is real.

b2-13-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Someone to Trust
b2-13-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what kind of person you want to work with in the office. You want someone you can trust.
b2-13-04.prompt: Tell Meg what kind of person you want to work with.
cues: Say you want to work with someone
Say you want to be able to trust that person
b2-13-04.target: Quiero trabajar con alguien en quien pueda confiar.
b2-13-04.english: I want to work with someone I can trust.
b2-13-04.canDo: I can ask for a person or place with a preposition + relative + subjunctive.

b2-13-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Job I Want
b2-13-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what kind of job you would like. You want a job that pays well and has a good schedule.
b2-13-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what kind of job you want.
cues: Say you want a job
Say what it should offer
b2-13-05.target: Quiero un trabajo que pague bien y tenga un buen horario.
b2-13-05.english: I want a job that pays well and has good hours.
b2-13-05.canDo: I can read and write a job ad with que + subjunctive.

b2-13-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Not Found Yet
b2-13-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what you are looking for in a new flat. You want a bright one, and so far you have not found any you like.
b2-13-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what kind of flat you want and that you have not found one.
cues: Say you are looking for a flat and what it should be like
Say you have not found one yet
b2-13-consolidation.target: Busco un apartamento que sea luminoso, pero todavía no he encontrado ninguno que me guste.
b2-13-consolidation.english: I'm looking for a flat that is bright, but I haven't found one I like yet.
b2-13-consolidation.canDo: I can describe what I am looking for with que + subjunctive and tell it from a real thing.

b2-colombiaandina-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Laws for the Páramos
b2-colombiaandina-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about the páramos of Colombia, and he asks what the environmental groups want.
b2-colombiaandina-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what the environmental groups ask for.
cues: Say that they ask for laws
Say what the laws should do
b2-colombiaandina-01.target: Piden leyes que protejan los páramos.
b2-colombiaandina-01.english: They are asking for laws that protect the páramos.
b2-colombiaandina-01.canDo: I can say what I am looking for or what does not exist with *que* + subjunctive (*Busco un guía que conozca…*).

b2-colombiaandina-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A City at 2,600 Metres
b2-colombiaandina-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are planning a trip and reading about Bogotá, and she asks what surprises visitors.
b2-colombiaandina-02.prompt: Tell Meg what surprises many visitors, commenting on the fact.
cues: Mention the height of the city
Say that it surprises many visitors
b2-colombiaandina-02.target: El hecho de que la ciudad esté a 2600 metros sorprende a muchos visitantes.
b2-colombiaandina-02.english: The fact that the city is at 2,600 metres surprises many visitors.
b2-colombiaandina-02.canDo: I can comment on a known fact with *el hecho de que* + subjunctive (Colombia I).

b2-colombiaandina-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The City of Eternal Spring
b2-colombiaandina-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading an article about Medellín, and he asks whether it is a hot city.
b2-colombiaandina-03.prompt: Correct the idea that Medellín is hot and give the real reason.
cues: Reject the idea that it is hot
Say what its climate is like
b2-colombiaandina-03.target: No es que haga mucho calor, sino que la temperatura casi no cambia.
b2-colombiaandina-03.english: It is not that it is very hot, but that the temperature hardly changes.
b2-colombiaandina-03.canDo: I can reject a reason and give the real one with *no es que* + subjunctive and *sino que* + indicative.

b2-colombiaandina-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Coffee Picked by Hand
b2-colombiaandina-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are watching a documentary about the Coffee Cultural Landscape, and she asks how the coffee is harvested.
b2-colombiaandina-04.prompt: Tell Meg how the coffee is harvested.
cues: Say how it is picked
Say why it is done that way
b2-colombiaandina-04.target: El café se recoge a mano, porque el terreno es difícil.
b2-colombiaandina-04.english: The coffee is picked by hand, because the terrain is difficult.
b2-colombiaandina-04.canDo: I can describe how something is done with the passive *se* (*se recoge*, *se secan*).

b2-colombiaandina-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Where Gabo Began
b2-colombiaandina-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading about García Márquez, and he asks whether he began as a novelist.
b2-colombiaandina-05.prompt: Correct Carlos with a stance adverb: say how he really began his career.
cues: Use an adverb that corrects an expectation
Say what his first work was
b2-colombiaandina-05.target: En realidad, empezó su carrera como periodista.
b2-colombiaandina-05.english: In fact, he began his career as a journalist.
b2-colombiaandina-05.canDo: I can comment on a fact with a stance adverb such as *en realidad*, *en rigor* or *afortunadamente*.

b2-colombiaandina-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Crops for the Páramo
b2-colombiaandina-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. After the unit on the Colombian Andes, Meg asks what the farmers of the páramos need.
b2-colombiaandina-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what the farmers of the páramo need.
cues: Say that they need crops
Say that the crops should not harm the water
b2-colombiaandina-consolidation.target: Los campesinos necesitan cultivos que no dañen el agua del páramo.
b2-colombiaandina-consolidation.english: The farmers need crops that do not harm the water of the páramo.
b2-colombiaandina-consolidation.canDo: I can say what I am looking for or what does not exist with *que* + subjunctive.

b2-14-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Wherever You Go
b2-14-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos says he will miss you when you are away from Budapest. You promise to call him wherever you go.
b2-14-01.prompt: Promise Carlos that you will call him wherever you go.
cues: Say that you will call him
Say that it does not matter where you go
b2-14-01.target: Dondequiera que vaya, te voy a llamar.
b2-14-01.english: Wherever I go, I'm going to call you.
b2-14-01.canDo: I can say whoever, whichever and wherever with quienquiera que, cualquiera que and dondequiera que.

b2-14-02.title: Communicative Challenge: An Expensive Trip
b2-14-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg says a trip she wants to take is too expensive. You tell her that however much she saves, the trip will still be expensive.
b2-14-02.prompt: Tell Meg that however much she saves, the trip stays expensive.
cues: Say that it makes no difference how much she saves
Say that the trip is still expensive
b2-14-02.target: Por más que ahorres, ese viaje va a seguir siendo caro.
b2-14-02.english: However much you save, that trip is going to stay expensive.
b2-14-02.canDo: I can say however much, however many with por más or por mucho + noun + que + subjunctive.

b2-14-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Whatever They Think
b2-14-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos says people at the office criticise his plan and asks what to do. You tell him that whatever they think, the decision is his.
b2-14-03.prompt: Tell Carlos that whatever people think, he decides.
cues: Say that it makes no difference what they think
Say that the decision is his
b2-14-03.target: Opinen lo que opinen, tú decides.
b2-14-03.canDo: I can say sea quien sea, sea cual sea and sea lo que sea for whoever and whatever it is.

b2-14-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Everyone Is Welcome
b2-14-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks who can come to a party. You say that anyone who wants to come is welcome.
b2-14-04.prompt: Tell Meg that anyone who wants to come is welcome.
cues: Say who is welcome
Say that they must want to come
b2-14-04.target: Todo aquel que quiera venir es bienvenido.
b2-14-04.english: Anyone who wants to come is welcome.
b2-14-04.canDo: I can say everything that and everyone who with todo lo que, todos los que and todo aquel que.

b2-14-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Notice for the Building
b2-14-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks you to write a short notice for the neighbours of a building in Budapest. It asks them politely not to make noise after ten o'clock.
b2-14-05.prompt: Write the notice for the neighbours.
cues: Address the neighbours
Ask politely for no noise after ten
b2-14-05.target: Estimados vecinos: se ruega no hacer ruido después de las diez.
b2-14-05.english: Dear neighbours: please do not make noise after ten o'clock.
b2-14-05.canDo: I can read and write short notices with todo aquel que, cualquier persona que and se ruega.

b2-14-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Rule for Late Arrivals
b2-14-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what the rule is for people who arrive late to a meeting. You say that anyone who arrives late must wait, whoever it is.
b2-14-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg the rule for people who arrive late.
cues: Say who must wait
Say that it makes no difference who it is
b2-14-consolidation.target: Cualquiera que llegue tarde deberá esperar, sea quien sea.
b2-14-consolidation.english: Anyone who arrives late must wait, whoever it is.
b2-14-consolidation.canDo: I can say that it makes no difference who, which or where, in several ways.

b2-colombiaperiferias-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Founded Cartagena
b2-colombiaperiferias-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about Cartagena, and he asks what the narrator said about the city.
b2-colombiaperiferias-01.prompt: Tell Carlos who founded Cartagena and when.
cues: Say that the city was founded
Say by whom and in which year
b2-colombiaperiferias-01.target: Cartagena fue fundada en 1533 por Pedro de Heredia.
b2-colombiaperiferias-01.english: Cartagena was founded in 1533 by Pedro de Heredia.
b2-colombiaperiferias-01.canDo: I can say who founded or built something with *ser* + past participle.

b2-colombiaperiferias-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Why So Few Roads
b2-colombiaperiferias-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You have read an article about the Pacific coast of Colombia, and Meg asks how people travel there.
b2-colombiaperiferias-02.prompt: Tell Meg why there are few roads on the Pacific coast.
cues: Give the reason with a formal connector
Say that there are few roads
b2-colombiaperiferias-02.target: Debido a la lluvia y a la selva, hay pocas carreteras en el Pacífico.
b2-colombiaperiferias-02.english: Because of the rain and the forest, there are few roads on the Pacific coast.
b2-colombiaperiferias-02.canDo: I can give a cause with *debido a* or *a raíz de* followed by a noun.

b2-colombiaperiferias-03.title: Communicative Challenge: A Rule for Collective Lands
b2-colombiaperiferias-03.scenario: You are Meg. You are telling Carlos what you read about Law 70 of 1993 for a talk you are planning.
b2-colombiaperiferias-03.prompt: Say what the law says about the collective lands, in the formal register of a law.
cues: Say that the lands cannot be sold
Use a formal future form
b2-colombiaperiferias-03.target: Las tierras colectivas no podrán venderse.
b2-colombiaperiferias-03.english: The collective lands may not be sold.
b2-colombiaperiferias-03.canDo: I can turn an everyday request into a formal rule with *todo aquel que*, the future and *se*.

b2-colombiaperiferias-04.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Commission Said
b2-colombiaperiferias-04.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a news report about the Truth Commission, and he asks what it said about the conflict.
b2-colombiaperiferias-04.prompt: Tell Carlos what the Commission said in its 2022 report.
cues: Say who said it
Say what the conflict had left behind
b2-colombiaperiferias-04.target: La Comisión dijo en su informe que el conflicto había dejado cientos de miles de muertos.
b2-colombiaperiferias-04.english: The Commission said in its report that the conflict had left hundreds of thousands dead.
b2-colombiaperiferias-04.canDo: I can report what someone said with *dijo que* and the right tense shift.

b2-colombiaperiferias-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Park Closed to Tourists
b2-colombiaperiferias-05.scenario: You are Carlos. You have read an article about Chiribiquete, and Meg asks whether tourists can visit the park.
b2-colombiaperiferias-05.prompt: Tell Meg that the park is closed, and that people still know its paintings.
cues: Say that the park is closed to tourists
Say that many people still know the paintings
b2-colombiaperiferias-05.target: Aun cuando el parque está cerrado a los turistas, muchas personas conocen sus pinturas.
b2-colombiaperiferias-05.english: Even though the park is closed to tourists, many people know its paintings.
b2-colombiaperiferias-05.canDo: I can use *aun cuando* with the subjunctive for a possibility and with the indicative for a fact.

b2-colombiaperiferias-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Palenque and UNESCO
b2-colombiaperiferias-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. You are telling Carlos what you remember from your reading about Colombia.
b2-colombiaperiferias-consolidation.prompt: Say what UNESCO did for Palenque in 2005.
cues: Say who recognised Palenque
Say the year
b2-colombiaperiferias-consolidation.target: Palenque fue reconocido por la UNESCO en 2005.
b2-colombiaperiferias-consolidation.english: Palenque was recognised by UNESCO in 2005.
b2-colombiaperiferias-consolidation.canDo: I can say who founded, built or recognised something with *ser* + past participle.

b2-15-01.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Boss Wanted
b2-15-01.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks why you are in a hurry after the meeting at the office. Your boss wanted everyone to hand in the report on Friday.
b2-15-01.prompt: Tell Meg what your boss wanted.
cues: Say who wanted something
Say what everyone had to hand in, and when
b2-15-01.target: Mi jefe quería que todos entregáramos el informe el viernes.
b2-15-01.english: My boss wanted all of us to hand in the report on Friday.
b2-15-01.canDo: I can form the imperfect subjunctive from the ellos form of the preterite.

b2-15-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Same Tense
b2-15-02.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos finds si yo tuviese tiempo in an old book and asks whether it means the same as si yo tuviera tiempo.
b2-15-02.prompt: Tell Carlos whether the two forms mean the same, and which one you use.
cues: Say that the two forms mean the same
Say which one you use when you speak
b2-15-02.target: Sí, es lo mismo, pero yo siempre digo si tuviera tiempo.
b2-15-02.english: Yes, it is the same, but I always say "si tuviera tiempo".
b2-15-02.canDo: I can tell that -ra and -se are two forms of the same tense with the same meaning.

b2-15-03.title: Communicative Challenge: At the Counter
b2-15-03.scenario: You are Meg. You are at the university office and you want to ask the clerk, politely, to explain how to do a procedure.
b2-15-03.prompt: Politely ask the clerk to explain the procedure to you.
cues: Greet the clerk
Say politely that you would like the clerk to explain how the procedure works
b2-15-03.target: Buenos días, quisiera que me explicara cómo se hace este trámite.
b2-15-03.english: Good morning, I would like you to explain to me how this procedure is done.
b2-15-03.canDo: I can soften a request with quisiera, pudiera and debiera.

b2-15-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Talks as If He Knew Everything
b2-15-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks about your new colleague at the office. He talks as if he knew everything, and you wish you knew more.
b2-15-04.prompt: Tell Meg how your colleague talks and what you wish.
cues: Say how your colleague talks
Say what you wish about yourself
b2-15-04.target: Mi compañero habla como si lo supiera todo. Ojalá yo supiera más.
b2-15-04.english: My colleague talks as if he knew everything. I wish I knew more.
b2-15-04.canDo: I can compare something to an unreal situation with como si + imperfect subjunctive.

b2-15-05.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Newspaper Means
b2-15-05.scenario: You are Meg. You are reading a newspaper article with Carlos. He asks what el libro que publicara en 1950 means.
b2-15-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what the phrase means and what kind of style it is.
cues: Say what the phrase means in everyday Spanish
Say what kind of style it is
b2-15-05.target: Es lo mismo que el libro que publicó en 1950; es un estilo formal.
b2-15-05.english: It is the same as "el libro que publicó en 1950"; it is a formal style.
b2-15-05.canDo: I can recognise a -ra form used like a past indicative, as in el que fuera presidente.

b2-15-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Class Reading
b2-15-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what your teacher wanted you to do for class. She wanted you to read a text about Gallegos and to talk about his novel.
b2-15-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos what the teacher wanted.
cues: Say what the teacher wanted you to read
Say what she wanted you to talk about
b2-15-consolidation.target: La profesora quería que leyéramos un texto sobre Gallegos y que habláramos de su novela.
b2-15-consolidation.english: The teacher wanted us to read a text about Gallegos and to talk about his novel.
b2-15-consolidation.canDo: I can form the imperfect subjunctive and use it after a past verb, with -ra or -se.

b2-venezuelapetroleo-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Valley of Caracas
b2-venezuelapetroleo-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about Caracas, and he asks where the city was founded.
b2-venezuelapetroleo-01.prompt: Tell Carlos where Caracas was founded, putting the place first.
cues: Put the place at the start of the sentence
Say that the city was founded there
b2-venezuelapetroleo-01.target: En un valle estrecho fue fundada Caracas en 1567.
b2-venezuelapetroleo-01.english: Caracas was founded in 1567 in a narrow valley.
b2-venezuelapetroleo-01.canDo: I can put a place or a quality first for emphasis, as in *En un valle estrecho fue fundada Caracas*.

b2-venezuelapetroleo-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Before the Oil
b2-venezuelapetroleo-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You have read an article about the first oil wells, and Meg asks what Venezuela lived from before oil.
b2-venezuelapetroleo-02.prompt: Tell Meg what Venezuela lived from before oil was discovered.
cues: Start with a "before" clause
Say what the country lived from
b2-venezuelapetroleo-02.target: Antes de que se descubriera el petróleo, Venezuela vivía del café y del cacao.
b2-venezuelapetroleo-02.english: Before oil was discovered, Venezuela lived from coffee and cacao.
b2-venezuelapetroleo-02.canDo: I can say what was true before something happened with *antes de que* and the subjunctive.

b2-venezuelapetroleo-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Clouds in the Aula Magna
b2-venezuelapetroleo-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are looking at photographs of the Ciudad Universitaria in Caracas, and he asks about the Calder panels.
b2-venezuelapetroleo-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what the Calder panels look like.
cues: Say that they hang from the ceiling
Compare them to real clouds
b2-venezuelapetroleo-03.target: Las Nubes de Calder cuelgan del techo como si fueran nubes de verdad.
b2-venezuelapetroleo-03.english: Calder's Clouds hang from the ceiling as if they were real clouds.
b2-venezuelapetroleo-03.canDo: I can make a comparison with something unreal using *como si* and the imperfect subjunctive.

b2-venezuelapetroleo-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Where Was Soto Born
b2-venezuelapetroleo-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos says that Jesús Soto was born in Caracas, but the article you read says something else.
b2-venezuelapetroleo-04.prompt: Correct Carlos politely, with a stance adverb.
cues: Start with a stance adverb
Say where Soto was born
b2-venezuelapetroleo-04.target: En realidad, Soto nació en Ciudad Bolívar, no en Caracas.
b2-venezuelapetroleo-04.english: Actually, Soto was born in Ciudad Bolívar, not in Caracas.
b2-venezuelapetroleo-04.canDo: I can show my attitude to a fact with stance adverbs such as *en realidad* and *lamentablemente*.

b2-venezuelapetroleo-05.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Country Should Have Done
b2-venezuelapetroleo-05.scenario: You are Carlos. You are telling Meg what economists say about the years of high oil prices.
b2-venezuelapetroleo-05.prompt: Tell Meg what several economists say the country should have done.
cues: Say whose opinion it is
Say what the country should have done
b2-venezuelapetroleo-05.target: Según varios economistas, el país debería haber ahorrado más en los años de precios altos.
b2-venezuelapetroleo-05.english: According to several economists, the country should have saved more in the years of high prices.
b2-venezuelapetroleo-05.canDo: I can say what should have been done with *debería haber* + past participle.

b2-venezuelapetroleo-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Short Summary
b2-venezuelapetroleo-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. You are telling Carlos what you remember about the Ciudad Universitaria.
b2-venezuelapetroleo-consolidation.prompt: Say what UNESCO decided in 2000, and compare the campus to something.
cues: Say what UNESCO decided
Compare the campus to a city
b2-venezuelapetroleo-consolidation.target: En 2000 la UNESCO declaró la Ciudad Universitaria Patrimonio de la Humanidad. Parece una ciudad pequeña, como si tuviera sus propias calles.
b2-venezuelapetroleo-consolidation.english: In 2000 UNESCO declared the Ciudad Universitaria a World Heritage site. It looks like a small city, as if it had its own streets.
b2-venezuelapetroleo-consolidation.canDo: I can put a place or a quality first for emphasis.

b2-16-01.title: Communicative Challenge: A Careless Slip
b2-16-01.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks why you paid a fine. You did not look at the date.
b2-16-01.prompt: Tell Meg why you paid the fine and what you would have done.
cues: Say what you would have done differently
Say that you paid the fine
b2-16-01.target: Si hubiera mirado la fecha, no habría pagado la multa.
b2-16-01.english: If I had looked at the date, I would not have paid the fine.
b2-16-01.canDo: I can form the pluperfect subjunctive with hubiera or hubiese and a past participle.

b2-16-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Too Late for Tickets
b2-16-02.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks why you look sad. The concert tickets sold out, and you did not buy them in time.
b2-16-02.prompt: Tell Carlos what you wish you had done.
cues: Say that you wish you had bought the tickets
Say when you should have bought them
b2-16-02.target: Ojalá hubiera comprado los boletos a tiempo.
b2-16-02.english: I wish I had bought the tickets in time.
b2-16-02.canDo: I can say a wish about the past with ojalá + hubiera or hubiese + participle.

b2-16-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Leaving Earlier
b2-16-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos says he missed the train because he left home late. Tell him that, without si, he would have arrived on time if he had left earlier.
b2-16-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what would have happened if he had left earlier.
cues: Say what he should have done earlier
Say what would have happened
b2-16-03.target: De haber salido antes, habrías llegado a tiempo.
b2-16-03.english: Had you left earlier, you would have arrived on time.
b2-16-03.canDo: I can say an unreal past condition with si hubiera, de haber or hubiera at the start.

b2-16-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Pity You Missed It
b2-16-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos did not come to a party yesterday. Tell him that it surprised you and that it was a pity.
b2-16-04.prompt: Tell Carlos how you felt about his not coming.
cues: Say that it surprised you that he had not come
Say that it was a pity
b2-16-04.target: Me sorprendió que no hubieras venido a la fiesta; fue una lástima.
b2-16-04.english: It surprised me that you had not come to the party; it was a pity.
b2-16-04.canDo: I can judge the past with habría sido mejor que + hubiera + participle.

b2-16-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Old Edition
b2-16-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos finds hubiese in an old edition of a book and asks if it is the same as hubiera.
b2-16-05.prompt: Tell Carlos whether the two forms are the same, and which one you would say.
cues: Say that the two forms are the same
Say which one you would say when you speak
b2-16-05.target: Sí, es lo mismo; en la conversación yo diría hubiera.
b2-16-05.english: Yes, it is the same; in conversation I would say "hubiera".
b2-16-05.canDo: I can recognise hubiese + participle as the same as hubiera + participle.

b2-16-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Nobody Told Me
b2-16-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks why you did not go to the party. Nobody had told you about it.
b2-16-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos why you did not go.
cues: Say what you would have done if they had told you
Say that nobody told you
b2-16-consolidation.target: Si me hubieran avisado, habría ido a la fiesta.
b2-16-consolidation.english: If they had told me, I would have gone to the party.
b2-16-consolidation.canDo: I can use the pluperfect subjunctive in conditions, wishes and judgments about the past.

b2-venezuelasabana-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Is a Llanero
b2-venezuelasabana-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about the Llanos of Venezuela, and he asks what a llanero is.
b2-venezuelasabana-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what a llanero is.
cues: Say that he is a man
Say what he does with the cattle
b2-venezuelasabana-01.target: El llanero es el hombre que cuida el ganado a caballo.
b2-venezuelasabana-01.english: The llanero is the man who looks after the cattle on horseback.
b2-venezuelasabana-01.canDo: I can describe a person, a thing or a place with *que*, *quien* and *donde*.

b2-venezuelasabana-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Saw the Waterfall First
b2-venezuelasabana-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You have read an article about Angel Falls, and Meg asks where its current name comes from.
b2-venezuelasabana-02.prompt: Tell Meg who flew over the waterfall in 1933, stressing the person.
cues: Stress who did it
Say what he did and when
b2-venezuelasabana-02.target: Fue el piloto Jimmie Angel quien sobrevoló la cascada en 1933.
b2-venezuelasabana-02.english: It was the pilot Jimmie Angel who flew over the waterfall in 1933.
b2-venezuelasabana-02.canDo: I can spotlight a person, a place or a time with *Fue ... quien / donde / cuando* and *Lo que ... es*.

b2-venezuelasabana-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Why Income Fell
b2-venezuelasabana-03.scenario: You are Meg. You are telling Carlos what you read about the Venezuelan economy.
b2-venezuelasabana-03.prompt: Tell Carlos why the income of the country fell, using a formal connector.
cues: Give the cause with a formal connector
Say what fell
b2-venezuelasabana-03.target: Debido a la caída del precio del petróleo en 2014, los ingresos del país bajaron.
b2-venezuelasabana-03.english: Because of the fall in the oil price in 2014, the country's income fell.
b2-venezuelasabana-03.canDo: I can give a cause with *debido a* or *a raíz de* followed by a noun (Venezuela II).

b2-venezuelasabana-04.title: Communicative Challenge: How Many Are Abroad
b2-venezuelasabana-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You are reading a report about Venezuelan migration, and Meg asks how many Venezuelans live abroad.
b2-venezuelasabana-04.prompt: Tell Meg the figure, with its source and its date.
cues: Name the source
Say the figure and the date
b2-venezuelasabana-04.target: Según ACNUR, a finales de 2025 había unos 7,9 millones de venezolanos fuera del país.
b2-venezuelasabana-04.english: According to UNHCR, at the end of 2025 there were about 7.9 million Venezuelans outside the country.
