b2-venezuelasabana-04.canDo: I can give the source of a statement with *según* and report it with *informó de que* or *explica que*.

b2-venezuelasabana-05.title: Communicative Challenge: What Some Migrants Wish
b2-venezuelasabana-05.scenario: You are Meg. You are telling Carlos what you read about the feelings of some Venezuelan migrants.
b2-venezuelasabana-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what some migrants say about staying in their country.
cues: Say who says it
Use a wish about the past
b2-venezuelasabana-05.target: Algunos migrantes dicen que ojalá hubieran podido quedarse en su país.
b2-venezuelasabana-05.english: Some migrants say that they wish they had been able to stay in their country.
b2-venezuelasabana-05.canDo: I can express a wish about the past with *ojalá* + *hubiera* and a participle.

b2-venezuelasabana-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Short Summary
b2-venezuelasabana-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. You are telling Carlos what you remember about the music of the Llanos.
b2-venezuelasabana-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos what the joropo is.
cues: Say what the joropo is
Say where it is danced
b2-venezuelasabana-consolidation.target: El joropo es la música que se baila en los Llanos.
b2-venezuelasabana-consolidation.english: The joropo is the music that is danced in the Llanos.
b2-venezuelasabana-consolidation.canDo: I can describe a person, a thing or a place with *que*, *quien* and *donde* (review).

b2-17-01.title: Communicative Challenge: What Ana Said
b2-17-01.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what a colleague of yours said about the report. She said that she had already finished it and that she would send it the next day.
b2-17-01.prompt: Tell Meg what your colleague said about the report.
cues: Say what she said she had already done
Say what she said she would do the next day
b2-17-01.target: Mi compañera dijo que ya había terminado el informe y que lo enviaría al día siguiente.
b2-17-01.english: My colleague said that she had already finished the report and that she would send it the next day.
b2-17-01.canDo: I can report what someone said and move the verb back (dijo que tenía, había llegado, llegaría).

b2-17-02.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Teacher Asked
b2-17-02.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what your teacher asked you at the end of the class. She asked whether you had finished the exercise and when you would hand in the work.
b2-17-02.prompt: Tell Carlos what the teacher asked you.
cues: Report her yes/no question about the exercise
Report her question about when you would hand in the work
b2-17-02.target: La profesora me preguntó si había terminado el ejercicio y cuándo entregaría el trabajo.
b2-17-02.english: The teacher asked me whether I had finished the exercise and when I would hand in the work.
b2-17-02.canDo: I can report a yes/no question with si and an information question with its question word after a past verb.

b2-17-03.title: Communicative Challenge: What My Boss Asked
b2-17-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks why you wrote to a client. Your boss asked you to write to him and to send him the report.
b2-17-03.prompt: Tell Meg what your boss asked you to do.
cues: Say what your boss asked you to do first
Say the second thing your boss asked
b2-17-03.target: Mi jefe me pidió que escribiera a un cliente y que le enviara el informe.
b2-17-03.english: My boss asked me to write to a client and to send him the report.
b2-17-03.canDo: I can report an order or a request with que + the imperfect subjunctive, also when it was asked as a question.

b2-17-04.title: Communicative Challenge: What Ana Told Me
b2-17-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what a classmate of yours told you when she phoned from Lima last week. She said that she had arrived in Lima the day before and had a meeting there that day.
b2-17-04.prompt: Tell Carlos what your classmate told you.
cues: Say when she had arrived in Lima
Say what she had that day and where
b2-17-04.target: Mi compañera me dijo que el día anterior había llegado a Lima y que aquel día tenía una reunión allí.
b2-17-04.english: My classmate told me that the day before she had arrived in Lima and that that day she had a meeting there.
b2-17-04.canDo: I can change time and place words when I retell what someone said (hoy becomes aquel día, aquí becomes allí).

b2-17-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Luis Waits
b2-17-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks you to continue a short story: Luis is waiting at the station for a friend who is late. Show what Luis thinks as a question in the narrator’s voice, without a verb like pensó.
b2-17-05.prompt: Tell the next lines of the story.
cues: Say that Luis looked at the clock
Give his thought as a question
Add what he thinks about his friend being late
b2-17-05.target: Luis miró el reloj. ¿Dónde estaba su amigo? Otra vez llegaba tarde.
b2-17-05.english: Luis looked at the clock. Where was his friend? He was late again.
b2-17-05.canDo: I can spot free indirect speech in a story: a character’s question, doubt or exclamation told in the narrator’s past tense.

b2-17-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Class Yesterday
b2-17-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what your teacher said about the novel in class yesterday. She asked whether you had read the first chapter, and she asked you to read the second one by the next day.
b2-17-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos what the teacher asked.
cues: Report her yes/no question about the first chapter
Report her request about the second chapter
Say by when she asked you to read it
b2-17-consolidation.target: La profesora preguntó si habíamos leído el primer capítulo y nos pidió que leyéramos el segundo al día siguiente.
b2-17-consolidation.english: The teacher asked whether we had read the first chapter and asked us to read the second one the next day.
b2-17-consolidation.canDo: I can report statements, questions and requests after a past verb.

b2-ecuador-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Volcano That Is Still Active
b2-ecuador-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are planning a trip to Ecuador and reading about its volcanoes. He asks which one is still active.
b2-ecuador-01.prompt: Tell Carlos which volcano is still active, with a relative clause.
cues: Name the volcano
Say that it is still active
b2-ecuador-01.target: El Cotopaxi es un volcán que sigue activo.
b2-ecuador-01.english: Cotopaxi is a volcano that is still active.
b2-ecuador-01.canDo: I can describe a place or a person with a relative clause (*que*, *quien*).

b2-ecuador-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Islands Declared a Park
b2-ecuador-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are watching a documentary about the Galápagos, and she asks when the islands were protected.
b2-ecuador-02.prompt: Tell Meg when the islands were declared a national park, using the passive.
cues: Say what was done to the islands
Give the year
b2-ecuador-02.target: Las islas fueron declaradas parque nacional en 1959.
b2-ecuador-02.english: The islands were declared a national park in 1959.
b2-ecuador-02.canDo: I can say what was done to a place with the passive (*fue declarada*, *fueron creadas*).

b2-ecuador-03.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Article Said
b2-ecuador-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you told him about your reading on Ecuador's indigenous movement the day before.
b2-ecuador-03.prompt: Tell Carlos that the day before you said you had read about the uprising, retelling with the right time word.
cues: Start with what you said
Say that the day before you had read about the uprising
b2-ecuador-03.target: Dije que el día anterior había leído sobre el levantamiento.
b2-ecuador-03.english: I said that the day before I had read about the uprising.
b2-ecuador-03.canDo: I can retell what someone said, shifting the time and place words (*ese día*, *el día anterior*, *allí*).

b2-ecuador-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Fact That Nature Has Rights
b2-ecuador-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading an article about Ecuador's 2008 constitution, and she asks what you think is important about it.
b2-ecuador-04.prompt: Tell Meg that the fact that nature has rights in the constitution is important.
cues: Start with the fact
Say that it is important
b2-ecuador-04.target: El hecho de que la naturaleza tenga derechos en la Constitución es importante.
b2-ecuador-04.english: The fact that nature has rights in the constitution is important.
b2-ecuador-04.canDo: I can comment on a known fact with *el hecho de que* + subjunctive (Ecuador).

b2-ecuador-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Although the Vote Was Clear
b2-ecuador-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are preparing a short talk about Yasuní, and he asks what makes the topic difficult.
b2-ecuador-05.prompt: Tell Carlos that although the vote was clear, applying it is taking years.
cues: Grant the point formally
Say that applying it takes years
b2-ecuador-05.target: Si bien la consulta fue clara, su aplicación lleva años.
b2-ecuador-05.english: Although the vote was clear, applying it is taking years.
b2-ecuador-05.canDo: I can grant a point formally with *si bien* + indicative.

b2-ecuador-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Ecuador in Review
b2-ecuador-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing a short talk about Ecuador, and she asks which city has four rivers.
b2-ecuador-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg which city has four rivers, with a relative clause.
cues: Name the city
Say that it has four rivers
b2-ecuador-consolidation.target: La ciudad que tiene cuatro ríos es Cuenca.
b2-ecuador-consolidation.english: The city that has four rivers is Cuenca.
b2-ecuador-consolidation.canDo: I can describe a place with a relative clause (*que*, *quien*).

b2-18-01.title: Communicative Challenge: What Ana Told Me
b2-18-01.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what a colleague of yours said after the meeting. She admitted that she had made a mistake and added that she would call again.
b2-18-01.prompt: Tell Meg what your colleague said after the meeting.
cues: Say that she admitted something
Say what she added
b2-18-01.target: Mi compañera admitió que se había equivocado y añadió que llamaría otra vez.
b2-18-01.english: My colleague admitted that she had made a mistake and added that she would call again.
b2-18-01.canDo: I can choose a reporting verb that says how something was said (afirmar, explicar, añadir, admitir, negar, advertir, recordar, reprochar, sugerir).

b2-18-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Saw the Message
b2-18-02.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what two of your classmates said about a message. One denied having seen it, and the other answered back that he had read it.
b2-18-02.prompt: Tell Carlos what your two classmates said.
cues: Report the first one’s denial
Report the other one’s answer
b2-18-02.target: Un compañero negó haber visto el mensaje, pero otra compañera replicó que lo había leído.
b2-18-02.english: One classmate denied having seen the message, but another answered back that he had read it.
b2-18-02.canDo: I can report a denial with negar que + subjunctive or negar + haber + participle, and an admission with admitir que + indicative.

b2-18-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Before the Storm
b2-18-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks why you closed all the windows. A colleague warned you that there would be a storm and reminded you to close them.
b2-18-03.prompt: Tell Meg what your colleague said.
cues: Report her warning about the weather
Report what she reminded you to do
b2-18-03.target: Mi compañera me advirtió que habría una tormenta y me recordó que cerrara las ventanas.
b2-18-03.english: My colleague warned me that there would be a storm and reminded me to close the windows.
b2-18-03.canDo: I can report a warning or a reminder of a fact with advertir or recordar + que + indicative.

b2-18-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Why Ana Is Upset
b2-18-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks why a classmate of yours is upset with you. She reproached you for not having called her, and she blamed you for the delay.
b2-18-04.prompt: Tell Carlos what your classmate said.
cues: Report her reproach about the call
Say what she blamed you for
b2-18-04.target: Mi compañera me reprochó que no la hubiera llamado y me culpó del retraso.
b2-18-04.english: My classmate reproached me for not having called her and blamed me for the delay.
b2-18-04.canDo: I can report a reproach with reprochar or echar en cara + que + subjunctive.

b2-18-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Is the Shop Closed?
b2-18-05.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks if the shop has closed. A neighbour says it closed last month, but nobody has confirmed it.
b2-18-05.prompt: Tell Meg what you heard, without saying it is certain.
cues: Say who told you that the shop closed
Say that it is not confirmed
b2-18-05.target: Según un vecino, la tienda cerró el mes pasado, pero al parecer nadie lo ha confirmado.
b2-18-05.english: According to a neighbour, the shop closed last month, but apparently nobody has confirmed it.
b2-18-05.canDo: I can report a claim without saying it is true, with según, al parecer, supuestamente and presunto.

b2-18-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Ana’s Book
b2-18-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what a classmate of yours said about a novel she read. She said it was very hard, admitted that she had taken a month to read it, and reminded you to read it slowly.
b2-18-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos what your classmate said about the novel.
cues: Report what she stated about the novel
Report what she admitted
Report what she reminded you to do
b2-18-consolidation.target: Mi compañera afirmó que la novela era muy difícil y admitió que había tardado un mes en leerla. Me recordó que la leyera con calma.
b2-18-consolidation.english: My classmate stated that the novel was very hard and admitted that she had taken a month to read it. She reminded me to read it calmly.
b2-18-consolidation.canDo: I can choose the reporting verb and the mood for statements, denials, warnings and reproaches.

b2-peruandino-01.title: Communicative Challenge: What Worries Scientists
b2-peruandino-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about the glaciers of the Cordillera Blanca, and he asks what the scientists worry about.
b2-peruandino-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what worries the scientists most, putting that idea in the spotlight.
cues: Start with what worries them
Say that it is the melting
b2-peruandino-01.target: Lo que más preocupa a los científicos es el deshielo.
b2-peruandino-01.english: What worries the scientists most is the melting.
b2-peruandino-01.canDo: I can put one idea in the spotlight with a cleft sentence (*Lo que..., Fue en... cuando...*).

b2-peruandino-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Before the Incas
b2-peruandino-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading an article about Caral, and she asks what existed before the Incas.
b2-peruandino-02.prompt: Tell Meg that before the Incas came, there were already cities in the Andes.
cues: Say what came first
Say that cities already existed
b2-peruandino-02.target: Antes de que llegaran los incas, ya había ciudades en los Andes.
b2-peruandino-02.english: Before the Incas arrived, there were already cities in the Andes.
b2-peruandino-02.canDo: I can order events with *antes de que* and *después de que* and the right mood.

b2-peruandino-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Quipus in the Empire
b2-peruandino-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading about the Inca empire for a short talk, and he asks how numbers were recorded.
b2-peruandino-03.prompt: Tell Carlos how numbers were recorded in the Inca empire, using the passive with se.
cues: Say what was used
Say what it was used for
b2-peruandino-03.target: En el imperio inca se usaban quipus para anotar números.
b2-peruandino-03.english: In the Inca empire quipus were used to record numbers.
b2-peruandino-03.canDo: I can say what was built, used or kept with the passive *se* (*se construyeron*, *se usaban*).

b2-peruandino-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Names Barely Known
b2-peruandino-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are visiting a talk about the Cusco School of painting, and she asks about the painters.
b2-peruandino-04.prompt: Tell Meg, with your own regret, that the names of many painters are barely known.
cues: Show how you feel about it
Say that the names are barely known
b2-peruandino-04.target: Lamentablemente, de muchos pintores apenas se conoce el nombre.
b2-peruandino-04.english: Unfortunately, the name of many painters is barely known.
b2-peruandino-04.canDo: I can show my attitude to a fact with stance adverbs (*lamentablemente*, *en rigor*, *precisamente*, *apenas*).

b2-peruandino-05.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Linguists Say
b2-peruandino-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading an article about Quechua, and he asks what the linguists say about young speakers.
b2-peruandino-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what several linguists point out about young speakers of Quechua in the cities.
cues: Report who says it
Say that young speakers are being lost
b2-peruandino-05.target: Varios lingüistas señalan que el quechua pierde hablantes jóvenes en las ciudades.
b2-peruandino-05.english: Several linguists point out that Quechua is losing young speakers in the cities.
b2-peruandino-05.canDo: I can report what experts and speakers say with reporting verbs (*señalar*, *afirmar*, *recordar*, *negar*).

b2-peruandino-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Andes in Review
b2-peruandino-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing a short talk about the Peruvian Andes, and she asks what road network the Incas built.
b2-peruandino-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg which road network the Incas built, putting the idea in the spotlight.
cues: Start with what it was
Name the road network
b2-peruandino-consolidation.target: Lo que construyeron los incas fue el Qhapaq Ñan.
b2-peruandino-consolidation.english: What the Incas built was the Qhapaq Ñan.
b2-peruandino-consolidation.canDo: I can put one idea in the spotlight with a cleft sentence (*Lo que..., Fue en... cuando...*) (review).

b2-19-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Agreements and Rules
b2-19-01.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what happened at the office today. Two agreements were signed and the new rules were published.
b2-19-01.prompt: Tell Meg what was signed and what was published.
cues: Say what was signed
Say what was published
b2-19-01.target: Hoy se firmaron dos acuerdos y se publicaron las reglas nuevas.
b2-19-01.english: Today two agreements were signed and the new rules were published.
b2-19-01.canDo: I can make the verb agree with the noun after passive se.

b2-19-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Customers in a Shop
b2-19-02.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks about a shop near your home. In that shop all the customers are served very quickly.
b2-19-02.prompt: Tell Carlos how the customers are served in the shop.
cues: Say who is served
Say how they are served
b2-19-02.target: En esa tienda se atiende a todos los clientes muy rápido.
b2-19-02.english: In that shop all the customers are served very quickly.
b2-19-02.canDo: I can tell passive se, which agrees with a thing, from impersonal se, which stays singular.

b2-19-03.title: Communicative Challenge: A Building Without a Name
b2-19-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks about a new building near the office. It was built in 1990, and you do not know who built it.
b2-19-03.prompt: Tell Meg when the building was built and say you do not know who built it.
cues: Say when it was built
Say you do not know who built it
b2-19-03.target: El edificio se construyó en 1990 y no sé quién lo construyó.
b2-19-03.english: The building was built in 1990 and I do not know who built it.
b2-19-03.canDo: I can leave out who did it when I use passive se.

b2-19-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Notice at the Door
b2-19-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what the notice at the door of the building says. It asks for silence and says that flats are for rent.
b2-19-04.prompt: Tell Carlos what the notice says.
cues: Say what the notice asks for
Say what is for rent
b2-19-04.target: El aviso dice que se ruega silencio y que se alquilan departamentos.
b2-19-04.english: The notice says that silence is requested and that flats are for rent.
b2-19-04.canDo: I can read and write short notices and instructions with se.

b2-19-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Lost Keys
b2-19-05.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks why you cannot open the door. You lost your keys in the street.
b2-19-05.prompt: Tell Meg what happened to your keys.
cues: Say that you lost them by accident
Say where
b2-19-05.target: Se me perdieron las llaves en la calle.
b2-19-05.english: I lost my keys in the street.
b2-19-05.canDo: I can tell reflexive, reciprocal, passive, impersonal and accidental se apart.

b2-19-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Text About a Novel
b2-19-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you read about the novel La ciudad y los perros. You read that it was published in 1963 and that it takes place in a military school.
b2-19-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos what you read about the novel.
cues: Say when it was published
Say what it talks about
b2-19-consolidation.target: Leí que la novela se publicó en 1963 y que ocurre en un colegio militar de Lima.
b2-19-consolidation.english: I read that the novel was published in 1963 and that it takes place in a military school in Lima.
b2-19-consolidation.canDo: I can make the verb agree with the noun after passive se, and keep it singular with no noun or with personal a.

b2-perucosta-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Why It Hardly Rains
b2-perucosta-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about Peru's coast, and he asks why it almost never rains there.
b2-perucosta-01.prompt: Tell Carlos why it hardly rains on the coast, giving the cause formally.
cues: Give the cause with a formal connector
Say that it hardly rains
b2-perucosta-01.target: Debido a la corriente fría, casi no llueve en la costa.
b2-perucosta-01.english: Because of the cold current, it hardly rains on the coast.
b2-perucosta-01.canDo: I can explain a cause formally with *debido a* and *a raíz de* + noun.

b2-perucosta-02.title: Communicative Challenge: When Lima Was Founded
b2-perucosta-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading about colonial Lima, and she asks when the city was founded.
b2-perucosta-02.prompt: Tell Meg when Lima was founded, using the passive.
cues: Say what was done
Give the date
b2-perucosta-02.target: Lima fue fundada el 18 de enero de 1535.
b2-perucosta-02.canDo: I can say what was founded, listed or proclaimed with the passive (*fue fundada*, *fueron incluidos*).

b2-perucosta-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Even If the Origin Is Unknown
b2-perucosta-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading about the cajón for a short talk, and he asks whether anyone knows how it was born.
b2-perucosta-03.prompt: Tell Carlos that even if its exact origin is not known, the cajón is part of Peruvian music.
cues: Grant the point about the origin
Say what the cajón is part of
b2-perucosta-03.target: Aun cuando no se sepa su origen exacto, el cajón es parte de la música peruana.
b2-perucosta-03.english: Even if its exact origin is not known, the cajón is part of Peruvian music.
b2-perucosta-03.canDo: I can grant a point with *aun cuando* + indicative or subjunctive.

b2-perucosta-04.title: Communicative Challenge: How Cebiche Is Served
b2-perucosta-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are planning to try Peruvian food, and she asks how cebiche is served.
b2-perucosta-04.prompt: Tell Meg how cebiche is served, using the passive with se.
cues: Say what is served
Say how it is served
b2-perucosta-04.canDo: I can choose between passive and impersonal *se* (*se sirven los cebiches*, *se invitó a los vecinos*).

b2-perucosta-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Report I Should Have Read
b2-perucosta-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are preparing a talk about the rubber boom, and he asks if you read Casement's report.
b2-perucosta-05.prompt: Tell Carlos that you regret not having read Casement's report earlier.
cues: Express your regret
Mention the report
b2-perucosta-05.target: Me arrepiento de no haber leído antes el informe de Casement.
b2-perucosta-05.english: I regret not having read Casement's report earlier.
b2-perucosta-05.canDo: I can express regrets and reproaches with *debería haber* and *me arrepiento de haber* + participle.

b2-perucosta-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Peru in Review
b2-perucosta-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing a short talk about Peru, and she asks how to explain that the coast has fewer fish in some years.
b2-perucosta-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg that because of El Niño there is less anchoveta, giving the cause formally.
cues: Give the cause with a formal connector
Say that there is less anchoveta
b2-perucosta-consolidation.target: Debido a El Niño, hay menos anchoveta en la costa.
b2-perucosta-consolidation.english: Because of El Niño, there is less anchoveta on the coast.
b2-perucosta-consolidation.canDo: I can explain a cause formally with *debido a* and *a raíz de* + noun (review).

b2-20-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The New Museum
b2-20-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks when the new museum is going to open. You know it will be officially opened next week.
b2-20-01.prompt: Tell Carlos when the museum will be opened.
cues: Say that the museum will be opened officially
Say when
b2-20-01.target: El museo será inaugurado la semana próxima.
b2-20-01.english: The museum will be opened next week.
b2-20-01.canDo: I can use the passive with *ser* in the preterite, the present perfect and the future.

b2-20-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Built the Bridge
b2-20-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks you who built the new bridge. You know that a local company built it.
b2-20-02.prompt: Tell Meg who built the bridge.
cues: Say that the bridge was built
Say who built it
b2-20-02.target: El puente fue construido por una empresa local.
b2-20-02.english: The bridge was built by a local company.
b2-20-02.canDo: I can name the doer of a passive with *por* when it is important.

b2-20-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Closed Restaurant
b2-20-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos wants to eat at the restaurant near the office. You know it was closed on Monday and it is still closed.
b2-20-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what happened to the restaurant and what its situation is now.
cues: Say when it was closed
Say that it is still closed
b2-20-03.target: El restaurante fue cerrado el lunes y todavía está cerrado.
b2-20-03.english: The restaurant was closed on Monday and it is still closed.
b2-20-03.canDo: I can use *estar* + participle to describe the result of an action.

b2-20-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Printed Report
b2-20-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks if the report is ready. You have already printed it.
b2-20-04.prompt: Tell Meg that you have printed the report.
cues: Say that you have already printed it
Say that it is ready on paper
b2-20-04.target: Ya he imprimido el informe y está impreso en papel.
b2-20-04.english: I have already printed the report and it is printed on paper.
b2-20-04.canDo: I can use the regular participle after *haber* with *imprimir*, *freír*, *proveer* and *elegir*.

b2-20-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Statement
b2-20-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks who wrote the statement about the new agreement. The mayor wrote it and it is already published.
b2-20-05.prompt: Tell Carlos who wrote the statement and what its situation is now.
cues: Say who wrote the statement
Say that it is already published
b2-20-05.target: El comunicado fue redactado por el alcalde y ya está publicado.
b2-20-05.english: The statement was written by the mayor and it is already published.
b2-20-05.canDo: I can choose between an active verb, the passive with *ser*, passive *se* and *estar* + participle.

b2-20-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Novel by Arguedas
b2-20-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what you read about Alcides Arguedas. You read that his novel was published in 1919 and is considered the first text of Bolivian indigenismo.
b2-20-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what you read about the novel.
cues: Say when the novel was published
Say what it is considered
b2-20-consolidation.target: La novela fue publicada en 1919 y es considerada el primer texto del indigenismo boliviano.
b2-20-consolidation.english: The novel was published in 1919 and it is considered the first text of Bolivian indigenismo.
b2-20-consolidation.canDo: I can read a short text about Alcides Arguedas and his novel Raza de bronce.

b2-boliviaaltiplano-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Lake That Keeps the Frost Away
b2-boliviaaltiplano-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about Lake Titicaca, and he asks why families can grow crops by the lake.
b2-boliviaaltiplano-01.prompt: Tell Carlos which families can grow potatoes and barley, and why.
cues: Say who can grow potatoes
Say that the lake softens the frosts
b2-boliviaaltiplano-01.target: Las familias que viven cerca del lago pueden cultivar papa porque el agua suaviza las heladas.
b2-boliviaaltiplano-01.english: The families who live near the lake can grow potatoes because the water softens the frosts.
b2-boliviaaltiplano-01.canDo: I can describe the high plateau and Lake Titicaca with relative clauses introduced by *que* and *quien*.

b2-boliviaaltiplano-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Mint Is Now a Museum
b2-boliviaaltiplano-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are planning a trip to Potosí, and she asks what is left of the Mint.
b2-boliviaaltiplano-02.prompt: Tell Meg what the Mint of Potosí is today.
cues: Say that the Mint is a museum now
Say what it was used for
b2-boliviaaltiplano-02.target: Hoy la Casa de la Moneda está convertida en museo, y allí se acuñaban monedas de plata.
b2-boliviaaltiplano-02.english: Today the Mint is turned into a museum, and silver coins were minted there.
b2-boliviaaltiplano-02.canDo: I can say what Potosí looks like today with *estar* + participle.

b2-boliviaaltiplano-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Not a District, a City
b2-boliviaaltiplano-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading an article about La Paz and El Alto, and he thinks El Alto is a district of La Paz.
b2-boliviaaltiplano-03.prompt: Correct Carlos: El Alto is not a district.
cues: Reject the idea that it is a district
Say what El Alto really is
b2-boliviaaltiplano-03.target: No es que El Alto sea un barrio de La Paz, sino que es una ciudad con su propio gobierno.
b2-boliviaaltiplano-03.english: It is not that El Alto is a district of La Paz; it is a city with its own government.
b2-boliviaaltiplano-03.canDo: I can correct a wrong idea about La Paz and El Alto with *no es que… sino que…*.

b2-boliviaaltiplano-04.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Government Says About Coca
b2-boliviaaltiplano-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing a talk about the coca leaf, and she asks what the Bolivian government says.
b2-boliviaaltiplano-04.prompt: Tell Meg the government's position, naming the source.
cues: Name who says it
Say that coca is not cocaine
b2-boliviaaltiplano-04.target: El gobierno boliviano dice que la coca tiene usos tradicionales y que no es cocaína.
b2-boliviaaltiplano-04.english: The Bolivian government says that coca has traditional uses and that it is not cocaine.
b2-boliviaaltiplano-04.canDo: I can say who says what about the coca leaf, using *según* and *dice que*.

b2-boliviaaltiplano-05.title: Communicative Challenge: However Much It Is Discussed
b2-boliviaaltiplano-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a talk about the Constitution of 2009, and he asks which languages it recognises.
b2-boliviaaltiplano-05.prompt: Tell Carlos the languages are official in spite of the debate.
cues: Grant that Spanish is spoken in the cities
Say that the indigenous languages are official too
b2-boliviaaltiplano-05.target: Por más que se hable castellano en las ciudades, los idiomas indígenas también son oficiales.
b2-boliviaaltiplano-05.english: However much Spanish is spoken in the cities, the indigenous languages are official too.
b2-boliviaaltiplano-05.canDo: I can grant a point and still state my main idea with *por más que* + subjunctive.

b2-boliviaaltiplano-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Bolivian Highlands in Review
b2-boliviaaltiplano-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing a short talk about the Bolivian highlands, and she asks where Titicaca lies.
b2-boliviaaltiplano-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg which lake Bolivia shares with Peru.
cues: Name the lake
Say which country shares it
b2-boliviaaltiplano-consolidation.target: El lago Titicaca es el lago que Bolivia comparte con Perú.
b2-boliviaaltiplano-consolidation.english: Lake Titicaca is the lake that Bolivia shares with Peru.
b2-boliviaaltiplano-consolidation.canDo: I can describe the high plateau and Lake Titicaca with relative clauses introduced by *que* and *quien* (review).

b2-21-01.title: Communicative Challenge: A Rumour at the Office
b2-21-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you have heard about the director. You heard a rumour that the director is resigning tomorrow.
b2-21-01.prompt: Tell Carlos the rumour you heard.
cues: Say that it is a rumour
Say what the director is doing
b2-21-01.target: Dicen que el director renuncia mañana.
b2-21-01.english: They say the director is resigning tomorrow.
b2-21-01.canDo: I can use a plural verb with no subject for rumours and for unknown doers.

b2-21-02.title: Communicative Challenge: When You Are Tired
b2-21-02.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what happens when you are tired. You answer with a general remark: when you are tired, you work worse.
b2-21-02.prompt: Make a general remark to Carlos about working when you are tired.
cues: Say when it happens
Say what happens to your work
b2-21-02.target: Cuando uno está cansado, trabaja peor.
b2-21-02.english: When you are tired, you work worse.
b2-21-02.canDo: I can choose between se, a plural verb and uno to say who is part of the statement.

b2-21-03.title: Communicative Challenge: What Worries People
b2-21-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what worries people in the city. You say that the rise in prices worries many people.
b2-21-03.prompt: Tell Meg what worries many people.
cues: Name the change
Say who it worries
b2-21-03.target: La subida de los precios preocupa a muchas personas.
b2-21-03.english: The rise in prices worries many people.
b2-21-03.canDo: I can turn a verb clause into a noun phrase, as in la subida de los precios.

b2-21-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Planning a Party
b2-21-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what is needed for the party. You say that everyone needs to bring something to eat.
b2-21-04.prompt: Tell Carlos what is needed for the party.
cues: Say that something is necessary
Say what each person brings
b2-21-04.target: Hace falta que cada uno traiga algo de comer.
b2-21-04.english: Everyone needs to bring something to eat.
b2-21-04.canDo: I can use hace falta que, basta con que and urge que with the subjunctive.

b2-21-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Is the Plan Working?
b2-21-05.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks whether the plan is working. You are not completely sure, so you soften your answer and suggest checking the schedule.
b2-21-05.prompt: Answer Meg carefully and suggest checking the schedule.
cues: Say how things seem
Suggest checking the schedule gently
b2-21-05.target: Parece que el plan funciona, pero tal vez convendría revisar el horario.
b2-21-05.english: It seems the plan is working, but perhaps it would be a good idea to check the schedule.
b2-21-05.canDo: I can soften a claim with parece que, según parece or podría decirse que.

b2-21-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Text About Céspedes
b2-21-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you read about Augusto Céspedes. You read that his book of stories was published in 1936.
b2-21-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos what you read about Céspedes and his book.
cues: Say what kind of book it is
Say when it was published
b2-21-consolidation.target: Leí que el libro de cuentos de Céspedes se publicó en 1936.
b2-21-consolidation.english: I read that Céspedes's book of stories was published in 1936.
b2-21-consolidation.canDo: I can use a plural verb, se or uno to speak about unnamed people.

b2-boliviaoriente-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Missions Were Founded by Jesuits
b2-boliviaoriente-01.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are watching a documentary about the Chiquitos missions, and she asks who founded them.
b2-boliviaoriente-01.prompt: Tell Meg who founded the missions and when the first one was founded.
cues: Say who founded the missions
Say the year of the first one
b2-boliviaoriente-01.target: Las misiones fueron fundadas por jesuitas, y la primera fue fundada en 1691.
b2-boliviaoriente-01.english: The missions were founded by Jesuits, and the first one was founded in 1691.
b2-boliviaoriente-01.canDo: I can say what was founded, expelled and restored with *ser* + past participle.

b2-boliviaoriente-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A Big City, but a Small Past
b2-boliviaoriente-02.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading an article about Santa Cruz, and he asks if it was always a big city.
b2-boliviaoriente-02.prompt: Tell Carlos that it is large today but was small before.
cues: Say that it is the largest city
Contrast it with its past
b2-boliviaoriente-02.target: Santa Cruz es hoy la ciudad más poblada de Bolivia; sin embargo, durante siglos fue una población pequeña.
b2-boliviaoriente-02.english: Santa Cruz is today the most populous city in Bolivia; however, for centuries it was a small town.
b2-boliviaoriente-02.canDo: I can contrast two ideas about Santa Cruz with *sin embargo*, *no obstante* and *aunque*.

b2-boliviaoriente-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Apparently, Still Without Approval
b2-boliviaoriente-03.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing a talk about lithium, and she asks about the contracts of 2024.
b2-boliviaoriente-03.prompt: Tell Meg, with a hedge, what the situation of the contracts is in 2026.
cues: Soften your claim
Say that Congress has not approved them
b2-boliviaoriente-03.target: Según parece, los contratos de 2024 todavía no tienen la aprobación del Congreso.
b2-boliviaoriente-03.english: Apparently, the contracts of 2024 still do not have the approval of Congress.
b2-boliviaoriente-03.canDo: I can soften a claim about lithium with *parece que*, *según parece* and *podría decirse que*.

b2-boliviaoriente-04.title: Communicative Challenge: If They Had Had More Water
b2-boliviaoriente-04.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are visiting a museum exhibition about the Chaco War, and he asks what made the war so hard.
b2-boliviaoriente-04.prompt: Tell Carlos what would have helped the soldiers.
cues: Start with a condition about the past
Say that they would have suffered less
b2-boliviaoriente-04.target: Si los soldados hubieran tenido más agua, habrían sufrido menos.
b2-boliviaoriente-04.english: If the soldiers had had more water, they would have suffered less.
b2-boliviaoriente-04.canDo: I can talk about a past that did not happen with *si* + *hubiera* + participle and *habría* + participle.

b2-boliviaoriente-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Dancers Who Wear Masks
b2-boliviaoriente-05.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are watching a video of the Oruro carnival, and she asks who the dancers in masks are.
b2-boliviaoriente-05.prompt: Tell Meg who the dancers with masks are playing.
cues: Describe the dancers
Say who they represent
b2-boliviaoriente-05.target: Los bailarines que llevan máscaras de diablos participan en la diablada.
b2-boliviaoriente-05.english: The dancers who wear devil masks take part in the diablada.
b2-boliviaoriente-05.canDo: I can describe the dances and the people of the Oruro carnival with *que*, *quien* and *donde*.

b2-boliviaoriente-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Lowlands in Review
b2-boliviaoriente-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are preparing a short talk about the Bolivian lowlands, and he asks when the missions were declared World Heritage Sites.
b2-boliviaoriente-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos when UNESCO declared the missions a World Heritage Site.
cues: Say what was declared
Say the year
b2-boliviaoriente-consolidation.target: Las seis misiones fueron declaradas Patrimonio de la Humanidad en 1990.
b2-boliviaoriente-consolidation.english: The six missions were declared World Heritage Sites in 1990.
b2-boliviaoriente-consolidation.canDo: I can say what was founded, expelled and restored with *ser* + past participle (review).

b2-22-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Bad News
b2-22-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks how everyone reacted when the news about the office arrived. The news was bad: everyone got sad and nobody said anything.
b2-22-01.prompt: Tell Carlos how everyone reacted to the bad news.
cues: Say what the news did to everyone
Say that everyone stayed quiet
b2-22-01.target: La noticia nos puso tristes y nos quedamos callados.
b2-22-01.english: The news made us sad and we fell silent.
b2-22-01.canDo: I can use *ponerse* for a sudden change and *quedarse* for the state that stays.

b2-22-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A Man Who Changed
b2-22-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks about a man in the news. He studied law and became a lawyer, and with the years he has become very serious.
b2-22-02.prompt: Tell Meg what happened to the man.
cues: Say what profession he chose
Say how his character changed
b2-22-02.target: El hombre estudió derecho y se hizo abogado, pero se ha vuelto muy serio.
b2-22-02.english: The man studied law and became a lawyer, but he has become very serious.
b2-22-02.canDo: I can use *hacerse* + noun for a profession or a choice.

b2-22-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Old Station
b2-22-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what happened to the old station near the centre. The city turned it into a hotel.
b2-22-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what happened to the old station.
cues: Say what the station was before
Say what the city turned it into
b2-22-03.target: La ciudad convirtió la estación vieja en un hotel.
b2-22-03.english: The city turned the old station into a hotel.
b2-22-03.canDo: I can use *convertirse en* and *transformarse en* with a noun.

b2-22-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Long Road
b2-22-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks about a woman in the news. She worked hard for ten years and ended up as the director of a school.
b2-22-04.prompt: Tell Meg how the woman ended up as director.
cues: Say how long she worked
Say what she ended up as
b2-22-04.target: Trabajó durante diez años y llegó a ser directora de una escuela.
b2-22-04.english: She worked for ten years and ended up as the director of a school.
b2-22-04.canDo: I can use *llegar a ser* for a result reached after a long road.

b2-22-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Speechless
b2-22-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks how a man reacted when he heard the news at the meeting. He turned pale and could not say a word.
b2-22-05.prompt: Tell Carlos how the man reacted.
cues: Say that he turned pale
Say that he was left speechless
b2-22-05.target: El hombre palideció y se quedó sin palabras.
b2-22-05.english: The man turned pale and was left speechless.
b2-22-05.canDo: I can choose the right verb of change by asking what kind of change it is.

b2-22-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Men and a Dangerous Gallery
b2-22-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks about the story by Baldomero Lillo that you read. Two men were left without work, and then they accepted jobs in a dangerous gallery.
b2-22-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what happened to the two men in the story.
cues: Say what happened to their jobs
Say what they decided
b2-22-consolidation.target: Los dos hombres se quedaron sin trabajo y aceptaron un puesto en una galería peligrosa.
b2-22-consolidation.english: The two men were left without work and accepted a job in a dangerous gallery.
b2-22-consolidation.canDo: I can read a short retelling of a story by Baldomero Lillo and notice the verbs of change in it.

b2-chilecentro-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Between Two Mountain Ranges
b2-chilecentro-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about Chile, and he asks where most Chileans live.
b2-chilecentro-01.prompt: Tell Carlos where the Central Valley lies, putting the place first.
cues: Start with the place
Say what lies there
b2-chilecentro-01.target: Entre los Andes y la cordillera de la Costa se extiende el Valle Central.
b2-chilecentro-01.english: The Central Valley lies between the Andes and the Coastal Range.
b2-chilecentro-01.canDo: I can put a place, a time or a quality first to stress it when I describe the Central Valley.

b2-chilecentro-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Means to Go Up the Hills
b2-chilecentro-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are planning a trip to Valparaíso, and she asks how people get up to the hills.
b2-chilecentro-02.prompt: Tell Meg what the funiculars are for the people of Valparaíso.
cues: Say that the funiculars are a means
Say that people go up the hills with them
b2-chilecentro-02.target: Los ascensores son el medio con el que los porteños suben a los cerros.
b2-chilecentro-02.english: The funiculars are the means with which the people of Valparaíso go up the hills.
b2-chilecentro-02.canDo: I can describe the places and ways of Valparaíso with *en la que*, *con el que* and other prepositions with *el que*.

b2-chilecentro-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Strictly Speaking, in Parral
b2-chilecentro-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading an article about Pablo Neruda, and he thinks the poet was born in Isla Negra.
b2-chilecentro-03.prompt: Correct Carlos with the exact truth about where Neruda was born.
cues: Show that you are being exact
Say where Neruda was born
b2-chilecentro-03.target: En rigor, Neruda no nació en Isla Negra, sino en Parral.
b2-chilecentro-03.english: Strictly speaking, Neruda was not born in Isla Negra but in Parral.
b2-chilecentro-03.canDo: I can show my attitude to a fact about the poets with stance adverbs such as *en realidad*, *en rigor* and *lamentablemente*.

b2-chilecentro-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Before the Planes Came
b2-chilecentro-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing a talk about 11 September 1973, and she asks what Allende did that morning.
b2-chilecentro-04.prompt: Tell Meg what Allende did before the planes bombed the palace.
cues: Say what Allende did
Say it was before the bombing
b2-chilecentro-04.target: Allende habló por radio antes de que los aviones bombardearan el palacio.
b2-chilecentro-04.english: Allende spoke on the radio before the planes bombed the palace.
b2-chilecentro-04.canDo: I can put events in order with *antes de que* + subjunctive and *después de que* + indicative.

b2-chilecentro-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Although the No Won
b2-chilecentro-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about the 1988 plebiscite, and he asks if Pinochet left office right away.
b2-chilecentro-05.prompt: Tell Carlos that the No won but Pinochet stayed until 1990.
cues: Grant that the No won
Say what happened next
b2-chilecentro-05.target: Si bien el plebiscito de 1988 lo ganó el No, Pinochet siguió en el cargo hasta 1990.
b2-chilecentro-05.english: Although the No won the 1988 plebiscite, Pinochet stayed in office until 1990.
b2-chilecentro-05.canDo: I can grant a point and say what matters more with *si bien* + indicative.

b2-chilecentro-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Central Chile in Review
b2-chilecentro-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing a short talk about central Chile, and she asks when Valparaíso became a World Heritage Site.
b2-chilecentro-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg the year in which UNESCO declared Valparaíso a World Heritage Site.
cues: Say the year
Say what UNESCO declared
b2-chilecentro-consolidation.target: En 2003 declaró la UNESCO Patrimonio de la Humanidad el casco histórico de Valparaíso.
b2-chilecentro-consolidation.english: It was in 2003 that UNESCO declared Valparaíso's historic quarter a World Heritage Site.
b2-chilecentro-consolidation.canDo: I can put a place, a time or a quality first to stress it when I describe the Central Valley (review).

b2-23-01.title: Communicative Challenge: A Sudden Reaction
b2-23-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks how you reacted when you heard some very good news. You were so happy that you started to laugh at once.
b2-23-01.prompt: Tell Carlos how you reacted to the good news.
cues: Say when it happened
Say that you suddenly started to laugh
b2-23-01.target: Cuando oí la buena noticia, me eché a reír.
b2-23-01.english: When I heard the good news, I burst out laughing.
b2-23-01.canDo: I can use *echarse a* + infinitive for a sudden reaction such as crying, laughing or running.

b2-23-02.title: Communicative Challenge: After Dinner
b2-23-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what you did after dinner yesterday. You sat down and started to read a book.
b2-23-02.prompt: Tell Meg what you did after dinner.
cues: Say when you did it
Say that you set about reading
b2-23-02.target: Después de cenar, me puse a leer un libro.
b2-23-02.english: After dinner, I started reading a book.
b2-23-02.canDo: I can use *ponerse a* + infinitive to say that someone sets about a task, a reaction or a change in the weather.

b2-23-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The End of the Concert
b2-23-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what happened at the end of a concert. After a moment of silence, everyone started to applaud.
b2-23-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what happened at the end of the concert.
cues: Say that there was a silence first
Say that everyone suddenly applauded
b2-23-03.target: Después de un momento de silencio, todos rompieron a aplaudir.
b2-23-03.english: After a moment of silence, everyone burst into applause.
b2-23-03.canDo: I can use *romper a* + infinitive for sounds, tears and rain that burst out.

b2-23-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Promise
b2-23-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg says you were late for the last meeting and asks if it will happen again. You promise it will not.
b2-23-04.prompt: Promise Meg that you will not be late again.
cues: Say that you promise
Say that you will not be late again
b2-23-04.target: Te prometo que no volveré a llegar tarde.
b2-23-04.english: I promise you I will not be late again.
b2-23-04.canDo: I can use *volver a* + infinitive to say that something happens again.

b2-23-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Next Part
b2-23-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what comes next in your talk. You have finished the first part and now you move on to the second part.
b2-23-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what you will do next in your talk.
cues: Say that the first part is finished
Say that you move on to explain the second part
b2-23-05.target: Ya terminé la primera parte; ahora paso a explicar la segunda.
b2-23-05.english: I have finished the first part; now I move on to explain the second.
b2-23-05.canDo: I can use *pasar a* + infinitive to move on to the next step of a talk, a task or a career.

b2-23-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Busy Morning
b2-23-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks how your morning went. You started working early, then moved on to your messages, and you did not look at your phone again until noon.
b2-23-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg how your morning went.
cues: Say that you set about working early
Say what you moved on to afterwards
Say that you did not look at your phone again
b2-23-consolidation.target: Me puse a trabajar temprano y después pasé a leer mis mensajes. No volví a mirar el teléfono hasta el mediodía.
b2-23-consolidation.english: I set about working early and then moved on to reading my messages. I did not look at my phone again until noon.
b2-23-consolidation.canDo: I can tell the sudden starts (*echarse a*, *ponerse a*, *romper a*) apart and choose the right one.

b2-chileextremos-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Sky of Atacama
b2-chileextremos-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about the Atacama Desert, and he asks why astronomers work there.
b2-chileextremos-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what makes Atacama special for astronomy.
cues: Say what makes the desert special for astronomers
Stress it with a cleft sentence
b2-chileextremos-01.target: Lo que hace especial a Atacama es su cielo despejado.
b2-chileextremos-01.english: What makes Atacama special is its clear sky.
b2-chileextremos-01.canDo: I can put one fact about Atacama in the spotlight with a cleft sentence (*lo que… es…*, *fue… cuando…*, *fue… donde…*).

b2-chileextremos-02.title: Communicative Challenge: How Copper Is Obtained
b2-chileextremos-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading an article about copper mining in northern Chile, and she asks how the copper is obtained.
b2-chileextremos-02.prompt: Tell Meg one step of how copper is obtained.
cues: Say what is done with the rock first
Do not say who does it
b2-chileextremos-02.target: Primero se rompe la roca y después se aplica la lixiviación.
b2-chileextremos-02.english: First the rock is broken, and then leaching is applied.
b2-chileextremos-02.canDo: I can describe how copper is obtained with the passive *se* (*se tritura la roca*, *se construyen plantas*).

b2-chileextremos-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Says What
b2-chileextremos-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about the Mapuche, and he asks you what the organisations in the film want.
b2-chileextremos-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what the Mapuche organisations say about the land.
cues: Name who says it
Say what they want
b2-chileextremos-03.target: Las organizaciones mapuche dicen que el Estado debe devolver las tierras.
b2-chileextremos-03.english: Mapuche organisations say that the state must return the land.
b2-chileextremos-03.canDo: I can report who says what with *según* and *dice que* when a subject is disputed.

b2-chileextremos-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Again in Patagonia
b2-chileextremos-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are planning a trip to southern Chile, and she asks if people visit Torres del Paine more than once.
b2-chileextremos-04.prompt: Tell Meg that many travellers go to the park again.
cues: Say that many travellers do it
Say that they visit the park a second time
b2-chileextremos-04.target: Muchos viajeros vuelven a visitar Torres del Paine.
b2-chileextremos-04.english: Many travellers visit Torres del Paine again.
b2-chileextremos-04.canDo: I can say that something happens again with *volver a* + infinitive (*el viento vuelve a soplar*, *no volverán a crecer*).

b2-chileextremos-05.title: Communicative Challenge: If There Were More Lines
b2-chileextremos-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading an article about solar energy in Chile, and he asks what the problem is.
b2-chileextremos-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what would happen with more transmission lines.
cues: Imagine more lines
Say what would improve
b2-chileextremos-05.target: Si hubiera más líneas de transmisión, se aprovecharía mejor la energía solar.
b2-chileextremos-05.english: If there were more transmission lines, solar energy would be used better.
b2-chileextremos-05.canDo: I can imagine a different situation with *si* + imperfect subjunctive + conditional (*si hubiera más líneas, se aprovecharía más energía*).

b2-chileextremos-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: From Atacama to Patagonia
b2-chileextremos-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg have watched a whole documentary about Chile, and she asks what surprised you most.
b2-chileextremos-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg one fact you learned, using a cleft sentence.
cues: Say where something is
Stress the place
b2-chileextremos-consolidation.target: Fue en el llano de Chajnantor donde se instaló ALMA.
b2-chileextremos-consolidation.english: It was on the Chajnantor plateau that ALMA was built.
b2-chileextremos-consolidation.canDo: I can talk about the extreme landscapes of Chile, from Atacama to Patagonia.

b2-24-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Years at the Office
b2-24-01.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks how long you have been working in your office in Budapest. You have been working there for six years.
b2-24-01.prompt: Tell Meg how long you have been working in your office.
cues: Say how long you have been working there
Say where you work
b2-24-01.target: Llevo seis años trabajando en una oficina de Budapest.
b2-24-01.english: I have been working in an office in Budapest for six years.
b2-24-01.canDo: I can say how long something has been going on with llevar, a length of time and a gerund.

b2-24-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Still Studying
b2-24-02.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks if you are still studying, although it is late. You are, and you still have not finished your work.
b2-24-02.prompt: Tell Carlos that you are still studying and that you have not finished your work.
cues: Say that you are still studying
Say that you still have not finished
b2-24-02.target: Sigo estudiando, aunque ya es tarde, y sigo sin terminar mi trabajo.
b2-24-02.english: I am still studying, although it is already late, and I still have not finished my work.
b2-24-02.canDo: I can say that something is still going on with seguir and a gerund, in the present and the past.

b2-24-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Step by Step
b2-24-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks how the project at your office is going. It is moving forward little by little, and you understand the work better.
b2-24-03.prompt: Tell Meg how the project is going.
cues: Say that the project is moving forward little by little
Say that you understand the work better
b2-24-03.target: El proyecto va avanzando poco a poco, y yo voy entendiendo mejor el trabajo.
b2-24-03.english: The project is moving forward little by little, and I am coming to understand the work better.
b2-24-03.canDo: I can say that something happens gradually with ir and a gerund.

b2-24-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Looking for a House
b2-24-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks why you have not answered his messages. You have been going around Budapest looking for a house.
b2-24-04.prompt: Tell Carlos why you have not answered his messages.
cues: Say that you are sorry
Say that you are going around the city looking for a house
b2-24-04.target: Perdón, es que ando buscando casa por toda la ciudad.
b2-24-04.english: Sorry, it is just that I am going around the whole city looking for a house.
b2-24-04.canDo: I can say that someone is going around doing something, here and there, with andar and a gerund.

b2-24-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Rising Prices
b2-24-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks how life in Budapest is lately. Prices have been going up for months.
b2-24-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what has been happening with prices.
cues: Say what has been going up
Say for how long, without counting the time
b2-24-05.target: Los precios vienen subiendo desde hace meses en Budapest.
b2-24-05.english: Prices have been going up for months in Budapest.
b2-24-05.canDo: I can say that something has been developing up to now with venir and a gerund.

b2-24-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Late Letter
b2-24-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks about your week. You have been waiting two weeks for a letter, and it still has not arrived.
b2-24-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg how long you have been waiting for the letter and that it has not arrived.
cues: Say how long you have been waiting
Say that the letter still has not arrived
b2-24-consolidation.target: Llevo dos semanas esperando una carta y sigo sin recibirla.
b2-24-consolidation.english: I have been waiting for a letter for two weeks and I still have not received it.
b2-24-consolidation.canDo: I can tell llevar, seguir, ir, andar and venir with a gerund apart.

b2-argentinaba-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The River and the Port
b2-argentinaba-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about Buenos Aires, and he asks why big ships anchored far from the shore.
b2-argentinaba-01.prompt: Tell Carlos why, with a formal phrase of cause.
cues: Say what the cause was
Use a formal phrase before the noun
b2-argentinaba-01.target: Debido a la poca profundidad del río, los barcos grandes anclaban lejos.
b2-argentinaba-01.english: Because of the shallow river, big ships anchored far away.
b2-argentinaba-01.canDo: I can describe how Buenos Aires grew along its river with formal phrases such as *mediante*, *debido a* and *a raíz de*.

b2-argentinaba-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A Neighbourhood Filling Up
b2-argentinaba-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading an article about the immigrants of Buenos Aires, and she asks what happened to the neighbourhoods.
b2-argentinaba-02.prompt: Tell Meg how the neighbourhood changed, step by step.
cues: Say what the neighbourhood was doing
Show that it was gradual
b2-argentinaba-02.target: El barrio se iba llenando de familias que venían de Italia y de España.
b2-argentinaba-02.english: The neighbourhood was gradually filling up with families from Italy and Spain.
b2-argentinaba-02.canDo: I can describe how a neighbourhood changed little by little with *ir*, *seguir* and *venir* + gerund.

b2-argentinaba-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Tango and the UNESCO
b2-argentinaba-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are listening to tango in a documentary, and he asks what UNESCO did with it.
b2-argentinaba-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what UNESCO did, naming who did it.
cues: Say what was declared
Name who declared it
b2-argentinaba-03.target: El tango fue declarado Patrimonio Cultural Inmaterial por la UNESCO en 2009.
b2-argentinaba-03.english: Tango was declared Intangible Cultural Heritage by UNESCO in 2009.
b2-argentinaba-03.canDo: I can say who or what did something in the history of tango with the passive *ser* + participle.

b2-argentinaba-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Cafés of Buenos Aires
b2-argentinaba-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg have read an article about the cafés and bookshops of Buenos Aires, and she asks for the main idea.
b2-argentinaba-04.prompt: Sum up the article for Meg and stress the main point.
cues: Start with a summary marker
Say what the places are for
b2-argentinaba-04.target: En resumen, los cafés y las librerías son lugares para conversar.
b2-argentinaba-04.english: In short, the cafés and bookshops are places to talk.
b2-argentinaba-04.canDo: I can sum up an argument and stress the main point with *en resumen* and *lo más importante es que*.

b2-argentinaba-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Readers of Borges
b2-argentinaba-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are talking about a talk on Borges and Cortázar, and he asks if people still read them.
b2-argentinaba-05.prompt: Guess whether someone is reading Borges right now in the city.
cues: Guess about the present
Mention a bookshop
b2-argentinaba-05.target: En una librería de la calle Corrientes habrá alguien comprando un libro de Borges.
b2-argentinaba-05.english: In a bookshop on Corrientes Street, someone is probably buying a book by Borges.
b2-argentinaba-05.canDo: I can guess about the present with the future of probability (*estará*, *habrá*, *serán*).

b2-argentinaba-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Buenos Aires in a Sentence
b2-argentinaba-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg have watched a whole documentary about Buenos Aires, and she asks what you liked best.
b2-argentinaba-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg one fact about the city, saying who did it.
cues: Say what was done
Name who did it
b2-argentinaba-consolidation.target: La canción fue cantada por Carlos Gardel.
b2-argentinaba-consolidation.english: The song was sung by Carlos Gardel.
b2-argentinaba-consolidation.canDo: I can talk about the history and culture of Buenos Aires, from the port to the tango.

b2-25-01.title: Communicative Challenge: A Promise to Call
b2-25-01.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks you to call her when you arrive. You promise that you will not forget.
b2-25-01.prompt: Promise Meg that you will call her when you arrive.
cues: Tell her not to worry
Promise that you will call her
b2-25-01.target: No te preocupes: no dejaré de llamarte cuando llegue.
b2-25-01.english: Do not worry: I will be sure to call you when I arrive.
b2-25-01.canDo: I can use *dejar de* + infinitive for things that stop and *no dejes de* for "be sure to".

b2-25-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Just Arrived
b2-25-02.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos phones and asks where you are. You have just arrived at the station and you will wait for him at the entrance.
b2-25-02.prompt: Tell Carlos where you are and where you will wait.
cues: Say that you have just arrived
Say where you will wait for him
b2-25-02.target: Acabo de llegar a la estación. Te espero en la entrada.
b2-25-02.english: I have just arrived at the station. I will wait for you at the entrance.
b2-25-02.canDo: I can use *acabar de* for what has just happened and *acababa de* for the scene behind a story.

b2-25-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The End of the Meeting
b2-25-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks how the meeting ended. There was a long discussion, and in the end everyone accepted the plan.
b2-25-03.prompt: Tell Meg how the meeting ended.
cues: Say that the discussion was long
Say that everyone finally accepted the plan
b2-25-03.target: Después de una larga discusión, todos terminaron por aceptar el plan.
b2-25-03.english: After a long discussion, everyone ended up accepting the plan.
b2-25-03.canDo: I can use *terminar por* and *acabar por* + infinitive for what happens in the end.

b2-25-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Tired Day
b2-25-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks why you look tired. Yesterday you were so tired that you even fell asleep in class.
b2-25-04.prompt: Tell Carlos why you look tired.
cues: Say how tired you were
Say what you even did in class
b2-25-04.target: Estaba tan cansada que llegué a dormirme en la clase.
b2-25-04.english: I was so tired that I even fell asleep in class.
b2-25-04.canDo: I can use *llegar a* + infinitive for getting as far as doing something.

b2-25-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Lost Keys
b2-25-05.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks about your keys. You looked for them all day and then gave them up for lost.
b2-25-05.prompt: Tell Meg what happened to your keys.
cues: Say that you looked for them all day
Say that you gave them up for lost
b2-25-05.target: Después de buscar todo el día, di por perdidas las llaves.
b2-25-05.english: After looking all day, I gave the keys up for lost.
b2-25-05.canDo: I can use *dar por* + participle to treat something as finished, lost or certain.

b2-25-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Way Home
b2-25-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks how your trip home was. You have just arrived home. You stopped waiting for the bus and in the end you went on foot.
b2-25-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos about your trip home.
cues: Say that you have just arrived
Say that you stopped waiting for the bus
Say that in the end you went on foot
b2-25-consolidation.target: Acabo de llegar a casa. Dejé de esperar el autobús y terminé por ir a pie.
b2-25-consolidation.english: I have just arrived home. I stopped waiting for the bus and ended up going on foot.
b2-25-consolidation.canDo: I can choose between *dejar de*, *acabar de*, *terminar por*, *llegar a* and *dar por*.

b2-argentinaregiones-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Look of the Pampa
b2-argentinaregiones-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about the pampas, and he asks what the landscape is like.
b2-argentinaregiones-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what the pampa looks like and what it really has.
cues: Grant that it looks flat
Say what it has in spite of that
b2-argentinaregiones-01.target: Si bien la pampa parece plana, tiene paisajes muy variados.
b2-argentinaregiones-01.english: Although the pampa looks flat, it has very varied landscapes.
b2-argentinaregiones-01.canDo: I can grant a true point formally with *si bien* (*si bien la pampa parece plana, tiene paisajes variados*).

b2-argentinaregiones-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Grape of Mendoza
b2-argentinaregiones-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading an article about the wines of Mendoza, and she asks about the Malbec grape.
b2-argentinaregiones-02.prompt: Tell Meg what happened to the Malbec grape over time.
cues: Say what the grape became
Say that it took time
b2-argentinaregiones-02.target: Con el tiempo, el malbec llegó a convertirse en la uva más conocida del país.
b2-argentinaregiones-02.english: In time, Malbec became the best-known grape of the country.
b2-argentinaregiones-02.canDo: I can say that something reaches a point or an extreme with *llegar a* + infinitive (*llegó a convertirse*, *si llega a faltar*).

b2-argentinaregiones-03.title: Communicative Challenge: A Dry Valley
b2-argentinaregiones-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about the Quebrada de Humahuaca, and he asks if people can live there.
b2-argentinaregiones-03.prompt: Tell Carlos that the valley is dry but people live there.
cues: Say that the valley is dry
Contrast it with a fact about the communities
b2-argentinaregiones-03.target: La quebrada es muy seca; sin embargo, allí viven muchas comunidades.
b2-argentinaregiones-03.english: The ravine is very dry; however, many communities live there.
b2-argentinaregiones-03.canDo: I can set one fact against another with *sin embargo* and *no obstante* (*la quebrada es seca; sin embargo, allí viven comunidades*).

b2-argentinaregiones-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Welsh Settlers
b2-argentinaregiones-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading an article about Patagonia, and she asks why the Welsh settlers did not leave.
b2-argentinaregiones-04.prompt: Tell Meg that the settlers stayed despite the climate.
cues: Name the difficulty
Say what the settlers did
b2-argentinaregiones-04.target: A pesar de las dificultades del clima, los colonos galeses se quedaron.
b2-argentinaregiones-04.english: Despite the difficulties of the climate, the Welsh settlers stayed.
b2-argentinaregiones-04.canDo: I can say that something happened despite a difficulty with *a pesar de*, *a pesar de que* and *pese a*.

b2-argentinaregiones-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Train at the End of the World
b2-argentinaregiones-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are planning a trip to Ushuaia after a documentary, and he asks about the old train.
b2-argentinaregiones-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what became of the old train.
cues: Say what the train became
Show that it took a long process
b2-argentinaregiones-05.target: El viejo tren terminó por convertirse en una atracción turística.
b2-argentinaregiones-05.english: The old train ended up as a tourist attraction.
b2-argentinaregiones-05.canDo: I can say how a process ended with *terminar por* and *acabar por* + infinitive (*el tren terminó por convertirse en una atracción turística*).

b2-argentinaregiones-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: From the Pampas to the South
b2-argentinaregiones-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg have watched a whole documentary about Argentina, and she asks what surprised you.
b2-argentinaregiones-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg one thing that surprised you about Patagonia, with a contrast.
cues: Name the difficulty
Say what the Welsh settlers did all the same
b2-argentinaregiones-consolidation.target: A pesar de las dificultades del clima, los colonos galeses se quedaron en Patagonia y abrieron canales.
b2-argentinaregiones-consolidation.english: In spite of the difficult climate, the Welsh settlers stayed in Patagonia and dug canals.
b2-argentinaregiones-consolidation.canDo: I can talk about the regions of Argentina, from the pampas to Tierra del Fuego.

b2-26-01.title: Communicative Challenge: A Guess From the Evidence
b2-26-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos says that his boss is not answering the phone. You guess that the boss is in a meeting.
b2-26-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what you guess about his boss.
cues: Say that he is not answering
Guess where he is, with deber de
b2-26-01.target: Tu jefe no contesta; debe de estar en una reunión.
b2-26-01.english: Your boss is not answering; he must be in a meeting.
b2-26-01.canDo: I can use deber + infinitive for a duty and deber de + infinitive for a guess.

b2-26-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A Formal Duty
b2-26-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what you must do before Friday. You must hand in a report, and you want to say it in a formal way, with haber de.
b2-26-02.prompt: Tell Meg, in a formal way, what you must do before Friday.
cues: Say what you must hand in
Say when
b2-26-02.target: He de entregar el informe antes del viernes.
b2-26-02.english: I must hand in the report before Friday.
b2-26-02.canDo: I can use haber de + infinitive for a formal duty.

b2-26-03.title: Communicative Challenge: A Need and Its Reason
b2-26-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks you to come out tonight. You cannot, because you have to study and you have a lot of work.
b2-26-03.prompt: Tell Carlos that you cannot come and why.
cues: Say that you are sorry
Say what you have to do and give the reason
b2-26-03.target: Lo siento, tengo que estudiar porque tengo mucho trabajo.
b2-26-03.english: I am sorry, I have to study because I have a lot of work.
b2-26-03.canDo: I can use tener que for a need that comes from the situation, and give the reason.

b2-26-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Rule at the Door
b2-26-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks how to get into your office building. The rule is the same for everybody: you have to show a card at the door.
b2-26-04.prompt: Tell Meg the rule for getting into the building.
cues: Say what the rule is
Say where you have to show it
b2-26-04.target: Para entrar a la oficina hay que mostrar la tarjeta en la puerta.
b2-26-04.english: To get into the office you have to show the card at the door.
b2-26-04.canDo: I can use hay que for a rule or a need that is the same for everyone.

b2-26-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Will It Rain?
b2-26-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks if you will take an umbrella today in Budapest. There are many clouds, so it may rain this afternoon.
b2-26-05.prompt: Tell Carlos that it may rain and why you think so.
cues: Say that it may rain this afternoon, with puede que
Give the reason
b2-26-05.target: Puede que llueva esta tarde, porque hay muchas nubes.
b2-26-05.english: It may rain this afternoon, because there are many clouds.
b2-26-05.canDo: I can guess with deber de, poder and tener que, and show how sure I am.

b2-26-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: People Outside the Office
b2-26-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks why people are waiting outside your office. You guess that there is a meeting, and everybody has to wait outside.
b2-26-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what you guess and what everybody has to do.
cues: Guess why the people are there
Say what everybody has to do
b2-26-consolidation.target: Debe de haber una reunión y hay que esperar fuera.
b2-26-consolidation.english: There must be a meeting and you have to wait outside.
b2-26-consolidation.canDo: I can tell deber, deber de, haber de, tener que and hay que apart.

b2-argentinasociedad-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Views of Peronism
b2-argentinasociedad-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about Peronism, and he asks what you learned about Perón's government.
b2-argentinasociedad-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what supporters liked and what critics said, joined by a contrast connector.
cues: Say that the government extended rights
Add what critics said, with a contrast connector
b2-argentinasociedad-01.target: Se ampliaron los derechos laborales; no obstante, los críticos decían que el gobierno limitaba la prensa.
b2-argentinasociedad-01.english: Labour rights were extended; nevertheless, the critics said the government limited the press.
b2-argentinasociedad-01.canDo: I can set two views of Peronism side by side with *sin embargo* and *no obstante*.

b2-argentinasociedad-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The CONADEP
b2-argentinasociedad-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You have read an article about the last dictatorship, and Meg asks what the CONADEP was.
b2-argentinasociedad-02.prompt: Tell Meg who created the CONADEP and when, using a passive.
cues: Say who created it
Say in which year
b2-argentinasociedad-02.target: La CONADEP fue creada por el presidente Alfonsín en 1983.
b2-argentinasociedad-02.english: The CONADEP was created by President Alfonsín in 1983.
b2-argentinasociedad-02.canDo: I can say what was done to people and institutions under the dictatorship with *ser* + participle.

b2-argentinasociedad-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Search of the Abuelas
b2-argentinasociedad-03.scenario: You are Meg. You are reading about the Abuelas de Plaza de Mayo for a class, and Carlos asks what they do.
b2-argentinasociedad-03.prompt: Tell Carlos whom the Abuelas are looking for.
cues: Say that they look for grandchildren
Say that those people may not know their origin
b2-argentinasociedad-03.target: Las Abuelas buscan a nietos que no conozcan su verdadero origen.
b2-argentinasociedad-03.english: The Abuelas look for grandchildren who may not know their true origin.
b2-argentinasociedad-03.canDo: I can describe the people the Abuelas de Plaza de Mayo are looking for with a relative clause and the subjunctive.

b2-argentinasociedad-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Maradona
b2-argentinasociedad-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are watching a documentary about the 1986 World Cup, and she asks why Maradona is so famous.
b2-argentinasociedad-04.prompt: Tell Meg about Maradona, with a superlative.
cues: Say that he is one of the most famous players
Say in which World Cup Argentina won with him
b2-argentinasociedad-04.target: Maradona es uno de los jugadores más famosos de la historia, y en 1986 ganó el Mundial con Argentina.
b2-argentinasociedad-04.english: Maradona is one of the most famous players in history, and in 1986 he won the World Cup with Argentina.
b2-argentinasociedad-04.canDo: I can rank moments and people of Argentine football with *uno de los más…*.

b2-argentinasociedad-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Corralito
b2-argentinasociedad-05.scenario: You are Meg. You are giving a short talk about the crisis of 2001, and Carlos asks why people were angry.
b2-argentinasociedad-05.prompt: Tell Carlos why people could not use their money, with a cause connector.
cues: Say that there was a limit on withdrawals
Say what people could not do with their savings
