b2-argentinasociedad-05.target: Debido al corralito, mucha gente no podía sacar sus ahorros del banco.
b2-argentinasociedad-05.english: Because of the corralito, many people could not take their savings out of the bank.
b2-argentinasociedad-05.canDo: I can give the causes of the 2001 crisis with *debido a* and *a raíz de*.

b2-argentinasociedad-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Argentina in Brief
b2-argentinasociedad-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You are preparing a short talk about modern Argentina, and Meg asks you to try the first lines.
b2-argentinasociedad-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg one fact about Peronism, using a contrast connector.
cues: Say that Peronism was banned
Add that it stayed alive, with a contrast connector
b2-argentinasociedad-consolidation.target: Tras el golpe de 1955, el peronismo fue prohibido; sin embargo, siguió vivo entre los obreros.
b2-argentinasociedad-consolidation.english: After the 1955 coup Peronism was banned; however, it stayed alive among workers.
b2-argentinasociedad-consolidation.canDo: I can set two views of Peronism side by side with *sin embargo* and *no obstante* (review).

b2-27-01.title: Communicative Challenge: After the Accident
b2-27-01.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks why the city changed its traffic rules last month. They changed the rules because of an accident.
b2-27-01.prompt: Tell Meg why the city changed the traffic rules.
cues: Say what set the change off
Say what the city changed
b2-27-01.target: A raíz de un accidente, la ciudad cambió las normas de tráfico.
b2-27-01.english: Following an accident, the city changed its traffic rules.
b2-27-01.canDo: I can use *a raíz de* for an event that sets something off.

b2-27-02.title: Communicative Challenge: According to the Report
b2-27-02.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks if more tourists come to the city this year. A report says that the number went up.
b2-27-02.prompt: Tell Carlos what the report says about the tourists.
cues: Name the source of the information
Say what has changed this year
b2-27-02.target: De acuerdo con el informe, el número de turistas subió este año.
b2-27-02.english: According to the report, the number of tourists rose this year.
b2-27-02.canDo: I can use *de acuerdo con* and *según* to name a source.

b2-27-03.title: Communicative Challenge: At What Cost?
b2-27-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks why two neighbours stopped arguing. They both gave way for the sake of peace.
b2-27-03.prompt: Tell Meg why the two neighbours stopped arguing.
cues: Say that they gave way
Say what they did it for
b2-27-03.target: Los dos vecinos cedieron en aras de la paz.
b2-27-03.english: The two neighbours gave way for the sake of peace.
b2-27-03.canDo: I can use *en aras de* for the aim someone gives something up for.

b2-27-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The New Timetable
b2-27-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you think of the new timetable. You think it is better than the old one.
b2-27-04.prompt: Give Carlos your opinion of the new timetable.
cues: Make clear that this is your opinion
Compare it with the old timetable
b2-27-04.target: A mi juicio, el nuevo horario es mejor que el anterior.
b2-27-04.english: In my opinion, the new timetable is better than the old one.
b2-27-04.canDo: I can use *a juicio de* to give someone's opinion.

b2-27-05.title: Communicative Challenge: What Is the Book About?
b2-27-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what a book is about. It is about two brothers and a problem between them.
b2-27-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what the book is about.
cues: Say what the book is about
Say who the problem is between
b2-27-05.target: Se trata de un problema entre dos hermanos.
b2-27-05.english: It is about a problem between two brothers.
b2-27-05.canDo: I can use *consistir en*, *derivar en*, *tratarse de* and *abogar por* with the right preposition.

b2-27-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Snakes' Congress
b2-27-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks about the story by Horacio Quiroga that you read. The snakes held a congress, and they chose the culebra Ñacaniná to go to the Casa and see what the men were doing.
b2-27-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what the snakes did in the story.
cues: Say what the snakes held
Say who went to the Casa
b2-27-consolidation.target: Las serpientes hicieron un congreso y enviaron a la Ñacaniná a la Casa.
b2-27-consolidation.english: The snakes held a congress and sent the Ñacaniná to the Casa.
b2-27-consolidation.canDo: I can read a short retelling of the start of Horacio Quiroga's Anaconda.

b2-uruguay-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Why the Schools Are Free
b2-uruguay-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about Uruguay, and he asks why public school there is free.
b2-uruguay-01.prompt: Tell Carlos the reason, with a cause connector.
cues: Mention the reform of Varela
Say that public school is free and compulsory
b2-uruguay-01.target: A raíz de la reforma de Varela, la escuela pública es gratuita y obligatoria.
b2-uruguay-01.english: As a result of Varela's reform, public school is free and compulsory.
b2-uruguay-01.canDo: I can give reasons for the reforms of the 1900s with *debido a* and *a raíz de*.

b2-uruguay-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Candombe and UNESCO
b2-uruguay-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You have read an article about candombe, and Meg asks what UNESCO did in 2009.
b2-uruguay-02.prompt: Tell Meg what UNESCO did and what it was for.
cues: Say that UNESCO included candombe in its list
Say what it was for, with a purpose phrase
b2-uruguay-02.target: La UNESCO incluyó el candombe en su lista con el fin de ayudar a protegerlo.
b2-uruguay-02.english: UNESCO included candombe in its list in order to help protect it.
b2-uruguay-02.canDo: I can say what a tradition or a decision is for with *con miras a* and *con el fin de*.

b2-uruguay-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Plebiscite of 1980
b2-uruguay-03.scenario: You are Meg. You are giving a short talk about Uruguay, and Carlos asks what happened in 1980.
b2-uruguay-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what the military wanted and what the result was.
cues: Say what the military wanted to approve and how
Say who won the vote
b2-uruguay-03.target: Los militares quisieron aprobar una Constitución mediante un plebiscito, pero ganó el «No».
b2-uruguay-03.english: The military wanted to approve a constitution by means of a plebiscite, but the "No" won.
b2-uruguay-03.canDo: I can say how something was done in politics with *mediante*.

b2-uruguay-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Plan Ceibal
b2-uruguay-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading about Uruguay's schools, and she asks how the Plan Ceibal changed over time.
b2-uruguay-04.prompt: Tell Meg what the plan went on to include.
cues: Say that the plan changed with time
Say that it went on to include secondary students
b2-uruguay-04.target: Con el tiempo, el Plan Ceibal pasó a incluir a los alumnos de secundaria.
b2-uruguay-04.english: In time, the Plan Ceibal went on to include secondary students.
b2-uruguay-04.canDo: I can say what a policy went on to include with *pasar a* + infinitive.

b2-uruguay-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Mate in Montevideo
b2-uruguay-05.scenario: You are Meg. You watched a documentary about Montevideo, and Carlos asks what struck you.
b2-uruguay-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what you noticed about the mate.
cues: Say that you noticed something
Say what many people carry
b2-uruguay-05.target: Me di cuenta de que muchos uruguayos llevan un termo bajo el brazo.
b2-uruguay-05.english: I realised that many Uruguayans carry a thermos under their arm.
b2-uruguay-05.canDo: I can describe getting used to life in Montevideo with *acostumbrarse a* and *darse cuenta de*.

b2-uruguay-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Uruguay in Brief
b2-uruguay-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You are preparing a short talk about Uruguay, and Meg asks you to try one sentence about 1980.
b2-uruguay-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg how Uruguayans rejected the military's constitution.
cues: Say the year
Say how it was done, with a formal phrase
b2-uruguay-consolidation.target: En 1980, mediante un plebiscito, los uruguayos rechazaron la Constitución propuesta por los militares.
b2-uruguay-consolidation.english: In 1980, by means of a plebiscite, Uruguayans rejected the constitution proposed by the military.
b2-uruguay-consolidation.canDo: I can say how something was done in politics with *mediante* (review).

b2-28-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Planning a Talk
b2-28-01.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks how you will organise your short talk at the office. You will speak about three points: the price, the date and the place.
b2-28-01.prompt: Tell Meg the order of the three points of your talk.
cues: Say what you will talk about first
Say the second point
Say what comes last
b2-28-01.target: En primer lugar, hablaré del precio; en segundo lugar, de la fecha; por último, del lugar.
b2-28-01.english: First, I will talk about the price; second, about the date; lastly, about the place.
b2-28-01.canDo: I can order the points of a talk with en primer lugar, en segundo lugar and por último.

b2-28-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A Side Remark
b2-28-02.scenario: You are Meg. You are telling Carlos about the plan for the weekend and you suddenly remember something: you need to know if he has the tickets.
b2-28-02.prompt: Tell Carlos your plan and add a side remark with a question.
cues: Say what you plan to do
Add a side remark with a question about the tickets
b2-28-02.target: Mañana vamos al cine; por cierto, ¿ya compraste los boletos?
b2-28-02.english: Tomorrow we are going to the cinema; by the way, have you already bought the tickets?
b2-28-02.canDo: I can add a side remark with por cierto, a propósito (de) and dicho sea de paso.

b2-28-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Moving On
b2-28-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks about Saturday's dinner. You have just settled the date, and now you divide the food and the drinks between you.
b2-28-03.prompt: Tell Meg that the date is settled, then say who takes the food and who takes the drinks.
cues: Move on from the date to the next point
Say who takes the food
Say who takes the drinks
b2-28-03.target: Pues bien, ya tenemos la fecha. En cuanto a la comida, yo cocino; en cuanto a las bebidas, las traes tú.
b2-28-03.english: Well then, we have the date. As for the food, I will cook; as for the drinks, you bring them.
b2-28-03.canDo: I can move on to the next step with pues bien.

b2-28-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Sides of Living Downtown
b2-28-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you think about living in the centre of Budapest. You see two sides: it is comfortable, and it is expensive.
b2-28-04.prompt: Give Carlos the two sides of living in the centre.
cues: Give the first side
Give the second side
b2-28-04.target: Por una parte, vivir en el centro es cómodo; por otra, es caro.
b2-28-04.english: On the one hand, living in the centre is comfortable; on the other, it is expensive.
b2-28-04.canDo: I can set two sides of a point against each other with por una parte … por otra.

b2-28-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Closing an Opinion
b2-28-05.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what you think of the plan to have dinner at home on Saturday. The plan is cheap and easy.
b2-28-05.prompt: Give Meg your opinion of the plan and close with a final judgement.
cues: Say why the plan is good
Close your opinion with a closing marker
b2-28-05.target: El plan es barato y fácil. En definitiva, me parece una buena idea.
b2-28-05.english: The plan is cheap and easy. All in all, I think it is a good idea.
b2-28-05.canDo: I can close a text with en resumen, en conclusión, en definitiva or en suma.

b2-28-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Telling the Plan in Order
b2-28-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks you to tell him the plan for Saturday in order and then to sum it up.
b2-28-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos the plan in order and close with a summary.
cues: Give the three steps in order
Close with a summary
b2-28-consolidation.target: En primer lugar, compramos la comida; en segundo lugar, cocinamos; por último, cenamos. En resumen, será una noche tranquila.
b2-28-consolidation.english: First, we buy the food; second, we cook; lastly, we have dinner. To sum up, it will be a quiet evening.
b2-28-consolidation.canDo: I can structure a short talk from a first point to a closing summary.

b2-paraguay-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Languages
b2-paraguay-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about Paraguay, and he thinks Spanish is the only official language.
b2-paraguay-01.prompt: Correct Carlos with a stance adverb.
cues: Correct what he assumed
Say which languages are official
b2-paraguay-01.target: En realidad, Paraguay tiene dos lenguas oficiales: el español y el guaraní.
b2-paraguay-01.english: In fact, Paraguay has two official languages: Spanish and Guaraní.
b2-paraguay-01.canDo: I can correct an assumption about Guaraní and Spanish with stance adverbs such as *en realidad* and *en rigor*.

b2-paraguay-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Views of the Missions
b2-paraguay-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading about the Jesuit missions, and she asks what historians say.
b2-paraguay-02.prompt: Tell Meg two views of the missions, joined by a contrast connector.
cues: Say what some historians think
Add the opposite view, with a connector
b2-paraguay-02.target: Según algunos historiadores, las misiones protegieron a los guaraníes; sin embargo, otros dicen que los jesuitas controlaban su vida.
b2-paraguay-02.english: According to some historians, the missions protected the Guaraní; however, others say the Jesuits controlled their lives.
b2-paraguay-02.canDo: I can set two views of the Jesuit missions side by side with *sin embargo*, *no obstante* and *aunque*.

b2-paraguay-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Fortress of Humaitá
b2-paraguay-03.scenario: You are Meg. You are giving a short talk about the Triple Alliance War, and Carlos asks about the fortress of Humaitá.
b2-paraguay-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what happened to the fortress and when.
cues: Say what happened to the fortress
Give the year
b2-paraguay-03.target: La fortaleza de Humaitá fue tomada por las fuerzas aliadas en 1868.
b2-paraguay-03.english: The fortress of Humaitá was taken by the allied forces in 1868.
b2-paraguay-03.canDo: I can say what was signed, taken or occupied in the Triple Alliance War with *ser* + participle.

b2-paraguay-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Mennonites in the Chaco
b2-paraguay-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are talking about the Chaco, and you want to add a side remark.
b2-paraguay-04.prompt: Add a short side remark about the Mennonites.
cues: Mark it as a side remark
Say when they arrived
b2-paraguay-04.target: A propósito de los menonitas, llegaron al Chaco en 1927.
b2-paraguay-04.english: Speaking of the Mennonites, they arrived in the Chaco in 1927.
b2-paraguay-04.canDo: I can add a side remark about the Chaco with *por cierto* or *a propósito de* and come back to my point.

b2-paraguay-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Guampa
b2-paraguay-05.scenario: You are Meg. You watched a documentary about tereré, and Carlos asks what a guampa is.
b2-paraguay-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what the guampa is, with a relative clause.
cues: Say that it is a cup
Say what is served in it
b2-paraguay-05.target: La guampa es el vaso en el que se sirve el tereré.
b2-paraguay-05.english: The guampa is the cup in which tereré is served.
b2-paraguay-05.canDo: I can describe tereré and the guarania with *en el que*, *con la que* and *del que*.

b2-paraguay-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Paraguay in Brief
b2-paraguay-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You are preparing a short talk about Paraguay, and Meg asks you to try one sentence on the languages.
b2-paraguay-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg one exact fact about Guaraní, with a stance adverb.
cues: Start with a stance adverb
Say since when it is official
b2-paraguay-consolidation.target: En rigor, el guaraní es lengua oficial desde 1992.
b2-paraguay-consolidation.english: Strictly speaking, Guaraní has been an official language since 1992.
b2-paraguay-consolidation.canDo: I can correct an assumption about Guaraní and Spanish with stance adverbs such as *en realidad* and *en rigor* (review).

b2-29-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Saying It Another Way
b2-29-01.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what it means that tomorrow's meeting is optional.
b2-29-01.prompt: Explain to Meg what it means that the meeting is optional, restating it in other words.
cues: Say that the meeting is optional
Restate it with a marker for other words
b2-29-01.target: La reunión es opcional; en otras palabras, nadie tiene que ir.
b2-29-01.english: The meeting is optional; in other words, nobody has to go.
b2-29-01.canDo: I can restate an idea with es decir, o sea, en otras palabras and dicho de otro modo.

b2-29-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A Quick Correction
b2-29-02.scenario: You are Meg. You tell Carlos which day you arrived, but you say the wrong day and correct yourself. You arrived on Tuesday.
b2-29-02.prompt: Tell Carlos the day you arrived and correct yourself.
cues: Say the wrong day first (Monday)
Correct yourself with the right day (Tuesday)
b2-29-02.target: Llegué el lunes; mejor dicho, el martes.
b2-29-02.english: I arrived on Monday; or rather, on Tuesday.
b2-29-02.canDo: I can correct myself with mejor dicho.

b2-29-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Going Out Anyway
b2-29-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg says it may rain tomorrow. You still want to go out for a walk.
b2-29-03.prompt: Answer Meg: the rain does not change your plan.
cues: Mention the possible rain
Say that you will go for a walk anyway
b2-29-03.target: Puede que llueva; de todas formas, vamos a salir a caminar.
b2-29-03.english: It may rain; anyway, we are going out for a walk.
b2-29-03.canDo: I can say that a doubt does not change what follows, with de todos modos, de todas formas and en cualquier caso.

b2-29-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Plan in One Sentence
b2-29-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos says your explanation of the plan for Saturday was long and asks for the main idea. The plan is cheap and easy.
b2-29-04.prompt: Give Carlos the main idea of the plan in one short sentence.
cues: Use a marker that promises a short sentence
Say what the plan is like
b2-29-04.target: En pocas palabras, el plan es barato y fácil.
b2-29-04.english: In a few words, the plan is cheap and easy.
b2-29-04.canDo: I can condense a long explanation into one short sentence with en pocas palabras and resumiendo.

b2-29-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Ways to Save
b2-29-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks how you can save money. There are many ways.
b2-29-05.prompt: Tell Carlos there are many ways to save and give one example.
cues: Say there are many ways to save
Give one example with a marker
b2-29-05.target: Hay muchas formas de ahorrar; por ejemplo, puedes cocinar en casa.
b2-29-05.english: There are many ways to save; for example, you can cook at home.
b2-29-05.canDo: I can give an example with por ejemplo, así and como.

b2-29-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Change of Plan
b2-29-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks when you leave for the outing at the weekend. You get the day wrong, correct yourself, and say that you are going anyway.
b2-29-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos the day you leave, correct yourself, and say you are going anyway.
cues: Say the wrong day (Friday)
Correct yourself with the right day (Saturday)
Say that you are going anyway
b2-29-consolidation.target: Salimos el viernes; mejor dicho, el sábado. De todas formas, vamos a ir.
b2-29-consolidation.english: We leave on Friday; or rather, on Saturday. Anyway, we are going.
b2-29-consolidation.canDo: I can choose between restating an idea, correcting myself and brushing a doubt aside.

b2-brasilsudeste-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Why São Paulo Grew
b2-brasilsudeste-01.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are watching a documentary about São Paulo, and she asks how the city got rich in the 19th century.
b2-brasilsudeste-01.prompt: Tell Meg how São Paulo became rich, then say the same thing more plainly.
cues: Say that the city grew thanks to coffee
Restate it: coffee money paid for the railway
b2-brasilsudeste-01.target: São Paulo creció gracias al café; es decir, el dinero del café pagó el ferrocarril.
b2-brasilsudeste-01.english: São Paulo grew thanks to coffee; that is, the coffee money paid for the railway.
b2-brasilsudeste-01.canDo: I can restate an idea about São Paulo with *es decir*, *o sea* or *en otras palabras*.

b2-brasilsudeste-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Hills and Bay
b2-brasilsudeste-02.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are planning a trip and reading about Rio de Janeiro, and he asks what you learned about the royal court.
b2-brasilsudeste-02.prompt: Tell Carlos which city the Portuguese royal family settled in during 1808.
cues: Say that it was a city, using a relative clause
Give the year the family arrived
b2-brasilsudeste-02.target: La ciudad donde se instaló la familia real portuguesa en 1808 era Río de Janeiro.
b2-brasilsudeste-02.english: The city where the Portuguese royal family settled in 1808 was Rio de Janeiro.
b2-brasilsudeste-02.canDo: I can describe places in Rio with relative clauses such as *que*, *donde* and *cuyo*.

b2-brasilsudeste-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Week of 1922
b2-brasilsudeste-03.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing a short talk on Brazilian modernism, and she asks when the Modern Art Week took place.
b2-brasilsudeste-03.prompt: Tell Meg when and where the Modern Art Week was held, using a passive with *se*.
cues: Say that it was held in São Paulo
Give the year
b2-brasilsudeste-03.target: La Semana de Arte Moderna se celebró en São Paulo en 1922.
b2-brasilsudeste-03.english: The Modern Art Week was held in São Paulo in 1922.
b2-brasilsudeste-03.canDo: I can tell the different jobs of *se* in a text about the Modern Art Week of 1922.

b2-brasilsudeste-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Bossa Nova Facts
b2-brasilsudeste-04.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are listening to bossa nova and he thinks it came from the favelas.
b2-brasilsudeste-04.prompt: Correct Carlos: bossa nova began in apartments in the south of Rio.
cues: Correct what he assumes, with a stance adverb
Say where it began
b2-brasilsudeste-04.target: En realidad, la bossa nova nació en apartamentos de la zona sur de Río.
b2-brasilsudeste-04.english: In fact, bossa nova began in apartments in the south of Rio.
b2-brasilsudeste-04.canDo: I can add my view of a fact about Brazilian music with adverbs such as *en realidad* and *precisamente*.

b2-brasilsudeste-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Learning Portuguese
b2-brasilsudeste-05.scenario: You are Meg. You are telling Carlos how learning Portuguese is going after reading about the neighbour languages.
b2-brasilsudeste-05.prompt: Tell Carlos that the more you read in Portuguese, the more you understand.
cues: Use a *cuanto más* structure
Say that you understand more
b2-brasilsudeste-05.target: Cuanto más leo en portugués, más entiendo.
b2-brasilsudeste-05.english: The more I read in Portuguese, the more I understand.
b2-brasilsudeste-05.canDo: I can link two changes about learning Portuguese with *cuanto más ..., más ...* and *a medida que*.

b2-brasilsudeste-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Brazil in Review
b2-brasilsudeste-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing a short talk about Brazil's southeast, and she asks you to explain what the coffee railway meant for São Paulo.
b2-brasilsudeste-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg that coffee made São Paulo rich, then say it again in other words.
cues: Say that coffee made the city rich
Restate it in other words
b2-brasilsudeste-consolidation.target: El café hizo rica a São Paulo; en otras palabras, la ciudad creció gracias al café.
b2-brasilsudeste-consolidation.english: Coffee made São Paulo rich; in other words, the city grew thanks to coffee.
b2-brasilsudeste-consolidation.canDo: I can restate an idea about Brazil with *es decir*, *o sea* or *en otras palabras*.

b2-30-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Cafés
b2-30-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks which café is cheaper. The café on the square is expensive, but the one on the corner is cheap.
b2-30-01.prompt: Tell Carlos how the two cafés differ.
cues: Say that the café on the square is expensive
Say that the café on the corner is cheap
b2-30-01.target: El café de la plaza es caro; el de la esquina, en cambio, es barato.
b2-30-01.english: The café on the square is expensive; the one on the corner, on the other hand, is cheap.
b2-30-01.canDo: I can use *en cambio* to set two different things side by side.

b2-30-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Not the Cinema
b2-30-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks if you went to the cinema on Saturday. You did not go to the cinema: you went to the theatre.
b2-30-02.prompt: Tell Meg where you did not go and where you went.
cues: Say that you did not go to the cinema
Say where you went instead
b2-30-02.target: No fui al cine, sino al teatro.
b2-30-02.english: I did not go to the cinema, but to the theatre.
b2-30-02.canDo: I can use *sino* and *sino que* after a negative to replace an idea.

b2-30-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Out in the Rain
b2-30-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks if you went out in the rain yesterday. It was raining hard, but you went out all the same.
b2-30-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what the weather was like and what you did anyway.
cues: Say that it was raining hard
Say that you went out all the same
b2-30-03.english: It was raining hard; even so, I went out.
b2-30-03.canDo: I can use *aun así* to say that something happens in spite of a difficulty.

b2-30-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Life in the Centre
b2-30-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what you think about living in the centre of Budapest. It is convenient, but it is also very noisy.
b2-30-04.prompt: Tell Meg the good point and the bad point of living in the centre.
cues: Say what is good about the centre
Say what is bad about it
b2-30-04.target: Por un lado, el centro es cómodo; por otro, es muy ruidoso.
b2-30-04.english: On the one hand, the centre is convenient; on the other, it is very noisy.
b2-30-04.canDo: I can use *por un lado … por otro* to weigh an advantage and a drawback.

b2-30-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Book on Loan
b2-30-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks to borrow a book. You say yes, but he must bring it back on Monday.
b2-30-05.prompt: Tell Carlos that he can borrow the book, and on what condition.
cues: Say that you lend him the book
Say that he must return it on Monday
b2-30-05.target: Te presto el libro; eso sí, lo devuelves el lunes.
b2-30-05.english: I'll lend you the book; mind you, you give it back on Monday.
b2-30-05.canDo: I can use *eso sí* to accept something and add a condition.

b2-30-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Book about a War
b2-30-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what you read about Euclides da Cunha. He was a newspaper correspondent in the war of Canudos, but he did not only write articles: he wrote a book about the war.
b2-30-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what Da Cunha did with what he saw, and contrast it with what a correspondent usually does.
cues: Say what a correspondent usually writes
Contrast it with what Da Cunha wrote
b2-30-consolidation.target: Un corresponsal suele escribir artículos; Da Cunha, en cambio, escribió un libro sobre la guerra de Canudos.
b2-30-consolidation.english: A correspondent usually writes articles; Da Cunha, on the other hand, wrote a book about the war of Canudos.
b2-30-consolidation.canDo: I can read a short text about Euclides da Cunha and his book Los sertones.

b2-brasilnordeste-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Sides of Salvador
b2-brasilnordeste-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about Salvador, and he says the old port was mostly in the high part of the city.
b2-brasilnordeste-01.prompt: Correct Carlos: the Lower City is the port, and the Upper City is on the cliff, as a comparison.
cues: Say that the Lower City is the port
Compare it with the Upper City
b2-brasilnordeste-01.target: La Ciudad Baja es el puerto; la Ciudad Alta, en cambio, está sobre el acantilado.
b2-brasilnordeste-01.english: The Lower City is the port; the Upper City, on the other hand, is on the cliff.
b2-brasilnordeste-01.canDo: I can set one idea about Salvador against another with *en cambio*, *por el contrario*, *al contrario*, *no obstante* and *ahora bien*.

b2-brasilnordeste-02.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Drums Are For
b2-brasilnordeste-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are watching a documentary about Candomblé, and she asks why the drums are played in the ceremony.
b2-brasilnordeste-02.prompt: Tell Meg, as the tradition says, that the drums are played so that the orixá arrives.
cues: Say that the drums are played
Give the purpose with *para que*
b2-brasilnordeste-02.target: Según la tradición, se tocan los atabaques para que el orixá llegue al terreiro.
b2-brasilnordeste-02.english: According to the tradition, the drums are played so that the orixá arrives at the terreiro.
b2-brasilnordeste-02.canDo: I can say what something is for with *para que* + subjunctive, about Candomblé and capoeira.

b2-brasilnordeste-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Drought
b2-brasilnordeste-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading about the sertão, and he asks why so many families left it.
b2-brasilnordeste-03.prompt: Tell Carlos, as a guess about the past, that if it had rained more many families would not have left.
cues: Use *si hubiera* + participle
Say what would not have happened
b2-brasilnordeste-03.target: Si hubiera llovido más, muchas familias no habrían salido del sertão.
b2-brasilnordeste-03.english: If it had rained more, many families would not have left the sertão.
b2-brasilnordeste-03.canDo: I can say what would have happened in a different past with *si hubiera* + participle and *habría* + participle, about the sertão.

b2-brasilnordeste-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Remembering Zumbi
b2-brasilnordeste-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading about Palmares, and she asks what happened after the first expeditions.
b2-brasilnordeste-04.prompt: Tell Meg that the army attacked the quilombo again in 1694.
cues: Say that the army attacked
Use *volver a* to say it happened again, with the year
b2-brasilnordeste-04.target: El ejército volvió a atacar el quilombo en 1694.
b2-brasilnordeste-04.english: The army attacked the quilombo again in 1694.
b2-brasilnordeste-04.canDo: I can say that something happened again with *volver a* + infinitive, about Palmares and Zumbi.

b2-brasilnordeste-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Quota Law
b2-brasilnordeste-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are preparing a short talk, and he asks what the law of 2012 changed in universities.
b2-brasilnordeste-05.prompt: Tell Carlos that, as a result of the 2012 law, federal universities reserve places for public school students.
cues: Use *a raíz de* + noun
Say what the universities do
b2-brasilnordeste-05.target: A raíz de la ley de 2012, las universidades federales reservan plazas para estudiantes de escuelas públicas.
b2-brasilnordeste-05.english: As a result of the 2012 law, federal universities reserve places for public school students.
b2-brasilnordeste-05.canDo: I can explain a cause in a formal way with *debido a* and *a raíz de*, about race and equality in Brazil.

b2-brasilnordeste-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Northeast in Review
b2-brasilnordeste-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing a talk, and she asks you to compare the two levels of Salvador.
b2-brasilnordeste-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what existed in the interior of the Northeast in the 17th century and what happened to its leader.
cues: Say what existed and where
Say when its leader died
b2-brasilnordeste-consolidation.target: En el siglo XVII existió en el interior del Nordeste el Quilombo dos Palmares, y en 1695 murió su líder, Zumbi.
b2-brasilnordeste-consolidation.english: In the 17th century the Quilombo dos Palmares existed in the interior of the Northeast, and in 1695 its leader, Zumbi, died.
b2-brasilnordeste-consolidation.canDo: I can set one idea about Salvador against another with *en cambio*, *por el contrario*, *al contrario*, *no obstante* and *ahora bien* (review).

b2-31-01.title: Communicative Challenge: A Closed Museum
b2-31-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks why you did not see the museum. The museum was closed when you arrived, and you could not go in.
b2-31-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what happened at the museum and what followed.
cues: Say the museum was closed
Say what you could not do, with a formal result marker
b2-31-01.target: El museo estaba cerrado; por consiguiente, no pudimos entrar.
b2-31-01.english: The museum was closed; consequently, we could not go in.
b2-31-01.canDo: I can use *por lo tanto*, *por consiguiente* and *en consecuencia* to state a result.

b2-31-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A Crowded Party
b2-31-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks about the party you went to on Saturday. There were a lot of people, and you could not talk.
b2-31-02.prompt: Tell Meg how crowded the party was and what it led to.
cues: Say there were many people
Say the result, with que
b2-31-02.target: Había tanta gente que no pudimos hablar.
b2-31-02.english: There were so many people that we could not talk.
b2-31-02.canDo: I can say a result with *tan* … *que* and *tanto* … *que*.

b2-31-03.title: Communicative Challenge: A Quick Coffee
b2-31-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos says he is going to the bar to order another coffee. You would like a tea.
b2-31-03.prompt: Ask Carlos for a tea, giving his plan as the reason.
cues: Mention that he is going to the bar
Ask him for a tea
b2-31-03.target: Ya que vas a la barra, pídeme un té.
b2-31-03.english: Since you are going to the bar, get me a tea.
b2-31-03.canDo: I can give a known reason with *ya que*, *puesto que* and *dado que*.

b2-31-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Traffic in the City
b2-31-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks why so many people cycle to work in Budapest. There is a lot of traffic in the centre.
b2-31-04.prompt: Explain to Meg why many people cycle.
cues: Say there is a lot of traffic
Say that is why many people cycle
b2-31-04.target: Hay mucho tráfico; de ahí que mucha gente vaya en bicicleta.
b2-31-04.english: There is a lot of traffic; hence a lot of people cycle.
b2-31-04.canDo: I can draw a conclusion with *así pues* and *entonces*.

b2-31-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Missed Message
b2-31-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks why you did not answer his message. You did not have your phone.
b2-31-05.prompt: Explain to Carlos why you did not answer.
cues: Start with a marker that introduces an explanation
Say you did not have your phone
b2-31-05.target: Es que no tenía el teléfono.
b2-31-05.english: The thing is that I did not have my phone.
b2-31-05.canDo: I can justify myself with *es que*.

b2-31-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Why Not Yesterday?
b2-31-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks why you did not come yesterday. You had a lot of work, so you stayed at the office.
b2-31-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg why you did not come and what you did instead.
cues: Say you had a lot of work
Say the result, with a connector
b2-31-consolidation.target: Tenía mucho trabajo, así que me quedé en la oficina.
b2-31-consolidation.english: I had a lot of work, so I stayed at the office.
b2-31-consolidation.canDo: I can read a short text about Clarice Lispector and her novel.

b2-brasilinterior-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The New Capital
b2-brasilinterior-01.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are planning a trip and reading about Brasília, and she asks whether the city was built slowly.
b2-brasilinterior-01.prompt: Tell Meg how much the city grew and what resulted from it.
cues: Say how much the city grew
Say where more people live today
b2-brasilinterior-01.target: La ciudad creció tanto que hoy vive más gente en las ciudades satélite que en el Plano Piloto.
b2-brasilinterior-01.english: The city grew so much that more people now live in the satellite cities than in the Plano Piloto.
b2-brasilinterior-01.canDo: I can say how much, or in what way, something happened and what resulted, with *tan ... que*, *tanto ... que* and *de tal manera que*, about Brasília.

b2-brasilinterior-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Rubber and the Theatre
b2-brasilinterior-02.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about Manaus, and he asks what happened to the city when rubber lost its price.
b2-brasilinterior-02.prompt: Tell Carlos what happened to the economy of the region when the price of rubber fell.
cues: Use *cuando* + preterite
Say the economy went into crisis
b2-brasilinterior-02.target: Cuando bajó el precio del caucho, la economía de la región entró en crisis.
b2-brasilinterior-02.english: When the price of rubber fell, the economy of the region went into crisis.
b2-brasilinterior-02.canDo: I can link two events or two actions in the Amazon with *cuando* and *mientras*.

b2-brasilinterior-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Xingu Park
b2-brasilinterior-03.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing a talk on indigenous lands, and she asks what the Villas-Bôas brothers achieved.
b2-brasilinterior-03.prompt: Tell Meg what the 1988 Constitution says the State must do about indigenous lands, in a formal way.
cues: Name the Constitution
Say what the State must respect
b2-brasilinterior-03.target: Según la Constitución de 1988, el Estado ha de respetar las tierras que los indígenas ocupan tradicionalmente.
b2-brasilinterior-03.english: According to the 1988 Constitution, the State is to respect the lands that indigenous peoples have traditionally occupied.
b2-brasilinterior-03.canDo: I can state a duty or a story's "was to" formally with *haber de* + infinitive, about indigenous lands.

b2-brasilinterior-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Soy and Water
b2-brasilinterior-04.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading about the Cerrado, and he says it was always a rich farming region.
b2-brasilinterior-04.prompt: Correct Carlos: for centuries it was thought poor, but today it produces a lot of soy, as a comparison.
cues: Say that it was thought poor
Compare it with today
b2-brasilinterior-04.target: Durante siglos se consideró una región pobre; hoy, en cambio, produce mucha soja.
b2-brasilinterior-04.english: For centuries it was considered a poor region; today, on the other hand, it produces a lot of soy.
b2-brasilinterior-04.canDo: I can set one idea about the Cerrado against another with *en cambio*, *por el contrario*, *al contrario*, *no obstante* and *ahora bien*.

b2-brasilinterior-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Bridge and Roads
b2-brasilinterior-05.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are following the news about the bioceanic corridor, and she asks whether the road is finished.
b2-brasilinterior-05.prompt: Tell Meg that the bridge was joined in July 2026 but the access roads are due in 2027.
cues: Say the bridge is joined
Contrast it with the access roads, using *aunque*
b2-brasilinterior-05.target: Aunque el puente se unió en julio de 2026, los accesos terminarán en 2027.
b2-brasilinterior-05.english: Although the bridge was joined in July 2026, the access roads will be finished in 2027.
b2-brasilinterior-05.canDo: I can set facts against each other with *sin embargo*, *aunque* and *no obstante*, about Brazil and its neighbours.

b2-brasilinterior-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Brazil's Interior in Review
b2-brasilinterior-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are preparing a short talk about Brazil's interior, and he asks what you remember about Brasília.
b2-brasilinterior-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos when Brasília was inaugurated and who designed its main buildings.
cues: Say when the city was inaugurated
Say who designed its main buildings
b2-brasilinterior-consolidation.target: Brasilia fue inaugurada el 21 de abril de 1960, y Oscar Niemeyer proyectó sus principales edificios.
b2-brasilinterior-consolidation.english: Brasília was inaugurated on 21 April 1960, and Oscar Niemeyer designed its main buildings.
b2-brasilinterior-consolidation.canDo: I can review what I learned about Brasília, the Amazon, the Cerrado and Itamaraty.

b2-32-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Saving Money
b2-32-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks whether you manage to save money each month. You do: you always have something left.
b2-32-01.prompt: Tell Carlos that something is left, however little you save.
cues: Say however little you save
Say you will have something left
b2-32-01.target: Por poco que ahorres, algo te quedará.
b2-32-01.english: However little you save, you will have something left.
b2-32-01.canDo: I can use *por poco que* for "however little".

b2-32-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Telling the Truth
b2-32-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks whether you will tell a friend the truth. You will, and you know you could lose the friend.
b2-32-02.prompt: Tell Meg you will say it, and what you risk.
cues: Say you will tell the truth
Say the risk, with an expression for 'even at the risk of'
b2-32-02.target: Voy a decírselo, aun a riesgo de perder a un amigo.
b2-32-02.english: I am going to tell him, even at the risk of losing a friend.
b2-32-02.canDo: I can use *aun a riesgo de* with an infinitive or with *que* + subjunctive.

b2-32-03.title: Communicative Challenge: A Firm Decision
b2-32-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos says his boss thinks the plan is not possible. You are going to try anyway.
b2-32-03.prompt: Tell Carlos that you will try, whatever the boss says.
cues: Say whatever the boss says
Say you are going to try
b2-32-03.target: Diga lo que diga, vamos a intentarlo.
b2-32-03.english: Whatever he says, we are going to try.
b2-32-03.canDo: I can use *cueste lo que cueste*, *pase lo que pase* and *diga lo que diga*.

b2-32-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Making Coffee
b2-32-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks how you want him to make the coffee. You do not mind how.
b2-32-04.prompt: Tell Carlos he can make it however he likes.
cues: Say he can make it however he likes
Say it is all the same to you
b2-32-04.target: Prepara el café como quieras; me da igual.
b2-32-04.english: Make the coffee however you like; it is all the same to me.
b2-32-04.canDo: I can use *como* + verb for "the way" and "however".

b2-32-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Warm Greeting
b2-32-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks about the new neighbour. He greeted you in a friendly way, although you had never met.
b2-32-05.prompt: Tell Carlos how the neighbour spoke to you.
cues: Say he spoke to you
Compare it with something imagined, with 'as if'
b2-32-05.target: Me habló como si me conociera.
b2-32-05.english: He spoke to me as if he knew me.
b2-32-05.canDo: I can use *como si* + imperfect subjunctive for something imagined.

b2-32-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Doing It Your Way
b2-32-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks how you will write the report for your boss. You will do it as it seems best to you.
b2-32-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg how you will do it.
cues: Say you will write the report
Say you will choose how, as it seems best to you
b2-32-consolidation.target: Voy a hacer el informe según me parezca mejor.
b2-32-consolidation.english: I am going to write the report as seems best to me.
b2-32-consolidation.canDo: I can read a short text about Rómulo Gallegos and his novel.

b2-amazoniapan-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Why a Treaty
b2-amazoniapan-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading about the Amazon Cooperation Treaty, and he asks why the countries created a permanent secretariat.
b2-amazoniapan-01.prompt: Tell Carlos that the countries created a secretariat so that cooperation would be permanent.
cues: Say they created a secretariat
Give the purpose with *para que*
b2-amazoniapan-01.target: Los países crearon una secretaría para que la cooperación fuera permanente.
b2-amazoniapan-01.english: The countries created a secretariat so that cooperation would be permanent.
b2-amazoniapan-01.canDo: I can say what an agreement or a meeting is for with *para que* + subjunctive, about the Amazon Treaty.

b2-amazoniapan-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Open Border
b2-amazoniapan-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading about Leticia and Tabatinga, and she asks whether a fence divides the cities.
b2-amazoniapan-02.prompt: Tell Meg that there is no fence that separates the two cities.
cues: Say there is no fence
Use *que* + subjunctive
b2-amazoniapan-02.target: No hay ninguna valla que separe las dos ciudades.
b2-amazoniapan-02.english: There is no fence that separates the two cities.
b2-amazoniapan-02.canDo: I can tell a real thing from one that is only wanted or does not exist with *que* + indicative or subjunctive, about the Amazon borders.

b2-amazoniapan-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Andes and the Rain
b2-amazoniapan-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a talk about the Amazon's water cycle, and he asks why the humid air goes south.
b2-amazoniapan-03.prompt: Tell Carlos that, because of the Andes, the humid air turns south.
cues: Use *debido a* + noun
Say where the air goes
b2-amazoniapan-03.target: Debido a los Andes, el aire húmedo se desvía hacia el sur.
b2-amazoniapan-03.english: Because of the Andes, the humid air turns south.
b2-amazoniapan-03.canDo: I can give a cause in a formal way with *debido a* and *a raíz de*, about the Amazon's water cycle.

b2-amazoniapan-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Mercury in the River
b2-amazoniapan-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading a report about mercury, and she asks what the presence of mercury in fish suggests.
b2-amazoniapan-04.prompt: Tell Meg that if the fish have mercury there must be mines nearby, as a guess.
cues: Say the fish have mercury
Give your guess with *debe de*
b2-amazoniapan-04.target: Si los peces tienen mercurio, debe de haber minas cerca.
b2-amazoniapan-04.english: If the fish have mercury, there must be mines nearby.
b2-amazoniapan-04.canDo: I can say how sure I am with *puede*, *debe de* and *tiene que* + infinitive, about mercury in the Amazon rivers.

b2-amazoniapan-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Different Past
b2-amazoniapan-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading about the standing forest, and he asks what difference less logging would have made.
b2-amazoniapan-05.prompt: Tell Carlos that if fewer trees had been cut down in the last century there would be more forest today.
cues: Use *si hubiera* + participle
Say what there would be today
b2-amazoniapan-05.target: Si no se hubieran talado tantos árboles en el siglo XX, hoy habría más bosque.
b2-amazoniapan-05.english: If so many trees had not been cut down in the 20th century, there would be more forest today.
b2-amazoniapan-05.canDo: I can say how a different past would change the present with *si hubiera* + participle and the conditional, about the Amazon.

b2-amazoniapan-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Amazon in Review
b2-amazoniapan-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing a short talk about the Amazon basin, and she asks you to describe the border between the two cities.
b2-amazoniapan-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what eight countries signed in 1978 and why.
cues: Say what they signed and when
Say what it was for
b2-amazoniapan-consolidation.target: Ocho países firmaron en 1978 el Tratado de Cooperación Amazónica para trabajar juntos.
b2-amazoniapan-consolidation.english: Eight countries signed the Amazon Cooperation Treaty in 1978 to work together.
b2-amazoniapan-consolidation.canDo: I can review what I learned about the Amazon basin, from the treaty to the standing forest.

b2-33-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Lending a Bike
b2-33-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks if he can use your bike. You will lend it, but he must look after it.
b2-33-01.prompt: Tell Carlos you will lend him the bike on one strict condition.
cues: Say yes
Say the condition, that he looks after it
b2-33-01.target: Sí, te la presto siempre y cuando la cuides.
b2-33-01.english: Yes, I will lend it to you provided that you look after it.
b2-33-01.canDo: I can use *siempre y cuando* + subjunctive for a strict condition.

b2-33-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A Trip to the Countryside
b2-33-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks about the plan for Sunday. You will go to the countryside unless the weather is bad.
b2-33-02.prompt: Tell Meg the plan and the one exception.
cues: Say you will go to the countryside
Say the one exception, the rain
b2-33-02.target: Vamos al campo el domingo a no ser que llueva.
b2-33-02.english: We are going to the countryside on Sunday unless it rains.
b2-33-02.canDo: I can use *a menos que*, *a no ser que* and *salvo que* + subjunctive.

b2-33-03.title: Communicative Challenge: An Unanswered Call
b2-33-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos says a colleague of his does not answer the phone. You draw a conclusion from that.
b2-33-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what you conclude if the colleague does not answer.
cues: Say what is true: she does not answer
Say your conclusion about her
b2-33-03.english: If she does not answer, she must be busy.
b2-33-03.canDo: I can use *si* + indicative to mean "if it is true that".

b2-33-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Friendly Warning
b2-33-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg often arrives late. You warn her that, if she is late again, you will not let her in.
b2-33-04.prompt: Warn Meg about arriving late again.
cues: Say the condition, in the warning form
Say what will happen
b2-33-04.target: Como llegues tarde otra vez, no te dejo entrar.
b2-33-04.english: If you arrive late again, I won't let you in.
b2-33-04.canDo: I can use *como* + present subjunctive to warn someone.

b2-33-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Missed Party
b2-33-05.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg tells you a friend's party was great. You did not go, because nobody told you about it.
b2-33-05.prompt: Tell Meg what you wish about the party.
cues: Say what you wish you had done
Say you would have gone, had you known
b2-33-05.target: Ojalá hubiera ido; de haberlo sabido, habría ido.
b2-33-05.english: I wish I had gone; had I known, I would have gone.
b2-33-05.canDo: I can use *ojalá* + pluperfect subjunctive for a wish about the past.

b2-33-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Condition and an Exception
b2-33-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks whether you will help with her move. You will help only if she tells you the day, unless you have to work.
b2-33-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg the condition and the exception.
cues: Say you will help only if she tells you the day
Say the exception, that you have to work
b2-33-consolidation.target: Te ayudo solo si me dices el día, salvo que tenga que trabajar.
b2-33-consolidation.english: I will help you only if you tell me the day, unless I have to work.
b2-33-consolidation.canDo: I can read a short text about Julio Cortázar and his novel.

b2-integracion-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Rule for Changing the Tariff
b2-integracion-01.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading an article about Mercosur, and she asks when the common tariff can change.
b2-integracion-01.prompt: Tell Meg when the common tariff can change.
cues: Say that the tariff does not change
Say what all the partners have to do first
b2-integracion-01.target: El arancel común no cambia a menos que todos los socios estén de acuerdo.
b2-integracion-01.english: The common tariff does not change unless all the partners agree.
b2-integracion-01.canDo: I can state a condition with *siempre que*, *con tal de que* or *a menos que*.

b2-integracion-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A Day in Lima
b2-integracion-02.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading about the Pacific Alliance, and he asks what you would have liked to see.
b2-integracion-02.prompt: Tell Carlos what you would have seen on 28 April 2011.
cues: Say where you would have been
Say what you would have seen
b2-integracion-02.target: Hubiera estado en Lima el 28 de abril de 2011, habría visto la firma de la Declaración de Lima.
b2-integracion-02.english: Had I been in Lima on 28 April 2011, I would have seen the signing of the Lima Declaration.
b2-integracion-02.canDo: I can say what would have happened in a past situation, with *hubiera* + past participle and no *si*.

b2-integracion-03.title: Communicative Challenge: A Very Deep Port
b2-integracion-03.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are watching a documentary about the port of Chancay, and she asks why it matters.
b2-integracion-03.prompt: Tell Meg what is special about the depth of the port.
cues: Say that the port is deep
Say what that depth allows
b2-integracion-03.target: El puerto de Chancay es tan profundo que recibe barcos muy grandes.
b2-integracion-03.english: The port of Chancay is so deep that it receives very large ships.
b2-integracion-03.canDo: I can say how much of something led to a result, with *tan … que*, *tanto … que* and *de tal manera que*.

b2-integracion-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Paraguay's Share of Itaipú
b2-integracion-04.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading an article about the Itaipú power station, and he asks what happens when Paraguay uses more electricity.
b2-integracion-04.prompt: Tell Carlos how the surplus changes as Paraguay's consumption grows.
cues: Say that Paraguay's consumption grows
Say what happens to the surplus
b2-integracion-04.target: A medida que crece el consumo de Paraguay, queda menos excedente para vender a Brasil.
b2-integracion-04.english: As Paraguay's consumption grows, less surplus is left to sell to Brazil.
b2-integracion-04.canDo: I can describe two changes that grow together, with *a medida que* and *cuanto más … más …*.

b2-integracion-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Degrees Across Borders
b2-integracion-05.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading about the Residence Agreement, and she asks what you think should happen with university degrees.
b2-integracion-05.prompt: Tell Meg what you think the countries should do about degrees.
cues: Say that it is important
Say what the countries should recognise
b2-integracion-05.target: Es importante que los países reconozcan los títulos universitarios de otros países.
b2-integracion-05.english: It is important that countries recognise university degrees from other countries.
b2-integracion-05.canDo: I can say what should happen, with *es importante que* and other value judgments + subjunctive.

b2-integracion-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Why Integration Matters
b2-integracion-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are talking about the lessons on South American integration, and he asks for one condition for the agreements to work.
b2-integracion-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos one condition for the agreements to work.
cues: Say what will work
Say what everyone has to do
b2-integracion-consolidation.target: El acuerdo funcionará siempre que todos sigan las reglas.
b2-integracion-consolidation.english: The agreement will work as long as everyone follows the rules.
b2-integracion-consolidation.canDo: I can use conditions, past conditions, results and value judgments to talk about South American integration.

b2-34-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Greeting an Older Woman
b2-34-01.scenario: You are Meg. You meet an older woman you do not know, and you want to greet her politely.
b2-34-01.prompt: Greet the woman politely and ask how she is.
cues: Greet her with the right title
Ask how she is, using the formal form
b2-34-01.english: Good afternoon, madam. How are you?
b2-34-01.canDo: I can choose between *tú* and *usted* for the person I am talking to.

b2-34-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A Word for Mobile Phone
b2-34-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks which word she should use for a mobile phone in Latin America.
b2-34-02.prompt: Tell Meg which word is used.
cues: Say which word people use
Say where they use it
b2-34-02.target: En casi toda América Latina se dice celular.
b2-34-02.english: In almost all of Latin America people say celular.
b2-34-02.canDo: I can recognise common regional words, such as *carro* and *auto* or *departamento* and *apartamento*.

b2-34-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Closing the Window
b2-34-03.scenario: You are Carlos. In the office you want to ask a colleague, politely, to close the window.
b2-34-03.prompt: Ask your colleague politely to close the window.
cues: Excuse yourself first
Ask if the person would mind closing it
b2-34-03.english: Sorry, would you mind closing the window?
b2-34-03.canDo: I can make a request gentle with *quería*, *¿podría…?* and *¿le importaría…?*.

b2-34-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Please Sign Here
b2-34-04.scenario: You are Carlos. In the office a visitor needs to sign a form, and you ask him formally.
b2-34-04.prompt: Ask the visitor formally to sign the form here.
cues: Use a formal request
Say where to sign
b2-34-04.target: Le ruego que firme aquí, por favor.
b2-34-04.english: I ask you to sign here, please.
b2-34-04.canDo: I can ask for something formally with *le ruego que* and *le agradecería que*.

b2-34-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Ways to Say Hello
b2-34-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks how you say hello to a friend and how you say it to a stranger.
cues: Give the greeting for a friend
Give the greeting for a stranger
b2-34-05.target: A un amigo le pregunto qué tal; a un desconocido le pregunto cómo está.
b2-34-05.english: I ask a friend how things are going; I ask a stranger how he or she is.
b2-34-05.canDo: I can say the same message in a formal and an informal register.

b2-34-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Was Scorza?
b2-34-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks who Manuel Scorza was, after you both read a short text about him.
b2-34-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg who Scorza was and when he died.
cues: Say what he was and where he was from
Say the year he died
b2-34-consolidation.target: Manuel Scorza fue un escritor peruano; murió en 1983.
b2-34-consolidation.english: Manuel Scorza was a Peruvian writer; he died in 1983.
b2-34-consolidation.canDo: I can read a short text about Manuel Scorza and his novel Redoble por Rancas.

b2-migracion-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Documentary About Brazil
b2-migracion-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about immigration to Brazil, and he asks what you will tell him afterwards.
b2-migracion-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what you will tell him when the documentary ends.
cues: Say when you will tell him
Say which immigrants arrived in Brazil in 1908
b2-migracion-01.target: Cuando termine el documental, te diré que los primeros inmigrantes japoneses llegaron a Brasil en 1908.
b2-migracion-01.english: When the documentary ends, I will tell you that the first Japanese immigrants arrived in Brazil in 1908.
b2-migracion-01.canDo: I can say when something will happen, with *cuando*, *en cuanto* and *hasta que* + subjunctive.

b2-migracion-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Children and School
b2-migracion-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading a report about Venezuelan families in the region, and she asks what you think is most important for children.
b2-migracion-02.prompt: Tell Meg what you think is important for migrant children.
cues: Say that it is important
Say what the children should do
b2-migracion-02.target: Es importante que los niños migrantes vayan a la escuela.
b2-migracion-02.english: It is important that migrant children go to school.
b2-migracion-02.canDo: I can say what governments and aid agencies should do, with *es necesario que* and *es importante que* + subjunctive.

b2-migracion-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Whoever Reaches the Border
b2-migracion-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading an article about the border at Cúcuta, and he asks what people there need.
b2-migracion-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what anyone who reaches the border needs.
cues: Say who the sentence is about
Say what they need
b2-migracion-03.target: Cualquier persona que llegue a la frontera necesita información clara.
b2-migracion-03.english: Anyone who reaches the border needs clear information.
b2-migracion-03.canDo: I can talk about any person, place or route, with *cualquiera que*, *quienquiera que* and *dondequiera que* + subjunctive.

b2-migracion-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Money Sent Home
b2-migracion-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are listening to a talk about remittances, and she asks what the economists say.
b2-migracion-04.prompt: Tell Meg what economists say about remittances.
cues: Grant that remittances help families
Say what they do not replace
b2-migracion-04.target: Si bien las remesas ayudan a muchas familias, no sustituyen la inversión pública.
b2-migracion-04.english: Although remittances help many families, they do not replace public investment.
b2-migracion-04.canDo: I can grant a point and then make my own, with *si bien* + indicative.

b2-migracion-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Arepas in the Cities
b2-migracion-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading an article about migrants and food, and he asks where you can find Venezuelan food.
b2-migracion-05.prompt: Tell Carlos where Venezuelan arepas are sold.
cues: Say what is sold
Say where
b2-migracion-05.target: Se venden arepas venezolanas en muchas ciudades de Sudamérica.
b2-migracion-05.english: Venezuelan arepas are sold in many cities of South America.
b2-migracion-05.canDo: I can say what is done, sold or recognised without naming who does it, with *se* + verb.

b2-migracion-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Border Talk
b2-migracion-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing a short talk about borders and migration, and she asks what to say about the Darién.
b2-migracion-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg one fact about the Darién for the talk.
cues: Say what the Darién is
Say what happened in 2023
b2-migracion-consolidation.target: Entre Colombia y Panamá está la selva del Darién; según las autoridades panameñas, en 2023 la cruzaron más de quinientas mil personas.
b2-migracion-consolidation.english: The Darién jungle lies between Colombia and Panama; according to the Panamanian authorities, more than half a million people crossed it in 2023.
b2-migracion-consolidation.canDo: I can use time clauses, value judgments, whoever-clauses, *si bien* and *se* to talk about migration in South America.

b2-35-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Rising Prices
b2-35-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what worries families in the news. Prices have gone up.
b2-35-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what worries families, using a noun.
cues: Name the rise in prices
Say that it worries families
b2-35-01.target: El aumento de los precios preocupa a muchas familias.
b2-35-01.english: The rise in prices worries many families.
b2-35-01.canDo: I can turn a verb into a noun, such as *aumentar* into *el aumento*, in formal writing.

b2-35-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Minister's Visit
b2-35-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks how a news report says that the minister is expected tomorrow.
b2-35-02.prompt: Say it as a newspaper would.
cues: Use an impersonal expression
Say the minister arrives tomorrow
b2-35-02.target: Se espera que el ministro llegue mañana.
b2-35-02.english: The minister is expected to arrive tomorrow.
b2-35-02.canDo: I can report a fact impersonally with *se estima que* and *se espera que*.

b2-35-03.title: Communicative Challenge: A Plan with Advantages
b2-35-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos says the plan is expensive. You agree, but you want to point out its advantages.
b2-35-03.prompt: Grant that the plan is expensive, then say what it offers.
cues: Grant that it is expensive
Say it offers many advantages
b2-35-03.target: Si bien es cierto que el plan es caro, ofrece muchas ventajas.
b2-35-03.english: It is true that the plan is expensive, but it offers many advantages.
b2-35-03.canDo: I can grant a point with *si bien es cierto que* and then limit it.

b2-35-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Formal Letter
b2-35-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You start a formal letter to a man you do not know, to ask for information.
b2-35-04.prompt: Write the opening and the reason for writing.
cues: Open the letter formally
Say you are writing to ask for information
b2-35-04.target: Estimado señor: Le escribo para pedirle información.
b2-35-04.english: Dear Sir, I am writing to ask you for information.
b2-35-04.canDo: I can open a formal letter with *Estimado señor:* or *Estimada señora:*.

b2-35-05.title: Communicative Challenge: After the Class
b2-35-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you and your classmates did when the class was over. You left together.
b2-35-05.prompt: Tell Carlos with a participle clause.
cues: Say the class was over
Say that you left together
b2-35-05.english: Once the class was over, we left together.
b2-35-05.canDo: I can open a clause with a participle that agrees with its noun, as in *Terminada la reunión, salimos*.

b2-35-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Was Arguedas?
b2-35-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks who José María Arguedas was, after you both read a short text about him.
b2-35-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg who Arguedas was and when he died.
cues: Say what he was and where he was from
Say the year he died
b2-35-consolidation.target: José María Arguedas fue un escritor peruano; murió en 1969.
b2-35-consolidation.english: José María Arguedas was a Peruvian writer; he died in 1969.
b2-35-consolidation.canDo: I can read a short text about José María Arguedas and his novel Los ríos profundos.

b2-pluralismo-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The 1989 Convention
b2-pluralismo-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading an article about indigenous rights, and he asks if the problems are solved.
b2-pluralismo-01.prompt: Tell Carlos that the convention exists but problems remain.
cues: Say when the convention dates from
Say that conflicts remain
b2-pluralismo-01.target: El Convenio 169 es de 1989; no obstante, muchos conflictos por la consulta siguen abiertos.
b2-pluralismo-01.english: Convention 169 dates from 1989; nevertheless, many conflicts over consultation remain open.
b2-pluralismo-01.canDo: I can contrast two facts with *sin embargo* and *no obstante*.

b2-pluralismo-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Peasant Patrols
b2-pluralismo-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are watching a documentary about the rondas campesinas, and she asks about the law.
b2-pluralismo-02.prompt: Tell Meg about the law that recognised the patrols.
cues: Say which country
Say what the law did
b2-pluralismo-02.target: La ley de 2003 es la norma con la que Perú reconoció a las rondas campesinas.
b2-pluralismo-02.english: The 2003 law is the rule with which Peru recognised the peasant patrols.
b2-pluralismo-02.canDo: I can describe a place, a law or an institution with *en la que*, *con la que* and other relatives with a preposition.

b2-pluralismo-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Rivers With Rights
b2-pluralismo-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading about the Atrato river, and he asks what you think about legal protection for rivers.
b2-pluralismo-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what you think is important for rivers.
cues: Say that it is important
Say what rivers should have
b2-pluralismo-03.target: Es importante que los ríos tengan protección legal.
b2-pluralismo-03.english: It is important that rivers have legal protection.
b2-pluralismo-03.canDo: I can say what should happen to rivers and forests, with *es importante que* and *es necesario que* + subjunctive.

b2-pluralismo-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Language Becomes Official
b2-pluralismo-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are listening to a talk about languages, and she asks about Paraguay.
b2-pluralismo-04.prompt: Tell Meg why Guaraní is an official language of Paraguay.
cues: Say which Constitution
Say that Guaraní is official next to Spanish
b2-pluralismo-04.target: A raíz de la Constitución de 1992, el guaraní es lengua oficial de Paraguay junto al castellano.
b2-pluralismo-04.english: As a result of the 1992 Constitution, Guaraní is an official language of Paraguay together with Spanish.
b2-pluralismo-04.canDo: I can give a cause with *debido a* and *a raíz de*.

b2-pluralismo-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Escazú Agreement
b2-pluralismo-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading an article about defenders of the environment, and he asks what the Escazú Agreement says.
b2-pluralismo-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what the Escazú Agreement says States must do.
cues: Mention the agreement
Say whom the States must protect
b2-pluralismo-05.target: Según el Acuerdo de Escazú, los Estados han de proteger a las personas defensoras del ambiente.
b2-pluralismo-05.english: According to the Escazú Agreement, States must protect people who defend the environment.
b2-pluralismo-05.canDo: I can say what must be done, in a formal register, with *han de*, *has de* and other *haber de* + infinitive forms.

b2-pluralismo-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Languages and Migration
b2-pluralismo-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing a short talk about native languages, and she asks for one cause and one remedy.
b2-pluralismo-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg why children are losing their languages and what exists to help.
cues: Give the cause
Say that there are apps
b2-pluralismo-consolidation.target: Debido a la migración a las ciudades, muchos niños ya no aprenden la lengua de sus abuelos; no obstante, existen aplicaciones para aprenderla.
b2-pluralismo-consolidation.english: Because of migration to the cities, many children no longer learn their grandparents' language; nevertheless, there are apps to learn it.
b2-pluralismo-consolidation.canDo: I can use contrast and cause connectors, relatives, value judgments and *haber de* to talk about indigenous rights.

b2-36-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Money or Time?
b2-36-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks if the problem is money. It is not money; it is time.
b2-36-01.prompt: Correct Carlos with a balanced sentence.
cues: Say it is not a problem of money
Say it is a problem of time
b2-36-01.target: No es un problema de dinero, sino de tiempo.
b2-36-01.english: It is not a problem of money but of time.
b2-36-01.canDo: I can balance a sentence with *no… sino…*, *tanto… como…* and *ni… ni…*.

b2-36-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A Sure Answer
b2-36-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks if the plan will work. You are completely sure.
b2-36-02.prompt: Answer Meg and show you are sure.
cues: Use a strong expression of certainty
Say the plan will work
b2-36-02.target: No cabe duda de que el plan funcionará.
b2-36-02.english: There is no doubt that the plan will work.
b2-36-02.canDo: I can say I am sure with *no cabe duda de que* and *no dudo que*.

b2-36-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Planning an Essay
b2-36-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks how you will organise your essay. You will speak about the price first and then about the advantages.
b2-36-03.prompt: Tell Carlos the order of your two points.
cues: Say what you cover first
Say what you cover second
b2-36-03.target: En primer lugar, hablaré del precio; en segundo lugar, de las ventajas.
b2-36-03.english: First, I will talk about the price; second, about the advantages.
b2-36-03.canDo: I can move an essay forward with *llegados a este punto* and *en suma*.

b2-36-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Time in a Phrase
b2-36-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks you for a short metaphor about time.
b2-36-04.prompt: Give Meg a metaphor about time.
cues: Say what time is
Compare it with something without using como
b2-36-04.canDo: I can recognise and use a metaphor, a rhetorical question and repetition for emphasis.

b2-36-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Closing Line
b2-36-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks you for the last sentence of an essay about the rise in prices.
cues: Start with a closing marker
Say that the rise in prices needs measures
b2-36-05.target: En suma, el aumento de los precios exige medidas.
b2-36-05.english: In short, the rise in prices calls for measures.
b2-36-05.canDo: I can choose the right register for the person I am writing to.

b2-36-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Was Borges?
b2-36-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks who Jorge Luis Borges was, after you both read a short text about him.
b2-36-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg who Borges was and when he died.
cues: Say what he was and where he was from
Say the year he died
b2-36-consolidation.target: Jorge Luis Borges fue un escritor argentino; murió en 1986.
b2-36-consolidation.english: Jorge Luis Borges was an Argentine writer; he died in 1986.
b2-36-consolidation.canDo: I can read a short text about Jorge Luis Borges and his book El Aleph.

b2-futuro-01.title: Communicative Challenge: How Long Is the Film?
b2-futuro-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos will watch the Mexican film Roma tonight, and he asks how long it is. You do not know, but you guess.
b2-futuro-01.prompt: Tell Carlos that you do not know how long Roma is, and make a guess.
cues: Say that you do not know
Guess how long it lasts
b2-futuro-01.target: No sé cuánto dura Roma; durará unas dos horas.
b2-futuro-01.english: I do not know how long Roma is; it probably lasts about two hours.
b2-futuro-01.canDo: I can make a guess about the present or the past with the future and the conditional of probability.

b2-futuro-02.title: Communicative Challenge: After the Boom
b2-futuro-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading about Latin American writers, and she asks what changed after the Boom.
b2-futuro-02.prompt: Tell Meg what changed after the Boom.
cues: Grant a point about the Boom authors
Say what is true today
b2-futuro-02.target: Si bien casi todos los autores del Boom eran hombres, hoy muchas escritoras tienen lectores en todo el mundo.
b2-futuro-02.english: Although almost all the Boom authors were men, today many women writers have readers all over the world.
b2-futuro-02.canDo: I can grant a point and then make my own, with *si bien* + indicative (América Latina en el escenario global).

b2-futuro-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Water and Lithium
b2-futuro-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about the salt flats, and he asks what you think should be done.
b2-futuro-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what you think is important when lithium is extracted.
cues: Say that it is important
Say what countries should do with water
b2-futuro-03.target: Es importante que los países usen el agua con cuidado cuando extraen litio.
b2-futuro-03.english: It is important that countries use water carefully when they extract lithium.
b2-futuro-03.canDo: I can say what should be done about resources, with *es importante que* and *es necesario que* + subjunctive.

b2-futuro-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Where It Began
b2-futuro-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are watching a documentary about the protests of 2019, and she asks where they began.
b2-futuro-04.prompt: Tell Meg in which country the protests of 2019 began.
cues: Say the country
Say the year
b2-futuro-04.target: Chile es el país en el que empezaron las protestas de 2019.
b2-futuro-04.english: Chile is the country in which the 2019 protests began.
b2-futuro-04.canDo: I can describe a movement, a place or a group with *en el que*, *con el que* and other relatives with a preposition.

b2-futuro-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Rhetorical Question
b2-futuro-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are preparing a short talk about Latin American identity, and he asks for a strong sentence to open it.
b2-futuro-05.prompt: Open the talk with a question that makes a point about diversity.
cues: Ask a question
Make the point that the region is diverse
b2-futuro-05.target: ¿Quién puede negar que América Latina es una región muy diversa?
b2-futuro-05.english: Who can deny that Latin America is a very diverse region?
b2-futuro-05.canDo: I can use a metaphor, a rhetorical question or repetition to make a point.

b2-futuro-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Trade Partners
b2-futuro-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing a short talk about trade, and she asks for a point with two sides.
b2-futuro-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg a point with two sides about trade in the region.
cues: Grant that China is the largest partner
Say what the EU and Mercosur did in January 2026
b2-futuro-consolidation.target: Si bien China es hoy el mayor socio comercial de Brasil, Chile y Perú, la Unión Europea y el Mercosur firmaron un acuerdo en enero de 2026.
b2-futuro-consolidation.english: Although China is today the largest trading partner of Brazil, Chile and Peru, the European Union and Mercosur signed an agreement in January 2026.
b2-futuro-consolidation.canDo: I can use probability, *si bien*, value judgments, relatives and rhetorical devices to talk about Latin America today.

c1-01-01.title: Communicative Challenge: State a Thesis
c1-01-01.scenario: You are Meg. You are writing an essay, and Carlos asks what you want to show in it. You want to say that working from home improves results and that the data back this up.
c1-01-01.prompt: Answer Carlos with your thesis and one reason.
cues: Say that you maintain a claim about working from home
Say that the data back it up
c1-01-01.target: Sostengo que trabajar desde casa mejora los resultados, y los datos lo respaldan.
c1-01-01.english: I maintain that working from home improves results, and the data back it up.
c1-01-01.canDo: I can state a thesis and back it up with evidence.

c1-01-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Having Done It First
c1-01-02.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague at the office asks why the author of a report was criticised. She had not checked her sources.
c1-01-02.prompt: Tell your colleague why the author was criticised.
cues: Say that people criticised her
Give the reason: she had not checked her sources
c1-01-02.target: La criticaron por no haber contrastado sus fuentes.
c1-01-02.english: They criticised her for not having checked her sources.
c1-01-02.canDo: I can use *haber* + participle after a preposition, as in *tras haberlo leído*.

c1-01-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Compact Style
c1-01-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what in your essay affects performance. It is the fact that people travel less.
c1-01-03.prompt: Answer Carlos with a noun phrase as the subject of your sentence.
cues: Start with a noun phrase about travelling less
Say what it affects
c1-01-03.target: La reducción de los desplazamientos incide en el rendimiento.
