c1-01-03.english: The reduction in travel affects performance.
c1-01-03.canDo: I can turn a verb clause into a noun phrase that works as the subject.

c1-01-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Restate and Correct
c1-01-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks if the sample in your report is large enough. You say it is small, correct yourself, and restate what that means.
cues: Say the sample is small
Correct yourself: it is too small
Restate: it is not enough
c1-01-04.target: La muestra es pequeña; mejor dicho, demasiado pequeña. Esto es, no basta.
c1-01-04.english: The sample is small; or rather, too small. That is, it is not enough.
c1-01-04.canDo: I can restate an idea with *esto es* and correct it with *mejor dicho*.

c1-01-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Qualify a Claim
c1-01-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks if the data prove that working from home is better. You answer carefully.
c1-01-05.prompt: Answer Carlos without claiming too much.
cues: Say it is not fully proven
Say what the data seem to indicate
Warn against generalising
c1-01-05.target: No del todo. Todo parece indicar que sí, pero no conviene generalizar.
c1-01-05.english: Not quite. Everything seems to indicate that it is, but it is not advisable to generalise.
c1-01-05.canDo: I can match the strength of a claim to the evidence with *todo parece indicar* and *cabe suponer que*.

c1-01-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Argue Your Case
c1-01-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. You tell Carlos how your essay argues its case: your thesis, a point you grant, a limit on it and a conclusion.
c1-01-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos your argument in three sentences.
cues: State the thesis
Grant a point and limit it
Close with a conclusion
c1-01-consolidation.target: Sostengo que trabajar desde casa mejora los resultados. Es cierto que exige disciplina; ahora bien, esa disciplina se aprende. En definitiva, mi tesis se sostiene.
c1-01-consolidation.english: I maintain that working from home improves results. It is true that it takes discipline; that said, discipline can be learned. In short, my thesis holds.
c1-01-consolidation.canDo: I can build a short academic argument with a thesis, a concession, a rebuttal and a conclusion.

c1-02-01.title: Communicative Challenge: A Mistake in the Report
c1-02-01.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague asks why you changed a sentence in the report. You found a mistake and you are sure the new sentence is right.
c1-02-01.prompt: Tell your colleague why you changed the sentence.
cues: Say you noticed there was a mistake
Say you are sure the new sentence is correct
c1-02-01.target: Me di cuenta de que había un error y estoy seguro de que la frase nueva es correcta.
c1-02-01.english: I realised there was a mistake and I am sure the new sentence is correct.
c1-02-01.canDo: I can tell when a verb, noun or adjective needs *de* before *que*.

c1-02-02.title: Communicative Challenge: How the Report Was Made
c1-02-02.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks how the report for your course was prepared. The data were published and the authors were interviewed.
c1-02-02.prompt: Tell Carlos how the report was prepared.
cues: Say what happened to the data
Say what happened to the authors
c1-02-02.target: Se publicaron los datos y se entrevistó a los autores.
c1-02-02.english: The data were published and the authors were interviewed.
c1-02-02.canDo: I can make the verb agree with the thing after passive *se* (*se publicaron los datos*).

c1-02-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Correcting a Draft
c1-02-03.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague asks how you checked a long text before sending it. You read it aloud and corrected it at the same time.
c1-02-03.prompt: Tell your colleague how you checked the text.
cues: Say you checked the text
Say how: by reading it aloud at the same time
c1-02-03.target: Revisé el texto leyendo en voz alta.
c1-02-03.english: I checked the text by reading it aloud.
c1-02-03.canDo: I can use the gerund for an action at the same time as the main verb or for the way it happens.

c1-02-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Committee Report
c1-02-04.scenario: You are Meg. You are writing a short report for your course. The committee asked yesterday for the draft to be revised, and it has now asked for it to be handed in before the deadline.
c1-02-04.prompt: Report both requests of the committee in one sentence.
cues: Say what the committee asked for yesterday
Say what it has asked for now
c1-02-04.target: La comisión pidió que se revisara el borrador y ha pedido que se entregue antes del plazo.
c1-02-04.english: The committee asked for the draft to be revised and has asked for it to be handed in before the deadline.
c1-02-04.canDo: I can report a request in the past with the imperfect subjunctive (*pidió que se revisara*).

c1-02-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Printed Style Guide
c1-02-05.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague asks whether the style guide is ready. The printing house has printed it and the copies are on your desk.
c1-02-05.prompt: Tell your colleague the style guide is ready.
cues: Say the printing house has printed it
Say the copies are already printed
c1-02-05.target: La imprenta ha impreso el manual de estilo y los ejemplares ya están impresos.
c1-02-05.english: The printing house has printed the style guide and the copies are already printed.
c1-02-05.canDo: I can pick the right participle when it describes a noun (*pescado frito*, *un texto impreso*).

c1-02-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Checking an Article
c1-02-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. A friend asks you to check an article before she sends it. You read it and found that the misprints were corrected.
c1-02-consolidation.prompt: Tell your friend the article is ready.
cues: Say you are sure the text is clear
Say the misprints were corrected
c1-02-consolidation.target: Estoy segura de que el texto es claro y se corrigieron las erratas.
c1-02-consolidation.english: I am sure the text is clear and the misprints were corrected.
c1-02-consolidation.canDo: I can choose between *que* and *de que*, and keep *se* and the gerund within the written norm.

c1-03-01.title: Communicative Challenge: What Heat Does
c1-03-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what the heat does to the mixture in your class experiment.
c1-03-01.prompt: Answer with a noun built from a verb.
cues: Say that the heat speeds up something
Name the process of the mixture changing with yeast
c1-03-01.target: El calor acelera la fermentación de la mezcla.
c1-03-01.english: Heat speeds up the fermentation of the mixture.
c1-03-01.canDo: I can name a process with a noun built from a verb or an adjective (*fermentar → fermentación*).

c1-03-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Preparing the Dough
c1-03-02.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks how the dough is prepared.
c1-03-02.prompt: Describe two steps without naming who does them.
cues: Say that the ingredients are mixed
Say that the dough is left to rest
c1-03-02.target: Se mezclan los ingredientes y se deja reposar la masa.
c1-03-02.english: The ingredients are mixed and the dough is left to rest.
c1-03-02.canDo: I can describe the steps of a process with *se*, the verb agreeing with the thing (*se miden las sustancias*).

c1-03-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Measurements
c1-03-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg shows you two measurements that do not match.
c1-03-03.prompt: Give your conclusion with a modal verb.
cues: Say that you are nearly sure about the cause
Say that the cause is an error in the measurement
c1-03-03.target: Tiene que haber un error en la medición.
c1-03-03.english: There must be an error in the measurement.
c1-03-03.canDo: I can say how sure I am of a result with *tener que*, *deber de* and *poder*.

c1-03-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Why Dough Rises
c1-03-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks why the dough rises.
c1-03-04.prompt: Explain with a cause and a consequence.
cues: Say that the yeast releases gas
Say that, as a consequence, the dough rises
c1-03-04.target: La levadura libera gas; por consiguiente, la masa sube.
c1-03-04.english: The yeast releases gas; consequently, the dough rises.
c1-03-04.canDo: I can state a result with *por consiguiente*, and with *de ahí que* + the subjunctive.

c1-03-05.title: Communicative Challenge: After the Oven
c1-03-05.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what to do once the bread comes out of the oven.
c1-03-05.prompt: Give the next step with a participle clause.
cues: Say that the baking is finished
Say that the bread is left to cool
c1-03-05.target: Terminada la cocción, se deja enfriar el pan.
c1-03-05.english: Once the baking is finished, the bread is left to cool.
c1-03-05.canDo: I can start a step of a method with a participle clause (*obtenida la masa, …*).

c1-03-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Method in One Sentence
c1-03-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks how you would write one step of your experiment in the report.
c1-03-consolidation.prompt: Write one step of the method with its purpose.
cues: Say that the temperature is measured
Say that the aim is to control the fermentation
c1-03-consolidation.target: Se mide la temperatura con el fin de controlar la fermentación.
c1-03-consolidation.english: The temperature is measured in order to control the fermentation.
c1-03-consolidation.canDo: I can explain a method with *se*, participle clauses and purpose phrases.

c1-04-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Mayor
c1-04-01.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what the paper says about the mayor. The news is not confirmed.
c1-04-01.prompt: Pass on the news without confirming it.
cues: Say where the news comes from
Say the mayor has reportedly resigned
c1-04-01.target: Según fuentes, el alcalde habría dimitido.
c1-04-01.english: According to sources, the mayor has reportedly resigned.
c1-04-01.canDo: I can report an unconfirmed claim with the conditional (*el alcalde habría dimitido*).

c1-04-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Spokesperson
c1-04-02.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what the spokesperson said about the fire.
cues: Say who stated it
Say that the fire was under control
c1-04-02.target: El portavoz afirmó que el fuego estaba controlado.
c1-04-02.english: The spokesperson stated that the fire was under control.
c1-04-02.canDo: I can say what an official stated in a news report with *afirmar que* and *señalar que* + the indicative.

c1-04-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Headline
c1-04-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg shows you the newspaper headline «Dimite el alcalde» and asks what it means.
c1-04-03.prompt: Say what the headline stands for, as a full sentence.
cues: Say what has happened to the mayor
c1-04-03.canDo: I can read a headline and say what full sentence it stands for.

c1-04-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Rescue
c1-04-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what happened to the people in the warehouse.
cues: Say that two people were rescued
Say who rescued them
c1-04-04.target: Dos personas fueron rescatadas por los bomberos.
c1-04-04.english: Two people were rescued by the firefighters.
c1-04-04.canDo: I can name who did something with the *ser* passive and *por* (*fueron rescatadas por los bomberos*).

c1-04-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Cause
c1-04-05.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks whether the cause of the fire is confirmed.
c1-04-05.prompt: Say what is and is not confirmed.
cues: Say that for now there is no confirmation
Say what the firefighters say about where it began
c1-04-05.target: De momento no hay confirmación; según los bomberos, el fuego comenzó en el almacén.
c1-04-05.english: For now there is no confirmation; according to the firefighters, the fire started in the warehouse.
c1-04-05.canDo: I can attribute a claim to a source and report it with distance (*según los bomberos*, *parece que*).

c1-04-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Report
c1-04-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you would write about the mayor in a report.
c1-04-consolidation.prompt: Write the claim and say it is not confirmed.
cues: Say that the mayor has apparently resigned, as an unconfirmed report
Say there is no confirmation yet
c1-04-consolidation.target: Al parecer, el alcalde habría dimitido, pero aún no hay confirmación.
c1-04-consolidation.english: Apparently the mayor has reportedly resigned, but there is no confirmation yet.
c1-04-consolidation.canDo: I can pass on a report I have not confirmed, and say who said what.

c1-05-01.title: Communicative Challenge: A Newspaper Takes Sides
c1-05-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what the editorial thinks of the new pedestrian zone. You are sure it takes sides.
c1-05-01.prompt: Tell Carlos the editorial takes sides, with a stance adverb.
cues: Open with a word that says it is obvious
Say the editorial takes sides for the pedestrian zone
c1-05-01.target: Evidentemente, el editorial toma partido por la zona peatonal.
c1-05-01.english: Obviously, the editorial takes sides in favour of the pedestrian zone.
c1-05-01.canDo: I can open a sentence in an editorial with a stance adverb such as *evidentemente* or *a todas luces*.

c1-05-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Setting the Record Straight
c1-05-02.scenario: You are Carlos. A neighbour says the council wants to restrict trade in the centre. You think it only wants to bring order to the traffic.
c1-05-02.prompt: Correct your neighbour: reject one reading and give the other.
cues: Reject the idea that the council wants to restrict trade
Say what the council wants instead
c1-05-02.target: No es que el ayuntamiento quiera restringir el comercio, sino que quiere ordenar la circulación.
c1-05-02.english: It is not that the council wants to restrict trade, but that it wants to bring order to the traffic.
c1-05-02.canDo: I can reject a reading of my position with *No es que…, sino que…*.

c1-05-03.title: Communicative Challenge: A Fair Judgment
c1-05-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos tells you the council has not consulted the neighbours. You think it is unacceptable.
c1-05-03.prompt: Judge the fact with a formal expression.
cues: Say it is unacceptable
Say the council has not consulted the neighbours
c1-05-03.target: Resulta inadmisible que el ayuntamiento no haya consultado a los vecinos.
c1-05-03.english: It is unacceptable that the council has not consulted the neighbours.
c1-05-03.canDo: I can judge a fact with *Resulta inadmisible que…* and *Es de lamentar que…* and the subjunctive.

c1-05-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Granting a Point
c1-05-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos says the residents' worry about parking is serious. You agree it is legitimate, but you still think the measure cannot wait.
c1-05-04.prompt: Concede the point formally and keep your position.
cues: Grant that the residents' concern is legitimate
Say the measure cannot wait
c1-05-04.target: Si bien la inquietud de los residentes es legítima, la medida no puede esperar.
c1-05-04.english: Although the residents' concern is legitimate, the measure cannot wait.
c1-05-04.canDo: I can grant an objection with *si bien*, *aun cuando* or *por más que* and still state my position.

c1-05-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Ending an Editorial
c1-05-05.scenario: You are Meg. For a class you are writing the last lines of an editorial about closing the centre to traffic. You want to end with a question, a list of three and a call.
c1-05-05.prompt: Write the closing question, the list of three and the call.
cues: Ask how long we are going to wait
Say we want a calmer, cleaner and safer centre
Call on the council to decide now
c1-05-05.target: ¿Hasta cuándo vamos a esperar? Queremos un centro más tranquilo, más limpio y más seguro. Que el ayuntamiento decida ya.
c1-05-05.english: How long are we going to wait? We want a calmer, cleaner and safer centre. May the council decide now.
c1-05-05.canDo: I can build an editorial paragraph with a rhetorical question, a list of three and a closing call.

c1-05-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Paper and the Plan
c1-05-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague says the newspaper is against the shopkeepers. In fact it takes a clear side for the plan to close the centre to traffic, and it wants to bring order to the traffic.
c1-05-consolidation.prompt: Say the paper takes sides for the plan and correct the misreading.
cues: Say, with a stance adverb, that the paper takes sides for the plan
Say the paper is not against the shopkeepers; it wants to bring order to the traffic
c1-05-consolidation.target: Evidentemente, el periódico toma partido por el plan. No es que esté en contra de los comerciantes, sino que quiere ordenar la circulación.
c1-05-consolidation.english: Obviously, the paper takes sides in favour of the plan. It is not that it is against the shopkeepers, but that it wants to bring order to the traffic.
c1-05-consolidation.canDo: I can take a clear position in an editorial voice and correct a misreading of it.

c1-06-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Rules of the Garden
c1-06-01.scenario: You are Carlos. A neighbour asks about the rules of the community garden. You have read that the members have to pay the fee in January.
c1-06-01.prompt: Tell your neighbour the duty, in the style of a rule.
cues: Say who has to do it
Say they must pay the fee in January
c1-06-01.target: Los socios deberán abonar la cuota en enero.
c1-06-01.english: Members must pay the fee in January.
c1-06-01.canDo: I can read the future as the voice of a rule: *Los socios abonarán la cuota*.

c1-06-02.title: Communicative Challenge: An Old Notice
c1-06-02.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos shows you an old notice with the words «quien infringiere la norma». You want to say the same thing in modern Spanish.
c1-06-02.prompt: Say in modern Spanish that whoever breaks the rule will lose the plot.
cues: Start with a word for whoever
Say the person will lose the plot
c1-06-02.target: Quien infrinja la norma perderá la parcela.
c1-06-02.english: Whoever breaks the rule will lose the plot.
c1-06-02.canDo: I can recognise the future subjunctive (*hablare*, *comiere*, *fuere*, *hubiere*) in an old legal text.

c1-06-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Can Apply
c1-06-03.scenario: You are Carlos. A neighbour asks who can ask for a plot in the community garden. The rules say anyone who wants to register can.
c1-06-03.prompt: Tell your neighbour who can ask for a plot, in the style of a rule.
cues: Start with any person
Say that this person wishes to register
c1-06-03.target: Cualquier persona que desee inscribirse puede pedir una parcela.
c1-06-03.english: Any person who wishes to register can ask for a plot.
c1-06-03.canDo: I can say who a rule applies to with *quien*, *cualquier socio que* and *las personas que* + subjunctive.

c1-06-04.title: Communicative Challenge: If a Member Cannot Pay
c1-06-04.scenario: You are Meg. A friend asks what the garden rules say if a member cannot pay the fee. The rules say the member must tell the board.
c1-06-04.prompt: Tell your friend what the rule says, starting with the case.
cues: Start with the case: the member cannot pay the fee
Say he must notify the board
c1-06-04.target: En caso de que el socio no pueda abonar la cuota, deberá avisar a la junta.
c1-06-04.english: In the event that the member cannot pay the fee, he must notify the board.
c1-06-04.canDo: I can set a condition in a rule with *en caso de que*, *siempre y cuando*, *salvo que* and *con tal de que* + subjunctive.

c1-06-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Ban in Legal Style
c1-06-05.scenario: You are Carlos. A neighbour asks what the garden rules say about using another member's plot. It is forbidden.
c1-06-05.prompt: Tell your neighbour the ban in the style of a rule.
cues: Open with the formula for a ban
Say that using another member's plot is not allowed
c1-06-05.target: Queda prohibido el uso de la parcela de otro socio.
c1-06-05.english: The use of another member's plot is prohibited.
c1-06-05.canDo: I can write a prohibition in legal style with *queda prohibido* + a noun.

c1-06-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Warning and the Penalty
c1-06-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. A friend asks what happens to a garden member who does not pay the fee. The rules give a warning first and then expulsion.
c1-06-consolidation.prompt: Tell your friend what the rules say, in legal style.
cues: Say that non-payment is grounds for a warning
Say that expulsion follows
c1-06-consolidation.target: El impago de la cuota será motivo de amonestación y, después, se procederá a la expulsión del socio.
c1-06-consolidation.english: Non-payment of the fee will be grounds for a warning and, after that, the member will be expelled.
c1-06-consolidation.canDo: I can read the future as the voice of a rule and recognise the old future subjunctive.

c1-07-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Why Was It Late?
c1-07-01.scenario: You are Carlos. A neighbour asks which office handles permits. You know it is the public body through which licences are processed.
c1-07-01.prompt: Name the office, with a formal relative after a preposition.
cues: Say it is the public body
Add that licences are processed through it
c1-07-01.target: Es el organismo a través del cual se tramitan las licencias.
c1-07-01.english: It is the public body through which licences are processed.
c1-07-01.canDo: I can use *el cual*, *la cual*, *los cuales* and *las cuales* after a preposition in a formal sentence.

c1-07-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Can Appeal
c1-07-02.scenario: You are Meg. A friend asks who can lodge an appeal at the city office. You know it is the user whose application was denied.
c1-07-02.prompt: Tell your friend who can appeal, with one relative clause.
cues: Say who the user is: the one whose application was denied
Say this user can lodge an appeal
c1-07-02.target: El usuario cuya solicitud fue denegada puede presentar un recurso.
c1-07-02.english: The user whose application was denied may lodge an appeal.
c1-07-02.canDo: I can attach a possession to a person or thing in a formal sentence with *cuyo*, *cuya*, *cuyos* and *cuyas*.

c1-07-03.title: Communicative Challenge: A Letter to the City Office
c1-07-03.scenario: You are Carlos. You are writing to the city office to ask for an appointment.
c1-07-03.prompt: Write the opening sentence of your formal letter.
cues: Say you are writing to the office
Say you want to request an appointment
c1-07-03.target: Me dirijo a ustedes para solicitar una cita previa.
c1-07-03.english: I am writing to you to request an appointment.
c1-07-03.canDo: I can open a formal letter with *Me dirijo a ustedes para…* and close it with *Atentamente*.

c1-07-04.title: Communicative Challenge: How the Office Works
c1-07-04.scenario: You are Meg. A friend asks how the city office attends to users. It does so in order of arrival.
c1-07-04.prompt: Say how users are attended to, in the impersonal.
cues: Use the impersonal to say users are attended to
Say it is in order of arrival
c1-07-04.target: Se atenderá a los usuarios por orden de llegada.
c1-07-04.english: Users will be attended to in order of arrival.
c1-07-04.canDo: I can write a notice with *se ruega* and *se atenderá*.

c1-07-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Plainer, Please
c1-07-05.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague shows you the sentence «Se efectuará el pago de la tasa» and asks for a plainer version.
c1-07-05.prompt: Say the same thing in a short plain sentence.
cues: Use the impersonal with a simple verb
Say that the fee will be paid
c1-07-05.canDo: I can rewrite a nominal bureaucratic sentence as a short verb sentence (*Se procedió a la revisión* as *Se revisó*).

c1-07-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Is the New Procedure Better?
c1-07-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. A friend asks if the new online procedure is better. The waiting time is shorter, and that speeds up the procedure.
c1-07-consolidation.prompt: Answer your friend with a formal comment on the whole fact.
cues: Say the waiting time is shorter
Add that this speeds up the procedure
c1-07-consolidation.target: La demora es menor, lo cual agiliza el trámite.
c1-07-consolidation.english: The delay is shorter, which speeds up the procedure.
c1-07-consolidation.canDo: I can use *el cual*, *lo cual* and *cuyo* in a formal sentence about a procedure.

c1-08-01.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Survey Says
c1-08-01.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague asks what people in the city think about the new survey. You know people think it is clear, and most respondents live in the centre.
c1-08-01.prompt: Reply with one sentence using a bare collective noun and a partitive phrase.
cues: Say what people think about the survey
Add where most of the respondents live
c1-08-01.target: La gente opina que la encuesta es clara, y la mayoría de los encuestados vive en el centro.
c1-08-01.english: People think that the survey is clear, and most of the respondents live in the centre.
c1-08-01.canDo: I can keep a singular verb after a bare collective noun such as *la gente*, *la población* or *el alumnado*.

c1-08-02.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Chart Shows
c1-08-02.scenario: You are Meg. You are discussing a demographic chart with Carlos. The population is gradually ageing and the birth rate even fell last year.
cues: Say that the population is gradually ageing
Add that the birth rate even dropped last year
c1-08-02.target: La población va envejeciendo progresivamente y la natalidad llegó a descender el año pasado.
c1-08-02.english: The population is gradually ageing and the birth rate even dropped last year.
c1-08-02.canDo: I can describe a gradual demographic shift with *ir* + gerund and time phrases such as *progresivamente* and *año tras año*.

c1-08-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Higher Than Forecast
c1-08-03.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague asks how emigration from the rural town compared with the official forecast. It grew more than the report expected, and more young people left than the forecast showed.
c1-08-03.prompt: Answer your colleague comparing the outcome with the forecast.
cues: Say that emigration grew more than expected
Mention that more young people left than the forecast showed
c1-08-03.target: La emigración creció más de lo que esperaba el informe y se marcharon más jóvenes de los que indicaba la proyección.
c1-08-03.english: Emigration grew more than the report expected and more young people left than the projection showed.
c1-08-03.canDo: I can compare an outcome with a forecast clause using *más de lo que* and *menos de lo que*.

c1-08-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Sharing the Figures
c1-08-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks about the share of older people in the town from your university reading. Around thirty per cent are over sixty-five.
c1-08-04.prompt: Give Carlos the approximate figure using a percentage and an approximation expression.
cues: State the percentage of older residents
Mention that the proportion is around a third
c1-08-04.target: El treinta por ciento de los habitantes supera los sesenta y cinco años: casi un tercio de la población.
c1-08-04.english: Thirty per cent of the inhabitants are over sixty-five: almost a third of the population.
c1-08-04.canDo: I can introduce percentages with *el* and keep agreement accurate with partitive figures.

c1-08-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Reading Without Overclaiming
c1-08-05.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague thinks the census proves one single cause for the population drop. You want to urge caution.
c1-08-05.prompt: Explain carefully that the figures do not prove one single cause.
cues: Say the census shows a correlation but not causation
Add that the drop could be due to several factors
c1-08-05.target: El censo refleja una correlación, pero no demuestra causalidad; el descenso podría deberse a varios factores.
c1-08-05.english: The census reflects a correlation, but does not prove causation; the drop could be due to several factors.
c1-08-05.canDo: I can distinguish correlation from causation and hedge conclusions with verbs such as *apuntar a* and *parecer indicar*.

c1-08-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Brief Data Summary
c1-08-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. A classmate asks you to summarise the regional demographic report in one sentence.
c1-08-consolidation.prompt: Give a brief, cautious summary of the trend and how it compares with expectations.
cues: Say that most towns lost more residents than the report forecast
Add that the change could be due to youth emigration
c1-08-consolidation.target: La mayoría de los municipios perdió más residentes de los que preveía el informe, y este cambio podría deberse a la emigración juvenil.
c1-08-consolidation.english: Most municipalities lost more residents than the report forecast, and this change could be due to youth emigration.
c1-08-consolidation.canDo: I can apply collective and partitive verb agreement accurately in demographic statements.

c1-09-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Explaining Rising Prices
c1-09-01.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague asks why household consumption fell this quarter. You know the drop happened because credit became more expensive and interest rates remain high.
c1-09-01.prompt: Explain the cause in one formal sentence using two cause connectors.
cues: State that consumption fell because of the rising cost of credit
Add the premise that interest rates remain high
c1-09-01.target: El consumo cayó debido al encarecimiento del crédito, dado que las tasas de interés siguen altas.
c1-09-01.english: Consumption fell because of the rising cost of credit, given that interest rates remain high.
c1-09-01.canDo: I can distinguish noun-phrase cause connectors (*debido a*, *a raíz de*, *como consecuencia de*) from clause-taking *dado que*.

c1-09-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A Market Forecast
c1-09-02.scenario: You are Meg. In your economics seminar, a classmate asks what will happen if the central bank does not lower interest rates and this slowdown continues.
c1-09-02.prompt: Give a concise forecast without using «si».
cues: State the condition of interest rates not falling
Warn that investment will slow down and the economy could enter stagnation
c1-09-02.target: De no bajar las tasas de interés, la inversión se frenará y la economía podría entrar en estancamiento.
c1-09-02.english: If interest rates do not fall, investment will slow down and the economy could enter stagnation.
c1-09-02.canDo: I can express possible and negative market conditions without *si* using *de* + infinitive and *de no* + infinitive.

c1-09-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Judging a Past Policy
c1-09-03.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague asks how mortgages and inflation would look today if the central bank had acted in time last year.
c1-09-03.prompt: Reply with one mixed conditional sentence linking the past action to today.
cues: Refer to the central bank having acted in time
State that inflation would be lower and mortgages more affordable today
c1-09-03.target: Si el banco central hubiera actuado a tiempo, hoy la inflación sería menor y las hipotecas serían más asequibles.
c1-09-03.english: If the central bank had acted in time, today inflation would be lower and mortgages would be more affordable.
c1-09-03.canDo: I can pair *si* + pluperfect subjunctive with the simple conditional to connect a past policy choice to a present outcome.

c1-09-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Firm Commitment
c1-09-04.scenario: You are Meg. A classmate asks whether the central bank will launch its stability plan even if markets show volatility this quarter.
c1-09-04.prompt: Reply using a reduplicated subjunctive formula and a support-verb collocation.
cues: Say that whatever happens in the markets
State that the central bank will launch the plan to protect the recovery
c1-09-04.target: Pase lo que pase, el banco central pondrá en marcha el plan para proteger la recuperación.
c1-09-04.english: Whatever happens, the central bank will launch the plan to protect the recovery.
c1-09-04.canDo: I can use reduplicated subjunctive formulas such as *pase lo que pase*, *cueste lo que cueste* and *digan lo que digan* in economic commentary.

c1-09-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Tracing a Market Shift
c1-09-05.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague asks you to summarise how domestic companies adapted after the central bank raised interest rates.
c1-09-05.prompt: Explain both the eventual policy outcome and the trade shift in one sentence.
cues: Say that the central bank ended up raising interest rates
Add that several companies went on to depend more on exports
c1-09-05.target: El banco central acabó por subir las tasas de interés y varias empresas pasaron a depender más de la exportación.
c1-09-05.english: The central bank ended up raising interest rates and several companies came to depend more on exports.
c1-09-05.canDo: I can describe the eventual result of an economic process with *terminar por* or *acabar por* + infinitive.

c1-09-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Summarising the Economic Column
c1-09-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. A classmate asks for a brief summary of the analysis column on inflation, interest rates and the outlook for the coming months.
c1-09-consolidation.prompt: Summarise the cause, the central bank's action and the future risk in two sentences.
cues: Say that inflation rose because of supply-chain problems and the central bank ended up raising interest rates
Warn without «si» that if rates stay high too long, the slowdown could give rise to stagnation
c1-09-consolidation.target: La inflación subió debido a los problemas en la cadena de suministro y el banco central acabó por subir las tasas de interés. De mantenerse altas demasiado tiempo, la desaceleración podría dar lugar a un estancamiento.
c1-09-consolidation.english: Inflation rose because of supply-chain problems and the central bank ended up raising interest rates. If they stay high too long, the slowdown could give rise to stagnation.
c1-09-consolidation.canDo: I can explain economic causes, forecasts and past-to-present policy links in formal register.

c1-10-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Reviewing a Workplace Policy
c1-10-01.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague asks about the new schedule policy at your office. Management expects to improve work-life balance, and it is advisable that the union review the working hours.
c1-10-01.prompt: Explain both points in one sentence, contrasting a same-subject infinitive with que + subjunctive.
cues: State that management expects to improve work-life balance
Add that it is advisable for the union to review the working day
c1-10-01.target: La dirección espera mejorar la conciliación y conviene que el sindicato revise la jornada laboral.
c1-10-01.english: Management expects to improve work-life balance, and it is advisable that the union review the working day.
c1-10-01.canDo: I can use the infinitive for general policies and same-subject goals in workplace Spanish.

c1-10-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Automation and Training Trends
c1-10-02.scenario: You are Meg. In a seminar, a classmate asks how automation and training affect staff turnover. You want to say that as automation advances, the more training a company offers, the lower staff turnover is.
c1-10-02.prompt: Summarise the trend in one formal sentence.
cues: Open with the gradual advance of automation
Link more training to lower staff turnover
c1-10-02.target: A medida que avanza la automatización, cuanta más capacitación ofrece una empresa, menor es la rotación.
c1-10-02.english: As automation advances, the more training a company offers, the lower staff turnover is.
c1-10-02.canDo: I can link two proportional labour trends with *cuanto más / menos* and agree *cuanto* before a noun.

c1-10-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Assessing Hybrid Work
c1-10-03.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague asks why your department supports the hybrid model. It not only gives flexible hours, but also improves staff retention.
c1-10-03.prompt: Give both reasons in one balanced sentence.
cues: Mention that the hybrid model provides flexible hours
Add with a second verb that it improves retention
c1-10-03.target: La modalidad híbrida no solo ofrece flexibilidad horaria, sino que también mejora la retención.
c1-10-03.english: The hybrid model not only offers flexible hours, but also improves retention.
c1-10-03.canDo: I can choose between *sino (también)* and *sino que (también)* depending on whether a second conjugated verb follows.

c1-10-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Payroll vs. Self-Employment
c1-10-04.scenario: You are Meg. A classmate asks about the difference between salaried work and freelancing. In many companies they pay good benefits on the payroll, whereas when a woman works self-employed, she covers her own benefits.
c1-10-04.prompt: Compare both situations in one sentence using a third-person plural impersonal and indefinite una.
cues: Say what many companies offer on the payroll without naming them
Contrast it with what a woman covers when working self-employed
c1-10-04.target: En muchas empresas ofrecen buenas prestaciones en nómina, mientras que cuando una trabaja por cuenta propia cubre sus propias prestaciones.
c1-10-04.english: In many companies they offer good benefits on the payroll, whereas when you (as a woman) work self-employed you cover your own benefits.
c1-10-04.canDo: I can describe unnamed employer or sector practices with a subjectless third-person plural verb.

c1-10-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Qualifying a Labour Policy
c1-10-05.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague says raising the minimum wage will solve every wage inequality. You agree that the minimum wage protects basic income, but add the caveat that the pay gap still persists.
c1-10-05.prompt: Respond in two sentences using a formal contrast marker that adds a limit.
cues: Acknowledge that the minimum wage protects basic income
Add the caveat that the pay gap persists
c1-10-05.target: El salario mínimo protege los ingresos básicos. Ahora bien, la brecha salarial persiste.
c1-10-05.english: The minimum wage protects basic income. That said, the pay gap persists.
c1-10-05.canDo: I can distinguish *en cambio*, *por el contrario*, *no obstante* and *ahora bien* in formal argument.

c1-10-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Summarising the Labour Market
c1-10-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. A classmate asks you to summarise the main takeaway of your labour-market seminar in one sentence: both continuous training and collective bargaining improve job stability, and it is advisable that management respect working hours.
c1-10-consolidation.prompt: Summarise the takeaway in one formal sentence.
cues: Pair continuous training and collective bargaining as equal factors for job stability
Add that it is advisable for management to respect the working day
c1-10-consolidation.target: Tanto la capacitación continua como la negociación colectiva mejoran la estabilidad laboral, y conviene que la dirección respete la jornada laboral.
c1-10-consolidation.english: Both continuous training and collective bargaining improve job stability, and it is advisable that management respect the working day.
c1-10-consolidation.canDo: I can contrast general workplace rules with obligations on another party using the infinitive and *que* + subjunctive.

c1-11-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Fronting a Known Debate Topic
c1-11-01.scenario: You are Carlos. At a work meeting, a colleague mentions a report everyone already knows and asks who prepared it. You want to say that the moderator prepared that report, and that you did not claim that in your contribution.
c1-11-01.prompt: Answer in one sentence using clitic left dislocation for both known topics.
cues: Front the known report with its matching clitic and say the moderator prepared it
Front 'that' with its clitic and state you did not claim it in your contribution
c1-11-01.target: Ese informe lo preparó el moderador y eso no lo afirmé en mi intervención.
c1-11-01.english: The moderator prepared that report, and I did not claim that in my contribution.
c1-11-01.canDo: I can front a known direct object as a topic with its matching clitic (*lo, la, los, las*).

c1-11-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Conceding Before Rebutting
c1-11-02.scenario: You are Meg. In a university seminar, a classmate argues that there is consensus on the proposal. You agree that there is consensus on the goal, but point out that the counter-rebuttal contains a fallacy.
c1-11-02.prompt: Respond in one formal sentence: concede with es cierto que and pivot with sin embargo.
cues: Concede that there is consensus on the goal
Add that the counter-rebuttal contains a fallacy
c1-11-02.target: Es cierto que existe consenso sobre el objetivo; sin embargo, esa contrarréplica contiene una falacia.
c1-11-02.english: It is true that there is consensus on the goal; however, that counter-rebuttal contains a fallacy.
c1-11-02.canDo: I can concede a factual point with *es cierto que* and pivot with *sin embargo* or *no obstante*.

c1-11-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Entering a Formal Discussion
c1-11-03.scenario: You are Carlos. During a formal meeting with senior managers, you want to ask politely for the floor to resume the previous point, keeping it brief.
c1-11-03.prompt: Make your polite intervention in one formal usted sentence using the polite imperfect.
cues: Ask formally for permission to intervene
Say with the polite imperfect that you wanted to resume the previous point with brevity
c1-11-03.target: Si me permite intervenir, quería retomar el punto anterior con brevedad.
c1-11-03.english: If you allow me to intervene, I wanted to resume the previous point briefly.
c1-11-03.canDo: I can soften an interruption or request to speak using the polite imperfect.

c1-11-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Rejecting a Distortion
c1-11-04.scenario: You are Meg. In a seminar debate, a classmate misstates your argument. You want to ask them not to distort your words and clarify, using a reformulation marker, that you want them to answer what you actually said.
cues: Ask your debate partner not to distort your words
Reformulate clearly that you want them to answer what you said
c1-11-04.target: No tergiverse mis palabras; en otras palabras, responda a lo que dije.
c1-11-04.english: Do not distort my words; in other words, answer what I said.
c1-11-04.canDo: I can paraphrase or sharpen a claim in debate using *es decir* and *en otras palabras*.

c1-11-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Wrapping Up a Round Table
c1-11-05.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague asks how yesterday's round table went. The debate grew to the point that the moderator asked for brevity, and he delivered the summary in such a way that the closing was clear.
c1-11-05.prompt: Summarise both outcomes in one sentence using consecutive clauses.
cues: Say the debate grew to the point that the moderator asked for brevity
Add that he presented the summary in such a way that the closing was clear
c1-11-05.target: El debate creció hasta el punto de que el moderador pidió brevedad, y presentó la síntesis de tal manera que el cierre quedó claro.
c1-11-05.english: The debate grew to the point that the moderator asked for brevity, and he presented the summary in such a way that the closing was clear.
c1-11-05.canDo: I can express a real or intended result with *de tal manera que* + indicative or subjunctive.

c1-11-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Synthesising a Debate
c1-11-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. A classmate asks you to summarise a televised debate in one sentence: you know that approach well, and although there were concessions, the speakers did not reach consensus before the wrap-up.
c1-11-consolidation.prompt: Summarise the debate in one formal sentence combining topic dislocation and concession.
cues: Front the known approach with its clitic pronoun
Concede that there were concessions while stating they did not reach consensus before the closing
c1-11-consolidation.target: Ese enfoque lo conozco bien y, si bien hubo concesiones, los ponentes no lograron consenso antes del cierre.
c1-11-consolidation.english: I know that approach well and, although there were concessions, the speakers did not reach consensus before the wrap-up.
c1-11-consolidation.canDo: I can front known direct and indirect objects as topics with matching clitic pronouns.

c1-12-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Meanings of One Verb
c1-12-01.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague asks about an unclear email from management. You want to say that you are sorry the implicit message is causing confusion, and that the director tells us to review the context.
c1-12-01.prompt: Respond in one sentence using sentir que (regret) and decir que (instruction).
cues: Express regret that the implicit message is causing confusion
Add that the director tells us to review the context
c1-12-01.target: Siento que el mensaje implícito cause confusión y la directora dice que revisemos el contexto.
c1-12-01.english: I am sorry that the implicit message is causing confusion, and the director tells us to review the context.
c1-12-01.canDo: I can contrast the indicative and subjunctive meanings of *decir*, *sentir*, *entender*, *temer* and *suponer*.

c1-12-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Weighing Ambiguity
c1-12-02.scenario: You are Meg. A classmate asks whether readers will understand an ambiguous passage in a seminar text. You suspect the text is ambiguous on purpose and doubt that readers will deduce the intention without context.
c1-12-02.prompt: State both points in one sentence contrasting indicative suspicion with subjunctive doubt.
cues: Say you suspect the text is ambiguous
Add that you doubt the reader will deduce the intention without context
c1-12-02.target: Sospecho que el texto es ambiguo y dudo que el lector deduzca la intención sin contexto.
c1-12-02.english: I suspect that the text is ambiguous and I doubt that the reader will deduce the intention without context.
c1-12-02.canDo: I can use the subjunctive after *dudo que*, *no creo que*, *no es seguro que* and *no está claro que*.

c1-12-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Reporting a Hidden Hint
c1-12-03.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague asks what the manager asked after the meeting. The manager asked you whether you had noticed the double meaning and hinted that there would be changes in the reading of the plan.
c1-12-03.prompt: Report both in one past-tense sentence.
cues: Report the yes/no question about whether you had noticed the double meaning
Add that he hinted there would be changes in the reading of the plan
c1-12-03.target: Me preguntó si había notado el doble sentido e insinuó que habría cambios en la lectura del plan.
c1-12-03.english: He asked me whether I had noticed the double meaning and hinted that there would be changes in the reading of the plan.
c1-12-03.canDo: I can report yes/no and open questions in the past with *si* and accented interrogative words.

c1-12-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Surface vs. Subtext
c1-12-04.scenario: You are Meg. A classmate shows you a short review and asks what it really means. On the surface the note is neutral, but underneath it has a subtle connotation and one has to read between the lines.
c1-12-04.prompt: Explain your reading in one sentence contrasting surface appearance with underlying meaning.
cues: State that on the surface the note is neutral
Contrast it with the underlying subtle connotation and the need to read between the lines
c1-12-04.target: En apariencia, la nota es neutral; en el fondo, tiene una connotación sutil y conviene leer entre líneas.
c1-12-04.english: On the surface, the note is neutral; underneath, it has a subtle connotation and it is advisable to read between the lines.
c1-12-04.canDo: I can contrast a surface reading (*en apariencia*, *aparentemente*) with an underlying meaning (*en el fondo*).

c1-12-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Explaining a Written Mix-Up
c1-12-05.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague asks why a joke in a work chat caused a mix-up. Explain that the other person reacted as if the irony were literal and answered as if they had not read the context.
c1-12-05.prompt: Explain both reactions in one sentence using como si.
cues: Say they reacted as if the irony were literal
Add that they answered as if they had not read the context
c1-12-05.target: Reaccionó como si la ironía fuera literal y contestó como si no hubiera leído el contexto.
c1-12-05.english: He reacted as if the irony were literal and answered as if he had not read the context.
c1-12-05.canDo: I can use *como si* + imperfect or pluperfect subjunctive to describe counterfactual reactions.

c1-12-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Analysing Tone in Writing
c1-12-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. A classmate asks you to summarise why written misunderstandings happen in one sentence: writing in a hurry entails leaving room for ambiguity, and people often react as if a subtle remark were literal.
c1-12-consolidation.prompt: Summarise the idea in one formal sentence combining suponer que (+ subjunctive) and como si.
cues: State that writing in a hurry entails leaving room for ambiguity
Add that people often react as if a subtle remark were literal
c1-12-consolidation.target: Escribir con prisa supone que dejemos margen para la ambigüedad y muchas veces reaccionamos como si una frase sutil fuera literal.
c1-12-consolidation.english: Writing in a hurry entails leaving room for ambiguity, and we often react as if a subtle sentence were literal.
c1-12-consolidation.canDo: I can contrast the indicative and subjunctive meanings of double-mood verbs such as *decir*, *sentir*, *comprender* and *suponer*.

c1-13-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Duty vs. Regulation
c1-13-01.scenario: You are Meg. After a bioethics seminar, a classmate asks why a clinic was criticised. Explain in one sentence that every doctor must protect confidentiality under the code of ethics, and that the clinic should have consulted the ethics committee.
c1-13-01.prompt: Respond in one sentence using deber + infinitive and debería haber + past participle.
cues: State the professional duty to protect confidentiality under the code of ethics
Add the retrospective critique that the clinic should have consulted the ethics committee
c1-13-01.target: Todo médico debe proteger la confidencialidad según el código ético, y la clínica debería haber consultado al comité de ética.
c1-13-01.english: Every doctor must protect confidentiality according to the code of ethics, and the clinic should have consulted the ethics committee.
c1-13-01.canDo: I can distinguish moral duty (*deber*, *haber de*) from external legal or institutional requirements (*tener que*).

c1-13-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Trial Protocol Order
c1-13-02.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague asks how a clinical trial protects participants before a new drug is given. Explain in one sentence that before the drug is prescribed, the patient signs the informed consent, and after the committee has evaluated the results, the trial begins.
c1-13-02.prompt: Respond in one sentence using antes de que + subjunctive and después de que + present perfect subjunctive.
cues: State that before the drug is prescribed, the patient signs the informed consent
Add that after the committee has evaluated the results, the clinical trial begins
c1-13-02.target: Antes de que se prescriba el fármaco, el paciente firma el consentimiento informado, y después de que el comité haya evaluado los resultados, empieza el ensayo clínico.
c1-13-02.english: Before the drug is prescribed, the patient signs the informed consent, and after the committee has evaluated the results, the clinical trial begins.
c1-13-02.canDo: I can use *antes de que* + subjunctive for clinical procedures involving a subject shift or passive *se*.

c1-13-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Weighing Risks and Efficacy
c1-13-03.scenario: You are Meg. During a university discussion on biomedical research, a student questions a new gene therapy. Reply in one sentence that despite having shown efficacy against the placebo, the treatment still needs monitoring even though side effects may be mild.
c1-13-03.prompt: Respond in one sentence using pese a haber + past participle and pese a que + subjunctive.
cues: Concede that the treatment has shown efficacy against the placebo
State that it still requires monitoring even though side effects may be mild
c1-13-03.target: Pese a haber mostrado eficacia frente al placebo, el tratamiento requiere vigilancia, pese a que los efectos secundarios sean leves.
c1-13-03.english: Despite having shown efficacy against the placebo, the treatment requires monitoring, even though the side effects may be mild.
c1-13-03.canDo: I can contrast indicative (established fact) and subjunctive (hypothetical or backgrounded objection) after *a pesar de que* and *pese a que*.

c1-13-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Universal Patient Rights
c1-13-04.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague asks how a hospital charter defines fair treatment for patients with serious conditions. Explain in one sentence that whatever the medical conditions may be, health equity guarantees palliative care and whoever acts as a donor receives full information.
c1-13-04.prompt: Respond in one sentence using cualesquiera que sean and quienquiera que + subjunctive.
cues: State that whatever the medical conditions may be, health equity guarantees palliative care
Add that whoever acts as a donor receives full information
c1-13-04.target: Cualesquiera que sean las patologías, la equidad sanitaria garantiza los cuidados paliativos, y quienquiera que actúe como donante recibe información completa.
c1-13-04.english: Whatever the medical conditions may be, health equity guarantees palliative care, and whoever acts as a donor receives full information.
c1-13-04.canDo: I can use plural *cualesquiera que sean* and past-tense *cualquiera que fuera* / *quienquiera que* + imperfect subjunctive.

c1-13-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Past Accountability
c1-13-05.scenario: You are Meg. After reading a bioethics essay on public health, a friend asks what went wrong in a past immunisation campaign. Explain in one sentence that if the authorities had acted with transparency, they would have avoided the accusation of negligence and today there would be less distrust.
c1-13-05.prompt: Respond in one sentence using si + hubiera + past participle, habría + past participle and a simple conditional.
cues: State the past counterfactual condition about acting with transparency
Give the past result of avoiding the accusation of negligence and the present result of less distrust today
c1-13-05.target: Si las autoridades hubieran actuado con transparencia, habrían evitado la acusación de negligencia y hoy habría menos desconfianza.
c1-13-05.english: If the authorities had acted with transparency, they would have avoided the accusation of negligence and today there would be less distrust.
c1-13-05.canDo: I can evaluate past institutional accountability with *si* + *hubiera/hubiese* + past participle and *habría* + past participle.

c1-13-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Bioethics Synthesis
c1-13-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. At an office lunch, a colleague asks what makes clinical trials ethically sound. Summarise in two sentences that before a drug is administered, the patient must sign the informed consent, and that if a centre had not consulted the ethics committee, it would have acted with negligence.
c1-13-consolidation.prompt: Respond in two sentences using antes de que + subjunctive, deber + infinitive and si + hubiera + past participle.
cues: State that before a drug is administered, the patient must sign the informed consent
Add that if a centre had not consulted the ethics committee, it would have acted with negligence
c1-13-consolidation.target: Antes de que se administre un fármaco, el paciente debe firmar el consentimiento informado. Si un centro no hubiera consultado al comité de ética, habría actuado con negligencia.
c1-13-consolidation.english: Before a drug is administered, the patient must sign the informed consent. If a centre had not consulted the ethics committee, it would have acted with negligence.
c1-13-consolidation.canDo: I can distinguish moral duty, retrospective ethical critique and legal requirement in health contexts.

c1-14-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Grid Targets
c1-14-01.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague asks about the regional energy transition plan. Explain in one sentence that by the time the reform enters into force, the electricity grid will have expanded its capacity and emissions will have been reduced.
c1-14-01.prompt: Respond in one sentence using para cuando + present subjunctive and futuro perfecto (active and passive se).
cues: State that by the time the reform enters into force, the electricity grid will have expanded its capacity
Add that emissions will have been reduced
c1-14-01.target: Para cuando entre en vigor la reforma, la red eléctrica habrá ampliado su capacidad y se habrán reducido las emisiones.
c1-14-01.english: By the time the reform enters into force, the electricity grid will have expanded its capacity and emissions will have been reduced.
c1-14-01.canDo: I can pair *para cuando* + present subjunctive with *futuro perfecto* to state future policy milestones.

c1-14-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Carbon Policy Scenario
c1-14-02.scenario: You are Meg. In a university policy seminar, a classmate asks how to cut fossil-fuel use. Reply in one sentence that if a carbon tax were applied and mitigation were incentivised, fossil-fuel use would fall faster.
c1-14-02.prompt: Respond in one sentence using si se + imperfect subjunctive and the conditional.
cues: State the condition of applying a carbon tax and incentivising mitigation
Give the conditional result that fossil-fuel use would fall faster
c1-14-02.target: Si se aplicara un impuesto al carbono y se incentivara la mitigación, el uso de combustibles fósiles bajaría más rápido.
c1-14-02.english: If a carbon tax were applied and mitigation were incentivised, fossil-fuel use would fall faster.
c1-14-02.canDo: I can model policy scenarios with *si se* + imperfect subjunctive (*-ra* or *-se*) and the conditional.

c1-14-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Wetland Rules
c1-14-03.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague asks what measures protect the nearby wetland. Explain in one sentence that industrial discharges must be controlled and ecological-restoration plans have been approved.
c1-14-03.prompt: Respond in one sentence using passive se with a plural modal and a plural compound tense.
cues: State that industrial discharges must be controlled
Add that ecological-restoration plans have been approved
c1-14-03.target: Se deben controlar los vertidos industriales y se han aprobado planes de restauración ecológica.
c1-14-03.english: Industrial discharges must be controlled and ecological-restoration plans have been approved.
c1-14-03.canDo: I can match plural nouns with plural modals (*se deben controlar*) and compound tenses (*se han aprobado*) in passive *se*.

c1-14-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Citing Climate Findings
c1-14-04.scenario: You are Meg. A friend asks what the latest environmental study says about dry regions. Summarise in one sentence that according to the study, global warming worsens water scarcity and threatens the ecosystem.
c1-14-04.prompt: Respond in one sentence using según + verb (without que) or de acuerdo con.
cues: Attribute the finding to the study without inserting que after según
State that global warming worsens water scarcity and threatens the ecosystem
c1-14-04.target: Según señala el estudio, el calentamiento global agrava la escasez hídrica y amenaza el ecosistema.
c1-14-04.english: As the study points out, global warming worsens water scarcity and threatens the ecosystem.
c1-14-04.canDo: I can attribute technical findings using *advertir*, *señalar*, *concluir* and *informar de que*.

c1-14-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Policy Priorities
c1-14-05.scenario: You are Carlos. After reading a climate-policy report, a colleague asks what matters most for real results. Reply in one sentence that what was agreed in the climate agreement demands oversight, and that the most urgent things are investments in water management.
c1-14-05.prompt: Respond in one sentence using lo acordado and lo más urgente son + plural noun.
cues: State that what was agreed in the climate agreement demands oversight
Add that the most urgent things are investments in water management
c1-14-05.target: Lo acordado en el acuerdo climático exige fiscalización, y lo más urgente son las inversiones en gestión hídrica.
c1-14-05.english: What was agreed in the climate agreement demands oversight, and the most urgent things are investments in water management.
c1-14-05.canDo: I can frame policy priorities with neuter *lo* + formal adjectives and past participles (*lo prioritario, lo acordado*).

c1-14-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Climate Policy Synthesis
c1-14-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. At a student panel on sustainability, someone asks how cities can reach climate neutrality. Summarise in two sentences that by 2040 emissions will have been reduced, and that the priority is to strengthen oversight and the circular economy.
c1-14-consolidation.prompt: Respond in two sentences using futuro perfecto with passive se, and lo prioritario.
cues: State that by 2040 emissions will have been reduced
Add that the priority is to strengthen oversight and the circular economy
c1-14-consolidation.target: Para 2040 se habrán reducido las emisiones. Lo prioritario es ampliar la fiscalización y la economía circular.
c1-14-consolidation.english: By 2040 emissions will have been reduced. The priority is to expand oversight and the circular economy.
c1-14-consolidation.canDo: I can express climate targets and estimates with *futuro perfecto*.

c1-15-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Questioning Neutrality
c1-15-01.scenario: You are Meg. In a university discussion on artificial intelligence, a classmate claims that a predictive model is completely fair. Reply in one sentence that you do not consider that the algorithm has eliminated algorithmic bias, and that opacity remains a problem.
c1-15-01.prompt: Respond in one sentence using no considero que + present perfect subjunctive.
cues: State that you do not consider that the algorithm has eliminated algorithmic bias
Add that opacity remains a problem
c1-15-01.target: No considero que el algoritmo haya eliminado el sesgo algorítmico, y la opacidad sigue siendo un problema.
c1-15-01.english: I do not consider that the algorithm has eliminated algorithmic bias, and opacity remains a problem.
c1-15-01.canDo: I can evaluate past or completed AI claims with *no considero que* + perfect subjunctive and *no creía que* + imperfect subjunctive.

c1-15-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Responding to a Data Breach
c1-15-02.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague asks why the office updated its privacy policy. Explain in one sentence that in the wake of the data breach, the company expanded encryption under the data-protection law.
c1-15-02.prompt: Respond in one sentence using a raíz de and en virtud de.
cues: State what happened in the wake of the data breach
Add that encryption was expanded under the data-protection law
c1-15-02.target: A raíz de la filtración de datos, la empresa amplió el cifrado en virtud de la ley de protección de datos.
c1-15-02.english: In the wake of the data breach, the company expanded encryption under the data-protection law.
c1-15-02.canDo: I can express cause, legal basis, topic and contrast with *a raíz de*, *en virtud de*, *frente a*, *en torno a* and *con respecto a*.

c1-15-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Framing Disinformation
c1-15-03.scenario: You are Meg. A friend asks why online rumours spread so fast. Explain in one sentence that it is not synthetic content that worries you most, but the lack of verification, and that it is in echo chambers where disinformation grows.
c1-15-03.prompt: Respond in one sentence using no es X lo que..., sino Y and es en... donde...
cues: Contrast synthetic content with the lack of verification using a contrastive cleft
Add that it is in the echo chamber where disinformation grows
c1-15-03.target: No es el contenido sintético lo que más me preocupa, sino la falta de verificación, y es en la cámara de eco donde crece la desinformación.
c1-15-03.english: It is not synthetic content that worries me most, but the lack of verification, and it is in the echo chamber where disinformation grows.
c1-15-03.canDo: I can use contrastive clefts (*no es X lo que..., sino Y*) and inverted pseudo-clefts (*X es lo que...*) for rhetorical focus.

c1-15-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Reporting a Tech Ruling
c1-15-04.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague asks what the oversight authority decided after inspecting a high-risk tool. Reply in one sentence that the authority ordered that the algorithm be audited and that human oversight be guaranteed.
c1-15-04.prompt: Respond in one sentence using ordenó que + passive se + imperfect subjunctive.
cues: Report that the authority ordered the algorithm to be audited
Add that it ordered human oversight to be guaranteed
c1-15-04.target: La autoridad ordenó que se auditara el algoritmo y que se garantizara la supervisión humana.
c1-15-04.english: The authority ordered that the algorithm be audited and that human oversight be guaranteed.
c1-15-04.canDo: I can report standing regulatory mandates (*exige que se audite*) and past rulings (*ordenó que se auditaran*) with passive *se*.

c1-15-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Challenging Tech Myths
c1-15-05.scenario: You are Meg. After reading an op-ed on tech ethics, a classmate says open-source tools solve bias automatically. Reply in one sentence that we must not take for granted that open source eliminates algorithmic discrimination, nor consider the doubts about intellectual property closed.
c1-15-05.prompt: Respond in one sentence using no debemos dar por sentado que + subjunctive and dar por cerradas + noun.
cues: Challenge the assumption that open source eliminates algorithmic discrimination
Add that we cannot consider the doubts about intellectual property closed
c1-15-05.target: No debemos dar por sentado que el código abierto elimine la discriminación algorítmica ni dar por cerradas las dudas sobre la propiedad intelectual.
c1-15-05.english: We must not take for granted that open source eliminates algorithmic discrimination, nor consider the doubts about intellectual property closed.
c1-15-05.canDo: I can contrast affirmative *dar por hecho/sentado que* (+ indicative) with negated *no dar por sentado que* (+ subjunctive).

c1-15-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Digital Ethics Synthesis
c1-15-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. At a work coffee break, a colleague asks what keeps artificial intelligence accountable. Summarise in two sentences that you do not consider that the system has guaranteed neutrality, and that tech regulation requires that every algorithm be audited.
c1-15-consolidation.prompt: Respond in two sentences using no considero que + present perfect subjunctive and exige que se + present subjunctive.
cues: Say that you do not consider that the system has guaranteed neutrality
Add that tech regulation requires every algorithm to be audited
c1-15-consolidation.target: No considero que el sistema haya garantizado la neutralidad. La regulación tecnológica exige que se audite cada algoritmo.
c1-15-consolidation.english: I do not consider that the system has guaranteed neutrality. Tech regulation requires that every algorithm be audited.
c1-15-consolidation.canDo: I can evaluate technological claims using formal opinion verbs across indicative and subjunctive.

c1-16-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Neighbourhood Change
c1-16-01.scenario: You are Meg. In a university seminar on urbanism, a classmate asks how the historic centre of a city changes under tourism. Reply in one sentence contrasting how the historic centre used to offer affordable housing with how holiday rentals have transformed the neighbourhood fabric.
c1-16-01.prompt: Respond in one sentence using the imperfect for the past baseline and the present perfect for the ongoing change.
cues: Contrast how the historic centre used to offer affordable housing
Add how holiday rentals have transformed the neighbourhood fabric
c1-16-01.target: Antes el casco histórico ofrecía vivienda asequible, pero el alquiler vacacional ha transformado el tejido vecinal.
c1-16-01.english: Before, the historic centre offered affordable housing, but holiday rentals have transformed the neighbourhood fabric.
c1-16-01.canDo: I can contrast a neighbourhood's past baseline (*imperfecto*) with ongoing housing shifts (present perfect).

c1-16-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Urban Pressure
c1-16-02.scenario: You are Carlos. At the office, a colleague asks why so many people are moving out of the city centre. Explain in one sentence that due to property speculation the housing market has become unsustainable for many tenants and several streets have been left depopulated.
c1-16-02.prompt: Respond in one sentence using volverse or hacerse and quedarse + adjective.
cues: Say that the housing market has become unsustainable for many tenants due to property speculation
Add that several streets have been left depopulated
c1-16-02.target: Por la especulación inmobiliaria, el mercado inmobiliario se ha vuelto insostenible para muchos inquilinos y varias calles se han quedado despobladas.
c1-16-02.english: Because of property speculation, the housing market has become unsustainable for many tenants and several streets have been left depopulated.
c1-16-02.canDo: I can distinguish *volverse*, *quedarse*, *convertirse en* and *hacerse* for urban and market shifts.

c1-16-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Policy Precision
c1-16-03.scenario: You are Meg. In a seminar presentation on social housing, explain in one sentence that the urban plan the municipality is backing supports social housing and curbs spatial segregation.
c1-16-03.prompt: Respond in one sentence using por el que with apostar por.
cues: Mention the urban plan that the municipality is backing
Say that it supports social housing and curbs spatial segregation
c1-16-03.target: El plan urbanístico por el que apuesta el municipio apoya la vivienda social y frena la segregación espacial.
c1-16-03.english: The urban plan that the municipality is backing supports social housing and curbs spatial segregation.
c1-16-03.canDo: I can keep verb-governed prepositions (*por*, *en*, *de*, *a*, *con*) before *el que / la que / los que / las que*.

c1-16-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Reframing the Debate
c1-16-04.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague argues that promoting urban sprawl is the only solution to the housing shortage. Reframe the debate in one sentence: it is not about promoting urban sprawl, but about renovating the housing stock and improving urban mobility.
c1-16-04.prompt: Respond in one sentence using no se trata de … sino de …
cues: Reject the idea that it is about promoting urban sprawl
Reframe it around renovating the housing stock and improving urban mobility
c1-16-04.target: No se trata de impulsar la expansión urbana, sino de rehabilitar el parque de viviendas y mejorar la movilidad urbana.
c1-16-04.english: It is not a matter of promoting urban sprawl, but of renovating the housing stock and improving urban mobility.
c1-16-04.canDo: I can reframe an urban-planning debate with *no se trata de X, sino de Y*.

c1-16-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Pacing Urban Shifts
c1-16-05.scenario: You are Meg. After reading a feature report on housing, summarise in two sentences that as capital gains grew, affordable housing declined, and that as soon as regulated rent is approved, tenants will have greater stability.
c1-16-05.prompt: Respond in two sentences using conforme + imperfect and en cuanto + present subjunctive.
cues: State that as capital gains grew, affordable housing declined
Add that as soon as regulated rent is approved, tenants will have greater stability
c1-16-05.target: Conforme crecía la plusvalía, disminuía la vivienda asequible. En cuanto se apruebe el alquiler regulado, los inquilinos tendrán mayor estabilidad.
c1-16-05.english: As capital gains grew, affordable housing declined. As soon as regulated rent is approved, tenants will have greater stability.
c1-16-05.canDo: I can pace past urban shifts with *apenas*, *al cabo de* and *conforme* + indicative.

c1-16-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Cities & Housing Synthesis
c1-16-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. In a workplace discussion about housing policy, summarise in two sentences that the neighbourhood used to offer affordable housing but the housing market has become unsustainable for many tenants, and that it is not only a matter of building more, but of renovating the housing stock in a compact city.
c1-16-consolidation.prompt: Respond in two sentences using imperfect vs present perfect with volverse, and no se trata solo de … sino de …
cues: Contrast how the neighbourhood used to offer affordable housing with how the housing market has become unsustainable for many tenants
Reframe the solution around renovating the housing stock in a compact city rather than only building more
c1-16-consolidation.target: Antes el barrio ofrecía vivienda asequible, pero el mercado inmobiliario se ha vuelto insostenible para muchos inquilinos. No se trata solo de edificar más, sino de rehabilitar el parque de viviendas en una ciudad compacta.
c1-16-consolidation.english: Before, the neighbourhood offered affordable housing, but the housing market has become unsustainable for many tenants. It is not only a matter of building more, but of renovating the housing stock in a compact city.
c1-16-consolidation.canDo: I can contrast historical neighbourhood baselines with ongoing shifts in housing affordability.

c1-17-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Aspectual Se
c1-17-01.scenario: You are Meg. After class, a classmate asks if you finished the novel she lent you. Reply in one sentence saying that you read the whole novel in one sitting and drank the cup of tea in one gulp.
c1-17-01.prompt: Respond in one sentence using me leí and me tomé or me bebí with whole, definite objects.
cues: Say that you read the whole novel in one sitting
Add that you drank the cup of tea in one gulp
c1-17-01.target: Me leí la novela entera de una sentada y me tomé la taza de té de un trago.
c1-17-01.english: I read the whole novel in one sitting and drank the cup of tea in one gulp.
c1-17-01.canDo: I can use aspectual *se* (*comerse*, *tomarse*, *leerse*, *saberse*) with whole, definite or quantified objects.

c1-17-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Kitchen Mishap
c1-17-02.scenario: You are Carlos. At the office, a colleague asks why you arrived a few minutes late. Explain in one sentence that due to a slip-up you accidentally forgot your keys and spilled broth on the tablecloth.
c1-17-02.prompt: Respond in one sentence using accidental se (se me olvidaron and se me derramó).
cues: Explain that due to a slip-up you accidentally forgot the keys
Add that you accidentally spilled broth on the tablecloth
c1-17-02.target: Por un despiste, se me olvidaron las llaves y se me derramó el caldo en el mantel.
c1-17-02.english: Due to a slip-up, I accidentally forgot the keys and spilled the broth on the tablecloth.
c1-17-02.canDo: I can form accidental *se* clauses with *se* before *me / te / le / nos / les*.

c1-17-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Lively Reactions
c1-17-03.scenario: You are Meg. A friend tells you that the sponge cake burned right before an afternoon gathering, but there are still snacks ready. React in one sentence saying what a shame that the sponge cake burned, and thank goodness she prepared some snacks.
c1-17-03.prompt: Respond in one sentence using ¡Qué pena que…! + present perfect subjunctive and menos mal que + indicative.
cues: Express regret that the sponge cake burned
Add relief that she prepared some snacks
c1-17-03.target: ¡Qué pena que se haya quemado el bizcocho, pero menos mal que preparaste un picoteo!
c1-17-03.english: What a shame that the sponge cake burned, but thank goodness you prepared some snacks!
c1-17-03.canDo: I can react to recent events with *¡Qué raro / pena / suerte que!* + present perfect subjunctive.

c1-17-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Changing Habits
c1-17-04.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague asks about your morning routine. Reply in one sentence saying that before you used to have a strong coffee in the morning, but you stopped drinking so much coffee last month.
c1-17-04.prompt: Respond in one sentence using solía tomarme and dejé de + infinitive.
cues: Say that before you used to have a strong coffee in the morning
Add that you stopped drinking so much coffee last month
c1-17-04.target: Antes solía tomarme un café cargado por la mañana, pero dejé de tomar tanto café el mes pasado.
c1-17-04.english: Before, I used to have a strong coffee in the morning, but I stopped drinking so much coffee last month.
c1-17-04.canDo: I can layer *soler* with aspectual *se* while avoiding invalid tenses.

c1-17-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Saving the Evening
c1-17-05.scenario: You are Meg. Tell a classmate in two sentences that you were on the verge of cancelling dinner but saved it by the skin of your teeth, and that you are never improvising a recipe at the last minute again.
c1-17-05.prompt: Respond in two sentences using estuve a punto de and no vuelvo a + infinitive.
cues: State that you were on the verge of cancelling dinner, but saved it by the skin of your teeth
Vow that you are never improvising a recipe at the last minute again
c1-17-05.target: Estuve a punto de cancelar la cena, pero nos salvamos por los pelos. No vuelvo a improvisar una receta a última hora.
c1-17-05.english: I was on the verge of cancelling dinner, but we saved it by the skin of our teeth. I am never improvising a recipe at the last minute again.
c1-17-05.canDo: I can narrate close calls with *estuve a punto de* + infinitive and *por los pelos*.

c1-17-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Everyday Aspect Synthesis
c1-17-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Tell a colleague in two sentences about a weekend dinner: the guests ate the whole stew without leaving a bite, even though earlier you were on the verge of cancelling after a slip-up.
c1-17-consolidation.prompt: Respond in two sentences using se comieron (aspectual se) and estuve a punto de + infinitive.
cues: Say that the guests ate the whole stew without leaving a bite
Add that earlier you were on the verge of cancelling because of a slip-up
c1-17-consolidation.target: Los invitados se comieron el guiso entero sin dejar ni un bocado. Antes estuve a punto de cancelar la cena por un despiste.
c1-17-consolidation.english: The guests ate the whole stew without leaving a bite. Earlier I was on the verge of cancelling dinner because of a slip-up.
c1-17-consolidation.canDo: I can use aspectual *se* with whole, definite or quantified objects in everyday speech.

c1-18-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Spoken Markers
