c1-18-01.scenario: You are Meg. After a university talk, a classmate asks if the guest speaker is staying for coffee. Answer in one sentence starting with well, explaining that he already left after the break, in short he isn't staying, and asking for agreement.
c1-18-01.prompt: Respond in one sentence using pues, vamos and ¿verdad? or ¿no?.
cues: Open your answer naturally and say that he left after the break
Sum up that he isn't staying and ask for agreement
c1-18-01.target: Pues, se fue después de la pausa; vamos, que no se queda, ¿verdad?
c1-18-01.english: Well, he left after the break; in short, he isn't staying, right?
c1-18-01.canDo: I can choose pan-Hispanic markers (*pues*, *bueno*, *mira/mire*, *oye/oiga*, *o sea*, *vamos*, *¿verdad?*) by function.

c1-18-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Softening an Excuse
c1-18-02.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague invites you to stay for a long chat after work, but you have too much work. Soften your refusal in one sentence saying it's not that you don't want to stay, it's just that you have too much work today.
c1-18-02.prompt: Respond in one sentence using no es que + subjunctive and es que + indicative.
cues: Reject the idea that you do not want to stay
Give the real reason that you have too much work today
c1-18-02.target: No es que no quiera quedarme, es que hoy tengo demasiado trabajo.
c1-18-02.english: It's not that I don't want to stay, it's just that today I have too much work.
c1-18-02.canDo: I can buy time with *a ver* and soften excuses with *es que* and *No es que* + subjunctive, *es que* + indicative.

c1-18-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Hedging Disagreement
c1-18-03.scenario: You are Meg. In a seminar, a classmate thinks the new dialogue format will fail. Reply in one sentence conceding that he may be right about the difficulty, but adding that maybe it will work better tomorrow.
c1-18-03.prompt: Respond in one sentence using puede que + subjunctive and a lo mejor + indicative.
cues: Concede that he may be right
Add that maybe it will work better tomorrow
c1-18-03.target: Puede que tengas razón, pero a lo mejor funciona mejor mañana.
c1-18-03.english: You may be right, but maybe it will work better tomorrow.
c1-18-03.canDo: I can soften disagreement with *puede que* and *dudo que* + subjunctive.

c1-18-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Retelling an Interview
c1-18-04.scenario: You are Carlos. A week after hearing a radio presenter on a local station, tell a colleague in one sentence that the presenter said she had prepared the anecdote the day before and would return there the next day.
c1-18-04.prompt: Respond in one sentence using shifted time and place pointers (el día anterior, allí, al día siguiente).
cues: Report that the presenter said she had prepared the anecdote the day before
Add that she would return there the next day
c1-18-04.target: La locutora dijo que había preparado la anécdota el día anterior y que volvería allí al día siguiente.
c1-18-04.english: The presenter said that she had prepared the anecdote the day before and that she would return there the next day.
c1-18-04.canDo: I can shift time and place words (*al día siguiente*, *el día anterior*, *allí*, *ir*) when retelling from another day or place.

c1-18-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Candid Interview Stance
c1-18-05.scenario: You are Meg. After listening to a radio interview with a local baker, tell a friend in two sentences: to tell the truth, opening a bakery sounds very hard; that said, the neighbourhood clientele clearly values her work.
c1-18-05.prompt: Respond in two sentences using a decir verdad and dicho esto.
cues: Open candidly that opening a bakery sounds very hard
Pivot to conclude that the clientele values her work
c1-18-05.target: A decir verdad, abrir una panadería parece muy difícil. Dicho esto, la clientela valora mucho su trabajo.
c1-18-05.english: To tell the truth, opening a bakery seems very hard. That said, the clientele values her work a lot.
c1-18-05.canDo: I can open candid answers with *a decir verdad*, *para ser sincero / sincera* and *con franqueza*.

c1-18-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Conversation Markers Synthesis
c1-18-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. In a workplace meeting that has drifted off-topic, speak up in two sentences: well, let's return to the topic and get to the point; to be honest, it's not that the aside isn't interesting, it's just that we have little time.
c1-18-consolidation.prompt: Respond in two sentences using bueno, para ser sincero and no es que + subjunctive / es que + indicative.
cues: Shift back to the topic and ask to get to the point
Add candidly that it's not that the aside isn't interesting, it's just that you have little time
c1-18-consolidation.target: Bueno, volvamos al tema y vayamos al grano. Para ser sincero, no es que el inciso no sea interesante, es que tenemos poco tiempo.
c1-18-consolidation.english: Well, let's return to the topic and get to the point. To be honest, it's not that the aside isn't interesting, it's just that we have little time.
c1-18-consolidation.canDo: I can organise everyday Spanish talk with pan-Hispanic markers like *pues*, *bueno*, *oiga*, *o sea* and *vamos*.

c1-19-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Deadline Warning
c1-19-01.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague keeps sending her part of a report late. Warn her in one sentence: if she doesn't send you her part before noon, you will hand in the report without it.
c1-19-01.prompt: Respond in one sentence using como + present subjunctive.
cues: Open with a conditional warning about her part not arriving before noon
State that you will hand in the report without it
c1-19-01.target: Como no me mandes tu parte antes del mediodía, entregaré el informe sin ella.
c1-19-01.english: If you don't send me your part before noon, I will hand in the report without it.
c1-19-01.canDo: I can issue a warning or threat with *como* + present or perfect subjunctive.

c1-19-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Mixed Condition Backup
c1-19-02.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague is about to close a shared file without making a copy. Warn her in one sentence: if she closes the file without a copy, she will lose today's work.
c1-19-02.prompt: Respond in one sentence using a real si-clause (si + present indicative, then the future).
cues: Open with a real condition about closing the file without a copy
State the result: she will lose today's work
c1-19-02.target: Si cierras el archivo sin hacer una copia, perderás el trabajo de hoy.
c1-19-02.english: If you close the file without making a copy, you will lose today's work.
c1-19-02.canDo: I can form real *si*-clause warnings with the indicative and never put the present subjunctive or conditional after *si*.

c1-19-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Setting Conditions
c1-19-03.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague asks you to bring a report delivery forward. Reply in one sentence that you can't do it unless she sends you the attachment today.
c1-19-03.prompt: Respond in one sentence using a menos que + subjunctive.
cues: Say that you cannot bring the delivery forward
Name the only exception: she sends you the attachment today
c1-19-03.target: No puedo adelantar la entrega a menos que me envíes el anexo hoy.
c1-19-03.english: I can't bring the delivery forward unless you send me the attachment today.
c1-19-03.canDo: I can state a sole exception with *a menos que* / *salvo que* + subjunctive.

c1-19-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Compact Formal Warning
c1-19-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Write one formal warning for a team memo: the report must be sent before five; if that is not the case, the client will apply a penalty, and had we seen the technical failure earlier, we would have avoided the surcharge.
c1-19-04.prompt: Respond in two sentences using de no ser así and de haber + past participle.
cues: State the deadline and add what happens if not using de no ser así
Add a past counterfactual using de haber + participle about the technical failure and surcharge
c1-19-04.target: El informe debe enviarse antes de las cinco; de no ser así, el cliente aplicará una penalización. De haber visto el fallo técnico antes, habríamos evitado el recargo.
c1-19-04.english: The report must be sent before five; if that is not the case, the client will apply a penalty. Had we seen the technical failure earlier, we would have avoided the surcharge.
c1-19-04.canDo: I can express formal conditions with *de no ser así* and *de* + infinitive.

c1-19-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Near-Miss Relief
c1-19-05.scenario: You are Carlos. After narrowly avoiding a missed deadline thanks to a backup, tell Meg in two sentences: we should have reviewed the attachment earlier; if we hadn't saved that backup, all the work would have been in vain.
c1-19-05.prompt: Respond in two sentences using deberíamos haber + participle and si + pluperfect subjunctive + conditional perfect.
cues: Express regret that you should have reviewed the attachment earlier
Describe the near miss if you hadn't saved that backup
c1-19-05.target: Deberíamos haber revisado el anexo antes. Si no hubiéramos guardado aquel respaldo, todo el trabajo habría sido en vano.
c1-19-05.english: We should have reviewed the attachment earlier. If we hadn't saved that backup, all the work would have been in vain.
c1-19-05.canDo: I can express past regrets and reproaches with *debería haber*, *tendría que haber* and *me arrepiento de haber*.

c1-19-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Warnings & Conditions Synthesis
c1-19-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Before a tight Friday deadline, speak to a colleague in two sentences: warn her that if the two of you run late again you will both get a penalty, and add that you can finish with plenty of time to spare provided that you both check the backup before four.
c1-19-consolidation.prompt: Respond in two sentences using como + subjunctive and siempre que + subjunctive.
cues: Issue a warning with como + subjunctive about running late and facing a penalty
Add that you can finish in plenty of time provided that you check the backup before four
c1-19-consolidation.target: Como nos retrasemos otra vez, nos aplicarán una penalización. Podemos terminar con tiempo de sobra siempre que comprobemos el respaldo antes de las cuatro.
c1-19-consolidation.english: If we run late again, they will apply a penalty to us. We can finish with plenty of time to spare provided that we check the backup before four.
c1-19-consolidation.canDo: I can issue warnings with *como* + subjunctive and contrast them with causal *como* + indicative.

c1-20-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Conceding a Cost
c1-20-01.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague complains that the new software for the office is too costly. Concede that it is costly, then reply that it is worth it because it saves time.
c1-20-01.prompt: Respond in one sentence using the concessive future before «pero».
cues: Concede that the software is costly using the simple future
Contrast with «pero» to say it is worth it for the time it saves
c1-20-01.target: Será costoso, pero vale la pena por el tiempo que ahorra.
c1-20-01.english: It may well be costly, but it is worth it for the time it saves.
c1-20-01.canDo: I can concede a present point with the simple future before *pero*.

c1-20-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Defending a Project
c1-20-02.scenario: You are Meg. In a university seminar, a classmate calls a city transport reform a waste of money. Reply that despite the initial cost overrun, the project will be cost-effective in the long run.
c1-20-02.prompt: Respond in one sentence using «pese a» + noun phrase.
cues: Open with a formal concession mentioning the initial cost overrun
State that the project will be cost-effective in the long run
c1-20-02.target: Pese al sobrecosto inicial, el proyecto será rentable a largo plazo.
c1-20-02.english: Despite the initial cost overrun, the project will be cost-effective in the long run.
c1-20-02.canDo: I can use *pese a* and *a pesar de* cleanly with nouns, infinitives and full clauses.

c1-20-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Evaluating a Service
c1-20-03.scenario: You are Carlos. You and a colleague are talking about the monthly bus pass after a recent price rise. Comment that considering how high the fare is, the service leaves a lot to be desired.
c1-20-03.prompt: Respond in one sentence using «con lo» + adjective + «que».
cues: Open by noting how high the fare is
Evaluate the service as leaving a lot to be desired
c1-20-03.target: Con lo alta que es la tarifa, el servicio deja mucho que desear.
c1-20-03.english: Considering how high the fare is, the service leaves a lot to be desired.
c1-20-03.canDo: I can express surprise or complaint with *con lo* + adjective/adverb + *que* and *con lo que*.

c1-20-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Criticising an Oversight
c1-20-04.scenario: You are Meg. A faculty committee published a report on campus transport without mentioning student complaints. Tell a classmate it is regrettable that they overlooked the students' complaint.
c1-20-04.prompt: Respond in one sentence using an evaluative trigger + present perfect subjunctive.
cues: Open with a C1 value judgement calling the oversight regrettable
Refer to their having overlooked the students' complaint
c1-20-04.target: Es lamentable que hayan pasado por alto el reclamo de los estudiantes.
c1-20-04.english: It is regrettable that they overlooked the students' complaint.
c1-20-04.canDo: I can use higher-register evaluative triggers like *resulta absurdo que* and *es lamentable que* with the subjunctive.

c1-20-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Balanced Verdict on the Tram
c1-20-05.scenario: You are Carlos. A neighbour asks what you think of the new tram line. Give a balanced reply in two sentences: admit that the tram is punctual, then add a reservation that its route left out two neighbourhoods.
c1-20-05.prompt: Respond in two sentences using «Ahora bien,» to introduce the reservation.
cues: State in the first sentence that the tram is punctual
Open the second sentence with a reservation noting that the route left out two neighbourhoods
c1-20-05.target: El tranvía es puntual. Ahora bien, el trazado dejó fuera dos barrios.
c1-20-05.english: The tram is punctual. That said, the route left out two neighbourhoods.
c1-20-05.canDo: I can distinguish *ahora bien*, *no obstante*, *en cambio* and *por el contrario* in balanced arguments.

c1-20-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Weighing a Costly Upgrade
c1-20-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. A classmate asks whether the expensive new library renovation is worth it. Give a two-sentence evaluation: concede that it is costly but say it is worth it, then add that considering how long the works took, the result is still positive.
c1-20-consolidation.prompt: Respond in two sentences using the concessive future and «con lo» + adjective + «que».
cues: Concede that the renovation is costly, then contrast to say it is worth it
Add a second sentence noting how long the works were and that the result is positive
c1-20-consolidation.target: Será costosa, pero vale la pena. Con lo largas que fueron las obras, el resultado es positivo.
c1-20-consolidation.english: It may well be costly, but it is worth it. Considering how long the works were, the result is positive.
c1-20-consolidation.canDo: I can concede present and past points naturally with the future and conditional before *pero*.

c1-21-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Rejecting an Exaggeration
c1-21-01.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague acts as if spending ten minutes checking a short table were an impossible ordeal. React ironically in one exclamation: as if it were so difficult!
c1-21-01.prompt: Respond with one ironic exclamation using «¡Ni que» + imperfect subjunctive.
cues: Open with an ironic exclamation rejecting the assumption
State that it is not as if it were so difficult
c1-21-01.english: As if it were so difficult!
c1-21-01.canDo: I can reject an absurd present assumption with *¡Ni que* + imperfect subjunctive!

c1-21-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Dry Understatement
c1-21-02.scenario: You are Meg. A classmate hands you a draft summary that is eighty pages long. Comment with dry understatement that the summary is a tiny bit long and takes up eighty pages.
c1-21-02.prompt: Respond in one sentence using «un poquito» as ironic understatement.
cues: Describe the summary with dry understatement as a tiny bit long
Add the concrete detail that it has eighty pages
c1-21-02.target: El resumen es un poquito largo: tiene ochenta páginas.
c1-21-02.english: The summary is a tiny bit long: it has eighty pages.
c1-21-02.canDo: I can convey dry irony through understatement with *no está mal* and *un poquito*.

c1-21-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Sarcastic Reaction
c1-21-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Management just called another late-afternoon meeting without warning. Tell a colleague sarcastically how wonderful it is that they have called another meeting without warning.
c1-21-03.prompt: Respond with one sarcastic exclamation using «¡Qué maravilla que» + present perfect subjunctive.
cues: Open with mock delight at the news
Refer to their having called another meeting without warning
c1-21-03.target: ¡Qué maravilla que hayan convocado otra reunión sin avisar!
c1-21-03.english: How wonderful that they have called another meeting without warning!
c1-21-03.canDo: I can use mock emotional reactions like *¡Me encanta que...!* and *¡Qué maravilla que...!* with the subjunctive.

c1-21-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Deadpan Pretence
c1-21-04.scenario: You are Meg. A classmate arrived forty minutes late to a seminar and casually sat down without apologising. Describe this to a friend: he sat down as if nothing had happened.
c1-21-04.prompt: Respond in one sentence using «como si» + pluperfect subjunctive.
cues: State that he sat down
Add an unreal past comparison saying as if nothing had happened
c1-21-04.target: Se sentó como si no hubiera pasado nada.
c1-21-04.english: He sat down as if nothing had happened.
c1-21-04.canDo: I can use *como si* + pluperfect subjunctive for unreal comparisons with an earlier event.

c1-21-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Satirical Question
c1-21-05.scenario: You are Carlos. Your office just scheduled a two-hour meeting to discuss something a short email could settle. Ask a colleague a satirical rhetorical question: why send a short email when we can call a two-hour meeting?
c1-21-05.prompt: Respond with one satirical rhetorical question starting with «¿Para qué».
cues: Ask why send a short email
Contrast it with being able to call a two-hour meeting
c1-21-05.target: ¿Para qué enviar un correo breve cuando podemos convocar una reunión de dos horas?
c1-21-05.english: Why send a short email when we can call a two-hour meeting?
c1-21-05.canDo: I can use rhetorical questions, mock-heroic metaphor and repetition for satirical effect.

c1-21-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Mocking a Boast
c1-21-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague brags for ten minutes about arriving on time to one meeting. React in two sentences: first reject the boast ironically (as if he had performed a miracle!), then add that he speaks as if he had achieved a feat.
c1-21-consolidation.prompt: Respond in two sentences using «¡Ni que» + pluperfect subjunctive and «como si» + pluperfect subjunctive.
cues: Reject the boast ironically with an exclamation about performing a miracle
Add that he speaks as if he had achieved a feat
c1-21-consolidation.target: ¡Ni que hubiera hecho un milagro! Habla como si hubiera logrado una hazaña.
c1-21-consolidation.english: As if he had performed a miracle! He talks as if he had achieved a feat.
c1-21-consolidation.canDo: I can use *¡Ni que* + imperfect or pluperfect subjunctive! to reject absurd assumptions ironically.

c1-22-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Warm Invitation
c1-22-01.scenario: You are Carlos. You and a colleague just finished a long morning of work in the office. Invite her warmly in one question to grab a friendly coffee right near the corner.
c1-22-01.prompt: Respond with one warm question using «un cafecito».
cues: Suggest having a friendly coffee together
Mention that it is near the corner
c1-22-01.target: ¿Nos tomamos un cafecito cerca de la esquina?
c1-22-01.english: Shall we have a friendly coffee near the corner?
c1-22-01.canDo: I can use diminutives like *un cafecito* and *ahorita* for warmth, politeness or regional tone.

c1-22-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Softening a Request
c1-22-02.scenario: You are Meg. You walk up to a librarian's desk to ask a quick favour about a book. Soften your request in one polite sentence using the polite imperfect and a diminutive.
c1-22-02.prompt: Respond in one sentence using «Quería pedirle» + a softening diminutive.
cues: Open politely using the polite imperfect to say you wanted to ask a small favour
Refer to checking a book
c1-22-02.target: Disculpe, quería pedirle un favorcito con este libro.
c1-22-02.english: Excuse me, I wanted to ask you a small favour with this book.
c1-22-02.canDo: I can combine the polite imperfect (*quería*, *venía*, *llamaba*) with diminutives to soften requests.

c1-22-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Vivid Market Verdict
c1-22-03.scenario: You are Carlos. A friend asks what the Saturday neighbourhood market was like. Reply in one sentence that the market turned out to be extremely lively and the bread was delicious.
c1-22-03.prompt: Respond in one sentence using «resultar» and an «-ísimo» superlative.
cues: Say the market turned out to be extremely lively
Add that the bread was delicious
c1-22-03.target: El mercado resultó animadísimo y el pan estuvo riquísimo.
c1-22-03.english: The market turned out to be extremely lively and the bread was delicious.
c1-22-03.canDo: I can form *-ísimo* superlatives accurately, including spelling changes like *riquísimo* and *larguísimo*.

c1-22-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Sketching a Square
c1-22-04.scenario: You are Meg. You are describing a picturesque square you visited for a class paper. Describe it in one sentence: it is a picturesque square whose awnings cover the fruit stalls.
cues: Introduce the picturesque square
Connect it with «whose» to the awnings covering the fruit stalls
c1-22-04.target: Es una plaza pintoresca cuyos toldos cubren los puestos de fruta.
c1-22-04.english: It is a picturesque square whose awnings cover the fruit stalls.
c1-22-04.canDo: I can use *cuyo / cuya / cuyos / cuyas* accurately to connect a place to its features.

c1-22-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Opening a Crónica Observation
c1-22-05.scenario: You are Carlos. You are telling a colleague about a bustling Saturday market you visited. Open with a sentence-level stance adverb («curiously») to remark that in the middle of so much hubbub, nobody loses patience.
c1-22-05.prompt: Respond in one sentence opening with «Curiosamente,».
cues: Open with a sentence-level stance adverb expressing mild surprise
Note that amid so much hubbub nobody loses patience
c1-22-05.target: Curiosamente, en medio de tanto bullicio nadie pierde la paciencia.
c1-22-05.english: Curiously, in the middle of so much hubbub nobody loses patience.
c1-22-05.canDo: I can distinguish sentence-level stance adverbs (*Curiosamente, ...*, *Irónicamente, ...*) from manner adverbs.

c1-22-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Warm Praise for a Neighbourhood
c1-22-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. A classmate asks whether the little town with the Saturday market is worth visiting. Reply in two sentences: first say it is no rundown little town because its square comes across as endearing, then add frankly that you love having a friendly coffee there.
c1-22-consolidation.prompt: Respond in two sentences using a pejorative suffix, «resultar» and a diminutive.
cues: Reject calling it a rundown little town and say its square comes across as endearing
Add frankly that you love having a friendly coffee there
c1-22-consolidation.target: No es ningún pueblucho porque su plaza resulta entrañable. Francamente, me encanta tomar un cafecito allí.
c1-22-consolidation.english: It is no rundown little town because its square comes across as endearing. Frankly, I love having a friendly coffee there.
c1-22-consolidation.canDo: I can use diminutives, augmentatives and pejoratives to signal warmth, admiration or disdain.

c1-23-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Laughing Off a Blunder
c1-23-01.scenario: You are Carlos. At the office, a colleague asks what went wrong during the meeting. Reply in two sentences: first say you put your foot in it by mentioning a secret project, then add that your colleague hit the nail on the head when she changed the subject.
c1-23-01.prompt: Respond in two sentences using «meter la pata» and «dar en el clavo».
cues: Admit you put your foot in it by mentioning a secret project
Say your colleague hit the nail on the head when she changed the subject
c1-23-01.target: Metí la pata al mencionar un proyecto secreto durante la reunión. Por suerte, mi compañera dio en el clavo al cambiar de tema.
c1-23-01.english: I put my foot in it by mentioning a secret project during the meeting. Luckily, my colleague hit the nail on the head by changing the subject.
c1-23-01.canDo: I can use everyday figurative idioms such as *meter la pata*, *dar en el clavo* and *tomar el pelo* accurately.

c1-23-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Finding the Real Cause
c1-23-02.scenario: You are Meg. A classmate asks how your group solved the error in the presentation. Reply in two sentences: first say that after an unexpected setback you finally hit upon the mistake, then add that nobody had to shoulder the blame alone.
c1-23-02.prompt: Respond in two sentences using «dar con» and «cargar con».
cues: Say that after a setback you finally hit upon the mistake
Add that nobody had to shoulder the blame alone
c1-23-02.target: Después de un tropiezo inesperado, por fin dimos con el error en los datos. Además, nadie tuvo que cargar con la culpa solo.
c1-23-02.english: After an unexpected setback, we finally hit upon the error in the data. Besides, nobody had to shoulder the blame alone.
c1-23-02.canDo: I can use figurative prepositional verbs such as *dar con*, *caer en la cuenta* and *cargar con* accurately.

c1-23-03.title: Communicative Challenge: A Timely Suggestion
c1-23-03.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague offers to move the weekly review to Thursday morning and asks how you want to prepare the summary. Reply in two sentences: first say that the new timetable suits the team like a glove, then say you can prepare the summary however seems best to them.
c1-23-03.prompt: Respond in two sentences using «como anillo al dedo» and «como mejor te parezca».
cues: Say the new timetable suits the team like a glove
Offer to prepare the summary however seems best to them
c1-23-03.target: El nuevo horario nos viene como anillo al dedo para la revisión. Puedo preparar el resumen como mejor te parezca.
c1-23-03.english: The new timetable suits us like a glove for the review. I can prepare the summary however seems best to you.
c1-23-03.canDo: I can use proverbial and figurative manner frames such as *como anillo al dedo* and *como quien no quiere la cosa*.

c1-23-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Speaking Straight to Break the Ice
c1-23-04.scenario: You are Meg. A classmate asks how the reading group resolved the misunderstanding about the assignment. Reply in two sentences: first say, fronting «Sin rodeos», that the teacher explained the instructions straight, then add that her joke broke the ice and helped everyone pick up the thread.
c1-23-04.prompt: Respond in two sentences fronting «Sin rodeos» with inversion and using «romper el hielo».
cues: Front «Sin rodeos» with subject-verb inversion to say the teacher explained the instructions
Add that her joke broke the ice and helped everyone pick up the thread
c1-23-04.target: Sin rodeos explicó la profesora las instrucciones del trabajo. Luego contó una broma para romper el hielo y recuperamos el hilo.
c1-23-04.english: Without beating around the bush, the teacher explained the instructions for the assignment. Then she told a joke to break the ice and we picked up the thread.
c1-23-04.canDo: I can front figurative phrases such as *sin rodeos*, *a ciegas* and *ni una palabra* with subject-verb inversion.

c1-23-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Keeping Calm at the Reading Circle
c1-23-05.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks how the owner handled the awkward question at the reading circle. Reply in two sentences: first say the owner answered while dodging the trap and feigning calm, then add that nobody wanted to throw in the towel before the end.
c1-23-05.prompt: Respond in two sentences using figurative gerunds («esquivando», «fingiendo») and «tirar la toalla».
cues: Say the owner answered while dodging the trap and feigning calm
Add that nobody wanted to throw in the towel before the end
c1-23-05.target: La dueña respondió esquivando la trampa y fingiendo calma. Aun así, nadie quiso tirar la toalla antes del cierre.
c1-23-05.english: The owner answered dodging the trap and feigning calm. Even so, nobody wanted to throw in the towel before closing time.
c1-23-05.canDo: I can use figurative gerunds such as *esquivando*, *fingiendo* and *haciendo la vista gorda* to show attitude.

c1-23-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Untangling a Mix-Up
c1-23-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. A classmate asks how the reading circle turned out after the mix-up over the note. Reply in two sentences: first say that at first you were stunned and felt like you were working blindly, then add that your comment hit the nail on the head and untangled the misunderstanding.
c1-23-consolidation.prompt: Respond in two sentences using «quedarse de piedra», «a ciegas» and «dar en el clavo».
cues: Say you were stunned at first and felt like you were working blindly
Add that your comment hit the nail on the head and untangled the misunderstanding
c1-23-consolidation.target: Al principio me quedé de piedra y sentí que trabajábamos a ciegas. Por suerte, mi comentario dio en el clavo y desenredó el malentendido.
c1-23-consolidation.english: At first I was stunned and felt we were working blindly. Luckily, my comment hit the nail on the head and untangled the misunderstanding.
c1-23-consolidation.canDo: I can use everyday Spanish idioms and figurative expressions accurately in speech and writing.

c1-24-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Urging Both Sides to Submit a Counter-Proposal
c1-24-01.scenario: You are Carlos. At your office in Budapest, you are helping mediate a scheduling disagreement between two project teams. Open the meeting in two sentences: first propose that the two teams bring their positions closer today, then urge the counterpart to submit a counter-proposal so that everyone makes the schedule more flexible.
c1-24-01.prompt: Open the mediation session in two sentences using a formal verb of proposal and a verb urging action with the subjunctive.
cues: Propose that the two teams bring their positions closer today
Urge the counterpart to submit a counter-proposal so that everyone makes the schedule more flexible
c1-24-01.target: Propongo que los dos equipos acerquen posturas hoy. Además, insto a que la contraparte presente una contrapropuesta para que flexibilicemos el calendario.
c1-24-01.english: I propose that the two teams bring their positions closer today. Furthermore, I urge the counterpart to submit a counter-proposal so that we make the schedule more flexible.
c1-24-01.canDo: I can frame formal proposals and mediation requests with «proponer que», «sugerir que», «solicitar que» and «instar a que» + subjunctive.

c1-24-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Adding a Safeguard Clause to a Pre-Agreement
c1-24-02.scenario: You are Meg. In a university student committee in Budapest, you are explaining why your group drafted a preliminary agreement in good faith. In two sentences, state that you sought a middle ground in order to settle the dispute, and add that you included a written guarantee so that the assembly ratifies the settlement on Friday.
c1-24-02.prompt: Explain the safeguard in two sentences using a same-subject purpose phrase and a cross-party purpose clause with the subjunctive.
cues: State that you drafted the pre-agreement in good faith and sought a middle ground in order to settle the dispute
Add that you included a written guarantee so that the assembly ratifies the settlement on Friday
c1-24-02.target: Redactamos el preacuerdo de buena fe y buscamos un término medio con el fin de zanjar la disputa. Además, incluimos una garantía escrita a fin de que la asamblea ratifique el arreglo el viernes.
c1-24-02.english: We drafted the pre-agreement in good faith and sought a middle ground in order to settle the dispute. In addition, we included a written guarantee so that the assembly ratifies the settlement on Friday.
c1-24-02.canDo: I can establish procedural safeguards with «para que», «a fin de que» and «con el objeto de que» + present or imperfect subjunctive.

c1-24-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Summarising Previous Rounds in the Minutes
c1-24-03.scenario: You are Carlos. At your office in Budapest, you are reading aloud from the minutes of yesterday's negotiation session with a supplier. In two sentences, report that the spokesperson maintained that the process had been stalled over the disagreement, warned that an ultimatum would not unlock that deadlock, and announced that they would renegotiate after the moratorium.
c1-24-03.prompt: Report yesterday's session in two sentences using formal reporting verbs with backshifted past tenses.
cues: Report that in yesterday's session the spokesperson maintained that the process had been stalled over the disagreement
Add that he warned that an ultimatum would not unlock that deadlock and announced that they would renegotiate after the moratorium
c1-24-03.target: En la sesión de ayer, el portavoz sostuvo que el proceso había estado estancado por el desacuerdo. También advirtió que un ultimátum no desbloquearía aquel punto muerto y anunció que renegociarían tras la moratoria.
c1-24-03.english: In yesterday's session, the spokesperson maintained that the process had been stalled over the disagreement. He also warned that an ultimatum would not unlock that deadlock and announced that they would renegotiate after the moratorium.
c1-24-03.canDo: I can report prior bargaining positions and conditional warnings in mediation minutes with «sostener», «advertir», «aclarar» and «anunciar».

c1-24-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Assessing What Saved the Truce
c1-24-04.scenario: You are Meg. After a student association mediation in Budapest, you are explaining to a classmate how a breakdown was avoided. State in one sentence that had the mediator not interceded to smooth over rough edges and calm tempers, neither side would have compromised on the list of demands or signed the truce.
c1-24-04.prompt: Explain what prevented a breakdown using a formal negative past counterfactual without «si».
cues: Open with the counterfactual condition that the mediator interceded to smooth over rough edges and calm tempers
State that otherwise neither side would have compromised on the list of demands or signed the truce
c1-24-04.target: De no haber intercedido la mediadora para limar asperezas y apaciguar los ánimos, ninguna de las partes habría transigido en el pliego ni habría firmado la tregua.
c1-24-04.english: Had the mediator not interceded to smooth over rough edges and calm tempers, neither side would have compromised on the list of demands or signed the truce.
c1-24-04.canDo: I can evaluate what averted or prolonged a breakdown using «De haber / De no haber» + participle and «si»-less «Hubiera / Hubiese» + participle.

c1-24-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Delivering the Mediator's Closing Synthesis
c1-24-05.scenario: You are Carlos. At your office in Budapest, you are closing a successful mediation round between two departments. In two sentences, state that in synthesis the conciliatory tone made it possible to sign the formal settlement and reconcile the two teams, and highlight that independent arbitration will settle any future doubt through its official ruling.
c1-24-05.prompt: Deliver the closing summary in two sentences using formal synthesis and highlighting markers.
cues: Summarise that the conciliatory tone made it possible to sign the formal settlement and reconcile the two teams
Highlight that independent arbitration will settle any future doubt through its official ruling
c1-24-05.target: En síntesis, el tono conciliador permitió firmar la avenencia y reconciliar a los dos equipos. Cabe destacar que un arbitraje independiente dirimirá cualquier duda futura mediante su laudo.
c1-24-05.english: In synthesis, the conciliatory tone made it possible to sign the formal settlement and reconcile the two teams. It is worth highlighting that independent arbitration will settle any future doubt through its official ruling.
c1-24-05.canDo: I can synthesise reciprocal concessions and close a mediation session with «por una parte … por otra parte», «cabe destacar que», «en síntesis» and «en definitiva».

c1-24-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Full Mediation Report and Settlement Proposal
c1-24-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Writing the final mediation summary for your student housing committee in Budapest, report in two sentences: first say that had the two sides not acted in good faith to unlock the deadlock, the disagreement would have ended in a legal dispute; then add that in synthesis, you urge everyone to sign the pact today so that the assembly ratifies the formal settlement on Friday.
c1-24-consolidation.prompt: Write the two-sentence mediation summary combining a past counterfactual without «si», a synthesis marker, a verb urging action, and a formal purpose safeguard.
cues: State that had the two sides not acted in good faith to unlock the deadlock, the disagreement would have ended in a legal dispute
Add that in synthesis, you urge everyone to sign the pact today so that the assembly ratifies the formal settlement on Friday
c1-24-consolidation.target: De no haber actuado las dos partes de buena fe para desbloquear el punto muerto, el desacuerdo habría terminado en un litigio. En síntesis, insto a que todos firmen el pacto hoy a fin de que la asamblea ratifique la avenencia el viernes.
c1-24-consolidation.english: Had the two sides not acted in good faith to unlock the deadlock, the disagreement would have ended in a legal dispute. In synthesis, I urge everyone to sign the pact today so that the assembly ratifies the formal settlement on Friday.
c1-24-consolidation.canDo: I can integrate subjunctive directives, formal purpose safeguards, reported bargaining shifts, counterfactual conditions and synthesis markers in C1 mediation discourse.

c1-25-01.title: Explaining a Peninsular Pronoun Usage
c1-25-01.scenario: You are Meg. In your literature seminar, a classmate asks why a novel from Madrid says «Al profesor le vimos ayer, pero a la directora la dijimos la hora» and how you would write that in standard Spanish.
c1-25-01.prompt: Explain that the norm accepts singular male-person leísmo, that the second clause shows laísmo, and state the standard version with direct object and indirect object pronouns.
cues: Explain that the educated norm accepts singular male-person leísmo
Note that the second part is a case of laísmo and give the standard version of the whole sentence
c1-25-01.target: La norma culta acepta ese leísmo de persona masculina singular, pero la segunda parte es un caso de laísmo. En el español estándar decimos: «Al profesor lo vimos ayer, pero a la directora le dijimos la hora».
c1-25-01.english: The educated norm accepts that singular male-person leísmo, but the second part is a case of laísmo. In standard Spanish we say: 'We saw the professor yesterday, but we told the director the time'.
c1-25-01.canDo: I can recognize leísmo, laísmo, and loísmo in peninsular Spanish and identify their standard lo/la/le equivalents

c1-25-02.title: Interpreting Address Forms Across Regions
c1-25-02.scenario: You are Carlos. At the office, a colleague shows you two messages—one from a friend in Buenos Aires using Rioplatense voseo and one from a relative in Colombia using family ustedeo—and asks what they express.
c1-25-02.prompt: Explain how Rioplatense voseo and Colombian family ustedeo express closeness in their respective regions while maintaining their own verb and possessive agreement.
cues: State that in the River Plate region voseo expresses everyday closeness
State that in parts of Colombia ustedeo expresses family affection while keeping third-person agreement with usted and su
c1-25-02.target: En el Río de la Plata el voseo expresa cercanía cotidiana en la conversación. En algunas regiones de Colombia el ustedeo también transmite cariño familiar y mantiene la concordancia con «usted» y «su».
c1-25-02.english: In the River Plate region, voseo expresses everyday closeness in conversation. In some regions of Colombia, ustedeo also conveys family affection and maintains agreement with 'usted' and 'su'.
c1-25-02.canDo: I can interpret regional shifts between tuteo, Rioplatense voseo, deferential usted, and affectionate family ustedeo

c1-25-03.title: Defending Transatlantic Lexical Synonyms
c1-25-03.scenario: You are Meg. While reviewing a bilingual glossary for an international student guide, a classmate wonders whether Latin American words or peninsular words should be marked as errors.
c1-25-03.prompt: State that the words of both regions function as educated synonyms and that the dictionary records them without marking either one as an error.
cues: Explain that the words function as synonyms in the educated lexicon of each region
Add that the dictionary records these Latin Americanisms and peninsular terms without marking either one as an error
c1-25-03.target: Los dos vocablos funcionan como sinónimos en el léxico culto de cada región. El diccionario registra tanto los americanismos como las voces peninsulares sin considerar ninguno de los dos un error.
c1-25-03.english: The two words function as synonyms in the educated lexicon of each region. The dictionary records both Latin Americanisms and peninsular words without considering either one an error.
c1-25-03.canDo: I can recognize major transatlantic lexical pairs such as carro/coche, computadora/ordenador, and jugo/zumo as equal educated standards

c1-25-04.title: Describing Phonetic Variation in Spanish
c1-25-04.scenario: You are Carlos. After listening to a podcast featuring speakers from Mexico, Andalusia, and the Caribbean, a friend asks you how linguists describe the main pronunciation traits you heard.
c1-25-04.prompt: Describe seseo as the majority phonetic feature of the Hispanic world and mention the aspiration of syllable-final -s and regional intonation.
cues: State that seseo is the majority phonetic feature across Latin America and parts of Spain
Mention the aspiration of the syllable-final consonant and the characteristic intonation of each region
c1-25-04.target: El seseo es el rasgo fonético mayoritario en América Latina y en partes de España. Además, en muchas costas se nota la aspiración de la consonante final de sílaba junto con la entonación propia de cada región.
c1-25-04.english: Seseo is the majority phonetic feature in Latin America and in parts of Spain. Furthermore, on many coasts one notices the aspiration of the syllable-final consonant along with the characteristic intonation of each region.
c1-25-04.canDo: I can describe major phonetic features of Spanish using precise terms (el seseo, el ceceo, la aspiración, la entonación)

c1-25-05.title: Stating an International Editorial Policy
c1-25-05.scenario: You are Meg. You are drafting the style guideline for a university journal read across the entire Spanish-speaking world.
c1-25-05.prompt: Write a formal guideline using «todo aquel que» + subjunctive and impersonal «se» stating that contributors must use a shared formal register and that all educated varieties have equal prestige.
cues: State that contributors who write for the journal must keep a shared formal register, using the universal relative with the subjunctive and the future
Note impersonally that all educated variants have equal prestige in the Spanish-speaking community
c1-25-05.target: Todo aquel que redacte un ensayo para la revista deberá mantener un registro formal comprensible para toda la comunidad hispanohablante. Se reconoce hoy que todas las variantes cultas tienen el mismo prestigio.
c1-25-05.english: Anyone who drafts an essay for the journal must maintain a formal register understandable to the entire Spanish-speaking community. It is recognized today that all educated variants have the same prestige.
c1-25-05.canDo: I can use formal pan-Hispanic register (todo aquel que / quienes + subjunctive, impersonal se) to write for an international readership

c1-25-consolidation.title: Synthesizing Pronominal and Regional Variation
c1-25-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. A friend studying advanced Spanish asks you to summarize how the educated norm treats peninsular object-pronoun variation and regional varieties.
c1-25-consolidation.prompt: Summarize that the academic norm accepts only singular male-person leísmo while rejecting laísmo and loísmo, and that standard Spanish uses lo/la/le while recognizing the prestige of all educated varieties.
cues: State that the norm accepts only singular male-person leísmo and rejects laísmo and loísmo
Add that in standard Spanish we use «lo», «la», and «le» according to syntactic function while respecting the prestige of all educated variants
c1-25-consolidation.target: La norma de la academia acepta solo el leísmo de persona masculina singular, pero rechaza el laísmo y el loísmo. En el español estándar usamos «lo», «la» y «le» según la función y respetamos el prestigio de todas las variantes cultas.
c1-25-consolidation.english: The academy's norm accepts only singular male-person leísmo, but rejects laísmo and loísmo. In standard Spanish we use 'lo', 'la', and 'le' according to function and respect the prestige of all educated variants.
c1-25-consolidation.canDo: I can recognize peninsular leísmo, laísmo, and loísmo, distinguish the accepted male-person leísmo, and supply standard lo/la/le forms

c1-26-01.title: Evaluating Enrolment and Student Retention
c1-26-01.scenario: You are Meg. In a university student-council meeting, a representative claims that because undergraduate enrolment rose this year, the faculty no longer needs to keep funding its scholarships.
c1-26-01.prompt: Reply using «el hecho de que» + subjunctive and «no significa que» + subjunctive to argue that rising undergraduate enrolment does not mean the dropout problem is solved.
cues: Say that more young people enrolling in the undergraduate degree does not mean the dropout problem is solved
Add that the faculty needs to keep the grants going during the first semester
c1-26-01.target: El hecho de que más jóvenes se matriculen en la licenciatura no significa que hayamos resuelto la deserción. Por eso la facultad necesita mantener las becas durante el primer semestre.
c1-26-01.english: The fact that more young people enrol in the undergraduate degree does not mean that we have solved the dropout rate. That is why the faculty needs to maintain the grants during the first semester.
c1-26-01.canDo: I can frame presupposed findings and institutional debates as sentence themes using el hecho de que + subjunctive

c1-26-02.title: Explaining Doctoral Requirements
c1-26-02.scenario: You are Carlos. A younger cousin who wants to apply for a PhD asks you what obligations doctoral candidates and full professors have in a traditional university department.
c1-26-02.prompt: Use «haber de» + infinitive to state that every doctoral candidate is to attend tutorial sessions and defend their research, and that the chairholder is to guide their work on campus.
cues: Say that every doctoral candidate is to attend the tutorial sessions and defend an original thesis
Add that the full professor is to guide each candidate on campus
c1-26-02.target: En el programa de doctorado, todo doctorando ha de asistir a las sesiones de tutoría y defender una tesis original. Además, el catedrático ha de orientar a cada doctorando en el campus.
c1-26-02.english: In the doctoral programme, every doctoral candidate is to attend tutorial sessions and defend an original thesis. Furthermore, the full professor is to guide each doctoral candidate on campus.
c1-26-02.canDo: I can express formal academic duties and doctoral regulations using haber de + infinitive

c1-26-03.title: Reporting on Degree Accreditation
c1-26-03.scenario: You are Meg. You are writing a short update for the faculty newsletter about the new interdisciplinary curriculum and how theses are reviewed.
c1-26-03.prompt: Combine «estar» + participle, «se» passive, and the «ser» passive with «por» to state that the degree programme is already accredited, new courses are taught this semester, and every thesis was evaluated by an independent panel.
cues: Say that the new degree programme is already accredited and that new courses are taught this semester
Add that every thesis was evaluated by an independent panel
c1-26-03.target: La nueva titulación ya está acreditada y este semestre se imparten nuevos cursos del currículo. Además, cada tesis fue evaluada por un tribunal independiente.
c1-26-03.english: The new degree programme is already accredited and this semester new courses from the curriculum are taught. Furthermore, each thesis was evaluated by an independent panel.
c1-26-03.canDo: I can choose accurately among se passive, ser + participle, and estar + participle in academic governance and peer review

c1-26-04.title: Adding a Bibliographic Aside in a Seminar
c1-26-04.scenario: You are Meg. During your seminar presentation on university autonomy and the humanities, you want to slip in a brief parenthetical comment about the updated reading list before returning to your main point.
c1-26-04.prompt: Use «dicho sea de paso» between commas to mention that the new bibliography is in the library, then use «volviendo a lo que decíamos» to return to the importance of the humanities.
cues: Add, between commas, a brief aside saying that the new bibliography is already in the library
Return to the main point: the humanities protect university autonomy
c1-26-04.target: La nueva bibliografía del seminario, dicho sea de paso, ya está disponible en la biblioteca. Volviendo a lo que decíamos, el estudio de las humanidades protege la autonomía universitaria.
c1-26-04.english: The new seminar bibliography, incidentally, is already available in the library. Going back to what we were saying, the study of the humanities strengthens university autonomy.
c1-26-04.canDo: I can weave relevant academic asides and parenthetical notes into lectures using a propósito de, dicho sea de paso, and por cierto

c1-26-05.title: Opening an Academic Conclusion with an Absolute Participle
c1-26-05.scenario: You are Meg. You are writing the closing paragraph of an essay on higher-education reform for a university course.
c1-26-05.prompt: Open with an absolute participle clause with «una vez» that agrees with its noun, and use «si bien es cierto que» to balance technical training with an interdisciplinary approach.
cues: Say that, once the new degree programmes were approved, the rectorate opened the academic year
Concede that technical training matters, but say the university needs an interdisciplinary approach
c1-26-05.target: Una vez aprobadas las nuevas titulaciones, el rectorado inauguró el año lectivo. Si bien es cierto que la preparación técnica es necesaria, la universidad necesita mantener un enfoque interdisciplinario.
c1-26-05.english: Once the new degree programmes had been approved, the rectorate opened the academic year. While it is true that technical training is necessary, the university needs to maintain an interdisciplinary approach.
c1-26-05.canDo: I can open high-density academic clauses with absolute participles (Aprobado el currículo, Una vez defendidas las tesis) agreed in gender and number

c1-26-consolidation.title: Synthesizing University Policy and Academic Style
c1-26-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. At the end of a conference on higher education, you summarise the panel's conclusions on enrolment and curriculum approval.
c1-26-consolidation.prompt: Use «el hecho de que» + subjunctive, an absolute participle clause, and «haber de» + infinitive to synthesize the panel's conclusions.
cues: Say that a rise in enrolment does not mean that dropping out falls
Add a clause that opens with the curriculum approved, and state with a formal obligation that the faculty is to expand the tutorial sessions
c1-26-consolidation.target: El hecho de que aumente la matrícula no significa que baje la deserción en el primer trimestre. Una vez aprobado el currículo, la facultad ha de ampliar las sesiones de tutoría en el campus.
c1-26-consolidation.english: The fact that enrolment increases does not mean that dropping out decreases in the first term. Once the curriculum is approved, the faculty is to strengthen tutorial sessions on campus.
c1-26-consolidation.canDo: I can frame academic findings with el hecho de que + subjunctive and express formal obligations and historical milestones with haber de + infinitive

c1-27-01.title: Reconstructing an Archival Timeline
c1-27-01.scenario: You are Carlos. At your office, a colleague asks who recorded the old neighbourhood market before it disappeared.
c1-27-01.prompt: Explain in two sentences that before the demolition, the neighbours had already drawn up an inventory, and that when the museum opened, the old building had already been demolished.
cues: State that before the demolition, the neighbours had already compiled an inventory
Add that when the museum opened, the old building had already been demolished
c1-27-01.target: Antes de la demolición, los vecinos ya habían preparado un inventario. Cuando abrió el museo, el antiguo edificio ya había sido demolido.
c1-27-01.english: Before the demolition, the neighbours had already prepared an inventory. When the museum opened, the old building had already been demolished.
c1-27-01.canDo: I can layer earlier historical conditions before a past turning point using the pluperfect indicative.

c1-27-02.title: Reporting an Archival Discovery
c1-27-02.scenario: You are Meg. After spending the afternoon in the newspaper archive for a university history project, you tell Carlos what you found about an old workshop.
c1-27-02.prompt: Explain in two sentences that the families knew the oral story, that you found out the exact year in the newspaper archive, and that the council refused to open the register at first.
cues: Contrast what the families knew with the exact year you discovered in the newspaper archive
Mention that the council refused to open the register at first
c1-27-02.target: Las familias sabían la historia oral, pero hoy supe el año exacto en la hemeroteca. Al principio el concejo no quiso abrir el registro.
c1-27-02.english: The families knew the oral story, but today I found out the exact year in the newspaper archive. At first the council refused to open the register.
c1-27-02.canDo: I can contrast standing knowledge (*sabía*, *conocía*) with archival discoveries and first encounters (*supo*, *conoció*).

c1-27-03.title: Explaining a Commemorative Plaque
c1-27-03.scenario: You are Meg. At a history exhibition in Budapest, Carlos asks why a Spanish-language plaque says «que albergara» for something that really happened.
c1-27-03.prompt: Explain in two sentences what the inscription says about the hall that had housed the old archive, and clarify that the formal -ra form here means a past fact.
cues: Explain that the inscription mentions the hall that had housed the old archive
Clarify that this formal form expresses a past fact and means the same as the pluperfect indicative
c1-27-03.target: La inscripción recuerda el recinto que albergara el antiguo archivo. En estos textos formales, esa forma expresa un hecho pasado y significa lo mismo que había albergado.
c1-27-03.english: The inscription commemorates the hall that had housed the old archive. In these formal texts, that form expresses a past fact and means the same as had housed.
c1-27-03.canDo: I can interpret the formal indicative *-ra* form (*que albergara*, *como señalara*) in plaques, obituaries and historical essays.

c1-27-04.title: Weighing a Historical Counterfactual
c1-27-04.scenario: You are Carlos. During a conversation after visiting a local history exhibition, you comment on a manuscript that was lost before anyone catalogued it.
c1-27-04.prompt: State in two sentences that if the archive had catalogued the documents in time, the manuscript would not have been lost, and that the chroniclers regretted those testimonies had not been preserved for posterity.
cues: Form a past counterfactual condition about cataloguing the documents and saving the manuscript
Add that chroniclers regretted the testimonies had not been preserved for posterity
c1-27-04.target: Si el archivo hubiera catalogado los documentos a tiempo, el manuscrito no se habría perdido. Los cronistas lamentaron que no se hubieran conservado aquellos testimonios para la posteridad.
c1-27-04.english: If the archive had catalogued the documents in time, the manuscript would not have been lost. The chroniclers regretted that those testimonies had not been preserved for posterity.
c1-27-04.canDo: I can formulate counterfactual historical conditions using *si* + *hubiera/hubiese* + participle and the conditional perfect.

c1-27-05.title: Evoking a Witness's Perspective
c1-27-05.scenario: You are Meg. For a university seminar on historical chronicles, you are drafting a short passage describing elderly residents looking at the empty plot where their neighbourhood market once stood.
c1-27-05.prompt: Write two sentences in the third person: first describe the residents looking at the empty plot, then add a free indirect question asking who would recall those afternoons now.
cues: Describe the residents gazing at the empty plot in the past tense
Follow with an unquoted question in the conditional asking who would recall those afternoons now
c1-27-05.target: Los vecinos miraban el solar vacío en silencio. ¿Quién rememoraría ahora aquellas tardes de mercado?
c1-27-05.english: The residents gazed at the empty plot in silence. Who would recall those market afternoons now?
c1-27-05.canDo: I can distinguish a witness's unquoted perspective in free indirect discourse from the historian's analytical voice.

c1-27-consolidation.title: Synthesising Archives and Collective Memory
c1-27-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. At a neighbourhood meeting about a commemorative plaque for an old workshop, you summarise what the archives showed and why living memory still matters.
c1-27-consolidation.prompt: Write two sentences: first note that before the demolition the families had already saved documents and memories, and then add that if the council had preserved the hall, the bronze plaque would not be the only trace left.
cues: Mention that before the demolition the families had already saved documents and memories
Add a past counterfactual saying that if the council had preserved the hall, the bronze plaque would not be the only trace
c1-27-consolidation.target: Antes de la demolición, las familias ya habían guardado documentos y recuerdos del taller. Si el concejo hubiera conservado el recinto, la placa de bronce no sería hoy la única huella.
c1-27-consolidation.english: Before the demolition, the families had already saved documents and memories of the workshop. If the council had preserved the hall, the bronze plaque would not be the only trace today.
c1-27-consolidation.canDo: I can layer historical chronology accurately with active and passive pluperfect forms.

c1-28-01.title: Pacing a Migration Chronicle
c1-28-01.scenario: You are Meg. After a university seminar on migration chronicles, Carlos asks how a newly arrived family handled its first steps in the port city.
c1-28-01.prompt: Explain in two sentences that the crossing had barely finished when they went to the consulate, and that as soon as they receive the residence permit, they will be able to rent a home.
cues: Use a pluperfect narrative time connector to state that the crossing had barely finished when they went to the consulate
Use a prospective time connector with the subjunctive to add that as soon as they receive the residence permit, they will be able to rent a home
c1-28-01.target: Apenas había terminado la travesía cuando acudieron al consulado. En cuanto reciban el permiso de residencia, podrán alquilar una casa.
c1-28-01.english: The crossing had barely finished when they went to the consulate. As soon as they receive the residence permit, they will be able to rent a home.
c1-28-01.canDo: I can pair narrative time connectors with the pluperfect and prospective subjunctive in migration chronicles.

c1-28-02.title: Describing Gradual Cultural Change
c1-28-02.scenario: You are Carlos. At your office, a colleague asks how traditions survive when families settle in a new city.
c1-28-02.prompt: Explain in two sentences that accents are gradually blending in the neighbourhood, and that those family recipes have been kept for decades.
cues: Use a passive construction with a gradual gerund periphrasis to state that accents are blending in the neighbourhood
Use a continuous-tradition gerund periphrasis to add that those family recipes have been preserved for decades
c1-28-02.target: En el barrio se van mezclando los acentos. Esas recetas familiares se vienen manteniendo desde hace décadas.
c1-28-02.english: In the neighbourhood, accents are gradually blending. Those family recipes have been kept for decades.
c1-28-02.canDo: I can use passive se with ir and venir + gerund while keeping verb-subject agreement.

c1-28-03.title: Expressing Quiet Belonging
c1-28-03.scenario: You are Meg. Over coffee in Budapest, Carlos asks whether the narrator in your reading ever felt like an outsider, and whether her children lost the family's language.
c1-28-03.prompt: Reply in two sentences that thanks to the neighbourhood's hospitality, she never quite came to feel like an outsider, and that the children never went so far as to lose their mother tongue.
cues: Use a negated understatement periphrasis to say that thanks to the neighbourhood's hospitality, she never came to feel like an outsider
Add with the same periphrasis that the children never went so far as to lose their mother tongue
c1-28-03.target: Gracias a la hospitalidad del barrio, nunca llegó a sentirse forastera. Los hijos tampoco llegaron a perder su lengua materna.
c1-28-03.english: Thanks to the hospitality of the neighbourhood, she never came to feel like an outsider. The children never went so far as to lose their mother tongue either.
c1-28-03.canDo: I can use negated no llegar a + infinitive for cautious understatement in testimony.

c1-28-04.title: Stating Persistence Across Distance
c1-28-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Talking with a colleague about families who move abroad, you comment on how they stay connected to their homeland.
c1-28-04.prompt: State in two sentences that no matter how many years pass, they never forget their homeland, and that no matter how many procedures nationality requires, they do not plan to give up.
cues: Use a noun-phrase concessive with an agreeing quantifier to say that no matter how many years pass, they never forget their homeland
Use a second noun-phrase concessive to add that no matter how many procedures nationality requires, they do not plan to give up
c1-28-04.target: Por muchos años que pasen, nunca olvidan su patria. Por más trámites que exija la nacionalidad, no piensan rendirse.
c1-28-04.english: No matter how many years pass, they never forget their homeland. No matter how many procedures nationality requires, they do not plan to give up.
c1-28-04.canDo: I can build noun-phrase concessives with por mucho/a/os/as, por poco/a/os/as and por más + noun + que.

c1-28-05.title: Voicing Longing and Past Regret
c1-28-05.scenario: You are Meg. After reading a testimony about a family bakery by the pier, you paraphrase the narrator's present longing and past regret.
c1-28-05.prompt: Express in two exclamations: first, an unreal present wish to walk along the old pier today; second, a past regret about not having kept the letters from the journey.
cues: Form an unreal present wish exclamation about being able to walk along the old pier today
Form a standalone past-regret exclamation about having kept the letters from the journey
c1-28-05.target: ¡Quién pudiera caminar hoy por el antiguo muelle! ¡Si al menos hubiéramos guardado las cartas del viaje!
c1-28-05.english: If only I could walk today along the old pier! If only we had kept the letters from the journey!
c1-28-05.canDo: I can contrast unreal present wishes (¡quién pudiera!) with past regrets (¡quién hubiera!, si al menos hubiera).

c1-28-consolidation.title: Reflecting on Migration and Dual Identity
c1-28-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. After reading a chronicle about a port neighbourhood, a colleague asks you to sum up how migrant families build a sense of home.
c1-28-consolidation.prompt: Summarise in two sentences that over the years support networks gradually formed in the neighbourhood, and that no matter how many years pass, families never come to lose their mother tongue.
cues: Open with an uncounted time-span phrase and a passive gradual gerund periphrasis about support networks forming in the neighbourhood
Add a noun-phrase concessive paired with a negated understatement periphrasis about families never losing their mother tongue
c1-28-consolidation.target: Al cabo de los años, en el barrio se fueron formando redes de apoyo. Por muchos años que pasen, las familias nunca llegan a perder su lengua materna.
c1-28-consolidation.english: Over the years, support networks gradually formed in the neighbourhood. No matter how many years pass, families never come to lose their mother tongue.
c1-28-consolidation.canDo: I can pace migration narratives with narrative time connectors, gerund periphrases, and llegar a + infinitive.

c1-29-01.title: Reporting Institutional Violations
c1-29-01.scenario: You are Meg. After a university seminar on institutional reports, Carlos asks what the oversight report found about local procedures.
c1-29-01.prompt: Explain in two sentences that due process has been violated by administrative delays, and that all complaints must be examined by an impartial committee.
cues: Use a present perfect passive construction to state that due process has been violated by administrative delays
Use a modal passive construction with an explicit agent to add that all complaints must be examined by an impartial committee
c1-29-01.target: El debido proceso ha sido vulnerado por demoras administrativas. Todas las quejas deben ser examinadas por un comité imparcial.
c1-29-01.english: Due process has been violated by administrative delays. All complaints must be examined by an impartial committee.
c1-29-01.canDo: I can form compound and modal ser passives in human-rights reports while keeping participle agreement.

c1-29-02.title: Stating Protective Mandates
c1-29-02.scenario: You are Carlos. At your office, a colleague asks why the ombudsman's office published a plain-language guide and opened new local offices.
c1-29-02.prompt: Explain in two sentences that the office opened new local offices in order to facilitate access to justice, and that it published a guide so that any citizen could request legal protection.
cues: Use a formal same-subject purpose connector with an infinitive to state why the office opened new desks
Use a formal different-subject purpose connector with the subjunctive to explain why it published a guide
c1-29-02.target: La defensoría abrió nuevas oficinas a fin de facilitar el acceso a la justicia. Publicó una guía con el objeto de que cualquier ciudadano pudiera solicitar amparo.
c1-29-02.english: The ombudsman's office opened new offices in order to facilitate access to justice. It published a guide so that any citizen could request legal protection.
c1-29-02.canDo: I can use formal purpose connectors with que + subjunctive (a fin de que, con el objeto de que, con el fin de que) when subjects differ.

c1-29-03.title: Stating Universal Safeguards
c1-29-03.scenario: You are Meg. Discussing legal safeguards with Carlos over coffee in Budapest, he asks whether an office can act without a formal complaint or after a minor deadline passes.
c1-29-03.prompt: Reply in two sentences that even if no formal complaint existed, the ombudsman's office could review an arbitrary decision, and that even if a deadline has expired, legal protection remains in force.
cues: Use a formal concessive with the imperfect subjunctive for the hypothetical safeguard without a formal complaint
Use the same formal concessive with the present perfect subjunctive for a deadline that has expired
c1-29-03.target: Aun cuando no existiera una denuncia formal, la defensoría podría revisar una decisión arbitraria. Aun cuando un plazo haya vencido, la tutela sigue vigente.
c1-29-03.english: Even if no formal complaint existed, the ombudsman's office could review an arbitrary decision. Even if a deadline has expired, legal protection remains in force.
c1-29-03.canDo: I can pair aun cuando with the imperfect and present perfect subjunctive for universal legal safeguards.

c1-29-04.title: Evaluating Compliance and Appeals
c1-29-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Summarising an annual oversight report for a colleague, you explain its verdict on compliance and pending appeals.
c1-29-04.prompt: State in two sentences that the commission regrets that the presumption of innocence has not been respected, and that the file will remain open until the appeal has been resolved.
cues: Use a passive present perfect subjunctive to state the commission's regret about the presumption of innocence
Use an anterior-to-future time clause with the present perfect subjunctive to state when the file will close
c1-29-04.target: La comisión lamenta que no se haya respetado la presunción de inocencia. El expediente seguirá abierto hasta que se haya resuelto la apelación.
c1-29-04.english: The commission regrets that the presumption of innocence has not been respected. The file will remain open until the appeal has been resolved.
c1-29-04.canDo: I can use passive present perfect subjunctive (haya sido + participle, se haya + participle) in oversight evaluations.

c1-29-05.title: Reporting a Commission Inquiry
c1-29-05.scenario: You are Meg. After reading the oversight report for class, you tell Carlos what the expert witness and the committee investigated.
c1-29-05.prompt: Explain in two sentences that the expert witness examined to what extent local offices had complied with each recommendation, and that the committee inquired into who held jurisdiction.
cues: Use a formal investigative verb with a prepositional indirect question about to what extent local offices had complied
Use a second investigative verb with a prepositional indirect question about who held jurisdiction
c1-29-05.target: El perito examinó en qué medida las oficinas locales habían cumplido cada recomendación. El comité indagó a quién correspondía la jurisdicción.
c1-29-05.english: The expert witness examined to what extent the local offices had complied with each recommendation. The committee inquired into who held jurisdiction.
c1-29-05.canDo: I can report commission inquiries with formal verbs (indagar si, examinar cómo, determinar quién, verificar por qué).

c1-29-consolidation.title: Summarising an Oversight Report
c1-29-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. At your office, a colleague asks for a brief summary of how an ombudsman's office monitors due process and remedies.
c1-29-consolidation.prompt: Summarise in two sentences that the safeguards have been violated by the local office, and that the office publishes guides so that citizens can request legal protection.
cues: Use a compound ser passive with an explicit agent to say that the safeguards have been violated by the local office
Use a formal purpose connector with que + subjunctive to explain why the office publishes guides
c1-29-consolidation.target: Las salvaguardias han sido vulneradas por la oficina local. La defensoría publica guías a fin de que los ciudadanos puedan solicitar amparo.
c1-29-consolidation.english: The safeguards have been violated by the local office. The ombudsman's office publishes guides so that citizens can request legal protection.
c1-29-consolidation.canDo: I can report obligations, violations, and mandates using compound ser passives and formal purpose connectors.

c1-30-01.title: Opening a Civic Address
c1-30-01.scenario: You are Meg. Preparing a short presentation for a university seminar on civic rhetoric, you practise opening an assembly speech with Carlos.
c1-30-01.prompt: State in two sentences using formal -ra conditional alternatives that we would like to highlight the value of deliberation for the common good, and that every motion ought to be debated with a sufficient quorum.
cues: Open with a 1st-person plural formal -ra verb to highlight deliberation for the common good
Use a 3rd-person singular formal -ra modal to add that every motion ought to be debated with a sufficient quorum
c1-30-01.target: Quisiéramos destacar el valor de la deliberación para el bien común. Toda moción debiera debatirse con quórum suficiente.
c1-30-01.english: We would like to highlight the value of deliberation for the common good. Every motion ought to be debated with a sufficient quorum.
c1-30-01.canDo: I can use formal -ra forms (quisiéramos, debiera, pudiera) and compound hubiera + participle in civic speeches.

c1-30-02.title: Pivoting in a Public Debate
c1-30-02.scenario: You are Carlos. At your office, a colleague asks how a municipal coalition can work when political polarisation is high.
c1-30-02.prompt: Reply in two sentences: first, concede that the debate was intense yet social dialogue remained open; second, state that dissent is healthy, adding the caveat that it must not block basic decisions.
cues: Use a formal concessive pivot after a semicolon to say that social dialogue remained open despite the intense debate
Use a formal caveat pivot to add that healthy dissent must not block basic decisions
c1-30-02.target: El debate fue intenso; con todo, el diálogo social siguió abierto. El disenso es saludable; ahora bien, no debe bloquear las decisiones básicas.
c1-30-02.english: The debate was intense; even so, social dialogue remained open. Dissent is healthy; that said, it must not block basic decisions.
c1-30-02.canDo: I can place no obstante parenthetically mid-clause and use con todo and ahora bien as parliamentary pivots.

c1-30-03.title: Explaining a Legislative Transition
c1-30-03.scenario: You are Meg. After reading a civic speech for class, Carlos asks how a bill moves forward and how the speaker introduces the next agenda item.
c1-30-03.prompt: Explain in two sentences that after committee review, the bill moves on to be debated in the full assembly, and invite the listeners to move on to examine the priorities of the new legislative term.
cues: Use a transition periphrasis with a passive infinitive to say that the bill moves on to be debated in the full assembly
Use a 1st-person plural agenda-shift command to move on to examine the priorities of the new legislative term
c1-30-03.target: Tras la revisión en comisión, el proyecto de ley pasa a ser debatido en el pleno. Pasemos a examinar las prioridades de la nueva legislatura.
c1-30-03.english: After committee review, the bill moves on to be debated in the full assembly. Let us move on to examine the priorities of the new legislative term.
c1-30-03.canDo: I can use pasar a + passive infinitive and institutional phrases (pasar a formar parte de, pasar a depender de).

c1-30-04.title: Voicing Democratic Inclusivity
c1-30-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Talking with a colleague about local elections, you sum up what democratic representation requires after the vote count.
c1-30-04.prompt: State in two sentences that whoever wins, every local councillor represents the whole electorate, and that whatever the differences may be, everyone must respect the vote count.
cues: Use an open-verb reduplicated subjunctive to say that whoever wins, every local councillor represents the whole electorate
Use a plural agreeing reduplicated subjunctive with a noun to add that whatever the differences may be, everyone must respect the vote count
c1-30-04.target: Gane quien gane, cada concejal representa a todo el electorado. Sean cuales sean las diferencias, todos deben respetar el escrutinio.
c1-30-04.english: Whoever wins, every local councillor represents the whole electorate. Whatever the differences may be, everyone must respect the vote count.
c1-30-04.canDo: I can use agreeing sea cual sea / sean cuales sean + noun and open civic verbs in reduplicated subjunctives.

c1-30-05.title: Closing a Civic Speech
c1-30-05.scenario: You are Meg. Wrapping up a practice civic address with Carlos in Budapest, you state your first priority and close with a synthesis.
c1-30-05.prompt: State in two sentences: first, open with a formal first-point marker to call for wider citizen participation; second, close with a formal synthesis marker stating that democratic coexistence depends on civic respect.
cues: Open with a formal first-point marker to call for wider citizen participation
Close with a formal synthesis marker stating that democratic coexistence depends on civic respect
c1-30-05.target: En primer término, debemos ampliar la participación ciudadana. En definitiva, la convivencia democrática depende del respeto cívico.
c1-30-05.english: First of all, we must widen citizen participation. In short, democratic coexistence depends on civic respect.
c1-30-05.canDo: I can order civic speech arguments with en primer término, en segundo lugar, and por último.

c1-30-consolidation.title: Summarising Democratic Institutions
c1-30-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. At your office, a colleague asks you to summarise the main message of the municipal assembly's opening speech.
c1-30-consolidation.prompt: Summarise in two sentences that the coalition, nevertheless, must listen to the opposition, and that whatever the result of the vote count may be, democratic coexistence requires citizen participation.
cues: Use a parenthetical contrast connector after the subject to say that the coalition must listen to the opposition
Use a singular reduplicated subjunctive about the vote count to add that democratic coexistence requires citizen participation
c1-30-consolidation.target: La coalición, no obstante, debe escuchar a la oposición. Sea cual sea el resultado del escrutinio, la convivencia democrática exige participación ciudadana.
c1-30-consolidation.english: The coalition, nevertheless, must listen to the opposition. Whatever the result of the vote count may be, democratic coexistence requires citizen participation.
c1-30-consolidation.canDo: I can use formal -ra conditional forms, parliamentary contrast pivots, and pasar a transitions in civic speeches.

c1-31-01.title: Evaluating an Exhibition Room
