c1-31-01.scenario: You are Meg. After visiting a contemporary art show together, you share your first impressions with Carlos over coffee.
c1-31-01.prompt: Give a two-sentence judgement: say that it is impossible to overlook the light-and-shadow contrast of the first room, and add that some bold pieces are difficult for the viewer to decipher.
cues: Open with an impersonal judgement verb + adjective + infinitive (no preposition) about overlooking the light-and-shadow contrast
Use the same verb with a concrete plural subject + adjective + de + infinitive to say that some bold pieces are hard to make sense of
c1-31-01.target: Resulta imposible pasar por alto el claroscuro de la primera sala. Algunas piezas audaces resultan difíciles de descifrar para el espectador.
c1-31-01.english: It is impossible to overlook the chiaroscuro of the first room. Some bold pieces are difficult for the viewer to decipher.
c1-31-01.canDo: I can use resultar + adjective + de + infinitive and impersonal resultar + adjective + infinitive without adding an extra preposition.

c1-31-02.title: Explaining the Curatorial Layout
c1-31-02.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague at your office asks how the new municipal exhibition is organised and whether the older paintings are in good condition.
c1-31-02.prompt: Answer in two sentences: describe how the exhibition is structured into three rooms with careful lighting, and add that the central canvas was restored by the museum workshop last year.
cues: Use the state passive (estar + participle) to describe how the exhibition is structured into three rooms
Use the action passive (preterite ser + participle with por) to report that the central canvas was restored by the museum workshop
c1-31-02.target: La exposición está articulada en tres salas con una iluminación muy cuidada. El lienzo central fue restaurado por el taller del museo el año pasado.
c1-31-02.english: The exhibition is structured into three rooms with very careful lighting. The central canvas was restored by the museum workshop last year.
c1-31-02.canDo: I can describe gallery layout, lighting, and visual composition with estar + past participle.

c1-31-03.title: Writing Measured Praise
c1-31-03.scenario: You are Meg. Drafting a short review for a university cultural journal, you read two sentences aloud to Carlos to check the tone.
c1-31-03.prompt: Write two sentences: call it the most restrained retrospective that the museum has presented, and note that the colour palette is extraordinarily rich even though the final room is exceedingly uneven.
cues: Use a relative superlative followed by que + present perfect subjunctive about the museum hosting the retrospective
Combine the spelling-change absolute superlative of 'rich' for the colour palette with a measured formal adverb before 'uneven'
c1-31-03.target: Es la retrospectiva más sobria que haya presentado el museo. La paleta cromática es riquísima, aunque la sala final es sumamente desigual.
c1-31-03.english: It is the most restrained retrospective that the museum has presented. The colour palette is extraordinarily rich, although the final room is exceedingly uneven.
c1-31-03.canDo: I can pair relative superlatives with que + subjunctive to make sweeping evaluative judgements in a review.

c1-31-04.title: Commenting on Technique and Light
c1-31-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Walking through a sculpture courtyard with Meg, you comment on a catalogue note and how the light affects a bronze relief.
c1-31-04.prompt: Say in two sentences that, just as the catalogue points out, the print belongs to the avant-garde, and that the relief changes depending on how the natural light varies.
cues: Cite the catalogue with a faithful manner connector + indicative about the print and the avant-garde
Explain with según + present subjunctive how the relief changes with natural light
c1-31-04.target: Tal como señala el catálogo, el grabado pertenece a la vanguardia. Además, el relieve cambia según varíe la luz natural.
c1-31-04.english: Just as the catalogue points out, the print belongs to the avant-garde. Moreover, the relief changes depending on how the natural light varies.
c1-31-04.canDo: I can cite curatorial notes and observable details with tal como + indicative.

c1-31-05.title: Summarising the Gallery Experience
c1-31-05.scenario: You are Meg. After reading an exhibition review, you tell Carlos how the gallery welcomes visitors and recognises the ceramic artisans.
c1-31-05.prompt: Explain in two sentences using impersonal se that visitors are invited to contemplate the charcoal portraits without hurry, and that the local ceramic artisans are honoured in the final gallery.
cues: Use invariable singular impersonal se before a + plural visitors about contemplating the charcoal portraits
Use invariable singular impersonal se before a + plural artisans about honouring them in the final gallery
c1-31-05.target: En la entrada se invita a los visitantes a contemplar los retratos al carboncillo sin prisa. En la galería final se homenajea a las artesanas de la cerámica.
c1-31-05.english: At the entrance visitors are invited to contemplate the charcoal portraits without hurry. In the final gallery the ceramic artisans are honoured.
c1-31-05.canDo: I can use invariable singular impersonal se before personal a + plural human objects (se invita a los visitantes, se homenajea a las artesanas).

c1-31-consolidation.title: Reviewing a Retrospective
c1-31-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague at your office asks whether the municipal museum's retrospective is worth visiting this weekend.
c1-31-consolidation.prompt: Recommend the show in two sentences: say that it is the boldest exhibition that the museum has presented and is structured into three rooms, and add that viewers are invited to contemplate the sculpture depending on how the light changes.
cues: Combine a relative superlative + subjunctive with a state passive (estar + participle) describing the three-room layout
Use invariable singular impersonal se before a + plural viewers together with según + subjunctive about the light
c1-31-consolidation.target: Es la exposición más audaz que haya presentado el museo y está articulada en tres salas. Se invita a los espectadores a contemplar la escultura según cambie la luz.
c1-31-consolidation.english: It is the boldest exhibition that the museum has presented and is structured into three rooms. Viewers are invited to contemplate the sculpture depending on how the light changes.
c1-31-consolidation.canDo: I can combine resultar evaluations, estar + participle descriptions, and critical superlatives in art criticism.

c1-32-01.title: Shifting into Free Indirect Discourse
c1-32-01.scenario: You are Meg. Preparing a short presentation for your literature seminar, you test a rewrite of a character's thought with Carlos.
c1-32-01.prompt: Write three sentences in past-tense narrative prose: state that the protagonist closed the letter, then give the thought 'Why does no one believe him now? Tomorrow he will explain everything' as free indirect discourse, with no reporting verb and no quotation marks.
cues: Open with a brief past-tense action sentence about the protagonist closing the letter
Follow with the character's question in the imperfect and his promise in the conditional, keeping the character's own time words
c1-32-01.target: El protagonista cerró la carta. ¿Por qué nadie le creía ahora? Mañana lo explicaría todo.
c1-32-01.english: The protagonist closed the letter. Why did no one believe him now? Tomorrow he would explain everything.
c1-32-01.canDo: I can convert direct or reported thought into free indirect discourse using imperfect, pluperfect, and conditional verbs with character-anchored deictics.

c1-32-02.title: Analysing Narrative Suspense
c1-32-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Talking with Meg after reading a short story, you explain how the author builds tension before the climax.
c1-32-02.prompt: Say in two sentences that in the third chapter the protagonist nearly revealed the secret but preferred to conceal it, and that just when the plot is about to reach the climax, a new voice bursts in.
cues: Use preterite estar a punto de + infinitive to report the averted turning point in the third chapter
Use critical-present estar a punto de + infinitive with the verb for 'burst in' to describe the moment before the climax
c1-32-02.target: En el tercer capítulo, el protagonista estuvo a punto de revelar el secreto, pero prefirió ocultarlo. Justo cuando la trama está a punto de alcanzar el clímax, irrumpe una voz nueva.
c1-32-02.english: In the third chapter, the protagonist nearly revealed the secret, but preferred to conceal it. Just when the plot is about to reach the climax, a new voice bursts in.
c1-32-02.canDo: I can use preterite estuvo a punto de + infinitive to summarise a turning point narrowly averted in a plot.

c1-32-03.title: Delivering Measured Literary Praise
c1-32-03.scenario: You are Meg. Drafting a short essay on the short story genre, you try out two understated critical sentences with Carlos.
c1-32-03.prompt: State in two sentences using litotes that ellipsis is nonetheless an effective literary device, and that the conciseness with which the story condenses the conflict never fails to surprise.
cues: Use no dejar de ser to affirm that ellipsis is nonetheless an effective literary device
Use no dejar de + verb of surprise to praise the conciseness that condenses the conflict
c1-32-03.target: La elipsis no deja de ser un recurso literario eficaz. Además, no deja de sorprender la concisión con que el relato condensa el conflicto.
c1-32-03.english: Ellipsis is nonetheless an effective literary device. Moreover, the conciseness with which the story condenses the conflict never fails to surprise.
c1-32-03.canDo: I can use no dejar de ser + adjective/noun to deliver measured, understated literary judgements.

c1-32-04.title: Tracing a Recurring Symbol
c1-32-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Discussing a short story with Meg, you point out why the mirror image matters on a second reading.
c1-32-04.prompt: Explain in two sentences that the mirror symbol resonates again in the closing, and that rereading invites one to revisit the opening clues.
cues: Use volver a + infinitive to say that the mirror symbol resonates again in the closing
Use volver sobre + noun to say that rereading invites one to revisit the opening clues
c1-32-04.target: El símbolo del espejo vuelve a resonar en el cierre. Por eso la relectura invita a volver sobre las pistas iniciales.
c1-32-04.english: The mirror symbol resonates again in the closing. That is why rereading invites one to revisit the opening clues.
c1-32-04.canDo: I can use volver a + infinitive (including passive se vuelve a leer) to trace motif recurrence and rereading.

c1-32-05.title: Explaining an Understated Ending
c1-32-05.scenario: You are Meg. After finishing a literary essay for class, you summarise its conclusion about fables and ambiguity for Carlos.
c1-32-05.prompt: Summarise in two sentences that upon finishing the epilogue one notices how the author paced the clues, and that ambiguity ends up making the plausibility of the fable evident.
cues: Use al terminar de + infinitive about reading the epilogue and noticing how the author paced the clues
Use terminar por + infinitive with an abstract subject to say that ambiguity ends up showing the plausibility of the fable
c1-32-05.target: Al terminar de leer el epílogo se nota cómo el autor supo dosificar las pistas. La ambigüedad termina por evidenciar la verosimilitud de la fábula.
c1-32-05.english: Upon finishing reading the epilogue one notices how the author knew how to pace the clues. Ambiguity ends up making the plausibility of the fable evident.
c1-32-05.canDo: I can use terminar por / acabar por + infinitive with abstract literary subjects to describe thematic convergence.

c1-32-consolidation.title: Commenting on a Short Story
c1-32-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague at your office asks why you enjoyed the collection of short stories you mentioned at lunch.
c1-32-consolidation.prompt: Explain in two sentences that the concise prose is nonetheless plausible and the mirror symbol resonates again at the end, and add that silence ends up revealing more than any epilogue.
cues: Combine no dejar de ser (about plausibility) with volver a + infinitive (about the mirror symbol resonating again)
Use terminar por + infinitive with an abstract subject to say that silence ends up revealing more than an epilogue
c1-32-consolidation.target: La prosa no deja de ser verosímil y el símbolo del espejo vuelve a resonar al final. Además, el silencio termina por revelar más que un epílogo.
c1-32-consolidation.english: The prose is nonetheless plausible and the mirror symbol resonates again at the end. Moreover, silence ends up revealing more than an epilogue.
c1-32-consolidation.canDo: I can produce and analyse free indirect discourse and averted turning points (estuvo a punto de) in narrative prose.

c1-33-01.title: Distinguishing Ethical Categories
c1-33-01.scenario: You are Meg. Preparing notes for a philosophy seminar, you test a two-sentence summary of an ethical debate with Carlos.
c1-33-01.prompt: State in two sentences using neuter lo that philosophy distinguishes what is rational from what is subjective, and that what is paradoxical about the dilemma is that not everything permissible coincides with what is moral.
cues: Use neuter lo + adjectives to contrast what is rational with what is subjective
Use neuter lo + adjective + de + noun for the paradox, with the permissible and the moral as the two categories that do not coincide
c1-33-01.target: La filosofía distingue lo racional de lo subjetivo. Lo paradójico del dilema es que no todo lo lícito coincide con lo moral.
c1-33-01.english: Philosophy distinguishes what is rational from what is subjective. What is paradoxical about the dilemma is that not everything permissible coincides with what is moral.
c1-33-01.canDo: I can use neuter lo + masculine singular adjective and lo + past participle to name abstract ethical categories (lo justo, lo lícito, lo debido).

c1-33-02.title: Separating Duty from Motive
c1-33-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Talking with a colleague at your office about a difficult workplace decision, you separate what someone ought to have done from what their motive probably was.
c1-33-02.prompt: Say in two sentences that one must act with honesty and dignity, and add that since the manager returned the gift in secret, he must have acted out of integrity rather than egoism.
cues: Use impersonal se debe + infinitive (without de) to state the duty to act with honesty and dignity
Use preterite deber de + infinitive to draw an inference about acting out of integrity rather than egoism
c1-33-02.target: Se debe obrar con honestidad y dignidad. Como devolvió el regalo en secreto, debió de obrar por integridad y no por egoísmo.
c1-33-02.english: One must act with honesty and dignity. Since he returned the gift in secret, he must have acted out of integrity and not out of egoism.
c1-33-02.canDo: I can contrast past moral duty (debió obrar) with past epistemic inference (debió de obrar / debe de haber actuado).

c1-33-03.title: Testing a Moral Principle
c1-33-03.scenario: You are Meg. Discussing an ethics reading with Carlos, you explain why breaking promises undermines social trust.
c1-33-03.prompt: Explain in two sentences that if a rule harms innocent third parties it loses legitimacy, and that if trust did not exist, no social pact would have survived.
cues: Use a universal gnomic si-clause (present + present) about a rule harming third parties and losing legitimacy
Use a mixed conditional (si + imperfect subjunctive + habría + participle) about trust and social pacts surviving
c1-33-03.target: Si una regla perjudica a terceros, pierde legitimidad. Además, si no existiera la confianza, ningún pacto habría durado.
c1-33-03.english: If a rule harms third parties, it loses legitimacy. Moreover, if trust did not exist, no pact would have survived.
c1-33-03.canDo: I can build mixed conditionals (si + imperfect subjunctive + habría + participle) to link timeless conditions to past outcomes.

c1-33-04.title: Judging Avoidable Harm
c1-33-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Reviewing a public controversy with Meg, you comment on what the decision-makers ought to have done differently.
c1-33-04.prompt: State in two sentences that the committee should have foreseen such an avoidable injustice, and that it could have chosen a less harmful option and had no reason to abstain.
cues: Use debería haber + participle to express the unfulfilled duty to foresee an avoidable injustice
Combine podría haber + participle (a less harmful option) with no tenía por qué + infinitive (abstaining)
c1-33-04.target: El comité debería haber previsto una injusticia tan evitable. Podría haber elegido una salida menos dañina y no tenía por qué abstenerse.
c1-33-04.english: The committee should have foreseen such an avoidable injustice. It could have chosen a less harmful way out and had no reason to abstain.
c1-33-04.canDo: I can distinguish unfulfilled moral duty (debería haber + participle) from unused ethical alternatives (podría haber + participle).

c1-33-05.title: Closing a Philosophical Argument
c1-33-05.scenario: You are Meg. Wrapping up a seminar debate on duty and utility, you summarise your logical conclusion for Carlos.
c1-33-05.prompt: Conclude in two sentences that the postulate contains a contradiction and hence loses coherence, and that we must set criteria so that no one ends up harmed.
cues: Use de ahí que + present subjunctive to link the contradiction in the postulate to a lack of coherence
Use de modo que + present subjunctive to express the normative aim that no one ends up harmed
c1-33-05.target: El postulado encierra una contradicción; de ahí que pierda coherencia. Debemos fijar criterios de modo que nadie salga perjudicado.
c1-33-05.english: The postulate contains a contradiction; hence it loses coherence. We must set criteria so that no one ends up harmed.
c1-33-05.canDo: I can use deductive luego and de ahí que + subjunctive to link ethical premises to logical conclusions.

c1-33-consolidation.title: Synthesising an Ethical Debate
c1-33-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague at your office asks you to sum up the main takeaway from the philosophy essay you read.
c1-33-consolidation.prompt: Summarise in two sentences that one must distinguish what is licit from what is just, and that if empathy did not exist few agreements would have lasted, hence logic needs empathy.
cues: Combine impersonal se debe with neuter lo to contrast what is licit and what is just
Combine a mixed conditional (si + imperfect subjunctive + habría + participle) with de ahí que + subjunctive about logic and empathy
c1-33-consolidation.target: Se debe distinguir lo lícito de lo justo. Si no existiera la empatía, pocos acuerdos habrían durado; de ahí que la lógica necesite empatía.
c1-33-consolidation.english: One must distinguish what is licit from what is just. If empathy did not exist, few agreements would have lasted; hence logic needs empathy.
c1-33-consolidation.canDo: I can combine neuter lo abstraction and deber vs deber de to separate moral duties from inferences.

c1-34-01.title: Explaining Trade Interdependence
c1-34-01.scenario: You are Carlos. At your office in Budapest, a colleague asks why trade negotiations between large regional blocs take so long.
c1-34-01.prompt: Explain in two sentences using proportional correlatives that the more partners participate in the bloc, the more complex the negotiation becomes, and that the greater the trade integration, the smaller each state's unilateral margin.
cues: Link the number of participating partners to how complex the negotiation becomes
Note that greater trade integration reduces unilateral room for manoeuvre
c1-34-01.target: Cuantos más socios participan en el bloque, más compleja resulta la negociación. Además, cuanta mayor integración comercial existe, menor es el margen unilateral.
c1-34-01.english: The more partners participate in the bloc, the more complex the negotiation becomes. Moreover, the greater the trade integration there is, the smaller the unilateral margin.
c1-34-01.canDo: I can express proportional relationships before nouns with agreeing cuanto, cuanta, cuantos, cuantas.

c1-34-02.title: Explaining Trade Costs & Treaties
c1-34-02.scenario: You are Carlos. A colleague in your Budapest office asks why a supplier switched to overland routes and avoided extra port charges.
c1-34-02.prompt: Explain in two sentences that they changed route because maritime freight rose, and that under the trade treaty those shipments did not pay extra charges at customs.
cues: Explain with a full causal clause that maritime freight charges rose
Add that under the trade treaty, those shipments stayed exempt at customs
c1-34-02.target: Cambiaron de ruta debido a que subió el flete marítimo. En virtud del tratado comercial, esos envíos no pagaron recargo en la aduana.
c1-34-02.english: They changed route because maritime freight rose. Under the trade treaty, those shipments did not pay a surcharge at customs.
c1-34-02.canDo: I can contrast prepositional debido a + noun with clausal debido a que + indicative.

c1-34-03.title: Reporting Multilateral Agreements
c1-34-03.scenario: You are Meg. In a seminar at your university in Budapest, a classmate asks what concrete steps regional blocs have taken to strengthen trade corridors.
c1-34-03.prompt: Report in two sentences using passive se that several bilateral cooperation agreements have been signed in recent years, and that multilateral corridors can be expanded if stability continues.
cues: Report without naming an agent that several bilateral cooperation agreements have been signed
Add that multilateral corridors can be expanded if stability continues
c1-34-03.target: En los últimos años se han suscrito varios convenios de cooperación bilateral. Además, se pueden ampliar los corredores multilaterales si se mantiene la estabilidad.
c1-34-03.english: In recent years several bilateral cooperation agreements have been signed. Moreover, multilateral corridors can be expanded if stability is maintained.
c1-34-03.canDo: I can agree passive se verbs with plural subjects in compound tenses and modal periphrases.

c1-34-04.title: Attributing Diplomatic Assessments
c1-34-04.scenario: You are Meg. During a university seminar in Budapest, you summarise an international report on border tensions without presenting its claims as your own.
c1-34-04.prompt: Summarise in two sentences what observers warn about the border dispute affecting regional trade, and what the report maintains about diplomacy needing greater stability.
cues: Cite what observers warn about the border dispute using a verbal source marker
Add neutrally that the report maintains that diplomacy needs greater stability
c1-34-04.target: Según advierten los observadores, la disputa fronteriza afecta al comercio regional. Además, el informe sostiene que la diplomacia necesita mayor estabilidad.
c1-34-04.english: As observers warn, the border dispute affects regional trade. Moreover, the report maintains that diplomacy needs greater stability.
c1-34-04.canDo: I can use verbal según + indicative (without que) and tal como + verb to cite sources.

c1-34-05.title: Inferring & Projecting Supply Shifts
c1-34-05.scenario: You are Carlos. At work in Budapest, a colleague wonders why regional import prices rose this quarter and what the next decade will bring.
c1-34-05.prompt: State in two sentences using the future perfect that the port delay has probably complicated regional supply, and that by the end of the decade supply routes will have been diversified.
cues: Make a measured conjecture that the recent port delay probably complicated supply
Project that by the end of the decade, supply routes will have been diversified
c1-34-05.target: El retraso en el puerto ya habrá complicado el abastecimiento regional. Para el final de la década se habrán diversificado las rutas de abastecimiento.
c1-34-05.english: The delay at the port has probably already complicated regional supply. By the end of the decade, supply routes will have been diversified.
c1-34-05.canDo: I can express measured conjecture about recent past events with the futuro perfecto.

c1-34-consolidation.title: Closing a Geopolitics Presentation
c1-34-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. You are closing a seminar presentation in Budapest on global trade corridors and regional alliances.
c1-34-consolidation.prompt: Conclude in two sentences by linking greater trade interdependence to multilateral cooperation, and citing observers to project that supply chains will have been reconfigured by the end of the decade.
cues: Link greater trade interdependence to the need for multilateral cooperation
Cite observers and project that supply chains will have been reconfigured by the end of the decade
c1-34-consolidation.target: Cuanta mayor interdependencia comercial existe, más necesaria resulta la cooperación multilateral. Según señalan los observadores, para el final de la década se habrán reconfigurado las cadenas de abastecimiento.
c1-34-consolidation.english: The greater the trade interdependence there is, the more necessary multilateral cooperation becomes. As observers point out, by the end of the decade supply chains will have been reconfigured.
c1-34-consolidation.canDo: I can express proportional interdependence and projected global shifts accurately.

c1-35-01.title: Opening a Formal Talk
c1-35-01.scenario: You are Carlos. At a business forum in Budapest, you step up to the podium to open a short presentation before a formal audience.
c1-35-01.prompt: Open your talk in two sentences using formal ustedes address: thank the attendees for their attentive presence, and politely ask them to allow you to begin with a single question.
cues: Open with a formal vocative and thank the attendees consistently in ustedes
Use a courteous audience imperative to ask permission to begin with one question
c1-35-01.target: Estimados asistentes, les agradezco su atenta presencia en este auditorio. Permítanme empezar mi intervención con una sola pregunta.
c1-35-01.english: Esteemed attendees, I thank you for your attentive presence in this auditorium. Allow me to begin my address with a single question.
c1-35-01.canDo: I can open a formal speech with appropriate vocatives and consistent ustedes pronouns and possessives.

c1-35-02.title: Delivering an Emphatic Opening
c1-35-02.scenario: You are Meg. Practising a speech for a university debate club in Budapest, you want to give your central claim stronger oratorical cadence.
c1-35-02.prompt: State in two sentences using fronted negative and restrictive adverbs that never must we sacrifice clarity for empty rhetoric, and that only in this way will a measured opening hold the room's attention.
cues: Front a negative adverb without double negation to reject sacrificing clarity
Front a restrictive adverb with verb-subject inversion to show how a measured opening works
c1-35-02.target: Jamás debemos sacrificar la claridad por una retórica vacía. Solo así mantendrá una apertura pausada la atención de la sala.
c1-35-02.english: Never must we sacrifice clarity for empty rhetoric. Only in this way will a measured opening hold the room's attention.
c1-35-02.canDo: I can open a rhetorical claim with nunca antes, jamás, en ningún caso and solo así.

c1-35-03.title: Spotlighting What Persuades
c1-35-03.scenario: You are Meg. After a university seminar in Budapest, a classmate asks what really makes a speaker persuasive on stage.
c1-35-03.prompt: Answer in two sentences using cleft sentences: contrast empty eloquence with concise diction, and highlight that it is to the attendees that a speaker must direct a steady gaze.
cues: Use a corrective cleft to contrast eloquence with concise diction
Use a prepositional cleft repeating the preposition to focus on the attendees
c1-35-03.target: No es la elocuencia vacía lo que convence, sino la dicción concisa. Además, es a los asistentes a quienes el orador debe dirigir una mirada firme.
c1-35-03.english: It is not empty eloquence that convinces, but concise diction. Moreover, it is to the attendees that the speaker must direct a steady gaze.
c1-35-03.canDo: I can contrast a misconception with a thesis using no es … lo que …, sino ….

c1-35-04.title: Managing a Brief Aside
c1-35-04.scenario: You are Carlos. During a formal presentation at your office in Budapest, you make a short aside to thank the attendees and then return to your main point.
c1-35-04.prompt: Deliver two sentences: open a brief aside to thank the attendees, then close the aside and pick up the thread to synthesise the main idea.
cues: Signal the start of a brief formal aside to thank the attendees
Close the aside and signal your return to synthesise the main idea
c1-35-04.target: Abro un breve paréntesis para agradecer a los asistentes. Cierro el paréntesis y retomo el hilo para sintetizar la idea principal.
c1-35-04.english: Let me open a brief aside to thank the attendees. I close the aside and pick up the thread to synthesise the main idea.
c1-35-04.canDo: I can open a brief formal aside with abro un paréntesis para and al margen de.

c1-35-05.title: Contrasting Effect and Goal
c1-35-05.scenario: You are Meg. Reviewing a guest lecture with a classmate in Budapest, you describe how the speaker moved the room and suggest how you both should prepare your closings.
c1-35-05.prompt: Write two sentences using de tal modo que / de tal manera que: report as a real result that the speaker captivated the auditorium by the way she spoke, and say that we must prepare the closing so that it persuades the audience.
cues: Report an achieved result in the indicative about captivating the auditorium
Express an intended persuasive goal in the subjunctive for a closing
c1-35-05.target: La oradora habló de tal manera que cautivó al auditorio. Nosotros debemos preparar el cierre de tal modo que persuada al público.
c1-35-05.english: The speaker spoke in such a way that she captivated the auditorium. We must prepare the closing in such a way that it persuades the audience.
c1-35-05.canDo: I can contrast de tal modo que + indicative (achieved result) with subjunctive (intended goal).

c1-35-consolidation.title: Closing a Public Forum
c1-35-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You are delivering the closing remarks at a formal forum in Budapest.
c1-35-consolidation.prompt: Deliver a two-sentence closing: address the attendees politely in ustedes, highlight with a corrective cleft that clarity rather than rapid applause measures good oratory, and frame a closing goal with de tal modo que + subjunctive.
cues: Address the attendees formally in ustedes and use a corrective cleft about clarity
State an intended persuasive goal with de tal modo que + subjunctive
c1-35-consolidation.target: Estimados asistentes, no es el aplauso rápido lo que mide la oratoria, sino la claridad. Hablemos siempre de tal modo que nuestra dicción concisa conmueva al auditorio.
c1-35-consolidation.english: Esteemed attendees, it is not quick applause that measures oratory, but clarity. Let us always speak in such a way that our concise diction moves the auditorium.
c1-35-consolidation.canDo: I can address a live audience with formal vocatives and consistent ustedes courtesy.

c1-36-01.title: Tightening a Formal Paragraph
c1-36-01.scenario: You are Carlos. At your office in Budapest, you summarise how your team finalised a written proposal.
c1-36-01.prompt: Explain in one or two formal sentences using a compound infinitive opener and lo cual that after having compared the two versions, you adjusted the main clause, which gave greater precision to the text.
cues: Open with a compound infinitive about comparing the two versions
Use clausal lo cual to state that adjusting the main clause added precision
c1-36-01.target: Tras haber comparado las dos versiones, ajustamos la oración principal, lo cual dio mayor precisión al texto.
c1-36-01.english: After having compared the two versions, we adjusted the main clause, which gave greater precision to the text.
c1-36-01.canDo: I can open a formal sentence with a compound infinitive (tras haber, el haber).

c1-36-02.title: Self-Editing a Draft
c1-36-02.scenario: You are Meg. After finishing an essay draft at your university in Budapest, you tell Carlos what you fixed during your final edit.
c1-36-02.prompt: State in two sentences without dequeísmo or non-normative gerunds that you are sure it is advisable to refine the draft, and that you rewrote a sentence that balances clarity and rigour.
cues: Use estar seguro de que cleanly to state that refining the draft is advisable
Describe rewriting a sentence with a finite relative clause rather than an adjectival gerund
c1-36-02.target: Estoy segura de que conviene depurar el borrador. Reescribí una oración que equilibra la claridad y el rigor.
c1-36-02.english: I am sure that it is advisable to refine the draft. I rewrote a sentence that balances clarity and rigour.
c1-36-02.canDo: I can spot and remove dequeísmo and queísmo in my own drafts.

c1-36-03.title: Shaping Stance with Mood & Order
c1-36-03.scenario: You are Meg. After a seminar in Budapest, you react to a classmate's argument and express regret that Carlos missed the session.
c1-36-03.prompt: Write two sentences: front the direct object 'that incisive argument' with its clitic to say you share it, and use sentir que + subjunctive to tell Carlos directly that you are sorry he could not attend.
cues: Front the direct object with its matching clitic pronoun
Use sentir que + subjunctive to express regret rather than perception
c1-36-03.target: Ese argumento incisivo lo comparto por completo. Siento que no hayas podido asistir a la charla.
c1-36-03.english: That incisive argument I share completely. I am sorry that you could not attend the talk.
c1-36-03.canDo: I can shift meaning cleanly with indicative vs subjunctive after sentir que and decir que.

c1-36-04.title: Conceding with Humour & Irony
c1-36-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Chatting with a colleague in Budapest about learning to alternate registers in Spanish, you concede the difficulty and reject an exaggeration ironically.
c1-36-04.prompt: Reply in two sentences: use the concessive future to grant that alternating registers may be demanding before countering with pero, and add an ironic ¡ni que! exclamation about a small slip.
cues: Use the concessive future + pero to concede difficulty and highlight agility
Add an ironic ¡ni que + imperfect subjunctive! remark about a small slip
c1-36-04.target: Será exigente alternar registros, pero te da una voz muy ágil. ¡Ni que un pequeño desliz fuera el fin del mundo!
c1-36-04.english: Alternating registers may be demanding, but it gives you a very agile voice. As if a small slip were the end of the world!
c1-36-04.canDo: I can concede a point before countering it with the concessive future (será …, pero …).

c1-36-05.title: Switching to Relaxed Speech
c1-36-05.scenario: You are Meg. Over coffee in Budapest, you tell Carlos informally that you read the whole book in two days and loved it.
c1-36-05.prompt: Say in two relaxed conversational sentences using spoken markers, aspectual se and a diminutive that you read the whole book in two days, and that expressing yourself with naturalness brings ease and authenticity.
cues: Use a conversational marker, bounded aspectual se and a diminutive to say you read the whole book
Note that expressing oneself with naturalness brings ease and authenticity
c1-36-05.target: Pues me leí el libro enterito en dos días y, vamos, me encantó. Expresarse con naturalidad te da mucha soltura y autenticidad.
c1-36-05.english: Well, I read the whole book in two days and, honestly, I loved it. Expressing yourself with naturalness gives you great ease and authenticity.
c1-36-05.canDo: I can shift the same idea smoothly between formal prose and natural conversation.

c1-36-consolidation.title: Reflecting on Your Own Voice
c1-36-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. At the end of a long project in Budapest, you reflect on what you have gained in Spanish.
c1-36-consolidation.prompt: Write two sentences combining C1 tools: open with a compound infinitive and lo cual to note that honing your drafts brought precision, and use the concessive future to concede the effort while celebrating your own voice.
cues: Combine a compound infinitive opener with clausal lo cual about precision
Use the concessive future + pero to celebrate expressing yourself in your own voice
c1-36-consolidation.target: Tras haber afinado muchos borradores, gané mayor precisión, lo cual mejoró mi dominio del idioma. Tendrá sus dificultades, pero expresarse con voz propia merece todo el esfuerzo.
c1-36-consolidation.english: After having honed many drafts, I gained greater precision, which improved my command of the language. It may have its difficulties, but expressing oneself in one's own voice is worth all the effort.
c1-36-consolidation.canDo: I can write dense, precise formal prose with compound infinitives and el cual / lo cual.
